nodos.desc: The first digit after the decimal point, representing one-tenth (0.1) of a unit.

nodos.label: Hundredth Place
nodos.desc: The second digit after the decimal point, representing one-hundredth (0.01) of a unit.

nodos.label: Thousandth Place
nodos.desc: The third digit after the decimal point, representing one-thousandth (0.001) of a unit.

nodos.label: Filler Zeros
nodos.desc: Zeros added to the end of a decimal to maintain place value alignment, which do not change the value but are used for comparison purposes.

nodos.label: Actual Value
nodos.desc: The exact result of a calculation, as opposed to an estimated value, used to compare with the estimated result.

nodos.label: Decimal places
nodos.desc: The individual positions after the decimal point: tenths (1/10), hundredths (1/100), and thousandths (1/1000), which determine the precision and alignment in decimal operations.

nodos.label: Maximum Exponent
nodos.desc: Para cada factor primo, se toma la potencia más alta en la descomposición de cualquiera de los dos números.

nodos.label: Reduction to Lowest Terms
nodos.desc: The process of simplifying a fraction by dividing both numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor (GCD) to express it in its simplest form.

nodos.label: Target Denominator
nodos.desc: The desired denominator to which fractions are converted to enable addition or subtraction, typically chosen as a common multiple of the original denominators.

nodos.label: Conversión de fracción impropia a mixta
nodos.desc: Proceso de transformar una fracción impropia en una fracción mixta, como 117/20 = 5 17/20.

nodos.label: Operación decimal
nodos.desc: Cálculo que utiliza números decimales para representar fracciones, como 0.625 para 13/20.

nodos.label: Conversion to Improper Fraction
nodos.desc: Transforming a mixed number into an improper fraction (e.g., 3 1/4 becomes 13/4) to simplify arithmetic operations.

nodos.label: Simplification of Fraction
nodos.desc: Reducing a fraction to its lowest terms by dividing both numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor, such as reducing 8/4 to 2/1 or 0.5.

nodos.label: Multiples of 10, 100, 1000
nodos.desc: Numbers that are divisible by 10, 100, or 1000, which can be broken down using place value to simplify division problems.

nodos.label: Análisis de costos
nodos.desc: Enfoque matemático que integra múltiples operaciones para determinar el costo total de producción, incluyendo materiales y mano de obra, en función de variables como cantidad y precio unitario.

nodos.label: Division as Multiplication by Reciprocal
nodos.desc: Dividing a whole number by another number can be expressed as multiplying the whole number by the reciprocal of the divisor, such as 8 ÷ 4 = 8 × (1/4).

nodos.label: Alineación vertical
nodos.desc: Técnica de alinear los dígitos de dos números en una operación de multiplicación para facilitar el cálculo.

nodos.label: Posición decimal
nodos.desc: Lugar de un dígito en una representación decimal, que determina su valor relativo (por ejemplo, décimas, centésimas).

nodos.label: Suma de cifras decimales
nodos.desc: El número total de dígitos decimales en los factores multiplicados, que determina la posición del punto decimal en el resultado final.

nodos.label: Número lineal
nodos.desc: Representación gráfica de números en una línea, utilizada para visualizar divisiones de decimales mediante segmentos iguales.

nodos.label: Longitud de arco
nodos.desc: Distancia entre marcas en una línea numérica, utilizada para medir cuántas veces cabe un segmento en un número decimal.

nodos.label: Segmento igual
nodos.desc: Parte uniforme de una línea numérica que se usa para dividir un número decimal en partes iguales.

nodos.label: Partes iguales
nodos.desc: División de un número en secciones de tamaño uniforme, que permite calcular el cociente mediante conteo de segmentos.

nodos.label: Desplazamiento de valor de lugar
nodos.desc: El desplazamiento de dígitos en una posición específica en un número decimal cambia el valor relativo de cada dígito, afectando el resultado final de operaciones aritméticas.

nodos.label: Sum of Volumes
nodos.desc: The total volume of a complex solid obtained by adding the volumes of its individual, smaller components.

nodos.label: Range of Volumes
nodos.desc: The difference between the minimum and maximum possible volumes of a variable-shaped object, such as a box with varying height.

nodos.label: Ángulo de giro
nodos.desc: Cambio de dirección en un movimiento, como un giro de 90 grados, que puede ser interpretado como una transformación de coordenadas en el plano.

nodos.label: Trayectoria de movimiento
nodos.desc: Secuencia de puntos que representa el recorrido de un objeto o persona en el plano cartesiano, basado en cambios de coordenadas.

nodos.label: Translation of Expressions
nodos.desc: The process of converting verbal descriptions into algebraic expressions using variables and mathematical symbols.

nodos.label: Operador
nodos.desc: Símbolo que indica una operación matemática como suma, resta, multiplicación o división.

nodos.label: Valor futuro
nodos.desc: Cálculo de una cantidad en un punto futuro, como la edad en cinco años, basado en el valor actual.

nodos.label: Patrones numéricos
nodos.desc: Secuencias o estructuras que siguen una regla fija, como el ciclo de los días de la semana, que se repite de forma periódica.

nodos.label: Secuencia numérica
nodos.desc: Una lista de números que siguen un patrón o regla, como las cantidades vendidas a diferentes precios.

nodos.label: Gráficación
nodos.desc: Proceso de representar datos como puntos en un plano cartesiano para visualizar patrones y relaciones entre variables.

nodos.label: Properties of a Trapezoid
nodos.desc: A trapezoid is a quadrilateral with at least one pair of parallel sides, known as bases, and the area is computed using the average of the bases multiplied by the height.

nodos.label: Isosceles Trapezoid
nodos.desc: A specialized trapezoid with symmetrical non-parallel sides (equal leg lengths), equal base angles, and diagonals that intersect at right angles, forming smaller right triangles.

nodos.label: Diagonal Intersection
nodos.desc: In an isosceles trapezoid, diagonals intersect at right angles, creating smaller right triangles within the shape.

nodos.label: Phospholipid
nodos.desc: A molecule that forms the basic structure of cell membranes, consisting of a hydrophilic head and two hydrophobic tails, enabling the formation of a lipid bilayer.

nodos.label: Plasma Membrane
nodos.desc: A selectively permeable membrane that surrounds the cell, regulating the movement of substances in and out through processes like diffusion and osmosis.

nodos.label: Diffusion
nodos.desc: The passive movement of molecules from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration until equilibrium is reached.

nodos.label: Osmosis
nodos.desc: The diffusion of water molecules across a semipermeable membrane from an area of low solute concentration to an area of high solute concentration.

nodos.label: Semipermeable Membrane
nodos.desc: A membrane that allows certain substances to pass through while restricting others, based on size, charge, or polarity.

nodos.label: Mitochondrion
nodos.desc: An organelle responsible for cellular respiration and energy (ATP) production through metabolic pathways involving enzyme-catalyzed reactions.

nodos.label: Enzyme
nodos.desc: A biological catalyst that speeds up chemical reactions in cells without being consumed, typically by lowering the activation energy required for the reaction.

nodos.label: Metabolic Pathway
nodos.desc: A series of interconnected chemical reactions that convert substrates into products, often involving enzymes to catalyze each step.

nodos.label: Cellular Function
nodos.desc: The specific role a cell or organelle plays in maintaining life processes, such as energy production, structural integrity, or regulation of internal environment.

nodos.label: Organelle
nodos.desc: A specialized structure within a cell that performs a specific function, such as the nucleolus in the nucleus or chloroplasts in plant cells.

nodos.label: Nuclear Envelope
nodos.desc: A protective layer composed of two lipid bilayers that encloses the nucleus, with pores allowing controlled exchange of molecules between the nucleus and cytoplasm.

nodos.label: Nucleolus
nodos.desc: A structure within the nucleus responsible for the assembly of ribosomes, which are essential for protein synthesis.

nodos.label: Cell Wall
nodos.desc: A rigid structure found only in plant cells, made of cellulose, that provides structural support and protection to the cell.

nodos.label: Cytoskeleton
nodos.desc: An internal network of protein fibers in animal cells that maintains cell shape, enables movement, and supports cellular functions.

nodos.label: Chloroplast
nodos.desc: An organelle found only in plant cells that conducts photosynthesis, converting light energy into chemical energy (glucose) using chlorophyll.

nodos.label: Homeostasis
nodos.desc: The process by which cells maintain a stable internal environment despite external changes, through regulated functions of organelles.

nodos.label: Photosynthesis
nodos.desc: A biological process in which plant cells use light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen, occurring in chloroplasts.

nodos.label: Lipid Bilayer
nodos.desc: A fundamental structure in cell membranes composed of two layers of lipid molecules, forming a selectively permeable barrier.

nodos.label: Collagen
nodos.desc: A fibrous protein in connective tissue that provides structural support and strength.

nodos.label: Elastin
nodos.desc: A protein in connective tissue that provides elasticity and flexibility to tissues.

nodos.label: Extracellular Matrix
nodos.desc: A combination of ground substance and fiber proteins that provides structural and functional support in connective tissue.

nodos.label: Fibroblasts
nodos.desc: Cells in the dermis that produce collagen and elastin fibers for structural support.

nodos.label: Macrophages
nodos.desc: Immune cells that engulf debris and microorganisms in connective tissue.

nodos.label: Mast Cells
nodos.desc: Cells that release histamine during inflammatory responses.

nodos.label: Loose Connective Tissue
nodos.desc: A type of connective tissue with low density and high fluid content, providing flexibility and support.

nodos.label: Dense Connective Tissue
nodos.desc: A type of connective tissue with high density and strong fibers, providing mechanical strength.

nodos.label: Fluid Connective Tissue
nodos.desc: A category of connective tissue including blood and lymph, which transport fluids and cells.

nodos.label: Adipose Tissue
nodos.desc: A specialized connective tissue that stores energy in the form of fat.

nodos.label: Cartilage
nodos.desc: A specialized connective tissue that provides flexible support and cushioning.

nodos.label: Bone
nodos.desc: A rigid connective tissue that provides structural support and protection for the body.

nodos.label: Hematopoietic Tissue
nodos.desc: Tissue in which blood cells are produced, such as red marrow in bones.

nodos.label: Artery
nodos.desc: A blood vessel that carries oxygen-rich blood away from the heart, with thick muscular walls and elastic fibers.

nodos.label: Vein
nodos.desc: A blood vessel that returns oxygen-poor blood to the heart, with thinner walls than arteries.

nodos.label: Capillary
nodos.desc: A tiny blood vessel with extremely narrow diameter (5–10 micrometers) that enables diffusion of gases and nutrients between blood and tissues.

nodos.label: Endothelial Cells
nodos.desc: Cells that line the lumen of blood vessels, ensuring smooth blood flow and regulating vascular function.

nodos.label: Tunica Intima
nodos.desc: The innermost layer of blood vessels composed of simple squamous epithelium and a basement membrane.

nodos.label: Tunica Media
nodos.desc: The middle layer of arteries composed of smooth muscle and elastic fibers that regulate vessel diameter and blood pressure.

nodos.label: Tunica Externa
nodos.desc: The outermost layer of arteries containing collagen fibers that anchor the vessel to surrounding structures.

nodos.label: Concentration Gradient
nodos.desc: A difference in concentration of substances across a membrane that drives passive diffusion in capillaries.

nodos.label: Vascular Structure
nodos.desc: The organization of blood vessels (arteries, capillaries, veins) that forms a network for circulation and exchange.

nodos.label: Reproduction
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual los organismos producen descendencia, asegurando la continuidad de su especie.

nodos.label: Sexual Reproduction
nodos.desc: Tipo de reproducción en la que dos padres contribuyen material genético, generando descendencia con diversidad genética.

nodos.label: Asexual Reproduction
nodos.desc: Tipo de reproducción que involucra un solo padre y produce descendencia genéticamente idéntica al padre.

nodos.label: Mitosis
nodos.desc: Proceso celular por el cual una célula se divide para producir dos células hijas idénticas en genética.

nodos.label: Genetic Diversity
nodos.desc: Variabilidad en el material genético de los organismos, que se incrementa en la reproducción sexual.

nodos.label: Biodiversity
nodos.desc: Variabilidad de los organismos vivos en un ecosistema, que se mantiene mediante procesos de reproducción.

nodos.label: Cell Division
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual una célula se divide para formar nuevas células, fundamental en la reproducción asexual.

nodos.label: Abiotic Factors
nodos.desc: Non-living components of an organism's environment, such as temperature, light, water availability, and soil composition, that influence survival and reproduction.

nodos.label: Biotic Factors
nodos.desc: Living components of an organism's environment, such as other organisms, that influence population size and distribution.

nodos.label: Environmental Influence
nodos.desc: The impact of external environmental conditions on organism growth, development, and reproductive success.

nodos.label: Human Impact
nodos.desc: The alteration of natural environments by human activities, which can affect organism growth and reproduction.

nodos.label: Reproductive Success
nodos.desc: The ability of organisms to produce offspring successfully, influenced by both biological and environmental factors.

nodos.label: Tamaño de la población
nodos.desc: Número total de individuos en una población.

nodos.label: Comunidad ecológica
nodos.desc: Colección de poblaciones interrelacionadas que viven en un área específica.

nodos.label: Predación
nodos.desc: Relación en la que un organismo (predador) consume a otro (presa).

nodos.label: Competencia
nodos.desc: Interacción entre especies que compiten por recursos como alimento o espacio.

nodos.label: Símbiosis
nodos.desc: Relación estrecha entre dos especies que beneficia a una o ambas.

nodos.label: Ecosistema
nodos.desc: Sistema que incluye a las comunidades vivas y los factores físicos del entorno en el que viven.

nodos.label: Red trófica
nodos.desc: Representación del flujo de energía y nutrientes entre organismos en un ecosistema.

nodos.label: Productores primarios
nodos.desc: Organismos fotosintéticos, como plantas y algas, que convierten la luz solar en energía química.

nodos.label: Consumidores primarios
nodos.desc: Organismos que se alimentan directamente de los productores primarios, como los herbívoros.

nodos.label: Consumidores secundarios
nodos.desc: Organismos que se alimentan de los consumidores primarios.

nodos.label: Consumidores terciarios
nodos.desc: Organismos que se alimentan de los consumidores secundarios.

nodos.label: Descomponedores
nodos.desc: Organismos que descomponen materia orgánica muerta y reciclan nutrientes.

nodos.label: Flujo de energía
nodos.desc: Proceso unidireccional en el que la energía se transfiere desde los productores hasta los consumidores a través de la cadena trófica.

nodos.label: Competitive Exclusion
nodos.desc: Un fenómeno en ecología donde dos especies no pueden ocupar exactamente el mismo nicho en un ecosistema, lo que lleva a que una especie excluya a la otra debido a la competencia intensa por recursos como alimento y espacio.

nodos.label: Niche
nodos.desc: El rol de una especie en su entorno, que incluye cómo obtiene recursos, dónde vive y cómo interactúa con otros organismos.

nodos.label: Mutualism
nodos.desc: Relación ecológica en la que dos especies benefician mutuamente al intercambiar recursos o servicios que mejoran la fitness de ambas.

nodos.label: Trophic Level
nodos.desc: A trophic level represents the position an organism occupies in a food chain, such as primary producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, and tertiary consumers, based on the flow of energy and matter through an ecosystem.

nodos.label: Food Chain
nodos.desc: A linear sequence of organisms through which matter and energy are transferred, showing how energy flows from one organism to another via consumption.

nodos.label: Matter Flow
nodos.desc: The movement of essential elements such as carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen through ecosystems, primarily via biological processes like photosynthesis, respiration, and decomposition.

nodos.label: Ecosystem Resilience
nodos.desc: The ability of an ecosystem to recover from disturbances, such as human activities or climate change, and maintain its structure and function over time.

nodos.label: Energy Transfer Efficiency
nodos.desc: The proportion of energy transferred from one trophic level to the next, typically around 10%, due to metabolic losses and heat production.

nodos.label: Cascading Effects
nodos.desc: A chain reaction of ecological impacts that occur when a change in one component of a food web affects multiple other components, leading to widespread ecosystem disturbances.

nodos.label: Phytoplankton
nodos.desc: Microscopic photosynthetic organisms that form the base of many aquatic food webs, converting solar energy into biomass through photosynthesis.

nodos.label: Zooplankton
nodos.desc: Tiny aquatic animals that consume phytoplankton and serve as a primary food source for larger organisms in marine food webs.

nodos.label: Cromosoma
nodos.desc: Estructura genética que contiene genes y determina características biológicas de un organismo.

nodos.label: Gen
nodos.desc: Segmento de ADN que codifica una proteína o función específica y determina un rasgo hereditario.

nodos.label: Alelo
nodos.desc: Versión alternativa de un gen que puede determinar diferentes expresiones de un rasgo, como el color de ojos.

nodos.label: Autómatos
nodos.desc: Cromosomas no sexuales que se parecen en ambos sexos y contienen genes relacionados con características generales del organismo.

nodos.label: Cromosoma sexual
nodos.desc: Cromosoma que determina el sexo del organismo, siendo XX en mujeres y XY en hombres.

nodos.label: Cromosomas homólogos
nodos.desc: Pares de cromosomas que contienen información genética similar, uno heredado de cada progenitor.

nodos.label: Meiosis
nodos.desc: Proceso de división celular que reduce el número de cromosomas a la mitad, produciendo gametos (espermatozoides y óvulos).

nodos.label: Cruce de cromosomas
nodos.desc: Intercambio de segmentos de ADN entre cromosomas homólogos durante la meiosis, generando variabilidad genética.

nodos.label: Haploide
nodos.desc: Estado celular que contiene la mitad del número de cromosomas de una célula somática, típico en gametos.

nodos.label: Diploide
nodos.desc: Estado celular que contiene dos copias de cada cromosoma, una de cada progenitor, típico en células somáticas.

nodos.label: Mutación
nodos.desc: Cambio en la secuencia de nucleótidos que constituyen un gen.

nodos.label: Delección
nodos.desc: Pérdida de una parte de un cromosoma.

nodos.label: Duplicación
nodos.desc: Replicación de una sección de un cromosoma, que puede ocurrir una o varias veces.

nodos.label: Translocación
nodos.desc: Intercambio de segmentos entre dos cromosomas no homólogos.

nodos.label: Inversión
nodos.desc: Rompimiento y reensamblaje de un segmento de cromosoma en orden inverso.

nodos.label: Selección natural
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual las características beneficiosas se vuelven más comunes en una población.

nodos.label: Abnormalidad genética
nodos.desc: Alteración en la información genética que puede causar problemas de desarrollo o de salud.

nodos.label: Fibrosis quística
nodos.desc: Trastorno genético causado por mutaciones en el gen CFTR, que afecta la función de proteínas que transportan iones.

nodos.label: Anemia falciforme
nodos.desc: Condición hereditaria causada por mutaciones en el gen de hemoglobina, que provoca que los glóbulos rojos adopten una forma de cuchilla.

nodos.label: Mutación neutral
nodos.desc: Mutación que no tiene impacto significativo en el funcionamiento de las proteínas.

nodos.label: Mutación dañina
nodos.desc: Mutación que causa daño significativo en el organismo que la lleva.

nodos.label: Recessive allele
nodos.desc: An allele that is not expressed unless present in two copies; masked by dominant alleles.

nodos.label: Recombination frequency
nodos.desc: The percentage of times linked genes are separated during meiosis, used to determine the distance between genes on a chromosome.

nodos.label: Sex determination system
nodos.desc: The mechanism by which an organism determines its sex based on its sex chromosomes; in humans, females have XX and males have XY.

nodos.label: Trait
nodos.desc: An observable feature or characteristic of an organism, such as hair color or disease susceptibility, determined by genetics and environment.

nodos.label: Zygote
nodos.desc: A fertilized egg formed by the union of sperm and egg cells, containing a full set of chromosomes.

nodos.label: Dominant allele
nodos.desc: An allele whose phenotype appears when present in either homozygous or heterozygous form, represented by a capital letter.

nodos.label: Homozygous
nodos.desc: When both alleles for a gene are identical, either both dominant (AA) or both recessive (aa).

nodos.label: Heterozygous
nodos.desc: When the two alleles for a gene differ, such as one dominant and one recessive (Aa).

nodos.label: Common Ancestor
nodos.desc: The concept that all living organisms share a single ancestral origin, forming the foundation of evolutionary theory.

nodos.label: Phylogenetic Tree
nodos.desc: A diagram that represents the evolutionary relationships among various biological species based on shared characteristics.

nodos.label: Clade
nodos.desc: A group of organisms that includes an ancestral species and all of its descendants, defined by shared derived characters.

nodos.label: Shared Derived Character
nodos.desc: A trait that is unique to a clade and inherited from a common ancestor, used to define and identify clades.

nodos.label: Monophyly
nodos.desc: A clade that includes an ancestor and all of its descendants, representing a complete evolutionary lineage.

nodos.label: Paraphyly
nodos.desc: A group that includes an ancestor but excludes some of its descendants, thus not representing a complete evolutionary lineage.

nodos.label: Polyphyly
nodos.desc: A group composed of multiple lineages that do not share a common ancestor, indicating separate evolutionary origins.

nodos.label: Morphological Data
nodos.desc: Physical characteristics such as body structure, organs, and developmental patterns used to infer evolutionary relationships.

nodos.label: Molecular Data
nodos.desc: Genetic information such as DNA sequences or protein structures used to compare organisms and infer evolutionary history.

nodos.label: Genetic Data
nodos.desc: Information derived from DNA or genes used to reconstruct evolutionary trees through computational methods.

nodos.label: Maximum Likelihood
nodos.desc: A statistical method used to infer evolutionary relationships by finding the tree that maximizes the probability of observing the data.

nodos.label: Bayesian Inference
nodos.desc: A statistical method that uses prior knowledge and observed data to compute the probability of different evolutionary trees.

nodos.label: Principio de superposición
nodos.desc: Concepto que establece que en una secuencia de capas de roca, las capas más superiores son más jóvenes que las inferiores.

nodos.label: Sucesión faunística
nodos.desc: Principio que indica que ciertas especies fósiles aparecen y desaparecen en momentos específicos de la historia geológica, permitiendo correlacionar capas de roca.

nodos.label: Relación cruzada
nodos.desc: Concepto que afirma que cualquier estructura que corte a otra debe ser más joven, utilizada para determinar el orden de formación de rocas y estructuras.

nodos.label: Datación absoluta
nodos.desc: Método que proporciona fechas exactas de formación de rocas mediante técnicas radiométricas, como el uranio-plomo, potasio-argón y argón-argón.

nodos.label: Biosignaturas
nodos.desc: Patrones en la distribución de organismos a través del tiempo que reflejan la historia evolutiva de la vida en la Tierra.

nodos.label: Formas transicionales
nodos.desc: Especies intermedias que muestran cambios graduales entre grupos taxonómicos, como en el caso de Archaeopteryx o Tiktaalik.

nodos.label: Extinción masiva
nodos.desc: Evento geológico que elimina una gran cantidad de especies, dejando espacio para la radiación adaptativa de nuevas líneas evolutivas.

nodos.label: Radiación adaptativa
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual las especies sobrevivientes se diversifican rápidamente para ocupar nichos ecológicos vacantes tras una extinción masiva.

nodos.label: Fósiles de índice
nodos.desc: Especies que existieron durante intervalos cortos y ampliamente distribuidos, utilizadas para correlacionar capas rocosas en diferentes regiones del mundo.

nodos.label: Escala geológica
nodos.desc: Marco temporal que organiza la historia de la Tierra en intervalos de tiempo definidos, como eras y períodos, y permite ubicar eventos fósiles en el tiempo.

nodos.label: Celestial Bodies
nodos.desc: Objects found in outer space, including planets, moons, asteroids, comets, stars, and galaxies.

nodos.label: Orbit
nodos.desc: The path taken by a celestial body moving around another, determined by their mutual gravitational attraction.

nodos.label: Constellation
nodos.desc: A group of stars arranged in a particular pattern as observed from Earth. There are 88 officially recognized constellations covering the entire sky.

nodos.label: Solar System
nodos.desc: A system consisting of eight planets, numerous moons, and countless small bodies like asteroids and comets, formed approximately 4.5 billion years ago from a cloud of dust and gas.

nodos.label: Earth's Orbit
nodos.desc: The path Earth follows around the Sun, governed by gravitational attraction between Earth and the Sun.

nodos.label: Sun
nodos.desc: The central star of the solar system, responsible for providing heat and light, and accounting for more than 99% of the total mass of the solar system.

nodos.label: Planetary Order
nodos.desc: The sequence of planets in our solar system from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

nodos.label: Gravitational Law
nodos.desc: The gravitational force between two objects is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

nodos.label: Perihelion
nodos.desc: The point in the Earth's orbit where it is closest to the Sun.

nodos.label: Aphelion
nodos.desc: The point in the Earth's orbit where it is farthest from the Sun.

nodos.label: Solstice
nodos.desc: An astronomical event that occurs twice a year when the Sun reaches its northernmost or southernmost point relative to the Earth's equator, marking the start of summer and winter.

nodos.label: Equinox
nodos.desc: An astronomical event when the Sun is directly above the Earth's equator, resulting in nearly equal day and night lengths across the globe.

nodos.label: Latitude
nodos.desc: A geographic coordinate that specifies the north-south position of a point on the Earth's surface, influencing climate and seasonal variation.

nodos.label: Proximity to Bodies of Water
nodos.desc: The closeness of a region to large bodies of water, which moderates temperature and influences climate patterns, leading to milder seasonal variations in coastal areas.

nodos.label: Axial Tilt
nodos.desc: The angle at which the Earth's rotational axis is inclined relative to its orbital plane, responsible for the changing seasons as the Earth orbits the Sun.

nodos.label: Lunar Phases
nodos.desc: The visible changes in the Moon's appearance from Earth, caused by the relative positions of the Earth, Sun, and Moon.

nodos.label: Precipitation
nodos.desc: The process of water falling from the atmosphere as rain, snow, sleet, or hail, influenced by atmospheric conditions and climate zones.

nodos.label: Ocean Currents
nodos.desc: The continuous, directed movement of seawater, which can influence coastal climates by transporting heat or cold water over long distances.

nodos.label: Weather
nodos.desc: Short-term atmospheric conditions such as temperature, precipitation, wind, and humidity, which vary from day to day and location to location.

nodos.label: Climate
nodos.desc: The long-term average of weather patterns in a region over periods of decades or centuries, reflecting typical conditions and trends.

nodos.label: Water Cycle
nodos.desc: The continuous movement of water on Earth, including evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and infiltration, which governs the distribution and availability of water in ecosystems.

nodos.label: Infiltration
nodos.desc: The process by which water seeps into the soil, affecting groundwater recharge and surface runoff, which in turn influences streamflow and flood risk.

nodos.label: Streamflow
nodos.desc: The volume of water flowing in a stream or river over time, influenced by precipitation, infiltration, and land use.

nodos.label: Flood Risk
nodos.desc: The likelihood of flooding in a given area, which increases when streamflow exceeds the capacity of natural or artificial drainage systems.

nodos.label: Coriolis Effect
nodos.desc: A phenomenon caused by the Earth's rotation, which deflects moving air and water to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere, influencing wind patterns and atmospheric circulation.

nodos.label: Influencia de los océanos
nodos.desc: Los océanos moderan las variaciones de temperatura debido a su capacidad para absorber y liberar calor lentamente, afectando el clima de las zonas costeras.

nodos.label: Patrones de viento
nodos.desc: Los vientos transportan humedad y calor entre regiones, influyendo en las temperaturas y patrones de precipitación locales.

nodos.label: Oxidation
nodos.desc: Un proceso de descomposición química en el que el oxígeno se combina con otros elementos en rocas, provocando la formación de óxidos, como el óxido de hierro (rust).

nodos.label: Carbonation
nodos.desc: Proceso químico en el que el dióxido de carbono de la atmósfera se disuelve en el agua de lluvia, formando ácido carbónico, que disuelve minerales como el calcario en rocas de caliza y mármol.

nodos.label: Weathering Biológico
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que organismos vivos, como lichenes y animales que burro, contribuyen a la descomposición de rocas mediante la producción de ácidos o el movimiento físico de sedimentos.

nodos.label: Erosión
nodos.desc: Movimiento y transporte de materiales desgastados por agentes naturales como el agua, el viento, los glaciares y la gravedad, que llevan a la redistribución de sedimentos en la superficie terrestre.

nodos.label: Erosión por agua
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que los ríos y las olas marinas transportan y desgastan sedimentos, formando valles y erosionando costas y estructuras rocosas.

nodos.label: Erosión por viento
nodos.desc: Transporte de partículas finas como arena y limo por el viento, que desgastan superficies y forman estructuras como dunes y arcos.

nodos.label: Erosión glacial
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que los glaciares se desplazan lentamente sobre la superficie, rascando y arrastrando fragmentos de roca, dejando depósitos como erráticos lejos de sus orígenes.

nodos.label: Desgaste mecánico
nodos.desc: Proceso físico en el que las rocas se rompen en fragmentos más pequeños sin cambios químicos, como por fricción o expansión térmica.

nodos.label: Desgaste químico
nodos.desc: Transformación de las rocas a través de reacciones químicas, como la oxidación y la carbonatación, que alteran la composición química de los minerales.

nodos.label: Deslizamiento por gravedad
nodos.desc: Tipo de erosión impulsado por la gravedad en que grandes cantidades de roca y sedimentos se deslizan por pendientes o suelos saturados.

nodos.label: Drought
nodos.desc: Periodo prolongado de precipitación por debajo del promedio, que causa escasez de agua y consecuencias ecológicas adversas.

nodos.label: Wildfire
nodos.desc: Incendios forestales que afectan amplias áreas, especialmente en regiones como California, Australia, Canadá, Rusia y Europa mediterránea, con impactos destructivos en ecosistemas y servicios humanos.

nodos.label: Loss of Life
nodos.desc: Consecuencia inmediata y trágica de los desastres naturales, con más de 2.5 millones de muertes globales entre 1998 y 2017, principalmente en países en desarrollo.

nodos.label: Economic Damage
nodos.desc: Daños económicos significativos en infraestructura, agricultura, empresas y gobiernos, con costos globales de desastres climáticos superiores a $2 trillones entre 1998 y 2017, y una proyección de $520 mil millones anuales por 2050.

nodos.label: Environmental Consequences
nodos.desc: Impactos negativos en ecosistemas, biodiversidad, paisajes y contaminación, incluyendo emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero, partículas tóxicas y contaminantes en aguas.

nodos.label: Social Effects
nodos.desc: Efectos sociales como desplazamiento, pobreza, desempleo, trauma mental y discordia social, que agravan desigualdades y sobrecargan economías locales durante la recuperación.

nodos.label: Greenhouse Effect
nodos.desc: The process by which greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere, regulating Earth's temperature and enabling life, but excessive concentrations lead to global warming.

nodos.label: Greenhouse Gases
nodos.desc: Gases in the atmosphere that trap heat, including carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide, primarily increased by human activities like burning fossil fuels and deforestation.

nodos.label: Global Warming
nodos.desc: The long-term rise in Earth's average surface temperature due to increased greenhouse gas concentrations, leading to changes in weather patterns and environmental impacts.

nodos.label: Habitat Fragmentation
nodos.desc: The breaking up of large, continuous habitats into smaller, isolated patches, reducing biodiversity and ecosystem resilience.

nodos.label: Second
nodos.desc: The base unit of time in the International System of Units (SI), defined as the duration of 9192631770 periods of the radiation corresponding to the transition between the two hyperfine levels of the ground state of the cesium-133 atom.

nodos.label: Newton's Second Law of Motion
nodos.desc: The force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration.

nodos.label: Momentum
nodos.desc: Momentum is the product of an object's mass and its velocity, representing the quantity of motion.

nodos.label: Principle of Action and Reaction Forces
nodos.desc: For every action force, there is an equal and opposite reaction force, illustrating Newton's Third Law of Motion.

nodos.label: Gravitational Force
nodos.desc: A fundamental force of nature that attracts any two objects with mass towards each other.

nodos.label: Carga eléctrica
nodos.desc: Propiedad física de los cuerpos que determina su interacción mediante fuerzas electromagnéticas, originada por un desequilibrio entre protones y electrones.

nodos.label: Fuerza electrostática
nodos.desc: Fuerza que actúa entre cuerpos cargados en reposo, descrita por la ley de Coulomb, que puede causar atracción o repulsión.

nodos.label: Ley de Coulomb
nodos.desc: Principio matemático que cuantifica la fuerza electrostática entre dos cargas puntuales, dependiendo de la magnitud de las cargas y la distancia entre ellas.

nodos.label: Campo eléctrico
nodos.desc: Región del espacio donde una carga eléctrica genera una fuerza sobre otras cargas, definido como fuerza por unidad de carga.

nodos.label: Magnetismo
nodos.desc: Propiedad física de ciertos materiales que permite generar fuerzas a distancia, originada por el movimiento de cargas, especialmente electrones en órbita.

nodos.label: Gravitational Potential Energy (GPE)
nodos.desc: The energy an object possesses due to its position in a gravitational field, calculated using the formula GPE = mgh.

nodos.label: Elastic Potential Energy (EPE)
nodos.desc: The energy stored in elastic materials when they are stretched or compressed, calculated using the formula ΔEPE = ½kx².

nodos.label: Spring Constant (k)
nodos.desc: A measure of the stiffness of a spring or elastic material, indicating how much force is required to deform it by a unit distance.

nodos.label: Chemical Potential Energy
nodos.desc: The energy stored in the bonds between atoms and molecules, released during chemical reactions such as combustion or cellular respiration.

nodos.label: Energy Conversion
nodos.desc: The process by which potential energy is transformed into other forms, such as kinetic energy, during mechanical motion or chemical reactions.

nodos.label: Joule
nodos.desc: The standard unit of energy in the International System of Units (SI), used to measure potential energy in both gravitational and elastic systems.

nodos.label: Ondas electromagnéticas
nodos.desc: Ondas que se propagan a través de oscilaciones de campos eléctricos y magnéticos, sin necesidad de un medio material.

nodos.label: Ondas mecánicas
nodos.desc: Ondas que requieren un medio material para propagarse mediante interacciones entre partículas.

nodos.label: Refracción
nodos.desc: Cambio de dirección de una onda al pasar de un medio a otro debido a la variación de su velocidad.

nodos.label: Índice de refracción
nodos.desc: Relación entre la velocidad de la luz en el vacío y su velocidad en un medio dado; indica cuán rápido se propaga la luz en ese medio.

nodos.label: Ángulo de refracción
nodos.desc: Ángulo entre la dirección de propagación de la onda tras pasar al nuevo medio y la normal a la superficie.

nodos.label: Ley de Snell
nodos.desc: Ecuación que relaciona los ángulos de incidencia y refracción con los índices de refracción de dos medios: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2).

nodos.label: Medio
nodos.desc: Sustancia o entorno por el cual una onda se propaga; cambios en la densidad del medio afectan la velocidad y dirección de la onda.

nodos.label: Information Processing
nodos.desc: El almacenamiento, transmisión y manipulación de información en sistemas vivos, desde el ADN hasta redes neuronales y comportamientos sociales.

nodos.label: Adaptation
nodos.desc: El proceso mediante el cual los organismos desarrollan rasgos que mejoran su aptitud en respuesta a presiones ambientales, tanto físicas como comportamentales.

nodos.label: Interdependence
nodos.desc: La reconocimiento de que todos los organismos existen en redes complejas de relaciones interdependientes.

nodos.label: Scientific Method
nodos.desc: Un procedimiento sistemático que los científicos utilizan para realizar experimentos, recopilar datos y probar hipótesis, asegurando la fiabilidad y reproducibilidad de los resultados.

nodos.label: Intensity
nodos.desc: A measure of the level or degree of a phenomenon, such as light or exercise, that influences a biological or physical response.

nodos.label: Light Intensity
nodos.desc: The amount of light energy per unit area, which affects plant growth and photosynthesis.

nodos.label: Heart Rate
nodos.desc: The number of heartbeats per minute, a physiological measure that increases with physical activity.

nodos.label: Carbon Atom
nodos.desc: An atom of carbon with four electrons in its outermost energy level, capable of forming strong covalent bonds with other elements.

nodos.label: Covalent Bond
nodos.desc: A chemical bond formed when atoms share electrons, enabling carbon to form stable structures with other elements.

nodos.label: Organic Molecule
nodos.desc: A molecule containing carbon, such as proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, and nucleic acids, which are fundamental to life.

nodos.label: Carbohydrate
nodos.desc: An organic molecule composed of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen, with a general formula of C~n(H2O)~m, and classified as polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones.

nodos.label: Monosaccharide
nodos.desc: A simple sugar consisting of a single sugar unit, such as trioses, tetroses, pentoses, and hexoses.

nodos.label: Polysaccharide
nodos.desc: A complex carbohydrate made up of many sugar units linked together, serving as energy storage or structural components in organisms.

nodos.label: Oligosaccharide
nodos.desc: A carbohydrate composed of a small chain of simple sugars, bridging the gap between monosaccharides and polysaccharides.

nodos.label: Carbon Count
nodos.desc: The number of carbon atoms in a sugar molecule, used to classify simple sugars: trioses (3C), tetroses (4C), pentoses (5C), hexoses (6C).

nodos.label: Molecular Formula
nodos.desc: A chemical expression showing the number and types of atoms in a molecule, such as C~n(H2O)~m for carbohydrates.

nodos.label: Aldehyde Group
nodos.desc: A functional group (-CHO) in carbohydrates that contains a carbon atom double-bonded to oxygen and bonded to a hydrogen atom.

nodos.label: Ketone Group
nodos.desc: A functional group (-CO-) in carbohydrates where a carbon atom is double-bonded to oxygen and bonded to two other carbon atoms.

nodos.label: Hydroxyl Group
nodos.desc: A functional group (-OH) present in carbohydrates, contributing to their polarity and reactivity.

nodos.label: Glycerol Backbone
nodos.desc: A three-carbon molecule that serves as the structural foundation for various lipids, such as diacylglycerols and phospholipids, with hydroxyl groups at each carbon position.

nodos.label: Fatty Acid Chain
nodos.desc: A long hydrocarbon chain attached to a glycerol backbone via an ester bond; typically composed of 16 or 18 carbon atoms and can be saturated or unsaturated.

nodos.label: Phosphatidic Acid
nodos.desc: A phospholipid precursor that contains a glycerol backbone with two fatty acid chains and a phosphate group; serves as the starting point for the biosynthesis of other phospholipids.

nodos.label: Phospholipid Headgroup
nodos.desc: The polar region of a phospholipid that varies in structure and includes examples such as phosphocholine, phosphoserine, and phosphoinositol, influencing membrane properties and signaling functions.

nodos.label: Cyclohexane Ring
nodos.desc: A six-membered carbon ring found in steroid structures, contributing to the rigid, planar framework of steroid molecules.

nodos.label: Cyclopentane Ring
nodos.desc: A five-membered carbon ring in steroid structures, fused to cyclohexane rings and contributing to the overall three-dimensional shape of steroid molecules.

nodos.label: Sterol Structure
nodos.desc: A class of lipids with a fused ring system of three cyclohexane and one cyclopentane rings, exemplified by cholesterol, which modulates membrane fluidity and serves as a precursor to steroid hormones.

nodos.label: Steroid Hormones
nodos.desc: Hormones derived from cholesterol, including cortisol, aldosterone, estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone, which regulate physiological processes such as stress response, electrolyte balance, and reproduction.

nodos.label: Wax Structure
nodos.desc: A lipid composed of a long-chain fatty acid or fatty alcohol esterified to a long-chain monohydric alcohol, forming protective coatings in plants and animals.

nodos.label: Esterification
nodos.desc: A chemical reaction in which a carboxylic acid and an alcohol form an ester bond, commonly observed in the formation of fatty acid chains in waxes and triacylglycerols.

nodos.label: Fatty Acid Synthase (FAS)
nodos.desc: A multienzyme complex that catalyzes the de novo synthesis of fatty acids by sequentially condensing acetyl-CoA and malonyl-CoA units, with reduction steps involving NADPH.

nodos.label: De Novo Synthesis
nodos.desc: A metabolic pathway that synthesizes fatty acids from simple precursors like acetyl-CoA and malonyl-CoA, involving multiple enzymatic steps and occurring primarily in the cytoplasm.

nodos.label: NADPH and NADH
nodos.desc: Coenzymes involved in redox reactions; NADPH provides reducing equivalents during fatty acid synthesis, while NADH is involved in energy metabolism and electron transport.

nodos.label: Chain Elongation
nodos.desc: A stepwise process in fatty acid biosynthesis where the growing fatty acid chain is extended by the addition of two-carbon units from malonyl-CoA, catalyzed by fatty acid synthase.

nodos.label: Desaturation
nodos.desc: A biochemical process that introduces double bonds into fatty acid chains, converting saturated fatty acids into unsaturated ones, typically mediated by desaturase enzymes.

nodos.label: Vitamin D
nodos.desc: A vitamin that modulates cell growth, neuromuscular function, and immune system regulation. Primarily synthesized in the skin upon sunlight exposure through ultraviolet radiation converting cholesterol to vitamin D3. Dietary sources include fatty fish, beef liver, cheese, mushrooms, and fortified foods. Deficiency causes rickets in children and osteoporosis in adults; overconsumption leads to hypercalcemia with risks like kidney stones and cardiac arrhythmias.

nodos.label: Vitamin E
nodos.desc: Acts as an antioxidant, preventing oxidative stress and damage to cell membranes. Found in vegetable oils, nuts, seeds, whole grains, avocado, and dark leafy greens. Deficiency is rare and may cause neurological issues and muscle weakness; high supplementation might increase all-cause mortality, though evidence is still emerging.

nodos.label: Vitamin K
nodos.desc: Essential for blood clotting and bone health by activating proteins involved in these processes. Phylloquinone (K1) is found in green vegetables; menaquinone (K2) comes from fermented foods, animal products, and gut microbiome. Deficiency is uncommon but can cause excessive bleeding; long-term antibiotics may reduce gut production and increase deficiency risk.

nodos.label: B-Complex Vitamins
nodos.desc: Eight vitamins involved in energy production, DNA replication, and neurotransmitter synthesis. Participate in one-carbon metabolism as coenzymes in methyl group transfer reactions. Found in whole grains, legumes, meat, poultry, fish, eggs, dairy, and leafy greens. Individual members include thiamine (B1) for carbohydrate metabolism and nerve function, riboflavin (B2) for energy metabolism, and others.

nodos.label: Hypercalcemia
nodos.desc: A condition caused by excessive calcium levels in the blood, resulting from overconsumption of vitamin D. It can lead to kidney stones, calcification of soft tissues, and cardiac arrhythmias.

nodos.label: One-Carbon Metabolism
nodos.desc: A biochemical pathway involving the transfer of methyl groups, where B vitamins act as coenzymes. Critical for DNA synthesis, methylation reactions, and amino acid metabolism.

nodos.label: Antioxidant
nodos.desc: A substance that inhibits oxidation, thereby preventing damage to cells and cell membranes. Vitamin E functions as an antioxidant to protect against oxidative stress.

nodos.label: Gut Microbiome
nodos.desc: A community of microorganisms in the digestive tract that can synthesize vitamin K (menaquinone), contributing to the body's vitamin K levels and influencing overall health.

nodos.label: Rickets
nodos.desc: A childhood disorder caused by vitamin D deficiency, leading to weakened bones and skeletal deformities.

nodos.label: Osteoporosis
nodos.desc: A condition in adults characterized by reduced bone density, increasing the risk of fractures and falls, often linked to vitamin D insufficiency.

nodos.label: Methyl Group Transfer
nodos.desc: A biochemical process in which methyl groups are transferred to molecules, facilitated by B vitamins as coenzymes in one-carbon metabolism.

nodos.label: Solvent
nodos.desc: Sustancia que disuelve otras sustancias para formar una solución, en este caso el agua actúa como solvente clave en procesos biológicos.

nodos.label: Actividad enzimática
nodos.desc: Proceso por el cual las enzimas catalizan reacciones químicas en células, y su eficacia depende de condiciones específicas como el pH y la temperatura.

nodos.label: Ionización
nodos.desc: Proceso por el cual los grupos funcionales de aminoácidos en proteínas cambian su carga en función del pH, afectando la estructura y función de las enzimas.

nodos.label: Regulación del pH intracelular
nodos.desc: Mecanismos biológicos que mantienen el pH interno de las células dentro de un rango estrecho para garantizar el funcionamiento adecuado de procesos celulares.

nodos.label: Célula
nodos.desc: La unidad básica de estructura y función en todos los organismos vivos, constituyendo la base de la organización de la vida.

nodos.label: Información hereditaria
nodos.desc: Datos genéticos almacenados en moléculas como el ADN, que se transmiten de una generación a otra.

nodos.label: ADN
nodos.desc: Molécula que almacena la información genética y sirve como base para la herencia y el desarrollo de organismos.

nodos.label: Orgánulos
nodos.desc: Estructuras membranosas dentro de las células que realizan funciones especializadas, como la producción de energía o síntesis de proteínas.

nodos.label: Biogénesis
nodos.desc: Principio que afirma que los nuevos organismos se forman a partir de células preexistentes, rechazando la generación espontánea.

nodos.label: Microtubule
nodos.desc: Hollow rod structure composed of tubulin proteins, providing structural support and enabling movement in cellular organelles.

nodos.label: 9+2 Arrangement
nodos.desc: A structural pattern in which nine pairs of microtubules surround a central pair, found in cilia and flagella, providing flexibility and coordinated movement.

nodos.label: Cilium
nodos.desc: Short, hair-like cellular projection that moves fluids and mucus, aiding in clearance of debris and pathogen removal in epithelial cells.

nodos.label: Flagellum
nodos.desc: Long, whip-like structure used for locomotion, typically found in spermatozoa and some bacteria, with a 9+0 microtubule arrangement.

nodos.label: Pseudopodium
nodos.desc: Temporary cytoplasmic extension used by amoeboid cells for movement, feeding (phagocytosis), or surface interaction.

nodos.label: Eukaryotic Cell
nodos.desc: A cell type with a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, housing specialized structures like cilia, flagella, and pseudopodia.

nodos.label: ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)
nodos.desc: Molécula que actúa como fuente de energía en células, utilizada en procesos como contracción muscular, transporte activo y síntesis de biomoléculas.

nodos.label: Contração muscular
nodos.desc: Proceso que implica el deslizamiento de filamentos de actina y miosina, alimentado por ATP para su realización.

nodos.label: Transporte activo
nodos.desc: Mecanismo por el cual las células mueven moléculas contra su gradiente de concentración utilizando pompas que consumen ATP.

nodos.label: Pompa de sodio-potasio
nodos.desc: Especializado transportador que utiliza ATP para intercambiar iones Na+ y K+ entre el interior y el exterior de la célula.

nodos.label: Reacciones biosintéticas
nodos.desc: Procesos en los que ATP actúa como fuente de energía y como precursor para cofactores como NAD+ y FAD.

nodos.label: NAD+ (Nicotinamida adenina dinucleótido)
nodos.desc: Cofactor esencial en reacciones de oxidación-reducción, derivado de ATP en vías metabólicas.

nodos.label: FAD (Flavin adenina dinucleótido)
nodos.desc: Cofactor que participa en reacciones de oxidación-reducción, también derivado de ATP.

nodos.label: Química de las velocidades
nodos.desc: Estudio de las tasas de reacciones químicas y de los factores que influyen en ellas, fundamental para entender el funcionamiento de enzimas.

nodos.label: Enzimas
nodos.desc: Catalizadores biológicos que aceleran reacciones químicas, cuya actividad puede ser influenciada por la energía de activación y la cinética.

nodos.label: Transformación de energía
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual la energía almacenada en ATP se convierte en trabajo celular, como movimiento o síntesis.

nodos.label: Active Site
nodos.desc: The specific region of an enzyme where the substrate binds and the catalytic reaction occurs.

nodos.label: Lock and Key Mechanism
nodos.desc: A model describing enzyme-substrate interaction where the enzyme (lock) has a specific shape that only fits the correct substrate (key).

nodos.label: Enzyme Specificity
nodos.desc: The property of enzymes to catalyze only one type of reaction or a specific group of related substrates due to structural compatibility.

nodos.label: pH Influence
nodos.desc: The effect of pH on enzyme activity, where extreme pH values can alter amino acid side chains and disrupt the enzyme's three-dimensional structure.

nodos.label: Temperature Effect
nodos.desc: The impact of temperature on enzyme activity; high temperatures cause denaturation, while low temperatures reduce reaction rates due to decreased molecular motion.

nodos.label: Substrate Concentration
nodos.desc: The relationship between substrate concentration and reaction rate, where rate increases with concentration until all active sites are saturated.

nodos.label: Competitive Inhibition
nodos.desc: A type of reversible inhibition where the inhibitor resembles the substrate and competes for binding to the active site of the enzyme.

nodos.label: Noncompetitive Inhibition
nodos.desc: A type of reversible inhibition where the inhibitor binds to a site other than the active site, altering enzyme conformation and reducing activity.

nodos.label: Irreversible Inhibition
nodos.desc: A form of inhibition where the inhibitor covalently binds to the enzyme, permanently altering its structure and abolishing its catalytic function.

nodos.label: Concentration Difference
nodos.desc: Diferencia en la densidad o cantidad de una sustancia en distintas zonas, que actúa como impulso para el transporte de partículas en sistemas biológicos.

nodos.label: Equilibrium
nodos.desc: Estado en el que las concentraciones de una sustancia se han igualado entre dos regiones, y no hay movimiento neto de partículas debido a la ausencia de gradiente de concentración.

nodos.label: Concentración de soluto
nodos.desc: La cantidad de sustancia disuelta en una solución, que influye en el movimiento de moléculas de solvente durante la osmosis.

nodos.label: Hipotónico
nodos.desc: Una solución con baja concentración de soluto en comparación con otra solución, desde la cual el agua tiende a moverse por osmosis.

nodos.label: Hiper-tónico
nodos.desc: Una solución con alta concentración de soluto, hacia la cual el agua se mueve por osmosis desde una solución hipotónica.

nodos.label: NADH
nodos.desc: Reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, a coenzyme involved in cellular respiration and fermentation, carrying high-energy electrons to the electron transport chain or used in redox reactions.

nodos.label: Glycolysis
nodos.desc: A metabolic pathway that converts glucose into pyruvate, generating a net gain of ATP and NADH, occurring in the cytoplasm and functioning under anaerobic conditions.

nodos.label: Pyruvate
nodos.desc: A three-carbon compound produced during glycolysis, which can be further metabolized in aerobic conditions or converted into lactate or ethanol in anaerobic conditions.

nodos.label: Lactate dehydrogenase
nodos.desc: An enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of pyruvate to lactate, regenerating NAD+ to sustain glycolytic flux under anaerobic conditions.

nodos.label: Anaerobic conditions
nodos.desc: Environmental conditions lacking oxygen, in which cells rely on fermentation pathways to generate ATP when oxidative phosphorylation is not possible.

nodos.label: Alcohol fermentation
nodos.desc: A metabolic process in which glucose is converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide, producing ATP and NADH, primarily in yeast and some microorganisms under anaerobic conditions.

nodos.label: Lactic acid fermentation
nodos.desc: A metabolic pathway where lactose is converted into lactic acid by bacteria, lowering pH and preserving food, and also serving as an anaerobic ATP production route in muscle cells.

nodos.label: Cromatida hermana
nodos.desc: Una de las dos copias idénticas de un cromosoma, unidas en el centromero, que se separan durante la división celular.

nodos.label: Centrómero
nodos.desc: Región central de un cromosoma donde se unen las cromatidas hermanas.

nodos.label: Cromatina
nodos.desc: Sustancia que contiene el ADN y proteínas histonas, que se encuentra en forma desorganizada cuando la célula no se divide.

nodos.label: Nucleósomo
nodos.desc: Unidad básica de organización de la cromatina, formada por 147 pares de bases de ADN enrolladas alrededor de un octámero de histonas.

nodos.label: Histona
nodos.desc: Proteína positivamente cargada que ayuda a compactar el ADN, permitiendo el almacenamiento eficiente del material genético en el núcleo.

nodos.label: Fibra de 30 nm
nodos.desc: Estructura de compresión superior de la cromatina, formada por la dobladura de nucleósomas en una estructura helicoidal.

nodos.label: Fase de interfase
nodos.desc: Fase más larga del ciclo celular, durante la cual la célula se prepara para dividirse, y la cromatina está en forma desorganizada.

nodos.label: Cell Cycle
nodos.desc: The sequence of events in a cell's life, including G1, S, G2, and M phases, during which a cell grows and divides.

nodos.label: G1 Phase
nodos.desc: The first phase of the cell cycle, where the cell grows and prepares for DNA replication.

nodos.label: S Phase
nodos.desc: The phase during which DNA replication occurs, resulting in duplication of the genome.

nodos.label: G2 Phase
nodos.desc: The phase where the cell grows further and prepares for mitosis, including synthesis of proteins and organelles.

nodos.label: M Phase
nodos.desc: The phase of the cell cycle involving mitosis, where the nucleus divides and chromosomes are separated into two daughter cells.

nodos.label: Cyclin B-CDK1 Complex
nodos.desc: A regulatory protein complex that drives the cell into mitosis when activated, and its activity declines as the cell exits mitosis.

nodos.label: Phosphatases
nodos.desc: Enzymes that remove phosphate groups from proteins, counteracting kinase-mediated phosphorylation and regulating mitotic processes.

nodos.label: Cdc14
nodos.desc: A phosphatase that reverses phosphorylation events necessary for mitotic progression and chromosomal segregation.

nodos.label: Greatwall Kinase
nodos.desc: A kinase that regulates Cdc14 activity through a feedback loop, integrating upstream signals to control mitotic entry and exit.

nodos.label: Asymmetric Division
nodos.desc: A type of cell division that produces daughter cells of different sizes or fates, observed in embryogenesis and tissue homeostasis.

nodos.label: Ploidy
nodos.desc: The number of sets of chromosomes in a cell; meiosis reduces ploidy from diploid to haploid.

nodos.label: Chromosomal Segregation
nodos.desc: The process by which chromosomes are separated into daughter cells during mitosis or meiosis.

nodos.label: Feedback Loop
nodos.desc: A regulatory mechanism in which the output of a system influences its input, such as the interaction between Greatwall kinase and Cdc14.

nodos.label: Upstream Pathways
nodos.desc: Signaling networks that provide inputs to regulate the master regulator of mitosis, such as the cell cycle control system.

nodos.label: CDK (Ciclin-Dependent Kinase)
nodos.desc: Enzima que regula las transiciones del ciclo celular, activada por ciclinas y que controla la expresión de genes relacionados con la división celular.

nodos.label: E2F
nodos.desc: Transcripcional que activa programas de transcripción para la entrada en la fase S del ciclo celular, facilitando la replicación del ADN.

nodos.label: Aurora kinase B (AURKB)
nodos.desc: Enzima que regula la formación del huso mitótico, la maduración de centrosomas y la captura de cromatidas, cuya sobreexpresión causa instabilidad genética y aneuploidía.

nodos.label: Aneuploidía
nodos.desc: Condición en la que las células tienen un número abnorme de cromosomas, resultado de errores en la segregación cromosómica durante la división celular.

nodos.label: Inhibidores de moléculas pequeñas
nodos.desc: Compuestos químicos que bloquean la actividad de enzimas como CDKs, utilizados en el tratamiento de tumores y que han recibido aprobación de la FDA.

nodos.label: Resistencia a medicamentos
nodos.desc: Problema común en el tratamiento de cáncer que ocurre cuando las células tumorales dejan de responder a los inhibidores de enzimas como CDKs.

nodos.label: Inestabilidad genómica
nodos.desc: Condición en la que los cromosomas se segregan de forma errónea durante la división celular, aumentando el riesgo de mutaciones y aneuploidía.

nodos.label: Apoptosis
nodos.desc: Programmed cell death that occurs in a controlled manner to maintain tissue homeostasis, eliminating damaged or unnecessary cells during development and physiological processes.

nodos.label: Intrinsic (Mitochondrial) Pathway
nodos.desc: Apoptotic pathway initiated within the cell due to internal stress signals, leading to mitochondrial membrane permeabilization and caspase activation.

nodos.label: Extrinsic (Death Receptor) Pathway
nodos.desc: Apoptotic pathway triggered by external signals binding to death receptors on the cell surface, initiating a cascade that results in caspase activation.

nodos.label: Caspases
nodos.desc: Cysteine proteases that are activated during apoptosis and cleave specific substrates to execute the cell death program, leading to morphological and biochemical changes.

nodos.label: Cell Shrinkage
nodos.desc: Morphological change observed during apoptosis, where the cell reduces in volume as part of the controlled death process.

nodos.label: Chromatin Condensation
nodos.desc: Compaction of chromatin structure in the nucleus during apoptosis, leading to the formation of dense, condensed DNA regions.

nodos.label: DNA Fragmentation
nodos.desc: Breakage of DNA into small fragments as a hallmark of apoptosis, resulting from caspase-mediated cleavage of nuclear components.

nodos.label: Apoptotic Bodies
nodos.desc: Membrane-bound vesicles formed during apoptosis that contain cellular debris and are subsequently engulfed by phagocytic cells.

nodos.label: Phagocytosis
nodos.desc: Process by which neighboring cells engulf apoptotic bodies to remove cellular debris, preventing inflammation and maintaining tissue integrity.

nodos.label: Germ Layers
nodos.desc: Three primary layers—ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm—formed during embryonic development from the inner cell mass, which give rise to all tissues and organs of the body.

nodos.label: Epiblast
nodos.desc: Lineage derived from the inner cell mass of the blastocyst that contributes to the formation of the ectoderm and mesoderm, and ultimately the embryo proper.

nodos.label: Hypoblast
nodos.desc: Lineage derived from the inner cell mass of the blastocyst that contributes to the formation of the endoderm and supports early embryonic development.

nodos.label: Blastocyst
nodos.desc: Multicellular structure formed after cleavage divisions following fertilization, capable of implanting into the uterine endometrium and initiating embryonic development.

nodos.label: Trophectoderm
nodos.desc: Outer layer of the blastocyst that differentiates into the placenta and other extra-embryonic tissues during development.

nodos.label: Cleavage Divisions
nodos.desc: Rapid cell divisions that occur after fertilization without growth, resulting in the formation of a multicellular blastocyst from a single zygote.

nodos.label: Genotype
nodos.desc: The combination of alleles inherited from each parent that determines the expression of a trait in an individual.

nodos.label: Phenotype
nodos.desc: The physical expression of a trait based on the underlying genotype.

nodos.label: Dominant Allele
nodos.desc: An allele that expresses its trait even when only one copy is present, masking the effect of a recessive allele.

nodos.label: Recessive Allele
nodos.desc: An allele that only expresses its trait when two copies are present (homozygous recessive).

nodos.label: Co-dominancia
nodos.desc: Es un patrón de herencia en el que ambos alelos de un par son expresados de forma independiente en el heterocigoto, resultando en fenotipos combinados, como en el grupo sanguíneo ABO donde los tipos AB muestran ambos alelos I^A e I^B.

nodos.label: Dominancia incompleta
nodos.desc: Es un patrón de herencia en el que el heterocigoto muestra un fenotipo intermedio entre los fenotipos de los homocigotos, como en las flores de snapdragons donde C^RC^W produce una flor rosa en lugar de roja o blanca.

nodos.label: Heterocigoto
nodos.desc: Indica un individuo que posee dos alelos diferentes para un gen, como I^Ai o C^RC^W, y puede expresar fenotipos intermedios o combinados según el tipo de dominancia.

nodos.label: Alelo
nodos.desc: Una variante de un gen que se hereda y puede presentarse en diferentes combinaciones, como I^A, I^B o C^R, C^W.

nodos.label: Fenotipo
nodos.desc: La expresión observable de un gen o conjunto de genes en un organismo, como el tipo de sangre o el color de la flor en snapdragons.

nodos.label: Homocigoto
nodos.desc: Un individuo que posee dos copias idénticas de un alelo para un gen, como C^RC^R o C^WC^W, que expresan un fenotipo específico.

nodos.label: Cuadro de Punnett
nodos.desc: Una herramienta gráfica utilizada para predecir los posibles genotipos y fenotipos de los descendientes de una cruza genética.

nodos.label: Restriction Endonuclease
nodos.desc: Enzyme that recognizes specific DNA sequences and cleaves the phosphodiester bonds within those sequences, enabling precise DNA cutting.

nodos.label: Molecular Cloning
nodos.desc: Process of assembling customized DNA constructs by cutting DNA at specific locations using restriction enzymes and joining them with ligase enzymes.

nodos.label: Site-Directed Mutagenesis
nodos.desc: Technique that introduces targeted changes to a gene's sequence using synthetic oligonucleotides during PCR amplification.

nodos.label: Promoter
nodos.desc: Regulatory DNA element that initiates transcription of a gene, controlling when and how much a gene is expressed.

nodos.label: Terminator
nodos.desc: Regulatory DNA element that signals the end of transcription, ensuring proper termination of gene expression.

nodos.label: Chaperone
nodos.desc: Protein that assists in the proper folding and assembly of other proteins, ensuring correct three-dimensional structure and function of gene products.

nodos.label: CRISPR-Cas9
nodos.desc: Genome editing technology that uses guide RNA to direct Cas9 nuclease to specific DNA sequences, creating double-stranded breaks for targeted modifications.

nodos.label: Double-Stranded Break
nodos.desc: A break in both strands of the DNA helix, introduced by Cas9, which is repaired through cellular mechanisms leading to gene edits.

nodos.label: Phosphodiester Bond
nodos.desc: Chemical bond linking nucleotides in DNA, which is cleaved by restriction endonucleases during DNA cutting.

nodos.label: Carga eléctrica
nodos.desc: Propiedad física de las partículas que determina su interacción con campos eléctricos; en este contexto, las partículas cargadas positivamente o negativamente se mueven hacia polos opuestos en un campo eléctrico.

nodos.label: Migración
nodos.desc: Movimiento de partículas a través de un medio (como gel) bajo la influencia de un campo eléctrico; depende de la carga, tamaño y forma de las partículas.

nodos.label: Dependencia del tamaño
nodos.desc: Relación entre el tamaño de una partícula y su velocidad de migración; partículas más pequeñas experimentan menos fricción y se mueven más rápido que las más grandes.

nodos.label: Resistencia friccional
nodos.desc: Fuerza que se opone al movimiento de partículas a través de un medio, mayor en partículas más grandes debido a su mayor superficie de contacto con el medio.

nodos.label: Electroforesis
nodos.desc: Técnica que utiliza un campo eléctrico para separar moléculas según su carga y tamaño; se aplica comúnmente para separar fragmentos de DNA.

nodos.label: Concentración del gel
nodos.desc: Propiedad del medio de separación que afecta la resolución; gels más densos separan mejor fragmentos de tamaño similar.

nodos.label: Tensión eléctrica
nodos.desc: Fuerza del campo eléctrico aplicado que influye en la velocidad de migración de las partículas; mayor tensión puede acelerar el proceso.

nodos.label: Separación de bandas
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual fragmentos de DNA se distribuyen en diferentes posiciones en el gel según su tamaño, permitiendo su identificación visual.

nodos.label: Ladder de estándares
nodos.desc: Muestra de fragmentos de DNA de tamaños conocidos que se usa como referencia para comparar y determinar el tamaño de fragmentos desconocidos.

nodos.label: Electroforesis de campo pulsado (PFGE)
nodos.desc: Variante de electroforesis que utiliza cambios periódicos de dirección del campo eléctrico para separar fragmentos de DNA muy grandes, como cromosomas.

nodos.label: Digestión por restricción
nodos.desc: Reacción enzimática que corta el DNA en fragmentos específicos, permitiendo su posterior separación por electroforesis para análisis genético.

nodos.label: Evolution
nodos.desc: The process by which species change over time through genetic variation and natural selection, leading to the diversity of life on Earth.

nodos.label: Genetic Makeup
nodos.desc: The complete set of genes or DNA in an organism, which determines its hereditary traits and influences its development and function.

nodos.label: Gene Editing
nodos.desc: A biotechnological process that allows precise modification of DNA sequences, such as through CRISPR-Cas9, to alter or correct genetic material.

nodos.label: Epigenetic Modifications
nodos.desc: Heritable changes in gene expression that do not involve alterations to the DNA sequence, influenced by environmental factors and development.

nodos.label: Developmental Processes
nodos.desc: Biological mechanisms that govern how a fertilized egg develops into a complex organism, including cell differentiation and tissue formation.

nodos.label: Variation
nodos.desc: Diferencias genéticas o fenotípicas presentes dentro de una especie que sirven como base para la selección natural y el cambio evolutivo.

nodos.label: Genetic Recombination
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual se mezclan alelos durante la reproducción, generando nuevas combinaciones genéticas.

nodos.label: Fossil Record
nodos.desc: Registro de fósiles que muestra el cambio en formas de organismos a lo largo del tiempo, proporcionando evidencia directa de la evolución.

nodos.label: Paleontological Evidence
nodos.desc: Tipo de evidencia basado en fósiles que permite inferir relaciones evolutivas entre especies y el desarrollo histórico de la vida.

nodos.label: Genetic Evidence
nodos.desc: Datos derivados de la secuencia de ADN que muestran similitudes y diferencias entre especies, apoyando la evolución común.

nodos.label: Evolutionary Mechanisms
nodos.desc: Procesos como la selección natural, la recombinación genética y las mutaciones que impulsan el cambio evolutivo en poblaciones.

nodos.label: Genetic Drift
nodos.desc: Random change in allele frequencies within a population over time, especially in small populations, leading to loss of genetic variation.

nodos.label: Differential Adaptation
nodos.desc: Variation in how populations respond to environmental pressures, leading to phenotypic and genetic divergence among groups.

nodos.label: Allele Frequencies
nodos.desc: Proportion of each allele in a population, used to assess genetic structure and infer evolutionary processes such as selection and drift.

nodos.label: Linkage Disequilibrium
nodos.desc: Non-random association of alleles at different loci, indicating potential historical recombination events or selective pressures.

nodos.label: Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium
nodos.desc: A principle stating that allele and genotype frequencies in a population remain constant from generation to generation in the absence of evolutionary forces.

nodos.label: Population Genetics
nodos.desc: Branch of genetics that studies the distribution and change of genetic variation within and among populations over time.

nodos.label: Demographic Changes
nodos.desc: Historical shifts in population size, structure, and migration patterns, inferred from genetic data to understand evolutionary history.

nodos.label: Selective Pressures
nodos.desc: Environmental or biological factors that influence the survival and reproduction of individuals, driving natural selection and adaptation.

nodos.label: Phenotypic Change
nodos.desc: Observable differences in traits among individuals, resulting from genetic and environmental influences, especially in response to environmental shifts.

nodos.label: Functional Morphology
nodos.desc: Study of the mechanical principles underlying biological structures and their functions, focusing on how form relates to function in living organisms.

nodos.label: Evolutionary Theory
nodos.desc: Framework explaining how species change over time through natural selection, genetic drift, and other mechanisms.

nodos.label: Species Boundaries
nodos.desc: Delineations that define the limits of species, maintained through reproductive isolation and genetic divergence, preventing gene flow between populations.

nodos.label: Gene Exchange
nodos.desc: Transfer of genetic material between populations or species, which can be inhibited by reproductive isolation and maintained by species boundaries.

nodos.label: Hybridization
nodos.desc: Mating between individuals from different populations or species, resulting in offspring with mixed genetic makeup, often leading to reduced fitness in hybrids.

nodos.label: Reticulation
nodos.desc: Complex network of gene flow between lineages, often observed in cases of hybridization, challenging traditional tree-like models of evolution.

nodos.label: Morphological Species
nodos.desc: Species defined based on observable physical characteristics, a traditional approach that may not capture genetic diversity or evolutionary relationships.

nodos.label: Phylogenetic Species
nodos.desc: Species defined by shared evolutionary history and genetic divergence, based on phylogenetic trees and molecular data.

nodos.label: Ecological Species
nodos.desc: Species defined by distinct ecological roles and adaptations, emphasizing niche differentiation and environmental specialization.

nodos.label: Recombination
nodos.desc: Process during meiosis that breaks up linkage disequilibrium by exchanging genetic material between homologous chromosomes, increasing genetic diversity.

nodos.label: Gene Flow
nodos.desc: Movement of individuals and their genetic material between populations, which can increase or decrease genetic diversity depending on the genetic similarity of immigrants.

nodos.label: Speciation
nodos.desc: The process by which one species evolves into two or more distinct species, typically driven by reproductive isolation.

nodos.label: Reproductive Isolation
nodos.desc: Mechanism preventing interbreeding between populations, arising through spatial, temporal, mechanical, or ecological differences.

nodos.label: Founder Effect
nodos.desc: A genetic bottleneck occurring when a small group of individuals establishes a new population, leading to reduced genetic diversity.

nodos.label: Character State Transitions
nodos.desc: Changes between different traits in a dataset, such as the presence or absence of legs or fins in animals, used to infer evolutionary relationships.

nodos.label: Parsimony
nodos.desc: A method that minimizes the number of evolutionary changes required to explain observed trait distributions, assuming that the simplest explanation is most likely.

nodos.label: Homologous Characters
nodos.desc: Traits that share a common origin due to inheritance from a shared ancestor, used as reliable indicators for phylogenetic analysis.

nodos.label: Convergent Evolution
nodos.desc: The independent evolution of similar traits in unrelated taxa due to adaptation to similar environments, which can lead to misleading phylogenetic inferences.

nodos.label: Evolutionary Model
nodos.desc: A mathematical framework that describes how traits evolve over time, used in maximum likelihood and Bayesian inference to compute probabilities of observed data.

nodos.label: Posterior Probability
nodos.desc: The updated probability of a tree topology after incorporating observed data and prior beliefs in a Bayesian analysis.

nodos.label: Tree Topology
nodos.desc: The structure of a phylogenetic tree that represents the evolutionary relationships among taxa, which is inferred using statistical methods.

nodos.label: Pressure Difference
nodos.desc: The difference in partial pressure of gases between the alveoli and the blood; this gradient drives the diffusion of oxygen into and carbon dioxide out of the bloodstream.

nodos.label: Diffusion Rate
nodos.desc: The speed at which gases move across a membrane; influenced by surface area, pressure gradient, and molecular weight, determining how quickly oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged.

nodos.label: Partial Pressure
nodos.desc: The pressure exerted by a single gas in a mixture; higher partial pressure of oxygen in inspired air drives oxygen into the blood, while lower partial pressure of carbon dioxide in blood promotes its elimination.

nodos.label: Gas Exchange
nodos.desc: The process by which oxygen diffuses from alveoli into blood and carbon dioxide diffuses from blood into alveoli for exhalation.

nodos.label: Pulmonary Veins
nodos.desc: Blood vessels that carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.

nodos.label: Aorta
nodos.desc: The main artery that carries oxygenated blood from the heart to the rest of the body.

nodos.label: Vena Cava
nodos.desc: Large veins that return deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart; superior and inferior vena cava collect blood from the body and deliver it to the right atrium.

nodos.label: Tricuspid Valve
nodos.desc: A valve in the heart that prevents backflow of blood from the right ventricle to the right atrium as blood is pumped into the ventricle.

nodos.label: Pulmonary Artery
nodos.desc: A blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs for oxygenation.

nodos.label: Alveoli
nodos.desc: Tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange occurs between the air and the bloodstream.

nodos.label: Bronchi
nodos.desc: Airways that branch from the trachea and lead into each lung, further dividing into bronchioles.

nodos.label: Bronchioles
nodos.desc: Smaller branches of the bronchi that lead to the alveoli and are involved in air distribution to the lungs.

nodos.label: COPD
