nodos.desc: A functional group with an oxygen atom bonded to two carbon atoms, represented as R-O-R'.

nodos.label: Epoxide
nodos.desc: A cyclic ether with a three-membered ring containing an oxygen atom, represented as (R-CH-)2O.

nodos.label: Aldimine
nodos.desc: A functional group with a carbon atom double bonded to a nitrogen atom and bonded to a hydrogen, represented as RC(H)=N-R'.

nodos.label: Ketimine
nodos.desc: A functional group with a carbon atom double bonded to a nitrogen atom and bonded to another carbon group, represented as RC(R)=N-R'.

nodos.label: Nitro Compound
nodos.desc: A functional group with a nitrogen atom double bonded to an oxygen atom and bonded to another oxygen atom, represented as -NO2.

nodos.label: Stereogenic Center
nodos.desc: Un átomo, generalmente carbono, que está unido a cuatro grupos diferentes, dando lugar a dos configuraciones espaciales no superpuestas, conocidas como enantiómeros.

nodos.label: Enantiomers
nodos.desc: Pares de moléculas que son imágenes especulares no superpuestas, que tienen propiedades físicas idénticas excepto en su interacción con luz polarizada y con otras moléculas chirales.

nodos.label: Plane-Polarized Light
nodos.desc: Luz que se ha polarizado en un plano específico, que puede ser rotada por moléculas chirales, lo que permite distinguir entre enantiómeros mediante su actividad óptica.

nodos.label: Cahn-Ingold-Prelog Rules
nodos.desc: Un conjunto de reglas para asignar prioridades a grupos químicos conectados a un átomo central basándose en los números atómicos de los átomos directamente unidos, utilizadas para determinar la configuración estereográfica.

nodos.label: Tetrahedral Carbon
nodos.desc: Un carbono con cuatro enlaces, formando una geometría tetraédrica, que es la base estructural para la existencia de centros estereogénicos en moléculas.

nodos.label: Optical Activity
nodos.desc: La capacidad de una sustancia para rotar el plano de la luz polarizada, un fenómeno que se manifiesta en enantiómeros, uno que gira la luz en sentido horario (+) y otro en sentido antihorario (-).

nodos.label: Thalidomide
nodos.desc: Un ejemplo histórico de la importancia de la chirales en medicina, donde un enantiómero es seguro y otro causa defectos fetales, destacando la necesidad de separar enantiómeros en fármacos.

nodos.label: Amino Acids
nodos.desc: Unidades estructurales de proteínas que tienen un carbono alfa con un grupo amino, un grupo carboxilo, un hidrógeno y un grupo lateral, siendo todos los aminoácidos naturales chiral en este centro alfa.

nodos.label: Asymmetric Center
nodos.desc: A carbon atom bonded to four different substituents, which is the source of chirality in molecules such as amino acids and carbohydrates.

nodos.label: Fischer Projection
nodos.desc: A two-dimensional representation used to visualize the spatial arrangement of functional groups around an asymmetric center in molecules like D-glucose.

nodos.label: Enantiomer
nodos.desc: One of a pair of stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other, exhibiting identical physical properties but differing in optical activity and biological interaction.

nodos.label: Meso Compound
nodos.desc: A molecule that contains chiral centers but has an internal plane of symmetry, making it optically inactive despite having chiral elements.

nodos.label: Stereoisomer
nodos.desc: Isomers that differ in the spatial arrangement of atoms or groups, including enantiomers and diastereomers, which have different physical and biological properties.

nodos.label: Alpha Carbon
nodos.desc: The carbon atom adjacent to the carboxyl group in amino acids, which is typically chiral and serves as the stereogenic center in proteinogenic amino acids.

nodos.label: Racemic Mixture
nodos.desc: An equimolar mixture of two enantiomers, resulting in optical inactivity due to cancellation of optical rotation.

nodos.label: Chirality Center
nodos.desc: A carbon atom bonded to four different groups, making it a stereocenter; essential for molecular asymmetry and the formation of enantiomers.

nodos.label: Asymmetric Synthesis
nodos.desc: A chemical method that selectively produces one enantiomer over another, enabling efficient and targeted synthesis of chiral molecules with minimal waste.

nodos.label: Chirality Element
nodos.desc: A structural feature, such as a carbon atom with four distinct substituents, that gives rise to chirality and leads to the formation of stereoisomers.

nodos.label: Internal Compensation
nodos.desc: A phenomenon in which the chirality elements within a molecule cancel each other out, resulting in a meso compound that is achiral despite having stereocenters.

nodos.label: Asignación de prioridades
nodos.desc: Procedimiento que asigna un orden de prioridad a los grupos conectados a un centro estereogénico basado en el número atómico de los átomos directamente unidos al centro.

nodos.label: Prioridad por número atómico
nodos.desc: Regla que establece que un átomo con mayor número atómico tiene mayor prioridad en la asignación de configuraciones estereográficas, siguiendo el orden O > N > P > S > Cl > Br > I > H.

nodos.label: Configuración R
nodos.desc: Configuración estereográfica asignada cuando, al observar el centro estereogénico con el grupo de menor prioridad apuntando hacia atrás, los grupos de mayor prioridad giran en sentido horario (rectus).

nodos.label: Configuración S
nodos.desc: Configuración estereográfica asignada cuando, al observar el centro estereogénico con el grupo de menor prioridad apuntando hacia atrás, los grupos de mayor prioridad giran en sentido antihorario (sinister).

nodos.label: Sistema CIP
nodos.desc: Marco matemático y químico para asignar configuraciones absolutas a centros estereogénicos mediante reglas de prioridad basadas en números atómicos.

nodos.label: Giro horario
nodos.desc: Dirección de rotación de los grupos de prioridad alrededor del centro estereogénico cuando se observa desde el grupo de menor prioridad, que define la configuración R.

nodos.label: Giro antihorario
nodos.desc: Dirección de rotación de los grupos de prioridad alrededor del centro estereogénico cuando se observa desde el grupo de menor prioridad, que define la configuración S.

nodos.label: Cahn-Ingold-Prelog rules
nodos.desc: A system for assigning priorities to substituents attached to a stereogenic center based on atomic number and the number of atoms in the substituents, used to determine R or S configurations.

nodos.label: Priority order
nodos.desc: The sequence of substituents ranked by atomic number, with higher atomic number groups receiving higher priority in stereochemical analysis.

nodos.label: R configuration
nodos.desc: A stereochemical designation indicating a clockwise arrangement of substituents when viewed from the highest priority group, as determined by the CIP rules.

nodos.label: S configuration
nodos.desc: A stereochemical designation indicating a counterclockwise arrangement of substituents when viewed from the highest priority group, as determined by the CIP rules.

nodos.label: Configuration naming
nodos.desc: The use of the R,S system to describe the stereochemistry of a molecule by assigning configurations to each stereogenic center and combining them in a systematic name, such as (2S,3S)-2-phenethanol.

nodos.label: Cahn-Ingold-Prelog (CIP) System
nodos.desc: A systematic method for assigning absolute configuration (R or S) to chiral centers based on the priority of substituents attached to a carbon atom.

nodos.label: Stereocenter
nodos.desc: A carbon atom bonded to four different groups, which gives rise to chirality and the possibility of enantiomerism.

nodos.label: Rotation of Polarization
nodos.desc: The phenomenon where plane polarized light is rotated upon passing through an optically active substance, with the direction indicating whether the enantiomer is dextrorotatory or levorotatory.

nodos.label: Diastereomers
nodos.desc: Stereoisomers that are not mirror images of each other and differ in three-dimensional configuration, exhibiting different physical and chemical properties.

nodos.label: Constitutional Isomers
nodos.desc: Isomers that differ in the connectivity of atoms, representing distinct bonding patterns for the same set of atoms.

nodos.label: Meso Compounds
nodos.desc: Molecules with multiple stereocenters but an internal plane of symmetry, resulting in overall achirality despite having chiral centers.

nodos.label: Cahn-Ingold-Prelog Rules
nodos.desc: A systematic method for assigning priority to substituents on a chiral center based on atomic number, used to determine the absolute configuration (R or S).

nodos.label: Atropisomers
nodos.desc: Stereoisomers arising from restricted rotation around a single bond, leading to chirality even in the absence of traditional asymmetric centers.

nodos.label: Centro chirales
nodos.desc: Átomo con cuatro grupos diferentes unidos, que puede existir en dos configuraciones no superpuestas, generando isómeros ópticos.

nodos.label: Rotación óptica
nodos.desc: Propiedad física que mide la capacidad de una sustancia para girar el plano de la luz polarizada, dependiendo de la configuración de sus centros chirales.

nodos.label: Plano de simetría
nodos.desc: Plano que divide una molécula en dos mitades idénticas, que al reflejarse se superponen, y que causa cancelación de rotación óptica en compuestos meso.

nodos.label: Cancelación de rotación
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que las contribuciones positivas y negativas de rotación óptica de centros chirales se neutralizan, resultando en actividad óptica nula.

nodos.label: Lone Pair
nodos.desc: A pair of valence electrons not involved in bonding; its availability influences nucleophilicity.

nodos.label: Negative Charge
nodos.desc: The magnitude of the negative charge on a nucleophile affects electron density, increasing nucleophilicity.

nodos.label: Steric Hindrance
nodos.desc: Bulky groups around a nucleophilic center can block access to the reactive site, reducing nucleophilicity.

nodos.label: Polarizability
nodos.desc: The ability of an atom or ion to distort its electron cloud; higher polarizability increases nucleophilicity, especially in heavier elements.

nodos.label: Solvation Effects
nodos.desc: Polar solvents stabilize nucleophiles through solvation, reducing their reactivity; less polar solvents enhance nucleophilicity.

nodos.label: Resonance Stabilization
nodos.desc: Delocalization of charge through resonance increases electron density at the nucleophilic center, enhancing reactivity.

nodos.label: Nucleophilicity
nodos.desc: A measure of how readily a species donates an electron pair to form a bond with an electrophile.

nodos.label: Carbocation
nodos.desc: A positively charged intermediate formed during SN1 reactions when the leaving group departs, creating a planar, electron-deficient carbon center that can be attacked by nucleophiles.

nodos.label: Nucleophilic Substitution
nodos.desc: A reaction mechanism where a nucleophile replaces a leaving group in a molecule, occurring via either SN1 (unimolecular) or SN2 (bimolecular) pathways.

nodos.label: Elimination Reaction
nodos.desc: A reaction that removes a group from a molecule to form a double bond, such as in E1 or E2 processes, which are distinct from substitution reactions.

nodos.label: E2 Mechanism
nodos.desc: A bimolecular elimination reaction with second-order kinetics, where the rate depends on both the substrate and base concentration. It proceeds via a concerted mechanism with backside attack, requiring a hydrogen on a beta carbon and a leaving group. Zaitsev's rule governs product stability, favoring the most substituted alkene.

nodos.label: E1 Mechanism
nodos.desc: A unimolecular elimination reaction with first-order kinetics, where the rate depends only on the substrate concentration. It involves a carbocation intermediate, allowing for rearrangements and multiple products due to kinetic and thermodynamic factors.

nodos.label: Rate Law for E2
nodos.desc: The rate of an E2 reaction is given by Rate = k[substrate][base], indicating it is second-order and dependent on both reactant concentrations.

nodos.label: Rate Law for E1
nodos.desc: The rate of an E1 reaction is given by Rate = k[substrate], indicating it is first-order and independent of the base concentration.

nodos.label: Beta Carbon
nodos.desc: A carbon atom adjacent to the carbon bearing the leaving group; a hydrogen on this carbon is typically removed in elimination reactions.

nodos.label: Zaitsev's Rule
nodos.desc: A principle stating that in elimination reactions, the more substituted alkene is the major product due to greater stability.

nodos.label: Backside Attack
nodos.desc: A stereochemical feature in E2 reactions where the base attacks the beta hydrogen from the opposite side of the leaving group, leading to anti-periplanar geometry.

nodos.label: Leaving Group
nodos.desc: A group that departs from a molecule during a reaction, facilitating ionization in SN1 reactions; its ability influences the reaction rate.

nodos.label: Curly Arrow
nodos.desc: A diagrammatic tool representing electron movement in chemical reactions, with the tail indicating electron source and the barb indicating electron sink.

nodos.label: Electron Source
nodos.desc: An atom or molecule that donates electrons, represented by the tail of a curly arrow.

nodos.label: Electron Sink
nodos.desc: An atom or molecule that accepts electrons, indicated by the barb of a curly arrow.

nodos.label: Reaction Steps
nodos.desc: A sequence of events in a reaction, such as dissociation followed by nucleophilic attack, used to depict mechanisms in SN1 reactions.

nodos.label: Axial Group
nodos.desc: A group attached to a cyclohexane ring in an axial position, experiencing greater steric repulsion due to eclipsed interactions compared to equatorial groups.

nodos.label: Equatorial Group
nodos.desc: A group attached to a cyclohexane ring in an equatorial position, experiencing minimal steric repulsion and lower energy compared to axial groups.

nodos.label: Eclipsed Interaction
nodos.desc: Steric repulsion that occurs when substituents on adjacent atoms are aligned in the same plane, increasing energy and destabilizing the conformation.

nodos.label: Energy State
nodos.desc: The potential energy level of a molecular configuration; axial groups occupy higher energy states due to increased repulsive forces.

nodos.label: SN1 Reaction
nodos.desc: A unimolecular nucleophilic substitution reaction that proceeds through a carbocation intermediate, with a rate-determining step involving ionization to form a carbocation.

nodos.label: Conformational Stability
nodos.desc: The stability of a molecular conformation, such as the chair form of cyclohexane, due to minimized angle and torsional strain.

nodos.label: Methyl Group Migration
nodos.desc: A 1,2-migration of a methyl group from one carbon to an adjacent carbon, shifting the positive charge and forming a more stable carbocation.

nodos.label: Hydride Ion Shift
nodos.desc: A 1,2-migration of a hydride ion (H⁻) from one carbon to an adjacent carbon, transferring the positive charge and stabilizing the carbocation.

nodos.label: Combined Hydride and Methyl Shift
nodos.desc: A concerted migration involving both a hydride and a methyl group, resulting in a change in the carbon skeleton and formation of a secondary carbocation.

nodos.label: Ring Closure (Cyclization)
nodos.desc: Formation of a cyclic structure through intramolecular bond formation between a carbocation and a nearby functional group, leading to a bicyclic system.

nodos.label: Constitutional Isomer
nodos.desc: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different connectivity of atoms, arising from rearrangement pathways in reactions.

nodos.label: Stabilidad del carbocatión
nodos.desc: La estabilidad de un carbocatión se ve influenciada por grupos electrónicamente donadores como alkoxy, amino o thioether, que estabilizan la carga positiva mediante efectos de resonancia o inductivo.

nodos.label: Grupos electronegativos
nodos.desc: Grupos como nitro, ciano, ácido carboxílico o éster disminuyen la reactividad de SN1 al destabilizar el carbocatión intermedio.

nodos.label: Polaredad del solvente
nodos.desc: Los solventes polares proticos, como el ácido acético, favorecen la formación de carbocatiónes mediante interacciones ion-dipolo, promoviendo la sustitución SN1 y reduciendo la eliminación E1.

nodos.label: Reacción SN1
nodos.desc: Mecanismo de sustitución nucleofílica unimolecular que involucra la formación de un carbocatión intermedio, con reactividad dependiente de la estabilidad del carbocatión y condiciones del medio.

nodos.label: Reacción SN2
nodos.desc: Mecanismo de sustitución nucleofílica bimolecular en el que un nucleófilo ataca desde el lado opuesto al grupo saliente, provocando inversión de configuración en el carbono central.

nodos.label: Cinética de SN1
nodos.desc: La reacción SN1 es de orden uno, ya que su velocidad depende únicamente de la concentración del reactivo (alkyl halide), no de la concentración del nucleófilo.

nodos.label: Cinética de SN2
nodos.desc: La reacción SN2 es de orden dos, ya que su velocidad depende de la concentración tanto del alkyl halide como del nucleófilo.

nodos.label: Preferencia de sustrato en SN2
nodos.desc: Los alquilo haluros primarios son más reactivos en SN2 debido a menor estericidad, facilitando el ataque desde el lado opuesto del carbono.

nodos.label: Inversión de configuración
nodos.desc: Cambio de orientación espacial en un centro químico durante una reacción SN2, donde el nucleófilo ataca desde el lado opuesto al grupo de salida, resultando en una configuración invertida.

nodos.label: Estructura molecular
nodos.desc: La disposición espacial de los átomos en una molécula que influye en la cinética y estereospecificidad de una reacción química.

nodos.label: Ion Pair
nodos.desc: Un conjunto de dos iones que se forman durante una reacción, donde uno es un cation y el otro un anión, interactuando directamente o separados por moléculas de solvente.

nodos.label: Contact Ion Pair
nodos.desc: Tipo de par de iones donde el anión se encuentra en contacto directo con el cation formado durante la disociación.

nodos.label: Solvent-Separated Ion Pair
nodos.desc: Tipo de par de iones donde una o más moléculas de solvente ocupan el espacio entre el cation y su anión.

nodos.label: Solvation Energy
nodos.desc: Energía liberada o absorbida cuando un ion o molécula se rodea por moléculas de solvente, afectando la estabilidad del estado de transición.

nodos.label: Polar Protic Solvent
nodos.desc: Solvente polar que contiene grupos hidroxilo o amonio, capaz de formar enlaces de hidrógeno con nucleófilos, reduciendo su reactividad.

nodos.label: Polar Aprotic Solvent
nodos.desc: Solvente polar que no contiene grupos hidroxilo o amonio, no forma enlaces de hidrógeno, permitiendo que nucleófilos actúen libremente.

nodos.label: Viscosity
nodos.desc: Propiedad del solvente que mide su resistencia al flujo; mayor viscosidad reduce la difusión, favoreciendo pares de iones cercanos.

nodos.label: Charge Separation
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que se separan cargas positivas y negativas, facilitando la estabilidad del estado de transición y la reactividad.

nodos.label: Haluros alílicos terciarios
nodos.desc: Presentan alta probabilidad de reacciones E1 debido a la estabilidad de sus carbocatiónes terciarios; ejemplos como el neopentil bromuro muestran transformaciones por E1 por falta de hidrógenos β.

nodos.label: Haluros alílicos secundarios
nodos.desc: Pueden seguir mecanismos E1, especialmente en condiciones ácidas, pero también compiten con S~N~1 y E2, dependiendo de los reactivos presentes.

nodos.label: Haluros alílicos primarios
nodos.desc: Tienen baja estabilidad de carbocatiónes, por lo que son poco propensos a E1, prefiriendo S~N~2; excepciones pueden ocurrir con grupos estéricamente voluminosos que disfrazan el ataque S~N~2.

nodos.label: Condiciones de reacción
nodos.desc: El tipo de reacción (E1) depende de factores como polaridad del disolvente, temperatura y naturaleza del sustrato, permitiendo controlar la distribución de productos.

nodos.label: Hyperconjugation
nodos.desc: The delocalization of electron density from a neighboring σ bond (such as a C–H bond) into an adjacent empty p orbital, typically in a carbocation, which stabilizes the positive charge and lowers the activation energy of the reaction.

nodos.label: Alpha Hydrogens
nodos.desc: Hydrogen atoms bonded to a carbon adjacent to a carbocation; their number determines the extent of hyperconjugation and thus the stability of the transition state.

nodos.label: Stereoselectivity
nodos.desc: The preference for the formation of one stereoisomer over another in a reaction, influenced by the stability of transition states due to steric and electronic factors.

nodos.label: E2 Mechanism
nodos.desc: A type of elimination reaction where both the nucleofuge and a beta hydrogen atom leave simultaneously, resulting in the formation of a double bond and the expulsion of a leaving group.

nodos.label: Regioselectivity
nodos.desc: The preferential formation of one product over others due to differences in electronic effects within a molecule, such as steric hindrance, hyperconjugation, and resonance.

nodos.label: Alkene Stability
nodos.desc: The thermodynamic stability of alkenes increases with the number of alkyl substituents on the double-bonded carbons, due to electron donation via hyperconjugation from adjacent C–H bonds to the pi* orbital of the double bond.

nodos.label: Angular Strain
nodos.desc: Torsional and geometric strain in small cycloalkanes that can be relieved through ring opening, lowering activation energy in elimination reactions.

nodos.label: E2 Elimination
nodos.desc: A concerted elimination reaction involving the simultaneous removal of a proton (H+) and a leaving group (X-) from adjacent carbon atoms, resulting in the formation of an alkene.

nodos.label: Second Order Kinetics
nodos.desc: The rate law for E2 reactions depends on the concentrations of both the substrate and the base, indicating a second-order reaction mechanism.

nodos.label: Antiperiplanar Geometry
nodos.desc: The optimal alignment of orbitals in E2 eliminations, where the p orbitals of the carbon with the leaving group and the carbon with the proton are oriented at approximately 180 degrees, enabling maximum orbital overlap and efficient elimination.

nodos.label: Stereospecificity
nodos.desc: The requirement for specific spatial arrangements of hydrogen atoms (e.g., axial vs. equatorial) in adjacent carbons to allow for syn or anti elimination, influencing the stereochemical outcome of the reaction.

nodos.label: Hyperconjugative Stabilization
nodos.desc: The stabilization of the transition state in E2 reactions through electron delocalization between adjacent sigma bonds and the forming pi bond, enhanced by antiperiplanar alignment.

nodos.label: Substrate Structure
nodos.desc: The molecular structure of the substrate (e.g., primary, secondary, tertiary) influences the likelihood and pathway of E2 elimination versus substitution or elimination reactions.

nodos.label: Carbanion Stability
nodos.desc: The relative stability of carbanions in E2 transition states, where more substituted carbanions are favored, explaining regioselectivity in certain eliminations.

nodos.label: Zaitsev Rule
nodos.desc: The principle that the most substituted alkene is the most thermodynamically stable and thus the major product in elimination reactions.

nodos.label: Anti-Periplanar Arrangement
nodos.desc: Geometric requirement in E2 reactions where the hydrogen and leaving group must be in an anti-coplanar orientation to facilitate elimination.

nodos.label: Base Strength
nodos.desc: The ability of a base to abstract a proton; stronger bases favor E2 reactions by promoting deprotonation, while weaker bases favor E1 reactions due to slower deprotonation.

nodos.label: Primary Substrate
nodos.desc: An organic molecule where the carbon bearing the functional group is bonded to only one other carbon atom, leading to limited carbocation stabilization and preference for SN2 or E2 reactions.

nodos.label: Secondary Substrate
nodos.desc: An organic molecule where the carbon bearing the functional group is bonded to two other carbon atoms, allowing for both substitution and elimination reactions under varying conditions.

nodos.label: Unimolecular Substitution (SN1)
nodos.desc: A substitution mechanism that proceeds through a carbocation intermediate, favored by tertiary substrates and polar protic solvents, with slower kinetics due to the formation of a high-energy intermediate.

nodos.label: Bimolecular Substitution (SN2)
nodos.desc: A substitution mechanism that occurs in a single step with simultaneous bond breaking and bond forming, favored by primary substrates and polar aprotic solvents due to minimal steric hindrance.

nodos.label: Pi electrons
nodos.desc: Electron density region in a double bond, delocalized above and below the molecular plane, weaker than sigma bonds.

nodos.label: Sigma electrons
nodos.desc: Electrons in a single covalent bond, located between adjacent atoms, stronger and more stable than pi electrons.

nodos.label: Exothermic reaction
nodos.desc: A chemical reaction that releases heat, indicating a net decrease in energy.

nodos.label: Transition state
nodos.desc: High-energy, unstable configuration during a reaction pathway, representing the peak of the energy profile between reactants and products.

nodos.label: Regiochemistry
nodos.desc: The orientation of atoms or groups in a molecule, determining the position of addition in a reaction.

nodos.label: Nucleophilic Attack
nodos.desc: A step in the reaction mechanism where a nucleophile, such as oxygen in water, attacks an electrophilic carbon atom.

nodos.label: Rate-Determining Step
nodos.desc: The slowest step in a reaction mechanism, which governs the overall reaction rate; in this case, the protonation of the alkene.

nodos.label: Oxonium Ion
nodos.desc: A transient, three-membered ring structure formed during nucleophilic attack, characterized by high strain and temporary stability due to resonance.

nodos.label: Reaction Kinetics
nodos.desc: The study of the rates of chemical reactions and the factors that influence them, such as temperature and concentration.

nodos.label: Substitution Stability
nodos.desc: Greater substitution of alkene or alkyne bonds increases stability due to more hyperconjugative interactions and greater electron delocalization.

nodos.label: Heat of Hydrogenation
nodos.desc: A thermodynamic measure of molecular stability; lower (less negative) values indicate greater stability in alkenes and alkynes.

nodos.label: Resonance Contributors
nodos.desc: Multiple structural forms of a molecule that contribute to the overall electronic structure, stabilizing the system through delocalization of electrons.

nodos.label: Ring Strain
nodos.desc: Energetic penalty in cyclic molecules due to deviation from ideal bond angles and planarity, particularly affecting cycloalkynes with small ring sizes.

nodos.label: Kinetic Control
nodos.desc: A reaction condition where the product distribution is determined by the activation energy of the transition state, favoring the least substituted product, even if it is not the most thermodynamically stable.

nodos.label: Thermodynamic Control
nodos.desc: A reaction condition where the product distribution is determined by the stability of the final product, favoring the most stable isomer, typically the most substituted alcohol in hydration reactions.

nodos.label: Acid-Catalyzed Hydration
nodos.desc: A reaction where water adds across the double bond of an alkene in the presence of an acid catalyst, forming an alcohol, with the mechanism involving protonation of the alkene to form a carbocation intermediate.

nodos.label: Alkene Reactivity
nodos.desc: The tendency of alkenes to undergo addition reactions due to the presence of a carbon-carbon double bond, which acts as a site of high electron density and susceptibility to electrophilic attack.

nodos.label: Alkene
nodos.desc: A hydrocarbon functional group with a carbon-carbon double bond, serving as the starting material in hydroboration-oxidation.

nodos.label: Borane
nodos.desc: A boron-containing reagent that adds across the double bond of an alkene in a hydroboration reaction.

nodos.label: Organoborane
nodos.desc: An intermediate species formed when borane adds to an alkene, containing a carbon-boron bond.

nodos.label: Anti-Markovnikov
nodos.desc: A regiochemical outcome where the boron atom attaches to the less substituted carbon of the alkene, leading to the final alcohol forming on the more substituted carbon.

nodos.label: Frontier Molecular Orbitals
nodos.desc: The highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) of the alkene and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) of borane interact to facilitate the addition reaction.

nodos.label: Chiral Centers
nodos.desc: Carbon atoms with four different substituents that can give rise to stereoisomers, formed during the addition process.

nodos.label: Chair Conformation
nodos.desc: A stable conformation of a cyclohexane ring where substituents prefer equatorial positions to minimize steric strain.

nodos.label: Boat Conformation
nodos.desc: An alternative conformation of a cyclohexane ring, less stable than chair, with axial substituents that may lead to steric strain.

nodos.label: Nucleophile
nodos.desc: Una especie química que dona un par de electrones para formar un enlace covalente, como el anión de un haluro de litio o sodio.

nodos.label: Bromonium Ion
nodos.desc: Un intermediario en reacciones de adición de halógenos, formado por la coordinación de un halógeno positivo a un átomo de carbono en un doble enlace.

nodos.label: Vicinal Dihalide
nodos.desc: Un compuesto orgánico en el que dos átomos de halógeno están unidos a carbonos adyacentes, formado por adición de halógeno a un doble enlace.

nodos.label: Syn Elimination
nodos.desc: Un proceso en el que dos grupos se eliminan simultáneamente desde el mismo lado de un compuesto, generando un enlace doble con una configuración específica.

nodos.label: Polyhalogenation
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que un alqueno sufre múltiples adiciones de halógenos, aunque en la práctica se detiene antes de saturación debido a factores como temperatura y concentración.

nodos.label: Molecular Orbitals
nodos.desc: Orbitales moleculares que describen la distribución de electrones en moléculas, y cuya alineación influye en la geometría y reactividad de compuestos.

nodos.label: Heterolytic Cleavage of Halogen Molecule
nodos.desc: Cleavage de un enlace de halógeno en dos iones, donde uno de los átomos se separa como un anión, generando un nucleófilo.

nodos.label: Cis-alkene
nodos.desc: An alkene where the two carbon atoms of the double bond have substituents on the same side, influencing stereochemical outcomes in reactions.

nodos.label: Trans-alkene
nodos.desc: An alkene where the two carbon atoms of the double bond have substituents on opposite sides, affecting reaction pathways and product formation.

nodos.label: Vicinal diol
nodos.desc: A compound with two hydroxyl (-OH) groups attached to adjacent carbon atoms, formed via dihydroxylation reactions of alkenes.

nodos.label: Osmium tetroxide (OsO4)
nodos.desc: A strong oxidizing agent that promotes syn dihydroxylation of alkenes to form vicinal diols with high stereochemical fidelity.

nodos.label: Anti dihydroxylation
nodos.desc: A reaction sequence where an epoxide is opened to form vicinal diols with opposite stereochemistry, typically via nucleophilic attack and subsequent quenching.

nodos.label: Backside attack
nodos.desc: A stereochemical mechanism where a nucleophile attacks from the opposite side of a leaving group, leading to inversion of configuration.

nodos.label: Transition metal oxidant
nodos.desc: A catalyst or reagent based on transition metals (e.g., V2O5, MoO3) used to facilitate oxidation reactions, offering alternatives to toxic reagents like OsO4.

nodos.label: Carbanion
nodos.desc: A negatively charged carbon species that acts as a nucleophile in organic reactions, often formed during deprotonation steps.

nodos.label: Thermally-driven reaction
nodos.desc: A reaction that proceeds under elevated temperature, providing sufficient energy to overcome activation barriers for ring-opening or rearrangement.

nodos.label: General-base catalysis
nodos.desc: A catalytic mechanism where a base deprotonates a molecule, enhancing nucleophilicity and facilitating reaction progression.

nodos.label: Número de átomos de carbono
nodos.desc: Concepto que indica la cantidad de átomos de carbono presentes en una molécula, utilizado para determinar la estructura de compuestos orgánicos como alquenos y alquinos.

nodos.label: Enlace triple
nodos.desc: Conexión química entre dos átomos de carbono formada por tres enlaces (uno sigma y dos pi), característico de los alquinos y que afecta su estructura y reactividad.

nodos.label: Ozonolisis
nodos.desc: Reacción química que rompe enlaces dobles o triples en alquenos y alquinos, produciendo compuestos de carbón como aldehídos o cetonas, útil para deducir estructuras moleculares.

nodos.label: Nomenclatura IUPAC
nodos.desc: Sistema estándar para nombrar compuestos orgánicos, que asigna números a los enlaces múltiples para identificar su posición en la cadena principal.

nodos.label: Estructura molecular
nodos.desc: Representación de la disposición de átomos en una molécula, que se puede deducir mediante análisis de productos de reacciones como la ozonolisis.

nodos.label: Geminal diols
nodos.desc: Compuestos orgánicos en los que dos grupos hidroxilo (OH) están unidos al mismo átomo de carbono.

nodos.label: Double elimination
nodos.desc: Reacción química que implica la eliminación de dos moléculas de agua para formar un triple enlace (alquino).

nodos.label: Alkynes
nodos.desc: Hidrocarburos insaturados que contienen un enlace triple entre dos átomos de carbono.

nodos.label: Catalytic hydrogenation
nodos.desc: Reacción de reducción de alquinos mediante adición de hidrógeno en presencia de un catalizador metálico.

nodos.label: Lindlar's catalyst
nodos.desc: Catalizador utilizado en la reducción parcial de alquinos para obtener alquenos cis.

nodos.label: Metal hydride reduction
nodos.desc: Método de reducción de alquinos utilizando compuestos de hidrógeno metálico como reactivos.

nodos.label: Addition reaction
nodos.desc: Reacción química en la que dos moléculas se combinan para formar una sola, típica en alquinos y diol.

nodos.label: Hydrogenation
nodos.desc: Proceso de adición de hidrógeno a una molécula, resultando en la saturación de enlaces múltiples.

nodos.label: Protonated Water (H3O+)
nodos.desc: The hydrated form of water with an extra proton, acting as an electrophile in nucleophilic attack reactions.

nodos.label: Tautomerization
nodos.desc: A chemical equilibrium between two isomers, where a hydrogen atom and a double bond shift positions, converting a carbonyl intermediate to an alcohol.

nodos.label: Anti-Markovnikov Hydration
nodos.desc: A reaction where the hydroxyl group adds to the less substituted carbon of an alkyne, facilitated by mercuric acetate, yielding primary alcohols.

nodos.label: Lindlar's Catalyst
nodos.desc: A palladium-based catalyst (Pd-BaSO4) used for selective semi-hydrogenation of alkynes to alkenes under controlled conditions.

nodos.label: Full Hydrogenation
nodos.desc: The complete reduction of alkynes to alkanes using catalysts such as Pt/S or Pd/C, involving addition of two equivalents of hydrogen.

nodos.label: Electrophilic Addition
nodos.desc: A reaction mechanism where an electrophile (e.g., Cl+ or Br+) attacks the alkyne, initiating halogenation via formation of a vinyl cation intermediate.

nodos.label: Halogenation
nodos.desc: The addition of halogen atoms (X2) to alkynes, resulting in haloalkenes or haloalkanes, with mono- and di-halogenation pathways.

nodos.label: Ozonolysis
nodos.desc: An oxidative cleavage reaction where ozone (O3) attacks alkynes to form intermediates that fragment into carbonyl compounds such as ketones, aldehydes, or carboxylic acids.

nodos.label: Molozonide
nodos.desc: A transient intermediate formed during ozonolysis, resulting from the initial addition of ozone to the alkyne triple bond.

nodos.label: Transition Metal Catalyst
nodos.desc: A class of catalysts (e.g., Pd, Pt) that facilitate bond formation or cleavage through surface-bound hydride species in hydrogenation reactions.

nodos.label: Heterolytic Cleavage
nodos.desc: A bond-breaking process where one atom retains both electrons, forming a hydride ion (H−) on the catalyst surface during hydrogenation.

nodos.label: Electrophilicity
nodos.desc: The tendency of a species to accept an electron pair; alcohols react with electrophilic reagents such as thionyl chloride (SOCl₂) in substitution reactions.

nodos.label: Substitution Reaction
nodos.desc: A chemical reaction in which one atom or group is replaced by another; alcohols undergo substitution reactions where the oxygen atom attacks an electrophilic center.

nodos.label: Preparación de alcoxidos
nodos.desc: Los alcoxidos son sales derivadas de alcoholes mediante reacción con hidruros metálicos o bases metálicas. Sirven como reactivos útiles en diversas reacciones químicas, especialmente en reacciones de tipo Grignard que implican la adición de organometálicos a compuestos carbónicos. Dos métodos comunes para la preparación de alcoxidos son: la reacción con hidruros metálicos y la desprotonación con bases fuertes.

nodos.label: Reacción con hidruros metálicos
nodos.desc: Una forma de preparar alcoxidos consiste en reaccionar un alcohol con un hidruro metálico adecuado, como el hidruro de aluminio litio (LiAlH4). Durante este proceso, el enlace O-H del alcohol se rompe heterolíticamente al interactuar con LiAlH4, resultando en la transferencia de un protón (H+) al ion hidruro (H−), formando gas H2. Al mismo tiempo, el átomo de oxígeno forma un enlace covalente con el ion litio, produciendo una sal de alcoxido. La reacción se representa como: R-OH + LiAlH4 → R-O−Li + AlH3 + H2. Se emplea exceso de LiAlH4 para asegurar la conversión completa y se debe excluir estrictamente el agua para evitar la descomposición prematura del alcoxido.

nodos.label: Desprotonación con base fuerte
nodos.desc: Otro método para generar alcoxidos consiste en desprotonar un alcohol utilizando una base fuerte capaz de extraer un protón del grupo hidroxilo. Reactivos comunes para este propósito incluyen el hidruro de sodio (NaH), el hidróxido de potasio (KOH) y el potasio.

nodos.label: Hidrofobicidad
nodos.desc: Propiedad que aumenta con la longitud de la cadena de carbono, debido a la naturaleza no polar de la estructura carbonada extendida, lo que reduce la solubilidad en agua.

nodos.label: Carbon Oxidation State
nodos.desc: Carbon in organic compounds typically has a formal oxidation state of zero when bonded in four single bonds (sp3 hybridization), calculated as +4 valence electrons minus 4 bonded pairs.

nodos.label: Oxygen Oxidation State
nodos.desc: Oxygen generally has an oxidation state between −1 and −2 in organic functional groups due to its high electronegativity and preference for forming two bonds via sp hybridization.

nodos.label: Alcohol Oxygen Oxidation State
nodos.desc: The oxygen in an alcohol group has a formal oxidation state closer to −1 than −2 due to its bent geometry and lone pair repulsion effects.

nodos.label: Electrophilic Moiety
nodos.desc: A chemical group capable of accepting a pair of electrons, such as Cr(VI), Mn(VII), or Se(IV), which participate in oxidation reactions involving alcohols.

nodos.label: Protecting group
nodos.desc: Un grupo protector es una molécula que se añade a un grupo funcional para bloquear su reactividad y evitar que participe en una reacción, permitiendo que otras transformaciones ocurran sin interferencia.

nodos.label: Eliminación
nodos.desc: Reacción química en la que se elimina un grupo funcional y se forma un doble enlace, como en la formación de alquenos a partir de alcoholes.

nodos.label: Eterificación
nodos.desc: Reacción química en la que un alcohol reacciona con un alcohol o un éter para formar un éter, como en el caso de la formación de MOE o THP.

nodos.label: Hidrólisis ácida
nodos.desc: Reacción en la que un compuesto se rompe en presencia de un ácido, comúnmente usada para desproteger grupos como MOE o THP.

nodos.label: Hidrólisis básica
nodos.desc: Reacción en la que un compuesto se rompe en presencia de una base, utilizada para desproteger grupos como acetatos.

nodos.label: Desilylación
nodos.desc: Proceso químico que consiste en eliminar un grupo silyl de un compuesto, generalmente mediante iones de flúor, como en el caso de silyl ethers.

nodos.label: Éter silyl
nodos.desc: Tipo de grupo protector formado por la adición de un cloruro de silyl a un alcohol, altamente estable y fácilmente eliminable por flúor.

nodos.label: Tetrahydropiránilo (THP)
nodos.desc: Grupo protector formado por reacción de un alcohol con pirano, estable en medios ácidos y fácilmente desprotegido por hidrólisis ácida o mercurio.

nodos.label: Metoxyetilo (MOE)
nodos.desc: Grupo protector robusto y estable en condiciones ácidas y básicas, formado mediante reacción de metanol y base, desprotegido por hidrólisis ácida.

nodos.label: Ion de flúor
nodos.desc: Ion que actúa como agente de desprotección en silyl ethers, facilitando la eliminación del grupo silyl mediante desilylación.

nodos.label: Reactivity
nodos.desc: The ability of a substance to undergo a chemical reaction, influenced by steric hindrance and molecular structure.

nodos.label: Elimination Process
nodos.desc: A reaction that removes atoms or groups from a molecule, often competing with substitution reactions, especially in highly substituted alkyl halides.

nodos.label: Reaction Temperature
nodos.desc: The temperature at which a reaction occurs; higher temperatures increase reaction rates and can help overcome energy barriers in bulky substrates.

nodos.label: Stoichiometric Ratio
nodos.desc: The molar ratio of reactants in a chemical reaction, critical for ensuring complete conversion and minimizing side products.

nodos.label: Ether Cleavage
nodos.desc: The breakdown of an ether bond under acidic conditions, resulting in the formation of two alcohol molecules.

nodos.label: Anti-Markovnikov Product
nodos.desc: Producto formado cuando el nucleófilo ataca al carbono menos sustituido de un epóxido, favorecido por un ataque de trasfondo (backside) en un centro más accesible.

nodos.label: Markovnikov Product
nodos.desc: Producto formado cuando el nucleófilo ataca al carbono más sustituido, influenciado por efectos de estabilidad y participación de grupos cercanos (anchimeric assistance).

nodos.label: Acid Catalysis
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que un ácido actúa como catalizador, facilitando la reacción mediante la formación de intermedios como iones oxonios en epóxidos.

nodos.label: Oxonium Ion Intermediate
nodos.desc: Intermedio de reacción en el que un oxígeno de un epóxido se protona, generando un ion oxonio que facilita la apertura del anillo y la formación de productos específicos.

nodos.label: Mild Reaction Conditions
nodos.desc: Condiciones de reacción suaves que permiten la preservación de grupos funcionales sensibles que podrían degradarse bajo condiciones más agresivas.

nodos.label: Conjugated Diene
nodos.desc: A molecule with alternating single and double bonds, capable of participating in Diels-Alder reactions to form cyclic structures.

nodos.label: Dienophile
nodos.desc: A molecule containing a double bond that reacts with a conjugated diene to form a six-membered ring via a pericyclic reaction.

nodos.label: Cis-Trans Configuration
nodos.desc: Stereochemical arrangement of substituents on a double bond, where cis refers to substituents on the same side and trans on opposite sides, influencing the stereochemistry of the Diels-Alder product.

nodos.label: Pericyclic Reaction
nodos.desc: A type of organic reaction that proceeds through a cyclic transition state without intermediates, such as the Diels-Alder reaction, which is a [4+2] cycloaddition.

nodos.label: Cyclohexene Ring
nodos.desc: A six-membered cyclic hydrocarbon with one double bond, formed as a product in Diels-Alder reactions between a diene and a dienophile.

nodos.label: Regioisomers
nodos.desc: Compounds with the same molecular formula and connectivity but differing in the position of functional groups or double bonds, arising from different alignment of reactants in Diels-Alder reactions.

nodos.label: HOMO
nodos.desc: El orbital molecular de mayor orden (HOMO) es el orbital de enlace más alto en energía que puede ser ocupado por electrones en una molécula, y participa en la interacción con el LUMO del dienófilo en la reacción de Diels-Alder.

nodos.label: LUMO
nodos.desc: El orbital molecular de menor orden (LUMO) es el orbital de enlace más bajo en energía que puede ser ocupado por electrones, y se superpone con el HOMO del diene para formar un complejo cíclico de orbitales p en la transición.

nodos.label: sigma complex
nodos.desc: Un complejo cíclico de orbitales p formado por la superposición del HOMO del diene y el LUMO del dienófilo durante el estado de transición en una reacción de Diels-Alder.

nodos.label: endo product
nodos.desc: Producto formado en una reacción de Diels-Alder donde un grupo sustituyente se dirige hacia el interior del anillo, favorecido por efectos electrónicos y estéricos.

nodos.label: exo product
nodos.desc: Producto formado en una reacción de Diels-Alder donde un grupo sustituyente se sitúa fuera del anillo, influenciado por la naturaleza electrónica del grupo sustituyente en el dienófilo.

nodos.label: diene configuration
nodos.desc: La configuración geométrica (cis o trans) del diene influye en la formación de isómeros específicos y en la selectividad de la reacción de Diels-Alder.

nodos.label: dienophile substituent
nodos.desc: Un grupo sustituyente en el dienófilo que afecta la reactividad y la orientación del producto, especialmente si es electronegativo o electropositivo.

nodos.label: Electronic Effects
nodos.desc: Influence of substituents on electron density in conjugated systems, where electron-donating groups enhance nucleophilicity at termini and electron-withdrawing groups reduce it, affecting regiochemical outcomes.

nodos.label: Frontier Orbitals
nodos.desc: Molecular orbitals involved in pericyclic reactions, particularly the interaction between the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) of the diene and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) of the dienophile, which governs reactivity and regioselectivity.

nodos.label: Stereocenters
nodos.desc: Atoms with four different substituents, which give rise to chirality and are critical in determining the three-dimensional structure of molecules in organic synthesis.

nodos.label: Chemo-Selectivity
nodos.desc: Preference for one type of chemical reaction over another in a molecule containing multiple reactive sites.

nodos.label: Regioselectivity
nodos.desc: The preference for the formation of one regioisomer over others in a reaction, particularly in Diels-Alder cycloadditions, driven by electronic and steric factors.

nodos.label: Enantioselectivity
nodos.desc: The preferential formation of one enantiomer over another, often achieved through chiral auxiliaries or catalysts in asymmetric synthesis.

nodos.label: Cycloaddition
nodos.desc: A pericyclic reaction in which two molecules combine to form a cyclic product, such as the Diels-Alder reaction, which constructs rings with defined stereochemistry.

nodos.label: Intramolecular Reaction
nodos.desc: A reaction where the reacting species are within the same molecule, enabling the formation of complex, polycyclic frameworks with multiple stereocenters in a single process.

nodos.label: Priority Rank
nodos.desc: A system that assigns relative priority to substituents on a benzene ring, such as -OH > -CH3, used to determine the correct order of naming in IUPAC nomenclature.

nodos.label: Locants
nodos.desc: Numerical positions on the benzene ring where substituents are attached, assigned to ensure the smallest possible set of locants for systematic naming.

nodos.label: Multiplicative Prefixes
nodos.desc: Prefixes like di-, tri-, tetra- used in IUPAC nomenclature to indicate the number of identical substituents, avoiding repetition of the full substituent name.

nodos.label: Ortho, Meta, Para
nodos.desc: Designations for the relative positions of two substituents on a benzene ring: ortho (adjacent), meta (separated by one carbon), para (opposite positions).

nodos.label: IUPAC Naming
nodos.desc: A standardized system for naming organic compounds, including benzene derivatives, to ensure consistency and clarity in chemical communication.

nodos.label: Substituent Groups
nodos.desc: Functional groups attached to a benzene ring, such as -OH (hydroxy), -CH3 (methyl), -NO2 (nitro), -F (fluoro), -NH2 (amino), which influence naming and reactivity.

nodos.label: Electrophile
nodos.desc: A species that accepts an electron pair, playing a key role in electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions like bromination of benzene.

nodos.label: Change in Entropy
nodos.desc: Variación en el desorden del sistema durante una reacción, que influye en la energía libre de Gibbs.

nodos.label: Aromatic Stability
nodos.desc: Estabilidad particular de compuestos cíclicos con sistemas de electrones π conjugados que cumplen las reglas de Hückel, como el benceno.

nodos.label: Resonance Energy
nodos.desc: Energía extra que se libera en compuestos aromáticos debido a la delocalización de electrones en un sistema conjugado.

nodos.label: Conjugated Pi-Electron System
nodos.desc: Sistema de enlaces π alternantes que permiten la delocalización de electrones, clave para la estabilidad aromática.

nodos.label: Acylium Ion
nodos.desc: Ion electropositivo formado cuando un ácido cloruro o anhídrido reacciona con un catalizador de Lewis (como AlCl3), que actúa como electrofílico en la reacción de acilación de Friedel-Crafts.

nodos.label: Aromatic Ring
nodos.desc: Estructura cíclica plana y conjugada que mantiene estabilidad por resonancia; actúa como nucleófilo en reacciones de sustitución electrophílica aromática.

nodos.label: Lewis Acid
nodos.desc: Sustancia que actúa como aceptor de pares de electrones; en este contexto, el aluminio tricloruro (AlCl3) actúa como catalizador para generar electrolitos activos en reacciones de Friedel-Crafts.

nodos.label: Electrophilic Substitution
nodos.desc: Reacción en la cual un grupo electropositivo se introduce en un anillo aromático mediante la ataque de un electrolito al sistema aromático, conservando la estructura aromática.

nodos.label: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution (EAS)
nodos.desc: A reaction in which an electrophile replaces a hydrogen atom on an aromatic ring, facilitated by regions of high electron density.

nodos.label: Ortho-Para Directors
nodos.desc: Functional groups that increase electron density at the ortho and para positions of a benzene ring, directing electrophilic substitution to these positions.

nodos.label: Meta Director
nodos.desc: A substituent that directs electrophilic aromatic substitution to the meta position of the benzene ring, typically due to electron-withdrawing properties that reduce electron density at ortho and para positions.

nodos.label: Electrophilic Attack
nodos.desc: A reaction mechanism in which an electrophile attacks an electron-rich aromatic ring, leading to substitution, with regioselectivity determined by existing substituents.

nodos.label: Ortho-Para Director
nodos.desc: A substituent that directs electrophilic substitution to the ortho and para positions, typically electron-donating groups that increase electron density in the aromatic ring.

nodos.label: Electron-Withdrawing Group (EWG)
nodos.desc: A functional group that reduces electron density in the aromatic ring, such as -NO₂, -CN, -COOH, -SO₃H, and halogens, which exhibit meta-directing behavior in electrophilic aromatic substitution.

nodos.label: Multiple Substituents
nodos.desc: Presence of more than one substituent on a benzene ring, leading to complex interactions between directing effects, where the overall regioselectivity is determined by the combined influence of each group.

nodos.label: Relative Directing Strength
nodos.desc: The comparative influence of different substituents on the directing effect in electrophilic aromatic substitution, where stronger activators (e.g., -NH₂) dominate over weaker ones (e.g., halogens).

nodos.label: Aromaticity
nodos.desc: A property of cyclic, planar molecules with delocalized electrons that confers stability, often described by Hückel's rule (4n+2 π electrons).

nodos.label: Electron Delocalization
nodos.desc: The spreading of π-electrons over multiple atoms in a conjugated system, contributing to stability and reactivity in aromatic compounds.

nodos.label: Reaction Selectivity
nodos.desc: The ability of a chemical reaction to produce a single major product with minimal side products, often achieved by controlling reaction conditions.

nodos.label: Solvent Effect
nodos.desc: The influence of the solvent on the rate and outcome of a chemical reaction, including selectivity and yield.

nodos.label: Functional Group Introduction
nodos.desc: The process of adding specific functional groups to an aromatic ring during a reaction, such as in Birch reduction, to create useful synthetic intermediates.

nodos.label: Carbon Ring Structures
nodos.desc: Molecular frameworks composed of carbon atoms arranged in pentagonal and hexagonal rings, such as in fullerenes, which exhibit unique physical and chemical properties.

nodos.label: C60 Fullerene
nodos.desc: A spherical fullerene molecule composed of 60 carbon atoms arranged in a truncated icosahedron, the most abundant fullerene and a key example in nanomaterials.

nodos.label: Alkali Metals
nodos.desc: Elements like sodium, lithium, and potassium that act as reducing agents in Birch reduction, with varying reactivity and side product formation.

nodos.label: Yield
nodos.desc: The amount of a desired product obtained from a reaction relative to the theoretical maximum, indicating efficiency and selectivity.

nodos.label: Side Products
nodos.desc: Unintended compounds formed during a reaction, which can reduce the efficiency and purity of the desired product.

nodos.label: Nucleophile Basicity
nodos.desc: The strength of a nucleophile's basicity influences whether a reaction proceeds via the Addition-Elimination (AEM) or Base-Mediated (BM) pathway; stronger bases favor AEM due to easier deprotonation, while weaker bases prefer BM to avoid forming negatively charged intermediates.

nodos.label: Solvents
nodos.desc: Polar protic solvents favor the Addition-Elimination (AEM) mechanism by stabilizing charged intermediates, whereas polar aprotic solvents enhance the Base-Mediated (BM) pathway by not solvating nucleophiles strongly, preserving their reactivity.

nodos.label: Nitroarenes
nodos.desc: Nitroarenes can act as electrophiles or nucleophiles depending on conditions; they participate in S~NAr reactions via the nitro group, which acts as an excellent leaving group, though they require forcing conditions due to low reactivity toward nucleophiles.

nodos.label: Halobenzenes
nodos.desc: Fluorinated halobenzenes are less reactive due to the strong C-F bond, while heavier halogens (Cl, Br, I) form more reactive substrates because of weaker C-X bonds, making them more prone to undergo S~NAr reactions.

nodos.label: Diazonium Salts
nodos.desc: Formed by diazotization of aromatic amines, diazonium salts are electrophilic intermediates that undergo substitution reactions with nucleophiles in Sandmeyer reactions, where the diazo group is replaced under controlled conditions.

nodos.label: Sulfonate Esters
nodos.desc: Arenesulfonyl chlorides and arenediazonium tetrafluoroborates are precursors to aryl sulfonate esters, which readily undergo S~NAr reactions due to powerful leaving groups, enabling substitution under mild conditions.

nodos.label: Oxidation Reaction
nodos.desc: A chemical reaction in which a compound loses electrons and gains oxygen, such as aldehydes being converted to carboxylic acids.

nodos.label: Carboxylic Acid
nodos.desc: A compound with a carbon atom double bonded to an oxygen atom and singly bonded to a hydroxyl group.

nodos.label: IUPAC Nomenclature
nodos.desc: A systematic method for naming organic compounds, including ketones, to ensure unambiguous communication among chemists.

nodos.label: Functional Group Position
nodos.desc: The location of the carbonyl group within the carbon chain, which determines the classification and properties of the compound.

nodos.label: Van der Waals Forces
nodos.desc: Weak intermolecular forces that increase with the size and surface area of molecules, contributing to higher boiling points in longer carbon chains.

nodos.label: Isomerism
nodos.desc: The phenomenon where molecules have the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements; geometric isomerism can affect crystal lattice formation and thus melting points.

nodos.label: Tetrahedral Intermediate
nodos.desc: A transient species formed during nucleophilic addition reactions, where the carbon atom of the carbonyl group becomes sp3 hybridized and bonded to four atoms or groups.

nodos.label: Polar Protic Solvents
nodos.desc: Solvents such as ethanol and methanol that contain both a polar bond and a hydrogen atom, capable of stabilizing charge separation in transition states, thereby promoting hydrate formation.

nodos.label: Structural Reactivity
nodos.desc: The tendency of a molecule to undergo a specific reaction, which is governed by its molecular structure and functional groups, such as the nature of the carbonyl group in aldehydes and ketones.

nodos.label: Carbono de un grupo carbónico
nodos.desc: Átomo de carbono en un grupo funcional carbónico (aldehído o cetona) que es electropositivo y susceptible a ataque por nucleófilos.

nodos.label: Diol geminal
nodos.desc: Compuesto formado por la adición de agua a un grupo carbónico, donde los dos grupos hidroxilo están unidos al mismo carbono.

nodos.label: Hemiacetal
nodos.desc: Compuesto formado por la adición de un alcohol a un grupo carbónico, con un grupo hidroxilo y un grupo alquilo unidos al mismo carbono.

nodos.label: Acetal
nodos.desc: Compuesto estable formado por la reacción de un hemiacetal con un alcohol, que no se hidroliza fácilmente y se usa como grupo protector en síntesis orgánica.

nodos.label: Base de Lewis
nodos.desc: Espécie que dona un par de electrones para formar un enlace covalente con un átomo electropositivo.

nodos.label: Catalización
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que un catalizador acelera una reacción sin ser consumido, facilitando la formación de productos mediante mecanismos específicos.

nodos.label: Carbonyl compound
nodos.desc: A molecule containing a carbon-oxygen double bond, such as aldehydes and ketones, which act as electrophiles in organic reactions.

nodos.label: Imine
nodos.desc: A compound formed by the condensation of a carbonyl compound with an amine, characterized by a carbon-nitrogen double bond (C=N), also known as a Schiff base.

nodos.label: Enamine
nodos.desc: A compound formed by the condensation of a carbonyl compound with a secondary amine under acidic conditions, featuring a carbon-nitrogen single bond and a double bond to an adjacent carbon.

nodos.label: Dipolar intermediate
nodos.desc: A transient species formed during imine formation, resulting from the nucleophilic attack of an amine on a carbonyl carbon, which carries a partial positive and negative charge.

nodos.label: E and Z configuration
nodos.desc: Stereochemical arrangements around the C=N bond in imines, where E refers to trans and Z to cis orientation of substituents.

nodos.label: Condensation reaction
nodos.desc: A reaction in which two molecules combine to form a larger molecule, with the elimination of a small molecule such as water.

nodos.label: Cyanohydrin
nodos.desc: A neutral organic compound formed by protonation at the oxygen atom of a carbonyl group when using KCN or NaCN, resulting from nucleophilic addition of cyanide to aldehydes or ketones.

nodos.label: α-Hydroxy carboxylic acid
nodos.desc: An organic acid formed by hydrolysis of the nitrile moiety in cyanohydrins under acidic conditions, containing a hydroxyl group adjacent to a carboxylic acid group.

nodos.label: Primary or secondary alcohol
nodos.desc: Alcohols obtained through reduction of α-hydroxy carboxylic acids, with primary alcohols formed using LiAlH4 and secondary alcohols using NaBH4.

nodos.label: Bisulfite adduct
nodos.desc: A product formed by the addition of bisulfite to aldehydes or ketones, serving as a protective group and a detection method for carbonyl compounds.

nodos.label: Oxa-Michael addition
nodos.desc: A type of nucleophilic addition reaction where sulfur from bisulfite acts as a nucleophile, formally classified as an oxa-Michael addition to carbonyl compounds.

nodos.label: Equilibrium shift
nodos.desc: A dynamic process in which the formation of a siloxane byproduct (Me3SiOSiMe3) decomposes to release methanol, driving the reaction equilibrium toward complete conversion of the carbonyl compound.

nodos.label: Toxicity
nodos.desc: The inherent hazard associated with HCN and its salts, requiring strict safety protocols during handling and use in chemical synthesis.

nodos.label: Catalyst system
nodos.desc: A combination of trimethylsilylcyanide (TMSCN) and boron trifluoride etherate (BFE) used to replace stoichiometric HCN, enabling safer and more efficient cyanation reactions.

nodos.label: Hydride Reducing Agent
nodos.desc: A chemical species that donates hydride (H⁻) to reduce carbonyl groups, such as aldehydes and ketones, to form alcohols; examples include LiAlH4 and NaCNBH3.

nodos.label: Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley Reduction
nodos.desc: An indirect method of reducing aldehydes and ketones using aluminum alkoxides, which operates via a cyclic transition state and is known for its selectivity and functional group tolerance.

nodos.label: Oppenauer Reduction
nodos.desc: An indirect reduction method that uses ketones as reducing agents to reduce aldehydes and ketones, typically in the presence of a ketone donor and a catalyst.

nodos.label: Tollens' Reagent
nodos.desc: A solution of silver nitrate, ammonia, and sodium hydroxide used to oxidize aldehydes to carboxylic acids, producing a silver mirror as a visible indicator of aldehyde presence.

nodos.label: Reduction Mechanism
nodos.desc: The step-by-step process by which a carbonyl group is reduced to an alcohol via hydride transfer, involving nucleophilic attack of hydride on the carbonyl carbon.

nodos.label: Selectivity
nodos.desc: The ability of a reagent or reaction to preferentially react with one functional group over another, such as the differential reactivity of aldehydes versus ketones in oxidation or reduction.

nodos.label: Functional Group Tolerance
nodos.desc: The capacity of a reducing or oxidizing agent to remain unreactive toward other functional groups present in a molecule, allowing for selective transformations in complex organic systems.

nodos.label: Polyol Framework
nodos.desc: A structural motif in organic molecules containing multiple hydroxyl (-OH) groups, commonly found in natural products like discodermolide, formed through sequential reductions of ketones and aldehydes.

nodos.label: Dehydration
nodos.desc: A chemical reaction in which a molecule loses a water molecule, typically occurring during the formation of acid anhydrides from carboxylic acids.

nodos.label: Acyl Chloride
nodos.desc: An organic compound derived from carboxylic acids by replacement of the hydroxyl group with a chlorine atom, highly reactive and used in synthesis.

nodos.label: Chlorination
nodos.desc: A chemical reaction involving the introduction of chlorine atoms into a molecule, often used in the conversion of carboxylic acids to acyl chlorides.

nodos.label: Intermediate
nodos.desc: A transient species formed during a chemical reaction, which does not appear in the final products but plays a key role in the reaction pathway.

nodos.label: Amide Functional Group
nodos.desc: A functional group where a carbonyl carbon is bonded to a nitrogen atom, with the nitrogen bonded to two alkyl or aryl groups, forming a stable structure important in polymers and pharmaceuticals.

nodos.label: Decarboxylation
nodos.desc: A chemical reaction in which a carboxyl group (-COOH) is removed from a molecule, resulting in the loss of carbon dioxide (CO2) and the formation of a smaller molecule with one fewer carbon atom.

nodos.label: Acid Catalyst
nodos.desc: A substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction by providing protons (H+), such as sulfuric acid, phosphoric acid, or Lewis acids like boron trifluoride etherate (BF3·Et2O).

nodos.label: Fischer Esterification
nodos.desc: A reaction in which a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst to form an ester and water, a fundamental method for ester preparation.

nodos.label: Coupling Agent
nodos.desc: A reagent used to facilitate the formation of a bond between two molecules, such as dicyclohexylcarbodiimide (DCC), which enables efficient and selective amide formation from carboxylic acids and amines.

nodos.label: Nucleophilic Acyl Substitution
nodos.desc: Un mecanismo fundamental en química orgánica que implica la sustitución de un nucleófilo por otro en un carbono de un grupo carbónilo. Se produce cuando un nucleófilo ataca el carbono electropositivo del grupo carbónilo, desplazando un grupo de salida (X).

nodos.label: Saponification
nodos.desc: Reacción de hidrólisis básica de ésteres que produce un sal de carboxilato y un alcohol. Es clave en la fabricación de jabones.

nodos.label: Transesterification
nodos.desc: Reacción en la cual un grupo alcohol de un éster se intercambia por otro alcohol, permitiendo la conversión de ésteres en otros ésteres bajo condiciones adecuadas.

nodos.label: Amides
nodos.desc: Derivados de ácidos carboxílicos en los que el grupo hidroxilo ha sido reemplazado por un grupo amino. Son relativamente inactivos debido a la donación de electrones del par de electrones del nitrógeno al carbono carbónilo.

nodos.label: Hydrolysis
nodos.desc: Reacción en la que un compuesto se rompe mediante la adición de agua, como en el caso de la hidrólisis ácida de amidas que produce ácidos carboxílicos y sales de aminas.

nodos.label: Base Catalysis
nodos.desc: A reaction mechanism where a base accepts a proton or donates electrons to increase the nucleophilicity of a species, such as water, enabling it to attack electrophilic centers in hydrolysis reactions.

nodos.label: Keto-Enol Tautomerization
nodos.desc: A chemical reaction involving the interconversion between a ketone or aldehyde and an enol, mediated by the formation of an enolate anion at the alpha carbon.

nodos.label: Enolate Anion
nodos.desc: A negatively charged species formed at the alpha carbon during keto-enol tautomerization, which is nucleophilic and reactive in organic chemistry.

nodos.label: Beta-Lactamase
nodos.desc: An enzyme that hydrolyzes beta-lactam antibiotics, leading to bacterial resistance.

nodos.label: Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase (ESBL)
nodos.desc: A type of beta-lactamase that confers resistance to multiple beta-lactam antibiotics, making treatment challenging.

nodos.label: Metallo-Beta-Lactamase (MBL)
nodos.desc: An enzyme capable of hydrolyzing virtually all beta-lactam agents, posing a significant threat due to limited therapeutic options.

nodos.label: Penicillin-Binding Proteins
nodos.desc: Proteins on bacterial cell surfaces that bind beta-lactam antibiotics; mutations in these proteins can lead to resistance.

nodos.label: Reduced Permeability or Active Efflux Pumps
nodos.desc: Mechanisms by which bacteria limit antibiotic entry or actively expel antibiotics, contributing to resistance.

nodos.label: Biofilm
nodos.desc: A structured community of microorganisms encased in a protective extracellular matrix, which can resist antibiotic treatment.

nodos.label: Keto-Enol Tautomerism
nodos.desc: Equilibrio entre dos formas isoméricas de un compuesto: la forma keto (carbón oxígeno) y la forma enol (carbono doble con hidrógeno en el carbono alfa), donde la forma keto es más estable en aldehídos.

nodos.label: Deprotonation
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que un protón es eliminado de un átomo de hidrógeno en el carbono alfa de un aldehído mediante una base fuerte, generando un enolato aniónico.

nodos.label: Enolate
nodos.desc: A nucleophilic species formed by deprotonation of the alpha carbon of a carbonyl compound, which can act as a nucleophile in reactions like aldol addition.

nodos.label: Keto-Enol Tautomerism
nodos.desc: A reversible equilibrium between a keto form (carbonyl) and an enol form (hydroxyl group attached to a double bond), involving the alpha carbon and facilitating enolate formation.

nodos.label: Kinetic Enolate
nodos.desc: An enolate formed under conditions of low temperature and strong base, which results in rapid deprotonation at the less substituted alpha carbon due to lower activation energy, leading to regioselectivity based on steric and electronic factors.

nodos.label: Thermodynamic Enolate
nodos.desc: An enolate formed under equilibrating conditions (e.g., higher temperature or longer reaction times), where the more stable enolate (often at the more substituted alpha carbon) predominates due to greater stability of the intermediate.

nodos.label: Aldol Reaction
nodos.desc: A carbon-carbon bond-forming reaction in which an enolate attacks a carbonyl compound to form a beta-hydroxy carbonyl intermediate, which can dehydrate to yield an alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl compound.

nodos.label: Stereochemical Control
nodos.desc: The ability to influence the spatial arrangement of atoms in a product through controlled reaction conditions, particularly important in multi-step synthetic pathways involving enolates.

nodos.label: Aldol Addition
nodos.desc: A reaction in which an enolate anion attacks the carbonyl carbon of another carbonyl compound, forming a beta-hydroxy carbonyl compound.

nodos.label: Conjugated Enone
nodos.desc: A system consisting of a carbonyl group conjugated to a carbon-carbon double bond, which is stabilized by resonance and is a common product in aldol condensations.

nodos.label: Regioisomeric Adducts
nodos.desc: Different structural isomers formed due to the nucleophilic attack of enolates on carbonyl groups at different positions, leading to multiple possible products.

nodos.label: Self-Condensation
nodos.desc: A side reaction in which a single carbonyl compound reacts with itself, leading to undesired byproducts and reducing the efficiency of mixed aldol reactions.

nodos.label: Cycloalkylamine
nodos.desc: An amine derived from cycloalkanes by replacing one hydrogen atom with an amino group (-NH₂), where the ring serves as the parent structure.

nodos.label: IUPAC rules
nodos.desc: Systematic naming conventions used to name organic compounds, including amines, based on structural features and functional group positioning.

nodos.label: Ring positioning
nodos.desc: The numbering of substituents on a ring, starting from the most highly substituted position and proceeding clockwise, to ensure consistent nomenclature.

nodos.label: Aromatic amine
nodos.desc: An amine where the nitrogen is attached to an aromatic ring, following specific resonance and naming conventions.

nodos.label: Force constant
nodos.desc: A measure of the stiffness of a bond, determining the vibrational frequency of a bond in a molecule.

nodos.label: Vibrational frequency
nodos.desc: The frequency at which a bond vibrates, determined by the force constant and reduced mass of the system.

nodos.label: Bond coupling
nodos.desc: The interaction between adjacent bonds due to disturbances in electric fields, affecting dipole moments and vibrational frequencies.

nodos.label: Stretching mode
nodos.desc: A vibrational motion where bonds are elongated or compressed, contributing to vibrational energy levels in molecules.

nodos.label: Deformation mode
nodos.desc: A vibrational motion involving changes in bond angles, adding to the vibrational spectrum of a molecule.

nodos.label: Vibrational energy levels
nodos.desc: Discrete energy states associated with molecular vibrations, formed by combinations of stretching and deformation modes.

nodos.label: IR transition
nodos.desc: A change in vibrational energy levels that can be excited by infrared radiation, resulting in absorption bands in IR spectra.

nodos.label: IR spectral peak
nodos.desc: A peak in an infrared spectrum indicating a specific vibrational mode, used to infer molecular structure and functional groups.

nodos.label: Intensidad de señal
nodos.desc: Mide la altura de un pico en un espectro, proporcionando información sobre la cantidad de grupos funcionales presentes en una molécula.

nodos.label: Coeficiente de absorptividad molar (ε)
nodos.desc: Valor que indica cuán eficazmente los enlaces absorben radiación; depende de la estructura molecular, polaridad del solvente y temperatura.

nodos.label: Longitud del camino (l)
nodos.desc: Distancia que recorre la luz a través de la muestra; mayor longitud aumenta la interacción con la muestra y por tanto la intensidad de la señal.

nodos.label: Número de enlaces
nodos.desc: La cantidad de enlaces que contribuyen a una banda de absorción influye en la intensidad, aunque no de forma lineal debido a efectos de saturación.

nodos.label: Modo vibracional
nodos.desc: Forma en que los enlaces se deforman y oscilan; cada tipo de enlace tiene una frecuencia característica de vibración.

nodos.label: Symmetric Stretch
nodos.desc: A type of vibrational mode where the atoms in a molecule move in such a way that the dipole moment change is minimal, often resulting in weak or no observable signal in the infrared spectrum.

nodos.label: Asymmetric Stretch
nodos.desc: A vibrational mode where the atoms move in a way that produces a significant change in dipole moment, leading to a strong absorption peak in the infrared spectrum.

nodos.label: Molecular Mass
nodos.desc: The total mass of a molecule, which affects the vibrational frequencies and the intensity of infrared absorption signals.

nodos.label: Carbonyl Stretch
nodos.desc: The infrared absorption band associated with the vibration of the C=O bond in carbonyl-containing compounds, typically occurring between 1650 and 1850 cm⁻¹.

nodos.label: Energy Levels
nodos.desc: Discrete energy states that electrons in atoms and molecules can occupy, with lower energy levels being more stable.

nodos.label: Electronic Transition
nodos.desc: The movement of an electron from a lower energy level to a higher one when absorbing a photon of specific energy.

nodos.label: Absorbance
nodos.desc: A measure of the amount of light absorbed by a sample, defined as the logarithmic ratio of incident to transmitted light intensity.

nodos.label: Beer-Lambetric Law
nodos.desc: A mathematical relationship that describes the absorbance of a solution as a function of its concentration, path length, and molar extinction coefficient: A = εlc.

nodos.label: Molar Extinction Coefficient
nodos.desc: A constant that quantifies the ability of a substance to absorb light at a specific wavelength, expressed in L·mol⁻¹·cm⁻¹.

nodos.label: Absorbance Bands
nodos.desc: Distinct regions in the UV/Vis spectrum where specific electronic transitions occur, providing information about molecular structure.

nodos.label: Quantitative Analysis
nodos.desc: A method in UV/Vis spectroscopy used to determine the concentration of a substance in a sample by comparing absorbance values to a calibration curve.

nodos.label: Calibration Curve
nodos.desc: A graph that plots absorbance against known concentrations of a standard solution, used to determine unknown concentrations in a sample.

nodos.label: HOMO-LUMO
nodos.desc: Diferencia de energía entre el orbital molecular más ocupado (HOMO) y el menos ocupado (LUMO); una menor diferencia implica una transición con menor energía de fotones.

nodos.label: Longitud de onda de absorción
nodos.desc: Longitud de onda de la luz absorbida por una molécula; a medida que aumenta la conjugación, se desplaza hacia longitudes de onda más largas, entrando en el rango visible.

nodos.label: Polienos
nodos.desc: Hidrocarburos con múltiples enlaces dobles consecutivos; ejemplos incluyen carotenoides, cuyos colores cambian con la longitud de la cadena conjugada.

nodos.label: Caroteno
nodos.desc: Polieno con 40 carbonos que absorbe máxima luz a alrededor de 450 nm, responsable del color naranja en rápex.

nodos.label: Lycopeno
nodos.desc: Polieno con más enlaces conjugados que el caroteno, absorbe luz máxima cerca de 500 nm, responsable del color rojo en tomates.

nodos.label: Antrocianinas
nodos.desc: Pigmentos solubles en agua de plantas que producen colores azules, morados y rojos debido a estructuras altamente conjugadas derivadas de cationes flavylium.

nodos.label: Trans-stilbene
nodos.desc: Ejemplo de sistema conjugado que puede ser incoloro debido a la cancelación de fuerzas oscilatorias en la excitación, reduciendo la intensidad de absorción visible.

nodos.label: Espectro electromagnético
nodos.desc: Rango de longitudes de onda de la luz, donde la absorción en el rango visible (400-700 nm) permite la percepción de colores por el ojo humano.

nodos.label: Nuclear Shielding
nodos.desc: Concepto que describe la protección de los núcleos atómicos de los efectos del campo magnético externo, influenciado por los electrones circundantes; determina la posición de los picos en el espectro de resonancia magnética nuclear (NMR).

nodos.label: Chemical Shift
nodos.desc: Desplazamiento de los picos en el espectro de NMR que refleja la posición de los núcleos en un campo magnético, influenciada por el entorno electrónico y la hidrofobicidad de los grupos funcionales.

nodos.label: Delocalized Pi Electrons
nodos.desc: Electrones pi distribuidos en un sistema conjugado cíclico, como en anillos aromáticos, que generan un entorno desprotegido, causando desplazamiento hacia el campo magnético más débil (deshielding).

nodos.label: Diastereotopic Splitting
nodos.desc: Patrón de división en espectros de NMR observado en grupos geminales o vicinales debido a efectos estéricos y diferencias en el entorno magnético de los núcleos.

nodos.label: Coupling Constants
nodos.desc: Valores que indican la interacción entre núcleos adyacentes en un compuesto, afectados por distancias espaciales y ángulos, y que permiten inferir estructuras moleculares.

nodos.label: Solvent Effects
nodos.desc: Influencia del medio en el cual se realiza la medición del espectro de NMR, especialmente en la modificación de la protección nuclear de los núcleos por interacciones de solvatación.

nodos.label: Deuterated Chloroform (CDCl₃)
nodos.desc: Solvente común en NMR que proporciona un entorno estable y sin interferencia magnética significativa por deuterio, facilitando la identificación de picos de hidrógeno.

nodos.label: Diamagnetic Anisotropy
