nodos.desc: Proceso de saturación de la sangre con oxígeno, fundamental para el funcionamiento de órganos vitales en el feto.

nodos.label: Compensatory Mechanism
nodos.desc: Mecanismo fisiológico que permite al feto mantener oxigenación adecuada bajo condiciones adversas, como la insuficiencia placentaria.

nodos.label: Pathophysiology
nodos.desc: Estudio de las causas y mecanismos subyacentes de enfermedades, como el desequilibrio en la circulación fetal por HPV exagerado.

nodos.label: Molecular Interactions
nodos.desc: Interacciones moleculares que regulan la activación de HPV, incluyendo cascadas de señalización y moléculas efectoras.

nodos.label: Preterm Neonate
nodos.desc: Niño nacido antes de las 37 semanas de gestación, con desarrollo pulmonar inmaduro y mayor riesgo de complicaciones respiratorias.

nodos.label: Asimptótico
nodos.desc: Estado en el que una persona no muestra síntomas clínicos, aunque pueda tener condiciones subyacentes.

nodos.label: Embolismo paradojal
nodos.desc: Eventualidad en la que un coágulo se desplaza hacia el sistema circulatorio y obstruye un vaso sanguíneo en una zona distal, causando complicaciones.

nodos.label: Stroke criptogénico
nodos.desc: Un accidente cerebrovascular cuya causa no se puede identificar clínicamente, aunque puede tener implicaciones matemáticas en modelos de flujo sanguíneo.

nodos.label: Síndrome de descompresión
nodos.desc: Condición que ocurre cuando el cuerpo libera gases disueltos al cambiar rápidamente de presión, modelada matemáticamente por ecuaciones de equilibrio de gases.

nodos.label: Dolor de cabeza migratorio
nodos.desc: Síntoma que puede estar relacionado con cambios en la presión sanguínea y flujo, que pueden ser analizados mediante modelos matemáticos de dinámica de fluidos.

nodos.label: Regresión del vaso umbilical
nodos.desc: Proceso fisiológico donde el vaso umbilical se involucra gradualmente, modelado por funciones de decaimiento exponencial.

nodos.label: Cambios hemodinámicos
nodos.desc: Variaciones en el flujo sanguíneo y presión, que pueden ser representadas mediante ecuaciones diferenciales del flujo sanguíneo.

nodos.label: Perfusión pulmonar
nodos.desc: Proceso por el cual el aire y el oxígeno se transfieren a la sangre en los pulmones, modelado matemáticamente por ecuaciones de transferencia de masa.

nodos.label: Resistencia vascular sistémica
nodos.desc: Parámetro que describe la oposición al flujo sanguíneo en los vasos sanguíneos, representado por una función de resistencia en circuitos circulatorios.

nodos.label: Relleno del ventrículo izquierdo
nodos.desc: Proceso que se modela mediante ecuaciones de dinámica de fluidos, donde el volumen de sangre se regula en función del tiempo.

nodos.label: Hematocrito
nodos.desc: Proporción de células rojas en la sangre, que cambia matemáticamente durante el desarrollo neonatal.

nodos.label: Hemoglobina fetal
nodos.desc: Forma de hemoglobina con mayor afinidad por el oxígeno que la hemoglobina adulta, modelada por ecuaciones de afinidad química.

nodos.label: Hemoglobina adulta
nodos.desc: Forma de hemoglobina que se convierte en la principal en el adulto, con menor afinidad por el oxígeno.

nodos.label: Epinefrina y norepinefrina
nodos.desc: Hormonas que aumentan la contractilidad cardíaca y la frecuencia cardíaca, modeladas por ecuaciones de dinámica de sistemas biológicos.

nodos.label: Anxiety
nodos.desc: A psychological state characterized by feelings of worry, tension, and unease, which may manifest as a symptom during cardiac events.

nodos.label: Cough
nodos.desc: A physical symptom that may accompany heart-related conditions, often due to fluid accumulation in the lungs.

nodos.label: Fainting
nodos.desc: A temporary loss of consciousness, which can be a sign of reduced blood flow to the brain, potentially linked to cardiac issues.

nodos.label: Palpitations
nodos.desc: The sensation of a rapid, irregular, or forceful heartbeat, often associated with arrhythmias or cardiac dysfunction.

nodos.label: Sudden Cardiac Arrest
nodos.desc: A sudden loss of heart function, breathing, and consciousness, requiring immediate medical intervention.

nodos.label: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
nodos.desc: A diagnostic tool that measures and records the electrical activity of the heart, used to detect abnormalities in heart rhythm and structure.

nodos.label: Echocardiography
nodos.desc: A non-invasive imaging technique using ultrasound to visualize the heart's structure and function, assessing contractility and valve function.

nodos.label: Ischemia
nodos.desc: A condition in which tissues receive insufficient blood flow, leading to reduced oxygen supply, commonly observed in heart disease.

nodos.label: Nuclear Imaging
nodos.desc: A diagnostic method involving the injection of radioactive tracers to visualize blood flow patterns in the heart, identifying areas of reduced perfusion.

nodos.label: Coronary Angiography
nodos.desc: An invasive procedure that uses X-rays and contrast dye to visualize the coronary arteries and detect blockages.

nodos.label: Lifestyle Modifications
nodos.desc: Changes in daily habits such as smoking cessation, exercise, nutrition, weight management, and stress reduction to improve cardiovascular health.

nodos.label: Pharmacological Therapy
nodos.desc: The use of medications to manage heart disease, including those that reduce blood pressure, lower lipids, prevent clotting, and control heart rhythm.

nodos.label: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI)
nodos.desc: A minimally invasive procedure involving balloon angioplasty and stent placement to open blocked coronary arteries.

nodos.label: Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG)
nodos.desc: A surgical procedure that creates new pathways for blood flow around blocked coronary arteries, improving blood supply to the heart.

nodos.label: Primary Prevention
nodos.desc: Strategies aimed at reducing the risk of heart disease before clinical symptoms appear, through lifestyle and medical interventions.

nodos.label: Secondary Prevention
nodos.desc: Interventions designed to prevent disease progression and recurrence in individuals already diagnosed with heart disease.

nodos.label: Cardiovascular Physiology
nodos.desc: The study of the mechanisms and functions of the cardiovascular system, including heart function, blood flow, and regulation.

nodos.label: Diagnostics
nodos.desc: The set of methods and tools used to identify and assess heart disease, including ECG, echocardiography, and imaging techniques.

nodos.label: Therapeutics
nodos.desc: The branch of medicine dealing with the treatment of diseases, including pharmacological and surgical interventions for heart conditions.

nodos.label: Preventive Measures
nodos.desc: Strategies and actions taken to reduce the incidence and impact of heart disease through early intervention and healthy living.

nodos.label: Endothelial Damage
nodos.desc: Initial injury to the endothelial cells lining the arterial wall, which allows lipids and immune cells to enter the arterial wall.

nodos.label: Lipid Accumulation
nodos.desc: Buildup of lipids, particularly low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, within the arterial wall following endothelial damage.

nodos.label: Foam Cells
nodos.desc: Macrophages that have engulfed lipids and become lipid-laden, contributing to plaque formation.

nodos.label: Plaque Growth
nodos.desc: Progressive accumulation of lipids, dead cells, calcium, and debris within the arterial wall, leading to plaque formation.

nodos.label: Fibrous Cap
nodos.desc: Layer of smooth muscle cells and extracellular matrix that covers the plaque; its thinning increases rupture risk.

nodos.label: Platelet Aggregation
nodos.desc: Clot formation at the site of plaque rupture due to platelet activation and aggregation.

nodos.label: Thrombus
nodos.desc: A blood clot that forms as a result of platelet aggregation, potentially obstructing blood flow and causing tissue infarction.

nodos.label: Tissue Infarction
nodos.desc: Death of tissue due to interruption of blood flow caused by a thrombus or occlusion.

nodos.label: Calcification
nodos.desc: Deposition of calcium in atherosclerotic plaques, leading to hardening and stabilization of lesions.

nodos.label: Luminal Narrowing
nodos.desc: Reduction in the diameter of the arterial lumen due to plaque buildup and healing responses.

nodos.label: Antiplatelet agents
nodos.desc: Drugs that prevent platelets from sticking together and forming clots in blood vessels.

nodos.label: Anticoagulants
nodos.desc: Medications that prevent existing clots from growing larger and causing damage.

nodos.label: Nitrates
nodos.desc: Medications that dilate blood vessels, increasing blood flow to the heart and reducing its workload.

nodos.label: Beta blockers
nodos.desc: Drugs that block adrenaline effects, slowing heart rate and lowering blood pressure to reduce heart oxygen demand.

nodos.label: ACE inhibitors
nodos.desc: Medications that widen blood vessels and reduce resistance, easing the heart's pumping effort, especially in heart failure post-MI.

nodos.label: Statins
nodos.desc: Cholesterol-lowering drugs that stabilize arterial plaques to reduce future cardiac events.

nodos.label: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI)
nodos.desc: Surgical procedure involving catheter insertion to open blocked arteries and place stents to maintain blood flow.

nodos.label: Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG)
nodos.desc: Surgical procedure that uses a healthy blood vessel to bypass blocked coronary arteries.

nodos.label: Arteriosclerosis
nodos.desc: Proceso generalizado de endurecimiento y pérdida de elasticidad de las paredes de arterias medianas y grandes, causado por daño en las células endoteliales, inflamación y depósito de lipidos, con acumulación de calcio y formación de placas, que reducen el flujo sanguíneo.

nodos.label: Arteriolosclerosis
nodos.desc: Proceso de endurecimiento y estrechamiento de arteriolas, que puede ocurrir como parte de la arteriosclerosis generalizada, afectando el microcircuito vascular y reduciendo el flujo sanguíneo en tejidos periféricos.

nodos.label: Placa
nodos.desc: Formación de tejido fibroso y lipídico en las paredes de las arterias, que se acumula con el tiempo y provoca estrechamiento del lumen vascular, reduciendo el flujo sanguíneo y aumentando el riesgo de trombosis.

nodos.label: Lumen
nodos.desc: Espacio central dentro de una arteria o vaso sanguíneo que permite el paso del flujo sanguíneo; su estrechamiento (stenosis) puede provocar disminución del flujo sanguíneo y complicaciones cardiovasculares.

nodos.label: Stenosis
nodos.desc: Reducción anatómica del diámetro de un vaso sanguíneo, que limita el flujo sanguíneo y puede provocar isquemia tisular o eventos cardiovasculares como infarto o accidente cerebrovascular.

nodos.label: Endotelio
nodos.desc: Capa celular que recubre la superficie interna de los vasos sanguíneos; su daño es un factor inicial en el desarrollo de arteriosclerosis y aterosclerosis, desencadenando inflamación y acumulación de lipidos.

nodos.label: Trombosis
nodos.desc: Formación de coágulos sanguíneos (trombos) dentro de un vaso sanguíneo, que pueden desprenderses y causar obstrucción en otras arterias, llevando a eventos como infarto o accidente cerebrovascular.

nodos.label: Riesgo
nodos.desc: Factor que aumenta la probabilidad de que ocurra una enfermedad, como la arteriosclerosis, y que puede ser influenciado por edad, estilo de vida, condiciones médicas o genética.

nodos.label: Placa
nodos.desc: Acumulación de colesterol, depósitos grasos, calcio y otras sustancias en las paredes de las arteriolas, que estrecha el lumen y reduce el flujo sanguíneo.

nodos.label: Factores de riesgo
nodos.desc: Elementos como edad, historia familiar, tabaquismo, hipertensión, diabetes y obesidad que aumentan la probabilidad de desarrollar arteriolosclerosis o aterosclerosis.

nodos.label: Flujo sanguíneo
nodos.desc: Movimiento de sangre a través de los vasos sanguíneos, que se ve reducido por el estrechamiento causado por placa en arteriolas o arterias.

nodos.label: Cerebral Blood Flow (CBF)
nodos.desc: El flujo sanguíneo al cerebro, esencial para funciones cognitivas como la memoria y el funcionamiento general de la salud cerebral.

nodos.label: Circle of Willis
nodos.desc: Una estructura vascular en la base del cerebro que garantiza una perfusión óptima del cerebro, formada por arterias internas carótidas, vertebrales, y otras ramas que se conectan en un círculo.

nodos.label: Internal Carotid Artery (ICA)
nodos.desc: Una arteria parietal que se origina en la bifurcación de la arteria común carótida, sube por el cuello y entra en la cabeza, donde se divide en ramas como la arteria ophthalmica y la arteria posterior comunicante.

nodos.label: Vertebral Artery
nodos.desc: Una arteria que proviene de las columnas vertebrales y contribuye al suministro sanguíneo al cerebro, integrándose en el círculo de Willis.

nodos.label: Molecular mediators of vascular injury and repair
nodos.desc: Mecanismos moleculares involucrados en el daño y la reparación vascular, que pueden ser objetivos terapéuticos para prevenir o mitigar enfermedades vasculares como la arteriolosclerosis.

nodos.label: Hemodynamic Forces
nodos.desc: Fuerzas hidrodinámicas que actúan sobre las arteriolas y vasos sanguíneos, influyendo en la presión y el flujo sanguíneo, y que interactúan con factores genéticos y ambientales en el desarrollo de enfermedades vasculares.

nodos.label: Genetic Predisposition
nodos.desc: Tendencia inherente a desarrollar enfermedades vasculares, influenciada por factores genéticos que interactúan con el entorno y las condiciones fisiológicas.

nodos.label: Environmental Exposures
nodos.desc: Factores ambientales, como el estrés, la contaminación o el hábito de fumar, que pueden contribuir al desarrollo de enfermedades vasculares como la arteriolosclerosis.

nodos.label: Regional Cerebral Blood Flow
nodos.desc: The flow of blood to specific regions of the brain, which decreases upon vascular occlusion and is a key factor in ischemic injury progression.

nodos.label: Anaerobic Respiration
nodos.desc: A metabolic process that occurs when oxygen is insufficient, leading to energy production without oxygen and resulting in lactic acid accumulation.

nodos.label: Intracellular Acidosis
nodos.desc: A decrease in pH within cells due to accumulation of lactic acid, disrupting cellular functions and contributing to neuronal damage.

nodos.label: Depletion of High-Energy Phosphate Reserves
nodos.desc: Loss of ATP and other high-energy molecules essential for cellular function, leading to failure of energy-dependent processes.

nodos.label: Ion Pump Failure
nodos.desc: Loss of function of pumps like Na+/K+-ATPase, leading to membrane depolarization and disruption of ion homeostasis.

nodos.label: Excitotoxicity via Glutamate
nodos.desc: Excessive release of glutamate, an excitatory neurotransmitter, leading to overstimulation of neurons and subsequent cell death.

nodos.label: Ischemic Core
nodos.desc: The central region of brain tissue that suffers irreversible damage due to complete loss of blood flow and metabolic activity.

nodos.label: Penumbra
nodos.desc: A peripheral zone surrounding the ischemic core with reduced perfusion but still viable cells, capable of recovery if blood flow is restored.

nodos.label: Collateral Vessels
nodos.desc: Alternative blood vessels that may maintain partial perfusion in the penumbra, supporting residual metabolic activity.

nodos.label: Reperfusion
nodos.desc: Restoration of blood flow to ischemic tissue, which can potentially rescue penumbral cells but may also trigger reperfusion injury.

nodos.label: Ion homeostasis
nodos.desc: The maintenance of balanced ion concentrations (e.g., sodium, potassium, calcium, chloride) across the plasma membrane through active transport mechanisms.

nodos.label: Sodium influx
nodos.desc: Increased entry of sodium ions into the cell due to failure of ion pumps during ATP depletion, disrupting cellular osmotic balance.

nodos.label: Calcium influx
nodos.desc: Accumulation of calcium ions inside the cell, which triggers various cellular pathways leading to damage and death.

nodos.label: Osmotic water influx
nodos.desc: Movement of water into the cell following ion imbalance, causing cellular swelling and potentially leading to lysis.

nodos.label: Proteases
nodos.desc: Enzymes that degrade proteins, activated during ATP depletion, contributing to structural breakdown of the cell membrane.

nodos.label: Phospholipases
nodos.desc: Enzymes that hydrolyze phospholipids in cell membranes, leading to membrane disruption and release of intracellular contents.

nodos.label: Free radicals
nodos.desc: Highly reactive molecules formed during lipid peroxidation, causing oxidative stress and damage to cellular components like DNA, proteins, and lipids.

nodos.label: NMDA receptors
nodos.desc: Ion channels on neuronal membranes that, when overactivated, allow excessive calcium entry, leading to neuronal death.

nodos.label: Neutrophils
nodos.desc: Immune cells recruited to injury sites that contribute to inflammation and tissue damage after ischemia.

nodos.label: Reversible ischemia
nodos.desc: A state in which cells remain viable despite ischemia, allowing potential recovery upon restoration of blood flow.

nodos.label: Neurological outcomes
nodos.desc: Functional impairments that persist after ischemic injury due to irreversible damage to neural tissue.

nodos.label: Ischemic cascade
nodos.desc: A sequence of biochemical and cellular events triggered by ischemia, leading to progressive tissue damage and cell death.

nodos.label: Thrombolytic Therapy
nodos.desc: Treatment using agents like alteplase (tPA) to dissolve blood clots in ischemic stroke, administered intravenously within a time window to restore cerebral circulation and reduce disability.

nodos.label: Endovascular Interventions
nodos.desc: Mechanical procedures involving catheters to remove or fragment clots in brain arteries, particularly effective within 6–24 hours of symptom onset for large vessel occlusions.

nodos.label: Blood Pressure Control
nodos.desc: Monitoring and managing elevated blood pressure to reduce edema and hemorrhage transformation risk in acute stroke patients.

nodos.label: Antithrombotic Medications
nodos.desc: Use of anticoagulants and antiplatelet agents to prevent recurrent strokes and manage conditions like atrial fibrillation, with careful dosing due to bleeding risks.

nodos.label: Surgical Interventions
nodos.desc: Surgical procedures to evacuate hematomas or repair ruptured aneurysms in hemorrhagic stroke cases, aiming to relieve mass effect and prevent secondary brain injury.

nodos.label: Tissue Plasminogen Activator
nodos.desc: Un agente trombolítico administrado intravenosamente dentro de 4.5 horas de inicio de síntomas para disolver coágulos en vasos cerebrales, convirtiendo plasminógeno en plasmina que degrada el fibrina.

nodos.label: Antihypertensive Agents
nodos.desc: Medicamentos que controlan la presión arterial elevada en pacientes con ictus, reduciendo el riesgo de hemorragia secundaria y edema, con acciones rápidas y de corta duración.

nodos.label: Blood Glucose Control
nodos.desc: Regulación estricta de la glucosa en sangre para prevenir daño neurológico por hiperglucemia, mediante infusión de insulina y mediciones frecuentes.

nodos.label: Neuroprotective Therapies
nodos.desc: Terapias diseñadas para salvar neuronas en riesgo durante el ictus isquémico, aunque aún no se ha validado ninguna con efectividad clínica definitiva.

nodos.label: Sistólica
nodos.desc: Presión sanguínea máxima durante la contracción del corazón, medida cuando se detectan los primeros sonidos de Korotkoff en la medición de presión.

nodos.label: Diastólica
nodos.desc: Presión sanguínea mínima entre las contracciones cardíacas, determinada por la desaparición de los sonidos de Korotkin en la medición de presión.

nodos.label: Relajación vascular
nodos.desc: Proceso que ocurre entre las contracciones cardíacas, afectando la resistencia vascular y la presión sanguínea en el sistema circulatorio.

nodos.label: Sphygmomanometría
nodos.desc: Método no invasivo para medir la presión sanguínea mediante un globo inflable alrededor del brazo, detectando sonidos turbulentes (Korotkoff).

nodos.label: Sonidos de Korotkoff
nodos.desc: Sonidos auditivos producidos por el flujo turbulento en una arteria parcialmente obstruida, utilizados para identificar los valores sistólico y diastólico de la presión sanguínea.

nodos.label: Rangos de presión sanguínea
nodos.desc: Clasificación de la presión sanguínea en categorías: normal (<120/<80), prehipertensión (120-139/<80-89), hipertensión estadio I (140-159/90-99), hipertensión estadio II (>160/>100).

nodos.label: Rigidez arterial
nodos.desc: Aumento de la resistencia en las arterias con la edad, que contribuye a una elevación del valor sistólico y mayor riesgo de enfermedades cardiovasculares.

nodos.label: Compliance vascular
nodos.desc: Capacidad de las arterias para estirarse y almacenar energía, que disminuye con la edad y afecta la presión diastólica en jóvenes.

nodos.label: Parámetros hemodinámicos
nodos.desc: Variables que describen el flujo sanguíneo y la presión dentro del sistema circulatorio, incluyendo presión sistólica y diastólica, y su relación con la función vascular.

nodos.label: Adrenal Gland Adenoma
nodos.desc: A rare tumor of the adrenal gland that secretes ectopic aldosterone, leading to sodium retention and potassium wasting.

nodos.label: Ectopic Aldosterone Secretion
nodos.desc: The abnormal release of aldosterone from adrenal adenomas, which promotes sodium reclamation and potassium loss in urine.

nodos.label: Expansion of Extracellular Compartment
nodos.desc: An increase in extracellular fluid volume due to sodium retention, contributing to elevated blood pressure.

nodos.label: Pheochromocytoma
nodos.desc: A tumor of chromaffin cells in the adrenal medulla that secretes excessive norepinephrine and epinephrine, causing vasoconstriction, tachycardia, and sweating.

nodos.label: Norepinephrine Release
nodos.desc: The secretion of norepinephrine by pheochromocytoma, triggering vasoconstriction and sympathetic overactivity.

nodos.label: Cushing's Syndrome
nodos.desc: A condition caused by excessive cortisol, resulting from pituitary or adrenal tumors, leading to catabolism of muscle and bone and increased visceral fat.

nodos.label: Pathologic Hypercorticism
nodos.desc: Abnormally high levels of cortisol that induce tissue catabolism and fat redistribution, contributing to hypertension.

nodos.label: Sympathoexcitatory Outflow
nodos.desc: Increased sympathetic nervous system activity that elevates vascular resistance and heart rate, contributing to hypertension.

nodos.label: Baroreceptor Feedback Control
nodos.desc: A regulatory mechanism in the brainstem that monitors blood pressure and adjusts sympathetic activity to maintain homeostasis.

nodos.label: Descending Inhibitory Tracts
nodos.desc: Neural pathways in the spinal cord that suppress alpha-adrenergic signaling and regulate sympathetic tone.

nodos.label: Paraganglioma
nodos.desc: A tumor that secretes excessive catecholamines, mimicking the symptoms of pheochromocytoma and causing hypertension.

nodos.label: Sleep Apnea Syndrome
nodos.desc: A condition involving recurrent breathing pauses during sleep, leading to hypoxia and reflexive sympathetic activation, causing oscillating blood pressure.

nodos.label: Chemoreflex
nodos.desc: A reflex response to hypoxia that activates sympathetic nerves, increasing blood pressure during sleep apnea episodes.

nodos.label: Oral Contraceptives
nodos.desc: Pharmaceuticals containing estrogen and progestin that can elevate blood pressure due to their hormonal effects.

nodos.label: Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs)
nodos.desc: Drugs that inhibit prostacyclin synthesis, leading to vasoconstriction and increased blood pressure.

nodos.label: Corticosteroids
nodos.desc: Medications that enhance mineralocorticoid action, promoting sodium retention and hypertension.

nodos.label: Appetite Suppressants
nodos.desc: Drugs that affect monoaminergic neurotransmission and may elevate blood pressure.

nodos.label: Immunomodulators
nodos.desc: Therapeutic agents used in autoimmune diseases that can induce hypertension as a side effect.

nodos.label: Secondary Hypertension
nodos.desc: A type of hypertension caused by an underlying medical condition, such as kidney disease or hormonal imbalances, rather than being primary or idiopathic.

nodos.label: Chronic Kidney Disease
nodos.desc: A progressive loss of kidney function over time, which can disrupt blood pressure regulation due to impaired filtration and hormonal imbalances.

nodos.label: Glomerulonephritis
nodos.desc: An inflammation of the glomeruli in the kidneys, impairing their ability to filter blood and contributing to secondary hypertension.

nodos.label: Renal Artery Stenosis
nodos.desc: A narrowing of the renal artery that reduces blood flow to the kidneys, leading to activation of the renin-angiotensin system and elevated blood pressure.

nodos.label: Hyperthyroidism
nodos.desc: A condition where the thyroid gland produces excessive thyroid hormones, which can increase metabolic rate and elevate blood pressure.

nodos.label: Cushing's Syndrome
nodos.desc: A disorder caused by prolonged exposure to high levels of cortisol, which can lead to increased blood pressure and fluid retention.

nodos.label: Diabetes
nodos.desc: A metabolic disorder characterized by high blood glucose levels, which can damage small blood vessels and contribute to hypertension.

nodos.label: CPAP Therapy
nodos.desc: A treatment for sleep apnea that delivers a continuous flow of air to keep airways open, thereby improving oxygen levels and reducing blood pressure.

nodos.label: Gestational Hypertension
nodos.desc: A form of secondary hypertension occurring after the 20th week of pregnancy, associated with hormonal and placental changes.

nodos.label: Pre-Eclampsia
nodos.desc: A serious pregnancy complication characterized by high blood pressure and protein in the urine, which can progress to seizures, stroke, or death if untreated.

nodos.label: Medications
nodos.desc: Drugs that can elevate blood pressure as a side effect, such as decongestants, NSAIDs, oral contraceptives, corticosteroids, and certain antidepressants.

nodos.label: Nitric Oxide Signaling
nodos.desc: A biological mechanism that regulates vascular tone and blood flow; deficiency is linked to impaired vasoreactivity in hypertension.

nodos.label: Pulse Wave Velocity
nodos.desc: A measure of how fast pressure waves travel through the arterial system; increased velocity is associated with reduced vessel elasticity and hypertension.

nodos.label: Arterial Buffering
nodos.desc: The capacity of arteries to absorb and dampen pulsatile pressure changes; impaired by reduced vascular compliance.

nodos.label: Ventriculoarterial Coupling
nodos.desc: The dynamic relationship between ventricular pressure and arterial resistance; impaired by vascular stiffness and contributes to increased cardiac workload.

nodos.label: Vessel Wall Thickening
nodos.desc: A structural change in blood vessels caused by chronic hypertension, resulting from proliferation of smooth muscle cells and narrowing of the vessel lumen.

nodos.label: Lumen Narrowing
nodos.desc: Reduction in the inner diameter of blood vessels, which increases resistance to blood flow and contributes to elevated blood pressure.

nodos.label: Target Organ Damage
nodos.desc: Damage to vital organs such as the brain and kidneys caused by amplified pressure waves and sustained high blood pressure.

nodos.label: Atherosclerotic Plaques
nodos.desc: Fatty, fibrous deposits that form within the walls of arteries, leading to luminal narrowing and reduced blood flow.

nodos.label: Coronary Perfusion
nodos.desc: The process by which blood flows through the coronary arteries to supply oxygen and nutrients to the myocardium.

nodos.label: Myocardial Infarction
nodos.desc: The death of heart muscle tissue due to prolonged ischemia, typically caused by occlusion of coronary arteries.

nodos.label: Valvular Dysfunction
nodos.desc: Impaired function of heart valves, such as mitral and aortic valves, leading to regurgitation and inefficient blood flow.

nodos.label: Regurgitation
nodos.desc: The backflow of blood into a chamber from which it was ejected, resulting from improper valve closure.

nodos.label: Left Ventricular Geometry
nodos.desc: The three-dimensional shape and structure of the left ventricle, which can be altered by chronic hypertension, affecting cardiac efficiency.

nodos.label: Ion Channel Dynamics
nodos.desc: The regulation of ion movement across cardiac cell membranes, influencing electrical activity and rhythm of the heart.

nodos.label: Gap Junction Architecture
nodos.desc: The structural arrangement of intercellular connections that allow electrical coupling between cardiac myocytes, essential for coordinated contraction.

nodos.label: Malignant Arrhythmias
nodos.desc: Severe, life-threatening heart rhythms that can lead to sudden cardiac arrest and death.

nodos.label: Hypertensive Urgency
nodos.desc: A condition characterized by elevated blood pressure without acute symptoms, posing a risk of organ dysfunction over time.

nodos.label: Hypertensive Emergency
nodos.desc: A severe condition involving rapid and extreme elevation of blood pressure resulting in acute organ damage.

nodos.label: Target Organs
nodos.desc: Organs vulnerable to damage from high blood pressure, including the brain, heart, kidneys, and lungs.

nodos.label: Symptoms
nodos.desc: Clinical manifestations such as headaches, dizziness, blurred vision, chest pain, or seizures that may indicate organ involvement.

nodos.label: Diagnostic Tools
nodos.desc: Medical tests like blood pressure monitoring, blood tests, urinalysis, ECG, chest X-ray, and CT scan used to assess organ function and hypertension causes.

nodos.label: Treatment
nodos.desc: Therapeutic interventions such as oral medications (e.g., calcium channel blockers, ACE inhibitors, beta blockers, diuretics) to gradually reduce blood pressure.

nodos.label: Organ Dysfunction
nodos.desc: Impaired function of vital organs due to prolonged or severe hypertension, potentially leading to irreversible damage.

nodos.label: Time Sensitivity
nodos.desc: The critical need for rapid intervention in hypertensive emergencies to prevent irreversible organ damage within minutes to hours.

nodos.label: Diuretics
nodos.desc: Medications that promote the excretion of water and salt by the kidneys, reducing blood volume and thus lowering blood pressure.

nodos.label: ARBs
nodos.desc: Drugs that block the action of angiotensin on blood vessel receptors, leading to vasodilation and reduced blood pressure.

nodos.label: Calcium Channel Blockers
nodos.desc: Medications that prevent calcium from entering smooth muscle cells in blood vessel walls, causing vasodilation.

nodos.label: Renin Inhibitors
nodos.desc: Drugs that inhibit the production of renin, an enzyme that initiates a cascade leading to increased blood pressure.

nodos.label: Multiple Medications
nodos.desc: The use of more than one class of antihypertensive drugs to achieve optimal blood pressure control in some patients.

nodos.label: Drug Interactions
nodos.desc: Pharmacological effects where the presence of one medication alters the action, side effects, or metabolism of another.

nodos.label: Relaxation Techniques
nodos.desc: Non-pharmacological methods such as progressive muscle relaxation, guided imagery, and biofeedback that reduce stress and may lower blood pressure.

nodos.label: Acupuncture
nodos.desc: A traditional therapy involving the insertion of fine needles into specific points on the body, with some evidence suggesting a mild effect on blood pressure.

nodos.label: Herbal Remedies
nodos.desc: Natural substances like hawthorn and garlic that have shown modest blood pressure-lowering effects, but require medical supervision.

nodos.label: Systolic Function
nodos.desc: Refers to the heart's ability to contract and eject blood during systole, measured by ejection fraction; reduced systolic function indicates impaired pumping capacity.

nodos.label: Ejection Fraction
nodos.desc: A percentage that quantifies the volume of blood pumped out of the left ventricle during systole relative to the end-diastolic volume; a key metric in diagnosing systolic heart failure.

nodos.label: Echocardiogram
nodos.desc: A non-invasive imaging technique using ultrasound to assess heart structure, motion, and function, including systolic and diastolic performance.

nodos.label: Radionuclide Imaging
nodos.desc: A diagnostic method involving radioactive tracers to evaluate organ perfusion and detect areas of reduced blood flow in the heart.

nodos.label: Cardiac MRI
nodos.desc: A high-resolution imaging technique that provides detailed visualization of heart size, shape, and motion, enabling accurate assessment of cardiac function.

nodos.label: CT Angiography
nodos.desc: A non-invasive imaging modality that evaluates coronary artery health by detecting blockages or vessel narrowing using contrast agents.

nodos.label: Serum Proteins
nodos.desc: Proteins released into the bloodstream during myocardial injury, such as troponins, used as biomarkers to confirm heart damage and assess prognosis.

nodos.label: Aldosterone Antagonists
nodos.desc: Medications that block aldosterone receptors, reducing fluid retention and blood pressure, thus alleviating symptoms of heart failure.

nodos.label: Anticoagulants
nodos.desc: Drugs that prevent blood clot formation, reducing the risk of thromboembolic events such as stroke in patients with heart failure.

nodos.label: Digitalis Glycosides
nodos.desc: Compounds that enhance myocardial contractility, improving cardiac output in cases of systolic heart failure.

nodos.label: Surgical Intervention
nodos.desc: Procedures such as implantable devices, coronary revascularization, valve repair/replacement, or heart transplantation used in severe, refractory heart failure cases.

nodos.label: Heart Failure Pathophysiology
nodos.desc: The underlying biological mechanisms of heart failure, including impaired cardiac contractility, reduced blood flow, and fluid accumulation, leading to clinical symptoms.

nodos.label: Diagnostic Techniques
nodos.desc: Methods used to identify heart failure, including imaging modalities and biomarker analysis, to confirm diagnosis and assess severity.

nodos.label: Therapeutic Approach
nodos.desc: A comprehensive strategy combining pharmacological and surgical interventions to manage symptoms, slow progression, and improve quality of life in heart failure patients.

nodos.label: Myocyte Hypertrophy
nodos.desc: Increase in cardiomyocyte size due to elevated afterload, leading to thickened ventricular walls and reduced chamber expansion during diastole.

nodos.label: Interstitial Fibrosis
nodos.desc: Excessive collagen deposition between cardiomyocytes that disrupts cell-to-cell communication and impairs force transmission, reducing diastolic function.

nodos.label: Cardiac Remodeling
nodos.desc: Maladaptive structural and geometric changes in the heart due to injury or stress, leading to impaired diastolic performance.

nodos.label: Calcium Homeostasis
nodos.desc: Dysregulation of intracellular calcium levels, including enhanced SR Ca²⁺ release and elevated cytosolic Ca²⁺, which disrupts relaxation and contractile function.

nodos.label: Bioenergetics
nodos.desc: Impaired ATP production due to mitochondrial dysfunction and shift toward glycolysis, reducing energy efficiency in cardiac muscle.

nodos.label: Neurohormonal Activation
nodos.desc: Persistent stimulation of neurohumoral systems that modulate cardiac function, contributing to diastolic dysfunction through sustained signaling pathways.

nodos.label: Dyspnea
nodos.desc: The sensation of shortness of breath, caused by fluid accumulation in the alveoli due to impaired left ventricular function and reduced pulmonary venous drainage.

nodos.label: Orthopnea
nodos.desc: Difficulty breathing when lying flat, resulting from gravitational redistribution of fluid into the lungs during supine positioning.

nodos.label: Paroxysmal Nocturnal Dyspnea
nodos.desc: Sudden episodes of severe shortness of breath during sleep, triggered by fluid accumulation in the lungs due to impaired left ventricular pumping.

nodos.label: Jugular Venous Distention
nodos.desc: Visible distension of the jugular veins in the neck, indicating elevated central venous pressure due to impaired cardiac function.

nodos.label: Brain Natriuretic Peptide (BNP)
nodos.desc: A hormone released by the heart in response to increased pressure and volume, used as a biomarker for heart failure severity.

nodos.label: Pulmonary Congestion
nodos.desc: Accumulation of fluid in the lungs' air sacs, a consequence of left-sided heart failure and impaired venous return to the lungs.

nodos.label: Compensatory Mechanisms
nodos.desc: Physiological adjustments such as increased heart rate and vasoconstriction that initially attempt to maintain adequate perfusion despite reduced cardiac output.

nodos.label: Decompensation
nodos.desc: The point at which the heart's compensatory mechanisms fail, leading to clinical manifestations of advanced heart failure.

nodos.label: Chamber Sizes
nodos.desc: Dimensions of the heart chambers, evaluated in echocardiography to assess structural abnormalities and cardiac function.

nodos.label: Wall Thickness
nodos.desc: The thickness of the heart muscle walls, used to evaluate myocardial hypertrophy or other structural changes.

nodos.label: Valve Integrity
nodos.desc: Assessment of the structure and function of heart valves to detect regurgitation, stenosis, or other abnormalities.

nodos.label: Diastolic Filling Patterns
nodos.desc: Patterns of how the heart fills during diastole, used to identify diastolic dysfunction.

nodos.label: Peak VO2
nodos.desc: The maximum oxygen consumption during exercise; decreased peak VO2 reflects functional limitation in heart failure and correlates with prognosis.

nodos.label: Myocardial Perfusion
nodos.desc: The blood flow to the heart muscle, assessed via nuclear imaging to detect ischemic or infarcted regions.

nodos.label: Left Ventricular Volumes
nodos.desc: Quantitative measurements of the volume of blood in the left ventricle at end-diastole and end-systole, used to calculate EF and assess cardiac function.

nodos.label: Coronary Artery Disease
nodos.desc: Atherosclerotic narrowing of coronary arteries, detected via imaging techniques such as SPECT, PET, or coronary angiography.

nodos.label: Aerobic Capacity
nodos.desc: The ability of the body to utilize oxygen during physical activity; decreased aerobic capacity is a hallmark of heart failure and reflects overall functional limitation.

nodos.label: Exercise Stress Testing
nodos.desc: A diagnostic method that evaluates cardiac function under physical stress by monitoring ECG and vital signs to detect ischemia or reduced tolerance.

nodos.label: Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPX)
nodos.desc: An integrated assessment of cardiovascular, respiratory, and muscular responses during exercise, using respiratory gas exchange measurements.

nodos.label: Systolic Dysfunction
nodos.desc: A condition where the heart's ventricles fail to contract effectively, leading to reduced pumping capacity and impaired blood circulation.

nodos.label: QRS Complex
nodos.desc: An electrical signal on an electrocardiogram (ECG) that represents ventricular depolarization; a wide QRS complex indicates dyssynchrony in ventricular contraction.

nodos.label: Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillator (ICD)
nodos.desc: An electronic device implanted in the body to monitor heart rhythm and deliver shocks to correct life-threatening arrhythmias.

nodos.label: Biventricular Pacing
nodos.desc: A technique that synchronizes the contraction of both ventricles using specialized pacemakers to improve cardiac efficiency in heart failure patients.

nodos.label: Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy (CRT)
nodos.desc: A treatment that uses biventricular pacing to improve heart function in patients with dyssynchronous ventricular contractions and reduced ejection fraction.

nodos.label: Transvenous Lead Insertion
nodos.desc: A medical procedure where leads are inserted through veins into the heart chambers to deliver electrical stimulation for pacemakers or defibrillators.

nodos.label: Functional Capacity
nodos.desc: The ability of a patient to perform daily activities; improved functional capacity indicates better quality of life and cardiac performance.

nodos.label: Mortality Rate
nodos.desc: The proportion of individuals who die within a specified time period; reduced mortality rate indicates improved outcomes in heart failure treatment.

nodos.label: Aortic Dissection
nodos.desc: A tear in the wall of the aorta, which can propagate and lead to life-threatening complications such as rupture, stroke, or cardiac arrest.

nodos.label: Endovascular Repair
nodos.desc: A minimally invasive procedure involving the insertion of a stent graft via catheter to seal the tear in the aorta and prevent further propagation.

nodos.label: Open Surgical Repair
nodos.desc: A traditional surgical procedure used for complex aortic dissections, particularly those involving the ascending aorta, where endovascular repair is not feasible.

nodos.label: Shear Forces
nodos.desc: Mechanical forces exerted on the aortic wall due to blood flow; increased shear forces can exacerbate dissection and must be managed through medical treatment.

nodos.label: Treatment Factors
nodos.desc: Variables influencing treatment choice, including location and extent of tear, presence of complications, and patient's overall health status.

nodos.label: Medical Management
nodos.desc: Initial treatment approach for uncomplicated type B aortic dissections, focusing on pain relief and blood pressure control to stabilize the condition.

nodos.label: Complications
nodos.desc: Potential adverse outcomes of aortic dissection, such as organ malperfusion, rupture, stroke, or cardiac arrest, which necessitate prompt intervention.

nodos.label: Viral Infections
nodos.desc: Infectious agents such as adenoviruses, enteroviruses, and parvovirus B19 are common causes of myocarditis and pericarditis.

nodos.label: Bacterial Pathogens
nodos.desc: Pathogens like Streptococcus pyogenes or Staphylococcus aureus can lead to myocarditis or pericarditis, though less commonly.

nodos.label: Inflammatory Markers
nodos.desc: Markers such as C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) indicate inflammation in myocarditis and pericarditis.

nodos.label: Cardiac Enzymes
nodos.desc: Troponin I or T levels may be elevated due to myocyte necrosis in both myocarditis and pericarditis.

nodos.label: ECG Changes
nodos.desc: Diffuse ST segment elevation is characteristic of acute pericarditis, while nonspecific ST-T wave abnormalities are more typical of myocarditis.

nodos.label: Cardiovascular MRI
nodos.desc: An imaging modality providing detailed information on cardiac structure and function, including pericardial effusions.

nodos.label: Pericardial Effusion
nodos.desc: Excess fluid accumulation in the pericardial space, common in pericarditis but rare in myocarditis.

nodos.label: Exercise Intolerance
nodos.desc: Reduced ability to perform physical activity, a hallmark of myocarditis due to cardiac dysfunction.

nodos.label: Chest Pain
nodos.desc: Sharp, pleuritic chest pain in pericarditis, exacerbated by deep inspiration or lying flat.

nodos.label: Anti-Inflammatory Drugs
nodos.desc: NSAIDs or corticosteroids are used as first-line therapy for pericarditis.

nodos.label: Immunomodulatory Agents
nodos.desc: Used in refractory cases of myocarditis or pericarditis to modulate the immune response.

nodos.label: Differential Diagnosis
nodos.desc: Challenging due to overlapping symptoms such as fever, fatigue, shortness of breath, palpitations, and chest pain.

nodos.label: Biatrial Enlargement
nodos.desc: An enlargement of both atria, observed in RCM, reflecting diastolic dysfunction and increased filling pressures.

nodos.label: Mitral Inflow Pattern
nodos.desc: A restrictive mitral inflow pattern with rapid deceleration time is a key Doppler finding in RCM.

nodos.label: Early Diastolic Transmitral Flow Velocity (E)
nodos.desc: Velocity of blood flow during early diastole, used in Doppler assessment to evaluate diastolic function.

nodos.label: Late Diastolic Transmitral Flow Velocity (A)
nodos.desc: Velocity of blood flow during late diastole, used in conjunction with E to assess diastolic function.

nodos.label: E/A Ratio
nodos.desc: Ratio of early to late diastolic transmitral flow velocities; reduced in restrictive diastolic dysfunction, commonly seen in RCM.

nodos.label: Tissue Doppler Velocities
nodos.desc: Measurements of myocardial tissue movement, used to assess diastolic function and detect abnormalities in myocardial deformation.

nodos.label: Fibrosis
nodos.desc: Extracellular matrix deposition in the myocardium, detected via late gadolinium enhancement and T1 mapping in RCM.

nodos.label: Native T1 Mapping
nodos.desc: Quantitative MRI technique that measures T1 relaxation times to detect diffuse fibrosis before visible on conventional imaging.

nodos.label: Diastolic Dysfunction
nodos.desc: Impaired relaxation and filling of the heart chambers, central to the pathophysiology of RCM.

nodos.label: Congestive Heart Failure
nodos.desc: A clinical state resulting from impaired cardiac function, managed in RCM through symptom relief and therapeutic interventions.

nodos.label: Digoxin
nodos.desc: A cardiac glycoside used to improve contractility and manage symptoms of heart failure in RCM.

nodos.label: Multimodality Imaging
nodos.desc: Integration of echocardiography, CMR, and other imaging techniques to improve diagnostic accuracy in RCM.

nodos.label: Calcium ion (Ca²⁺)
nodos.desc: A divalent cation involved in intracellular signaling, particularly in the regulation of excitation-contraction coupling in cardiomyocytes by being sequestered within the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR).

nodos.label: Sinus node (SA node)
nodos.desc: The primary pacemaker region of the heart that generates spontaneous diastolic depolarizations via funny current (If) and HCN channels, initiating the heartbeat.

nodos.label: His-Purkinje network
nodos.desc: An extensive conduction system in the ventricles that rapidly transmits electrical impulses, enabling synchronized ventricular contraction and efficient cardiac output.

nodos.label: Electrical activation
nodos.desc: The process by which electrical signals propagate through myocardial tissue, leading to coordinated contraction of cardiac muscle cells.

nodos.label: Diastolic depolarization
nodos.desc: A slow depolarization of the cell membrane during diastole, driven by ion channels such as funny current (If) and HCN channels, which initiates action potential generation in pacemaker cells.

nodos.label: Shortness of breath
nodos.desc: Dyspnea related to increased oxygen demand and reduced diastolic filling time.

nodos.label: Lightheadedness or presyncope
nodos.desc: Decreased cerebral perfusion due to decreased stroke volume and increased heart rate.

nodos.label: Syncope
nodos.desc: Transient loss of consciousness resulting from profound hypotension and global cerebral hypoperfusion.

nodos.label: Age
nodos.desc: Elderly patients tend to tolerate tachyarrhythmias poorly compared to younger individuals.

nodos.label: Comorbid conditions
nodos.desc: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, congestive heart failure, valvular heart disease, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperthyroidism may exacerbate symptoms.

nodos.label: Electrocardiography (ECG)
nodos.desc: Twelve-lead resting ECG provides information on rhythm disturbances, chamber enlargement, previous infarction, pre-excitation, and axis deviation. Ambulatory monitoring captures intermittent episodes.

nodos.label: Laboratory testing
nodos.desc: Thyroid function studies identify hyperthyroid states; serum electrolyte levels are assessed for imbalances that can precipitate arrhythmias.

nodos.label: Imaging modalities
nodos.desc: CT or MRI may reveal alternative causes of symptoms such as pulmonary embolism or masses compressing the heart.

nodos.label: Vagal maneuvers
nodos.desc: Non-pharmacologic techniques to induce vagal stimulation and terminate SVT.

nodos.label: Adenosine
nodos.desc: A pharmacologic agent used to terminate SVT by transiently blocking conduction in the AV node.

nodos.label: Procainamide
nodos.desc: Antiarrhythmic drug used to treat SVT by stabilizing cardiac conduction.

nodos.label: Reentrant Circuit
nodos.desc: A circular pathway of electrical activation that sustains arrhythmia by repeatedly activating cardiac tissue.

nodos.label: Atrial Depolarization
nodos.desc: The process of electrical activation of atrial myocardial cells, resulting in rapid and regular contractions in atrial fibrillation.

nodos.label: F-Waves
nodos.desc: Sawtooth waves observed on electrocardiogram, indicating rapid atrial depolarization due to macroreentrant circuits in atrial fibrillation.

nodos.label: Ventricular Response
nodos.desc: The rate at which ventricles contract, typically ranging from 100 to 150 beats per minute due to AV nodal conduction properties.

nodos.label: Heart Failure Signs
nodos.desc: Clinical manifestations such as peripheral edema and jugular venous distention that may develop in chronic atrial fibrillation.

nodos.label: Electrocardiography (ECG)
nodos.desc: A diagnostic tool that records electrical activity of the heart, used to identify F-waves and assess arrhythmia patterns.

nodos.label: AV Nodal Block
nodos.desc: Intermittent conduction failure in the atrioventricular node, leading to irregular ventricular response on ECG.

nodos.label: Treatment Goals
nodos.desc: Control of ventricular rate, restoration of sinus rhythm, prevention of recurrence, and management of complications like stroke or heart failure.

nodos.label: Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
nodos.desc: Un tipo de taquicardia supraventricular caracterizado por actividad eléctrica anormal que origina el atrio y que se propaga a través de un camino accesorio entre el atrio y el ventrículo, formando circuitos de reentrada que provocan taquicardia rápida.

nodos.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) Syndrome
nodos.desc: Condición congénita con un camino accesorio (bundle of Kent) entre el atrio y el ventrículo que permite una conducción alternativa, causando reentrada y taquicardia. Se identifica en ECG por un intervalo PR reducido y una onda delta.

nodos.label: Permanent Junctional Reciprocating Tachycardia (PJRT)
nodos.desc: Forma rara de AVRT causada por un camino accesorio de conducción lento cerca del nodo atrioventricular, que se inserta en el septo interventricular derecho. Presenta prolongación del intervalo RP en ECG y se trata con medicamentos o ablación.

nodos.label: Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
nodos.desc: Causa común de taquicardia supraventricular que ocurre por una fisiología dual del nodo atrioventricular, con dos vías distintas: una lenta y otra rápida, que permiten circuitos de reentrada cuando se producen contracciones prematuras.

nodos.label: Intervalo PR
nodos.desc: Tiempo entre la aparición de un impulso atrial y la activación del ventrículo, que se reduce en WPW debido a la conducción por un camino accesorio.

nodos.label: Onda delta
nodos.desc: Onza en el electrocardiograma que indica preexcitación ventricular por conducción a través de un camino accesorio en WPW.

nodos.label: Intervalo RP
nodos.desc: Tiempo entre la activación del ventrículo y la llegada del impulso al nodo atrioventricular, que se prolonga en PJRT debido a la conducción lenta por el camino accesorio.

nodos.label: Contracción atrial prematura
nodos.desc: Evento que desencadena la activación de un camino específico dentro del nodo atrioventricular, favoreciendo la formación de circuitos de reentrada en AVNRT.

nodos.label: Ablación por catéter
nodos.desc: Procedimiento médico que elimina el camino accesorio responsable de la taquicardia mediante la aplicación de calor o energía eléctrica en el sitio específico del corazón.

nodos.label: QT Interval
nodos.desc: Electrocardiographic measure representing the time from the start of the Q wave to the end of the T wave, indicating the duration of ventricular depolarization and repolarization.

nodos.label: Long QT Syndrome (LQTS)
nodos.desc: Genetic or acquired disorder characterized by prolonged repolarization, leading to a lengthened QT interval and increased risk of TdP.

nodos.label: Early Afterdepolarizations (EADs)
nodos.desc: Abnormal depolarizations that occur during phase 3 of the action potential, often due to calcium ion imbalance, which can trigger premature ventricular contractions.

nodos.label: Delayed Afterdepolarizations (DADs)
nodos.desc: Abnormal depolarizations resulting from excessive intracellular calcium accumulation, often due to drug toxicity or metabolic disturbances.

nodos.label: Premature Ventricular Contractions (PVCs)
nodos.desc: Extra heartbeats originating in the ventricles that can initiate or contribute to the development of TdP.

nodos.label: Tachyarrhythmia
nodos.desc: A type of cardiac arrhythmia involving rapid heart rhythms that can be life-threatening, such as TdP.

nodos.label: Ventricular Fibrillation (VF)
nodos.desc: A chaotic, uncoordinated ventricular rhythm that results in ineffective cardiac contractions and can lead to sudden cardiac death.

nodos.label: R-on-T Phenomenon
nodos.desc: A pattern on ECG where a ventricular beat occurs immediately after a T wave, increasing the risk of triggering TdP.

nodos.label: ECG Tracing
nodos.desc: Graphical representation of the heart's electrical activity over time, used to diagnose arrhythmias such as TdP.

nodos.label: Pulseless Electrical Activity (PEA)
nodos.desc: Organized electrical activity on ECG without palpable central pulses, indicating that the heart generates electrical signals but fails to produce sufficient mechanical contraction to maintain blood flow.

nodos.label: Asystole
nodos.desc: Complete absence of electrical activity on ECG, appearing as a flatline, indicating no electrical activity in the heart and no chance of recovery.

nodos.label: Electrocardiogram
nodos.desc: A graphical representation of the electrical activity of the heart, used to diagnose cardiac rhythms such as PEA and asystole.

nodos.label: Acidosis
nodos.desc: A state of increased acidity in the body fluids, which can impair cardiac function and contribute to arrhythmias and cardiac arrest.

nodos.label: Hypothermia
nodos.desc: A condition of abnormally low body temperature, which can disrupt cardiac electrical activity and lead to cardiac arrest.

nodos.label: Hyperkalemia
nodos.desc: Elevated potassium levels in the blood, which can interfere with cardiac conduction and lead to arrhythmias and cardiac arrest.

nodos.label: Hypokalemia
nodos.desc: Reduced potassium levels in the blood, which can affect cardiac muscle function and contribute to arrhythmias.

nodos.label: Drug Overdose
nodos.desc: Excessive intake of drugs that can disrupt cardiac electrical activity and lead to cardiac arrest.

nodos.label: Clinical Assessment
nodos.desc: A medical evaluation of a patient's condition, including signs such as unresponsiveness, cyanosis, and dilated pupils, to help recognize PEA and asystole.

nodos.label: Energy Dosage
nodos.desc: The amount of energy delivered during electrocardioversion, typically ranging from 50–200 joules for monophasic waves and 70–150 joules for biphasic waves, is gradually escalated until successful termination of arrhythmia.

nodos.label: Synchronization
nodos.desc: A mode that aligns the shock delivery with the R-wave peak of the ECG to minimize the risk of inducing ventricular fibrillation.

nodos.label: Preprocedural Evaluation
nodos.desc: A comprehensive assessment of the patient's medical history, laboratory data, and imaging studies to identify comorbidities and guide safe procedure planning.

nodos.label: Sterility and Disposable Equipment
nodos.desc: Use of single-use, disposable electrodes and strict adherence to sterile techniques to reduce infection risk and ensure patient safety.

nodos.label: Vital Signs Monitoring
nodos.desc: Frequent monitoring of patient vital signs to detect early warning signals of deterioration and ensure timely intervention.

nodos.label: Post-Procedural Care
nodos.desc: A tailored care plan addressing pain management, infection prevention, and early mobilization to support recovery and prevent complications.

nodos.label: Procedural Complexity
nodos.desc: The degree of technical difficulty involved in performing electrocardioversion, influenced by electrode placement, synchronization, and patient-specific factors.

nodos.label: Arrhythmogenic Stimuli
nodos.desc: Stimuli that can trigger malignant arrhythmias, particularly in patients with underlying cardiac conditions or medication use.

nodos.label: Thromboembolic Events
nodos.desc: Events involving clot formation and embolization, which can occur despite anticoagulation and necessitate prophylactic measures and close follow-up.

nodos.label: Hypoxia
nodos.desc: A condition of low oxygen levels in tissues, potentially induced by sedatives, requiring supplemental oxygen and airway support.

nodos.label: Action Potential Duration
nodos.desc: The duration of the electrical activity in a cardiac cell, which determines how long the cell remains excitable after depolarization.

nodos.label: Effective Refractory Period
nodos.desc: The period during which a cardiac cell cannot be re-excited, ensuring that the heart muscle does not contract prematurely.

nodos.label: Excitable Gap
nodos.desc: The interval between wavefronts during cardiac activity where cells are still excitable, potentially allowing for reentry and arrhythmias.

nodos.label: L-Type Calcium Channels
nodos.desc: Ion channels in cardiac cells that allow calcium influx during phase 2 of the action potential, influencing contractility and automaticity.

nodos.label: Intracellular Calcium
nodos.desc: Calcium concentration inside cardiac cells, which regulates contractility, relaxation, and automaticity of cardiac tissue.

nodos.label: Antiarrhythmic Drugs
nodos.desc: Medications that modify cardiac electrical activity to prevent or treat arrhythmias, categorized by mechanism of action.

nodos.label: Ventricular Tachyarrhythmias
nodos.desc: Rapid and irregular heartbeats originating in the ventricles, which can be life-threatening and require immediate intervention.

nodos.label: Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillators (ICDs)
nodos.desc: Devices implanted in the chest to monitor and correct dangerous heart rhythms automatically.

nodos.label: Rate Control
nodos.desc: Therapeutic strategy to manage the heart rate in atrial fibrillation or flutter, reducing symptoms and preventing complications.

nodos.label: Automaticity
nodos.desc: The intrinsic ability of cardiac cells to generate electrical impulses without external stimulation, which can lead to arrhythmias.

nodos.label: Reentry
nodos.desc: A mechanism of arrhythmia where an electrical impulse circulates in a loop within cardiac tissue, causing sustained abnormal rhythms.

nodos.label: Valvula
nodos.desc: Componente del sistema circulatorio que asegura el flujo unidireccional de sangre en el corazón y en las grandes vasos.

nodos.label: Enfermedad valvular del corazón
nodos.desc: Patología que ocurre cuando los válvulas del corazón funcionan de forma anormal, provocando flujo inverso o disfunción.

nodos.label: Cuatro válvulas del corazón
nodos.desc: Las válvulas del corazón incluyen: tricúspide (entre atrio y ventrículo derecho), pulmonar, mitral (bícuspide) y aórtica, cada una que previene el flujo inverso de sangre durante los ciclos cardíacos.

nodos.label: Mutaciones genéticas
nodos.desc: Cambios en el ADN que pueden predisponer a individuos a desarrollar enfermedades valvulares, especialmente afectando proteínas estructurales de las válvulas.

nodos.label: Tissue conectivo
nodos.desc: Estructura que proporciona resistencia y estabilidad a las válvulas; alteraciones en su homeostasis pueden causar debilidad en las láminas valvulares.

nodos.label: Enfoques terapéuticos
nodos.desc: Estrategias para manejar enfermedades valvulares, que van desde modificaciones de estilo de vida y medicamentos hasta procedimientos invasivos como valvuloplastia o reemplazo valvular.

nodos.label: Hemodinámica
nodos.desc: Estudio de los flujos sanguíneos y presiones dentro del sistema circulatorio, que se alteran en enfermedades valvulares y se evalúan mediante signos vitales y estudios no invasivos.

nodos.label: Click de ejección
nodos.desc: Sonido agudo escuchado temprano en la sístole, causado por la apertura súbita de una válvula semilunar estenótica (aórtica o pulmonar), ocurriendo después del primer sonido cardíaco (S1).

nodos.label: Tiempo
nodos.desc: Momento en el ciclo cardíaco en que se escucha el murmullo, crucial para su clasificación y diagnóstico.

nodos.label: Tono
nodos.desc: Altura o frecuencia del sonido del murmullo, que puede ser agudo o grave, y ayuda a identificar la naturaleza del flujo.

nodos.label: Calidad
nodos.desc: Características sonoras del murmullo, como rugoso, agudo o de calidad específica, que reflejan la dinámica del flujo sanguíneo.

nodos.label: Ubicación
nodos.desc: Punto específico en el pecho donde se escucha el murmullo, asociado a áreas anatómicas como el área mitral, tricúspide, pulmonar o aórtica.

nodos.label: Radiación
nodos.desc: Desplazamiento del sonido hacia otras áreas del cuerpo, que puede indicar la extensión de la anomalía cardíaca.

nodos.label: Gradiente de presión
nodos.desc: Diferencia de presión entre estructuras cardíacas que causa turbulencia y, por tanto, el desarrollo de un murmullo.

nodos.label: Murmur inocente
nodos.desc: Murmur benigno comúnmente encontrado en niños y atletas, que no indica enfermedad cardíaca y no requiere tratamiento.

nodos.label: Aortic Valve
nodos.desc: One of four heart valves that directs blood flow from the left ventricle to the aorta during systole and prevents backflow during diastole.

nodos.label: Aortic Stenosis
nodos.desc: Narrowing of the aortic valve opening that impedes antegrade blood flow, leading to increased left ventricular pressure, hypertrophy, and reduced ejection fraction.

nodos.label: Aortic Regurgitation
nodos.desc: Backflow of blood from the aorta into the left ventricle during diastole due to valve dysfunction.

nodos.label: Heart Murmur
nodos.desc: An abnormal sound during auscultation of the heart, caused by turbulent blood flow, which can indicate valvular dysfunction or other cardiac pathologies.

nodos.label: Leaflets
nodos.desc: Crescent-shaped structures of the aortic valve that open and close during the cardiac cycle to regulate blood flow.

nodos.label: Hypertrophy
nodos.desc: Thickening of the heart muscle, particularly the left ventricle, in response to increased pressure, commonly seen in aortic stenosis.

nodos.label: Calcific Degeneration
nodos.desc: Progressive hardening and calcification of the aortic valve, most common in elderly individuals without prior heart disease.

nodos.label: Bicuspid Aortic Valve
nodos.desc: Congenital condition where the aortic valve has two leaflets instead of three, increasing the risk of aortic stenosis and regurgitation.

nodos.label: Pulmonary Murmur
nodos.desc: A machinery-like murmur caused by direct oxygenated blood flow from the aorta to the pulmonary artery via a persistent fetal connection.

nodos.label: Venous Hum
nodos.desc: A continuous sound heard during auscultation, possibly due to venous flow abnormalities, and may be mistaken for a heart murmur.

nodos.label: Pulmonary Arteriovenous Malformation
nodos.desc: Abnormal connection between pulmonary arteries and veins, leading to shunting of blood and potentially producing a murmur.

nodos.label: Ruptured Sinus of Valsalva Aneurysm
nodos.desc: A rare condition where the sinus of Valsalva ruptures, causing a vascular aneurysm and producing a characteristic murmur.

nodos.label: Reducción de afterload
nodos.desc: Proceso médico que consiste en disminuir la resistencia que el ventrículo debe superar para ejectar sangre, utilizando inhibidores de la enzima convertidora de angiotensina o bloqueadores de receptores de angiotensina.

nodos.label: Anticoagulación
nodos.desc: Tratamiento que previene la formación de coágulos sanguíneos, especialmente en pacientes con fibrilación auricular o atrio dilatado.

nodos.label: Cirugía de reparación
nodos.desc: Procedimiento quirúrgico para corregir anomalías valvulares, considerado cuando hay síntomas o disfunción ventricular, con el objetivo de restaurar la función valvular.

nodos.label: Sustitución prostética mecánica
nodos.desc: Tipo de intervención quirúrgica que reemplaza una válvula dañada por una prótesis mecánica, asociada a un mayor riesgo de trombosis y necesidad de anticoagulación.

nodos.label: Reparación transcatheter edge-to-edge
nodos.desc: Técnica mínimamente invasiva que utiliza dispositivos como el MitraClip para reparar la válvula mitral en pacientes de alto riesgo para cirugía.

nodos.label: Prolapso de la válvula mitral
nodos.desc: Condición en la que las láminas de la válvula mitral se elevan hacia el atrio durante la contracción, debido a alteraciones estructurales en las láminas o sus estructuras de soporte.

nodos.label: Degeneración mixomatosa
nodos.desc: Proceso patológico que afecta el tejido de las láminas de la válvula mitral, causando acumulación de mucopolisacáridos, lo que lleva a un espesor excesivo y predisposición al prolapso.

nodos.label: Enfermedad de Barlow
nodos.desc: Forma extensa de degeneración mi xomatosa que afecta todo el aparato valvular mitral, incluyendo anillo, láminas, cordones y músculos papilares, provocando una malcoaptación severa.

nodos.label: Deficiencia fibroelástica
nodos.desc: Alteración en la síntesis de colágeno y fibras elásticas que causa debilidad y fragilidad en las láminas de la válvula, impidiendo su coaptación normal.

nodos.label: Disfunción ventricular izquierda
nodos.desc: Afectación de la capacidad del ventrículo izquierdo para bombear sangre eficientemente, que puede ser indicativo de daño valvular o enfermedad cardíaca general.

nodos.label: Dilatación de cámara
nodos.desc: Aumento del tamaño de una cámara del corazón, especialmente del ventrículo izquierdo, que puede ser resultado de una disfunción valvular o cardiopatía.

nodos.label: Doppler Principle
nodos.desc: Mathematical principle used in echocardiography to measure blood flow velocity and calculate pressure gradients and regurgitant volumes.

nodos.label: Valve Area
nodos.desc: Geometric measure of the surface area of a heart valve, calculated using mathematical formulas derived from echocardiographic data.

nodos.label: Regurgitant Volume
nodos.desc: Volume of blood that flows backward through a diseased valve, computed using fluid dynamics and volumetric integration principles.

nodos.label: Cardiac Function
nodos.desc: Mathematical modeling of heart performance, including ejection fraction and ventricular function, used to assess overall cardiac health.

nodos.label: Pulmonary Pressure
nodos.desc: Pressure in the pulmonary circulation, estimated using hemodynamic equations and derived from echocardiographic measurements.

nodos.label: Right Ventricular Ejection Fraction
nodos.desc: Fraction of blood pumped out of the right ventricle per beat, calculated using volume measurements and represents a key functional parameter.

nodos.label: Spatial Resolution
nodos.desc: Measure of the smallest detail that can be distinguished in an image, a mathematical concept in imaging that affects accuracy in valve structure assessment.

nodos.label: Hemodynamic Consequences
nodos.desc: Mathematical modeling of blood flow dynamics, including pressure, velocity, and volume, to understand the impact of valvular disease on circulation.

nodos.label: Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA)
nodos.desc: A congenital heart defect where the ductus arteriosus fails to close after birth, resulting in abnormal blood flow between the aorta and pulmonary artery.

nodos.label: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy
nodos.desc: Thickening of the left ventricular wall due to increased blood volume and pressure, resulting from persistent shunting in PDA.

nodos.label: Pulmonary Hypertension
nodos.desc: Elevated pressure in the pulmonary vasculature caused by increased blood flow through the lungs, potentially leading to lung damage.

nodos.label: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
nodos.desc: A lung condition that may develop as a result of prolonged pulmonary hypertension due to PDA.

nodos.label: Exercise Tolerance
nodos.desc: The capacity of the body to endure physical exertion, assessed as part of postoperative follow-up in cardiac patients.

nodos.label: Electrocardiographic Findings
nodos.desc: Cardiac electrical activity measurements used to assess heart function and detect abnormalities postoperatively.

nodos.label: Residual Shunt
nodos.desc: A persistent blood flow between the aorta and pulmonary artery after treatment, indicating incomplete closure of PDA.

nodos.label: Tricuspid Regurgitation
nodos.desc: Backflow of blood from the right ventricle to the right atrium, a potential late complication following cardiac interventions.

nodos.label: Rhythm Disturbances
nodos.desc: Abnormal heart rhythms that may develop as late sequelae after cardiac surgery or intervention.

nodos.label: Shunt
nodos.desc: Un canal anormal entre las partes del corazón que permite el flujo de sangre entre el lado izquierdo y derecho, alterando la oxigenación de la sangre.

nodos.label: Left-to-Right Shunt
nodos.desc: Conexión anormal entre el lado izquierdo y derecho del corazón que permite que la sangre oxigenada fluya hacia el lado derecho, lo que provoca un aumento del flujo sanguíneo a los pulmones y puede causar hipertensión pulmonar y aumento del volumen cardíaco derecho.

nodos.label: Atrial Septal Defect (ASD)
nodos.desc: Defecto estructural en el septo interatrial que permite que la sangre oxigenada del atrio izquierdo fluya al atrio derecho.

nodos.label: Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD)
nodos.desc: Hole en el septo interventricular que permite que la sangre oxigenada del ventrículo izquierdo fluya al ventrículo derecho.

nodos.label: Right-to-Left Shunt
nodos.desc: Conexión anormal que permite que la sangre desoxigenada del lado derecho del corazón pase directamente al lado izquierdo, evitando que pase por los pulmones para ser oxigenada.

nodos.label: Persistent Truncus Arteriosus
nodos.desc: Defecto congénito en el que un solo tronco arterioso emerge del corazón en lugar de dos vasos separados (aórtico y pulmonar).

nodos.label: Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return
nodos.desc: Retorno anormal de las venas pulmonares a la circulación sistémica en lugar de a los pulmones.

nodos.label: Transposition of the Great Vessels
nodos.desc: Anomalía en la posición de los grandes vasos sanguíneos, donde las arterias aórtica y pulmonar están intercambiadas.

nodos.label: Eisenmenger Syndrome
nodos.desc: Síndrome caracterizado por una reasignación de flujo sanguíneo derecho a izquierdo debido a hipertensión pulmonar severa, causando desoxigenación de la sangre sistémica.

nodos.label: Systemic Circulation
nodos.desc: Circulación de la sangre desde el corazón hacia el resto del cuerpo, que puede verse afectada por el flujo de sangre no oxigenada en shunts.

nodos.label: Cardiac Workload
nodos.desc: Carga funcional del corazón, que aumenta cuando hay un flujo anormal de sangre, especialmente en el lado derecho del corazón en shunts izquierdos.

nodos.label: Cyanosis
nodos.desc: A medical condition characterized by a bluish discoloration of the skin and mucous membranes due to low oxygen levels in the blood.

nodos.label: Tet spells
nodos.desc: Sudden, life-threatening episodes of hypoxemia in patients with tetralogy of Fallot, marked by pallor, irritability, rapid breathing, and diminished peripheral pulses.

nodos.label: Central cyanosis
nodos.desc: Cyanosis observed in the central parts of the body, such as the lips and mucous membranes, indicating systemic hypoxia.

nodos.label: Polycythemia
nodos.desc: An increase in the number of red blood cells, often a compensatory response to chronic hypoxia.

nodos.label: Systolic murmur
nodos.desc: An abnormal sound heard during systole, typically due to turbulent blood flow, often localized in the lower left sternal border in congenital heart disease.

nodos.label: Systolic thrill
nodos.desc: A palpable vibration felt during systole, indicating turbulent blood flow in a vessel or valve.

nodos.label: Parasternal heave
nodos.desc: A visible bulge in the chest wall over the parasternal area, indicating right ventricular hypertrophy due to increased workload.

nodos.label: Femoral pulse
nodos.desc: A pulse located in the femoral artery, and its reduction or absence indicates decreased distal perfusion and poor circulation.

nodos.label: Boot-shaped profile
nodos.desc: A radiographic finding in chest X-ray of patients with tetralogy of Fallot, resulting from a dilated apex beat and hypoplastic pulmonary artery segments.

nodos.label: Right axis deviation
nodos.desc: A deviation of the electrical axis of the heart to the right, observed in electrocardiography, indicating right ventricular hypertrophy.

nodos.label: Right ventricular strain
nodos.desc: A pattern on ECG showing tall R waves in V1 and deep S waves in I and V6, reflecting increased workload on the right ventricle.

nodos.label: First-degree AV block
nodos.desc: A conduction disorder where the atrioventricular node delays the conduction of electrical impulses, indicated by a prolonged PR interval on ECG.

nodos.label: Pulmonary stenosis
nodos.desc: Narrowing of the pulmonary valve or outflow tract, leading to reduced blood flow to the lungs and a key feature in tetralogy of Fallot.

nodos.label: Right ventricular hypertrophy
nodos.desc: Thickening of the right ventricular wall due to chronic increased pressure, commonly seen in conditions like tetralogy of Fallot.

nodos.label: Pulmonary artery pressure
nodos.desc: The pressure within the pulmonary artery, which can be estimated via echocardiography and is critical in assessing severity of pulmonary stenosis.

nodos.label: Left Atrium
nodos.desc: Chamber of the heart that receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins and mixes it with deoxygenated blood from the body.

nodos.label: Right Atrium
nodos.desc: Chamber of the heart that normally receives deoxygenated blood from the body; in TAPVR, oxygenated blood may abnormally enter here.

nodos.label: Mitral Valve
nodos.desc: Valve that regulates blood flow from the left atrium to the left ventricle; blood typically passes through it after mixing in the left atrium.

nodos.label: Left Ventricle
nodos.desc: Chamber that pumps oxygenated blood from the heart into the aorta for distribution to the body.

nodos.label: Total Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Return (TAPVR)
nodos.desc: Congenital heart defect where all pulmonary veins connect abnormally to the right atrium or its tributaries, leading to oxygenated blood returning to the right side of the heart.

nodos.label: Metabolic Acidosis
nodos.desc: Condition where the body's pH drops due to prolonged hypoxemia, leading to electrolyte imbalances and organ dysfunction.

nodos.label: Atrial Septum
nodos.desc: Wall separating the left and right atria; in TAPVR, interatrial communication allows mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

nodos.label: Right Ventricle
nodos.desc: Chamber that pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs; in TAPVR, it receives mixed blood and bears increased workload.

nodos.label: Valve Abnormality
nodos.desc: Structural or functional defects in the tricuspid valve, including displacement of leaflets into the right ventricle, leading to impaired function and resulting in regurgitation or stenosis.

nodos.label: Right Atrial Enlargement
nodos.desc: An increase in the size of the right atrium due to increased volume load from impaired tricuspid valve function and regurgitation.

nodos.label: Right Ventricular Hypoplasia
nodos.desc: Reduced development or contraction of the right ventricular muscle, a consequence of chronic pressure overload and impaired valve function in Ebstein's anomaly.

nodos.label: Accessory Pathway
nodos.desc: Extra conduction pathways between atrial and ventricular myocardium that can lead to arrhythmias, such as Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

nodos.label: Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome
nodos.desc: A type of arrhythmia caused by an accessory pathway allowing abnormal electrical conduction between atria and ventricles, often associated with Ebstein's anomaly.

nodos.label: Severity Grading
nodos.desc: A systematic classification method used to assess the degree of tricuspid valve dysfunction and associated complications in Ebstein's anomaly, ranging from mild to severe.

nodos.label: Cardiac Catheterization
nodos.desc: Procedimiento en el que se inserta un catéter por una venas o arteria para medir presiones dentro de las cavidades cardíacas y evaluar la función de las válvulas.

nodos.label: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) o Computed Tomography (CT) Scan
nodos.desc: Técnicas de imagen que proporcionan imágenes detalladas del corazón y sus estructuras circundantes, útiles para evaluar defectos congénitos complejos.

nodos.label: Prostaglandins
nodos.desc: Sustancias químicas que pueden mantener la patología pulmonar en pacientes con defectos congénitos, especialmente en la presencia de válvulas defectuosas.

nodos.label: Shunt Placement
nodos.desc: Procedimiento quirúrgico que coloca un tubo para conectar vasos sanguíneos, mejorando el flujo sanguíneo hacia los pulmones o reduciendo el flujo a la circulación corporal.

nodos.label: Valve Repair or Replacement
nodos.desc: Procedimiento quirúrgico para reparar o reemplazar válvulas cardíacas dañadas, utilizando válvulas artificiales de metal, plástico o tejido animal.

nodos.label: Fontan Procedure
nodos.desc: Serie de cirugías que separan las circulaciones azules y rojas en pacientes con fisiología de un ventrículo, redirigiendo la sangre desoxigenada directamente a los pulmones.

nodos.label: Heart Transplant
nodos.desc: Tratamiento extremo en el que se reemplaza el corazón por uno donado, cuando no es posible reparar el corazón o tras múltiples cirugías fallidas.

nodos.label: Myocardial Depression
nodos.desc: La depresión miocárdica se refiere a una disminución de la función contractil del músculo cardíaco, que puede ocurrir en septic shock y contribuye a una reducción significativa de la salida cardíaca.

nodos.label: Massive Pulmonary Embolism
nodos.desc: Un embolismo pulmonar masivo oculta un vaso pulmonar principal, aumentando el afterload del ventrículo derecho y provocando insuficiencia cardíaca derecha.

nodos.label: Cardiac Tamponade
nodos.desc: Condición en la que el líquido acumulado en la cavidad pericárdica comprime el corazón, impidiendo su llenado y reduciendo así la salida cardíaca.

nodos.label: Tension Pneumothorax
