nodos.desc: Un estado en el que el aire se acumula en el tórax bajo presión, desplazando estructuras mediastínicas y comprimiendo vasos grandes, lo que interrumpe el retorno venoso y reduce el preload.

nodos.label: Anaphylactic Shock
nodos.desc: Tipo de shock causado por la liberación de histamina y mediadores de mastocitos en respuesta a alergenos, provocando vasodilatación intensa y broncoconstricción.

nodos.label: Septic Shock
nodos.desc: Forma de shock causada por una infección bacteriana grave que induce vasodilatación y depresión miocárdica, reduciendo significativamente la presión de afterload, preload y contractilidad.

nodos.label: Neurogenic Shock
nodos.desc: Shock causado por lesiones neurológicas severas que provocan pérdida de tono simpático y vasodilatación periférica.

nodos.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
nodos.desc: Grupo de enfermedades cardiovasculares que incluye infartos miocárdicos, causados por ruptura de placas en arterias coronarias y formación de trombos que bloquean el flujo sanguíneo.

nodos.label: Fulminant Myocarditis
nodos.desc: Inflamación rápida y severa de los miocitos del corazón que compromete gravemente la función ventricular y reduce la salida cardíaca.

nodos.label: Hypovolemic Shock
nodos.desc: Estado de shock causado por una reducción absoluta o relativa del volumen sanguíneo, que disminuye el preload y afecta la capacidad de llenado del corazón.

nodos.label: Obstructive Shock
nodos.desc: Tipo de shock en el que estructuras anatómicas impiden adecuadamente el llenado o el vaciado de cámaras cardíacas, reduciendo así la salida cardíaca.

nodos.label: Respiratory Rate
nodos.desc: The number of breaths per minute, indicating respiratory function and oxygenation status.

nodos.label: Oxygen Saturation
nodos.desc: The percentage of hemoglobin saturated with oxygen, measured by pulse oximetry, indicating tissue oxygenation.

nodos.label: Capnometry
nodos.desc: A method that measures exhaled carbon dioxide levels, used to assess alveolar ventilation and indirectly estimate cardiac output via the Fick principle.

nodos.label: Central Venous Pressure (CVP)
nodos.desc: A measure of right ventricular preload and fluid responsiveness, obtained via central venous catheterization.

nodos.label: Stroke Volume Variation (SVV)
nodos.desc: A dynamic index derived from arterial waveforms that predicts fluid responsiveness in mechanically ventilated patients.

nodos.label: Pulse Pressure Variation (PPV)
nodos.desc: A dynamic index derived from arterial waveforms that predicts fluid responsiveness in mechanically ventilated patients.

nodos.label: Mixed Venous Oxygen Saturation (SvO2)
nodos.desc: The oxygen saturation of blood in the pulmonary veins, reflecting oxygen delivery and consumption in tissues.

nodos.label: Pulmonary Capillary Wedge Pressure (PCWP)
nodos.desc: A measurement of left atrial pressure, used to assess left ventricular filling pressure and cardiac function.

nodos.label: Thermodynamic Dilution
nodos.desc: A method used in transpulmonary thermodilution to estimate cardiac output based on thermal indicator dilution curves.

nodos.label: Serum Lactate
nodos.desc: A biomarker indicating impaired aerobic metabolism due to reduced tissue perfusion, used as a surrogate for organ dysfunction.

nodos.label: Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome
nodos.desc: A systemic inflammatory state triggered by severe clinical insults, defined by two or more of: temperature >38°C or <36°C, heart rate >90 bpm, respiratory rate >20 breaths/min or PaCO2 <32 mmHg, and white blood cell count >12,000 or <4,000 cells/mm³ or >10% bands. Can be caused by both infectious and non-infectious conditions like trauma or pancreatitis.

nodos.label: Multiple Organ Dysfunction Syndrome
nodos.desc: A condition in which multiple organs exhibit altered function in an acutely ill patient, impairing homeostasis and requiring medical intervention. Commonly affects lungs, kidneys, liver, and cardiovascular system. Involves both injury and repair mechanisms.

nodos.label: Sepsis
nodos.desc: A life-threatening condition resulting from infection-induced SIRS, leading to widespread inflammation, organ dysfunction, and potential death. Severity ranges from mild (fever, tachycardia, tachypnea) to septic shock (hypotension, multi-organ failure, high mortality).

nodos.label: Cardiogenic Shock
nodos.desc: A life-threatening condition due to heart failure, leading to inadequate cardiac output. Managed through hemodynamic stabilization using devices like intra-aortic balloon counterpulsation, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or ventricular assist devices.

nodos.label: Hemodynamic Stabilization
nodos.desc: The maintenance of adequate blood flow and pressure in the circulatory system, achieved through mechanical circulatory assistance devices during acute cardiac failure.

nodos.label: Pathophysiological Processes
nodos.desc: The underlying biological mechanisms causing disease, such as inflammation, organ injury, and failure, which are central to understanding conditions like sepsis and cardiogenic shock.

nodos.label: Clinical Manifestations
nodos.desc: Observable signs and symptoms of a disease, such as fever, tachycardia, tachypnea, hypotension, and organ dysfunction, used to diagnose and assess severity in sepsis and cardiogenic shock.

nodos.label: Diagnostic Considerations
nodos.desc: The evaluation and criteria used to identify diseases such as SIRS and MODS, including laboratory values and physiological parameters, to determine the presence and severity of sepsis or organ dysfunction.

nodos.label: Therapeutic Options
nodos.desc: Interventions used to manage conditions such as sepsis and cardiogenic shock, including mechanical circulatory support and systemic treatments aimed at restoring homeostasis and preventing irreversible organ damage.

nodos.label: Homeostasis
nodos.desc: The body's ability to maintain stable internal conditions, which is disrupted in sepsis and cardiogenic shock, leading to organ dysfunction and requiring medical intervention.

nodos.label: Mean Arterial Pressure
nodos.desc: A measure of the average pressure in the arteries during one cardiac cycle, used to assess perfusion and guide treatment in septic shock.

nodos.label: Central Venous Pressure
nodos.desc: A measure of pressure in the thoracic vena cava near the right atrium, used to evaluate intravascular volume and guide fluid resuscitation.

nodos.label: Procalcitonin
nodos.desc: A biomarker used to differentiate bacterial infection from other causes of inflammation, aiding in diagnosis and guiding antibiotic therapy.

nodos.label: Fluid Resuscitation
nodos.desc: The administration of intravenous fluids to restore intravascular volume and improve cardiac output in septic shock.

nodos.label: Antimicrobial Therapy
nodos.desc: The administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics to treat or prevent infection in septic shock, ideally initiated within one hour of recognition.

nodos.label: Vasopressors
nodos.desc: Medications used to increase blood pressure and maintain mean arterial pressure ≥65 mmHg in septic shock when fluid resuscitation is insufficient.

nodos.label: Crystalloid Solutions
nodos.desc: IV fluids such as normal saline or lactated Ringer's used for initial fluid resuscitation in septic shock.

nodos.label: Urine Output
nodos.desc: A key indicator of renal perfusion and overall fluid balance, used to evaluate the effectiveness of resuscitation in shock management.

nodos.label: Hemodynamic Status
nodos.desc: A clinical assessment of the body's circulation and blood flow, used to determine appropriate fluid therapy (crystalloids, colloids, or blood products).

nodos.label: Parasympathetic Dominance
nodos.desc: A state where parasympathetic activity exceeds sympathetic activity, resulting in unopposed vasodilation and hypotension in neurogenic shock.

nodos.label: Clinical Manifestations
nodos.desc: Observable signs and symptoms of a condition, such as hypotension and altered mental status in shock states.

nodos.label: Diagnostic Approach
nodos.desc: The methodology used to identify and classify shock, including assessment of vital signs and laboratory values.

nodos.label: Therapeutic Interventions
nodos.desc: Treatments applied to manage shock, such as fluid administration, antibiotics, analgesia, and surgical procedures.

nodos.label: Acid-Base Balance
nodos.desc: The regulation of pH in the body's fluids, monitored during resuscitation to detect metabolic disturbances and guide treatment.

nodos.label: Serum Electrolytes
nodos.desc: Chemical components in blood that regulate cellular function and fluid balance; monitored to assess and correct imbalances during shock.

nodos.label: Epinephrine
nodos.desc: A hormone and neurotransmitter that constricts blood vessels, raises blood pressure, reduces swelling, and relaxes bronchial smooth muscles, improving breathing in anaphylactic shock.

nodos.label: Mast Cell Tryptase
nodos.desc: A biomarker indicating mast cell activation, often elevated in blood tests during anaphylactic shock.

nodos.label: Allergens
nodos.desc: Substances that trigger allergic reactions; identified through skin testing or challenge procedures in anaphylactic shock.

nodos.label: Myocardial Ischemia
nodos.desc: Reduced blood flow to the heart muscle, a potential complication of anaphylactic shock that may result from severe vasoconstriction or hypoxia.

nodos.label: Circulatory Derangements
nodos.desc: Severe disruptions in blood circulation, a hallmark of dissociative shock resulting from emotional or physical stress.

nodos.label: Neurogenic Dissociation
nodos.desc: A condition involving disruption of autonomic nervous system function leading to circulatory collapse, distinct from other types of shock.

nodos.label: Supportive Therapy
nodos.desc: Medical interventions such as antihistamines, corticosteroids, intravenous fluids, and oxygen to manage symptoms and stabilize the patient during anaphylactic shock.

nodos.label: Beta-blockers
nodos.desc: Pharmacological agents that inhibit the effects of catecholamines, reducing heart rate and myocardial contractility to mitigate arrhythmias and improve coronary perfusion.

nodos.label: Calcium Channel Blockers
nodos.desc: Drugs that inhibit calcium influx into cardiac cells, reducing heart rate and improving myocardial performance, with examples including verapamil and diltiazem.

nodos.label: Benzodiazepines
nodos.desc: Neuroactive drugs that enhance GABA-mediated inhibition, reducing neural excitability and providing rapid sedation and anxiolysis.

nodos.label: Antipsychotics
nodos.desc: Medications that modulate dopamine receptors, reducing hallucinations, delusions, and thought disorganization in dissociative shock.

nodos.label: Opioids
nodos.desc: Pain-relieving drugs that act on opioid receptors to reduce pain perception and facilitate analgesia during invasive procedures.

nodos.label: Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy
nodos.desc: A psychotherapeutic approach that helps individuals identify and modify maladaptive thought patterns and behaviors related to trauma.

nodos.label: Dialectical Behavioral Therapy
nodos.desc: A therapeutic model focusing on emotion regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness to manage trauma-related symptoms.

nodos.label: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR)
nodos.desc: A therapy that uses bilateral stimulation to help process traumatic memories and reduce their emotional impact.

nodos.label: Mindfulness Practices
nodos.desc: Techniques that promote present-moment awareness and non-judgmental observation to enhance emotional regulation and self-awareness.

nodos.label: Hemodynamic Stability
nodos.desc: The state of balanced blood flow and pressure in the circulatory system, essential for maintaining organ perfusion and preventing shock progression.

nodos.label: Neurobiological Systems
nodos.desc: Interconnected networks in the brain that regulate emotional responses, stress, and physiological functions, central to dissociative shock pathophysiology.

nodos.label: Psychological Trauma
nodos.desc: A profound emotional disturbance resulting from exposure to life-threatening events, which underlies dissociative shock and requires targeted therapeutic intervention.

nodos.label: Prognosis
nodos.desc: The likely outcome of a condition, in this case, improved recovery with early intervention, though residual symptoms like fatigue and memory issues may persist.

nodos.label: Elastic Fiber Destruction
nodos.desc: The breakdown of elastic fibers in the walls of medium-sized arteries, leading to vessel thickening and narrowing.

nodos.label: Aneurysm
nodos.desc: A ballooning of weakened vessel walls due to vascular damage, which can lead to rupture.

nodos.label: Thrombosis
nodos.desc: Formation of blood clots inside damaged blood vessels as a result of inflammation.

nodos.label: Age as Risk Factor
nodos.desc: PAN commonly occurs between ages 40 and 60, indicating a demographic susceptibility.

nodos.label: Gender as Risk Factor
nodos.desc: Men are more likely than women to develop PAN, suggesting a gender-based predisposition.

nodos.label: Hepatitis B Infection
nodos.desc: Up to 40% of PAN patients test positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, indicating a strong association with this infection.

nodos.label: Acute Phase Reactants
nodos.desc: Laboratory markers like erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) that increase during inflammation.

nodos.label: Vascular Lesions
nodos.desc: Pathological changes in blood vessels identified through imaging techniques such as CT angiography or MRI angiography.

nodos.label: Granulomatous Inflammation
nodos.desc: A type of chronic inflammation characterized by the formation of granulomas in affected tissues.

nodos.label: Fibrinoid Necrosis
nodos.desc: Degeneration of vessel wall tissue due to inflammation, visible in biopsy specimens.

nodos.label: Microaneurysms
nodos.desc: Small, localized bulges in vessel walls that are a hallmark of PAN pathology.

nodos.label: Fever Duration
nodos.desc: A clinical symptom requiring fever to persist for at least five days to meet diagnostic criteria for Kawasaki Disease.

nodos.label: Conjunctival Injection
nodos.desc: Redness of the eyes without exudate, one of the principal clinical features used in diagnosing Kawasaki Disease.

nodos.label: Oral Changes
nodos.desc: Manifestations such as red, cracked, or swollen lips and strawberry tongue, indicating inflammation in the oral cavity.

nodos.label: Polymorphous Rash
nodos.desc: A rash with varied appearance, often on trunk and extremities, used as a diagnostic criterion in Kawasaki Disease.

nodos.label: Hand and Foot Edema
nodos.desc: Erythema and edema of hands and feet, followed by desquamation after 1-2 weeks, a key clinical indicator.

nodos.label: Lymphadenopathy
nodos.desc: Swelling of cervical lymph nodes, typically unilateral and greater than 1.5 cm in diameter, a principal symptom in KD diagnosis.

nodos.label: Leukocytosis
nodos.desc: Elevated white blood cell count observed in laboratory tests during acute phase of Kawasaki Disease.

nodos.label: Thrombocytopenia
nodos.desc: Decreased platelet count during acute phase, which typically resolves within two weeks in Kawasaki Disease.

nodos.label: ESR and CRP
nodos.desc: Inflammatory markers elevated in Kawasaki Disease, used to support diagnosis when combined with clinical features.

nodos.label: Diagnostic Threshold
nodos.desc: A child must meet at least four out of six principal symptoms to be diagnosed with classic Kawasaki Disease according to AHA guidelines.

nodos.label: Coronary Artery Changes
nodos.desc: Imaging findings such as coronary artery abnormalities detected via echocardiography, which can support diagnosis in cases with insufficient clinical symptoms.

nodos.label: Eosinophil
nodos.desc: A type of white blood cell involved in fighting parasitic infections, allergic reactions, and asthma; in CSS, it becomes overactive and releases toxic proteins causing tissue injury and inflammation.

nodos.label: Antineutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibodies (ANCAs)
nodos.desc: Autoantibodies directed against neutrophils that contribute to immune cell activation and exacerbate inflammatory responses in CSS.

nodos.label: Vasculitis
nodos.desc: Inflammation of blood vessel walls, leading to reduced blood flow, ischemia, and organ infarction; a key pathological feature in CSS.

nodos.label: Allergic Rhinitis
nodos.desc: Nasal symptoms such as congestion, sinus pain, and postnasal drip that are common in CSS patients.

nodos.label: Skin Lesions
nodos.desc: Purpuric rashes, livedo reticularis, ulcers, and nodules resulting from cutaneous vasculitis in CSS.

nodos.label: Neuropathy
nodos.desc: An asymmetric neuropathy, specifically mononeuritis multiplex, affecting multiple nerves and causing weakness, numbness, or pain in limbs.

nodos.label: Pulmonary Involvement
nodos.desc: Lung abnormalities such as opacities, pleural effusions, or consolidations seen in up to half of CSS cases, sometimes progressing to chronic obstructive lung disease.

nodos.label: Renal Involvement
nodos.desc: Conditions such as glomerulonephritis, proteinuria, hematuria, and renal insufficiency due to renal vasculitis in CSS.

nodos.label: Gastrointestinal Involvement
nodos.desc: Symptoms like abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and bleeding due to mesenteric vasculitis in CSS.

nodos.label: Immune System
nodos.desc: Central to the pathogenesis of CSS, where immune dysregulation leads to activation of eosinophils and ANCAs, resulting in vascular inflammation.

nodos.label: Genetic Factors
nodos.desc: Hereditary predispositions believed to contribute to the development of CSS, interacting with environmental triggers.

nodos.label: Environmental Factors
nodos.desc: External triggers, such as infections or exposures, that may interact with genetic susceptibility to initiate CSS.

nodos.label: Tissue Injury
nodos.desc: Damage to organs and tissues caused by the release of toxic proteins from overactive eosinophils and inflammatory mediators in CSS.

nodos.label: Carbon Dioxide Production
nodos.desc: La producción de dióxido de carbono es un resultado de la metabolización celular, y se relaciona con el PaCO2 en el equilibrio alveolar.

nodos.label: Alveolar Gas Equation
nodos.desc: Ecuación que describe la relación entre la presión parcial de oxígeno y dióxido de carbono en los alvéolos pulmonares, considerando la ventilación, perfusión y la concentración de gases.

nodos.label: Metabolic Activity
nodos.desc: La actividad metabólica influye en la producción de CO2, lo que afecta directamente el PaCO2 y, por ende, el equilibrio gaseoso en los alvéolos.

nodos.label: Hypoxic Drive
nodos.desc: Mecanismo fisiológico que aumenta la ventilación en respuesta a niveles bajos de oxígeno; su supresión por oxígeno suplementario puede causar hipercapnia.

nodos.label: Hypercapnia
nodos.desc: Condición en la que el nivel de dióxido de carbono en la sangre es elevado, lo que puede provocar acidosis respiratoria y afectar la función cardiovascular.

nodos.label: Altitude Sickness
nodos.desc: Síndrome causado por la disminución de la presión atmosférica en alturas elevadas, que reduce el PAO2 y provoca hipoxia, con riesgo de edema pulmonar o cerebral.

nodos.label: Ventilatory Drive
nodos.desc: Estimulación del sistema respiratorio que aumenta la frecuencia y profundidad de las respiraciones en respuesta a cambios en la presión parcial de oxígeno.

nodos.label: Graham's Law of Diffusion
nodos.desc: A principle stating that the rate of diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass.

nodos.label: Rate of Diffusion
nodos.desc: The speed at which gas molecules spread out in a medium, typically measured in cm³/sec or mL/min.

nodos.label: Ideal Gas Behavior
nodos.desc: A theoretical condition where gas molecules do not interact with each other or with the solvent, leading to predictable solubility according to Henry's Law.

nodos.label: Fick's Law of Diffusion
nodos.desc: Una ley física que describe la tasa de difusión de una sustancia a través de una barrera, proporcional a la diferencia de concentración, al área de superficie disponible y al coeficiente de difusión, e inversamente proporcional al espesor de la barrera.

nodos.label: Gradiente de concentración
nodos.desc: Diferencia de concentración entre dos puntos, que actúa como impulso para el movimiento de moléculas por difusión.

nodos.label: Área de superficie
nodos.desc: El espacio disponible para que una sustancia se difunda a través de una membrana o barrera.

nodos.label: Coeficiente de difusión
nodos.desc: Propiedad física que mide la rapidez con que una sustancia se difunde en un medio.

nodos.label: Espesor de la barrera
nodos.desc: La distancia que debe recorrer una sustancia para difundirse a través de una membrana o capa.

nodos.label: Presión parcial
nodos.desc: La presión ejercida por una sustancia gaseosa en una mezcla gaseosa, relacionada directamente con su concentración.

nodos.label: Oxygen Level
nodos.desc: A measure of the concentration of oxygen in the arterial blood, which is detected by peripheral chemoreceptors to regulate breathing.

nodos.label: Carbon Dioxide Level
nodos.desc: A measure of the concentration of carbon dioxide in the blood, which influences pH and activates central chemoreceptors to regulate ventilation.

nodos.label: Hydrogen Ion Concentration
nodos.desc: The concentration of H+ ions in cerebrospinal fluid, which increases when CO2 levels rise and activates central chemoreceptors to stimulate ventilation.

nodos.label: Chemical Equilibrium
nodos.desc: The balance between reactants and products in the reaction where CO2 reacts with water to form carbonic acid and subsequently dissociates into bicarbonate and hydrogen ions.

nodos.label: Ventilation
nodos.desc: The process of breathing, which is regulated by chemoreceptors to maintain proper oxygen and carbon dioxide levels in the body.

nodos.label: Chemoreceptors
nodos.desc: Sensory structures that detect changes in blood chemistry, such as oxygen, carbon dioxide, and pH, and send signals to the brainstem to adjust breathing.

nodos.label: Brainstem Respiratory Centers
nodos.desc: Neural structures in the brainstem that receive signals from chemoreceptors and regulate the rate and depth of breathing.

nodos.label: Medical History
nodos.desc: Un proceso de recolección detallada de síntomas como tos, opresión torácica, dificultad respiratoria, especialmente por la noche o por la mañana, así como factores desencadenantes, antecedentes familiares de asma o condiciones respiratorias y predisposición a reacciones alérgicas (atopia).

nodos.label: Physical Examination
nodos.desc: Evaluación clínica que incluye escucha de los pulmones con estetoscopio para detectar signos de obstrucción o hiperinflación, como ronquidos, exhalación prolongada, disminución de sonidos respiratorios o uso de músculos accesoria, aunque no confirma el diagnóstico de asma por sí solo.

nodos.label: Spirometry
nodos.desc: Prueba no invasiva que mide la función pulmonar al evaluar el volumen de aire que una persona puede exhalar de forma rápida y fuerte tras una inhalación profunda. Se utilizan parámetros clave como el volumen vital forzado (FVC), el volumen expiratorio forzado en un segundo (FEV1) y la relación FEV1/FVC, que en pacientes con asma tienden a ser reducidos o alterados.

nodos.label: Airway Inflammation
nodos.desc: Proceso fisiológico caracterizado por inflamación de las vías respiratorias, que puede ser evaluado mediante estudios clínicos y es un componente clave en el entendimiento del asma.

nodos.label: Airflow Obstruction
nodos.desc: Aumento de la resistencia al flujo de aire en las vías respiratorias, que puede ser cuantificado mediante pruebas como la spirometría y que es un síntoma central en el asma.

nodos.label: Lung Function
nodos.desc: Capacidad de los pulmones para realizar funciones respiratorias, evaluada mediante pruebas como la spirometría, que proporciona datos objetivos sobre la salud pulmonar.

nodos.label: Protease
nodos.desc: Enzyme that breaks down proteins; in emphysema, elevated levels damage elastin fibers in alveolar walls.

nodos.label: Antiprotease
nodos.desc: Molecule that inhibits protease activity; deficiency leads to uncontrolled protease action and lung tissue damage.

nodos.label: Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD)
nodos.desc: Genetic condition where mutations in the SERPINA1 gene result in reduced antiprotease levels, increasing emphysema risk even with low smoking exposure.

nodos.label: Oxidative Stress
nodos.desc: Imbalance between reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and the body's antioxidant defenses, leading to cellular damage in lung tissue.

nodos.label: Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS)
nodos.desc: Chemical species like superoxide and hydroxyl radicals that are produced in excess in smokers, contributing to inflammation and tissue degradation.

nodos.label: FEV1/FVC Ratio
nodos.desc: Ratio of forced expiratory volume in one second to forced vital capacity; a decreased ratio indicates obstructive lung disease such as COPD.

nodos.label: Hyperinflation
nodos.desc: Abnormal expansion of the lungs due to loss of elastic recoil, visible in chest X-rays and CT scans in emphysema.

nodos.label: Bullae
nodos.desc: Large air sacs in the lungs that form due to alveolar wall destruction, visible on imaging studies in emphysema.

nodos.label: Arterial Blood Gases
nodos.desc: Test that measures oxygen and carbon dioxide levels in arterial blood, indicating hypoxemia and hypercapnia in advanced emphysema.

nodos.label: Pulse Oximetry
nodos.desc: Non-invasive method to continuously monitor peripheral capillary oxygen saturation in patients with emphysema.

nodos.label: Genetic Predisposition
nodos.desc: Inherited susceptibility to diseases; in emphysema, AATD affects about 1-3% of COPD patients and accelerates disease progression.

nodos.label: Risk Factors
nodos.desc: Conditions that increase the likelihood of developing emphysema, including smoking, secondhand smoke, biomass fuel exposure, air pollution, and occupational hazards.

nodos.label: Diffusing Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide
nodos.desc: Medida que refleja la capacidad de los pulmones para transferir gases desde los alvéolos hasta la sangre, utilizando dióxido de carbono como gas de prueba debido a su alta afinidad por la hemoglobina y baja metabolización en el cuerpo.

nodos.label: Body Plethysmography
nodos.desc: Técnica que permite una cuantificación precisa de los volúmenes y capacidades pulmonares, detectando desviaciones por aire atrapado o hipervolemia asociadas a la emfisema.

nodos.label: Diffusing Capacity Measurement
nodos.desc: Evaluación de las alteraciones en la difusión alveolo-capilar que resultan de distorsiones estructurales en los pulmones, indicando daño funcional en la membrana alveolo-capilar.

nodos.label: Bronchodilator Responsiveness Testing
nodos.desc: Prueba que permite distinguir entre componentes reversibles e irreversibles de obstrucción pulmonar, guiando estrategias farmacológicas de tratamiento.

nodos.label: Maximal Voluntary Ventilation (MVV)
nodos.desc: Medición que estima la capacidad máxima de respiración, mostrando limitaciones impuestas por alteraciones emfisémicas en las mecánicas ventilatorias.

nodos.label: Lung Volumes and Capacities
nodos.desc: Parámetros fisiológicos que describen el volumen de aire en los pulmones en diferentes estados, como reserva, residual y total, utilizados para evaluar la función respiratoria.

nodos.label: Alveolar-Capillary Membrane
nodos.desc: Estructura biológica que separa los alvéolos pulmonares de la circulación sanguínea y cuya integridad afecta la eficiencia de la difusión gaseosa.

nodos.label: Emphysema Severity
nodos.desc: Grado de alteración estructural y funcional en los pulmones causado por la emfisema, que se caracteriza por la destrucción de los alvéolos y pérdida de elasticidad.

nodos.label: Functional Assessment
nodos.desc: Evaluación de la función respiratoria mediante pruebas fisiológicas que miden la capacidad pulmonar y su respuesta a estímulos.

nodos.label: Respiratory Function
nodos.desc: Capacidad del sistema respiratorio para realizar intercambios gaseosos eficientes, influenciada por la estructura y función de los pulmones.

nodos.label: Cord
nodos.desc: A long, narrow, and flexible plastic cord that connects the catheter to external monitoring equipment.

nodos.label: Balloon Tip
nodos.desc: An inflatable balloon near the catheter tip that aids in navigation and provides precise pressure readings when inflated.

nodos.label: Thermistor
nodos.desc: A sensor near the catheter tip that measures blood temperature changes to calculate cardiac output using thermodynamic principles.

nodos.label: Right Atrial Pressure (RAP)
nodos.desc: The filling pressure of the right atrium, reflecting right ventricular function.

nodos.label: Right Ventricular Systolic Pressure (RVSP)
nodos.desc: The maximum pressure generated by the right ventricle during contraction.

nodos.label: Stewart-Hamilton Equation
nodos.desc: Ecuación matemática que calcula el gasto cardíaco basándose en la curva de disminución de temperatura registrada en el catéter Swan-Ganz.

nodos.label: Principio de Fick
nodos.desc: Método matemático que determina el gasto cardíaco a partir de la diferencia de saturación de oxígeno entre la sangre arterial y venosa mixta.

nodos.label: Cálculo de PVR
nodos.desc: Fórmula matemática que determina la presión vascular pulmonar como (presión media de la arteria pulmonar menos presión de la cavidad venosa pulmonar) dividido por el gasto cardíaco.

nodos.label: Rango normal de PVR
nodos.desc: Valor que varía según edad, sexo y superficie corporal, generalmente inferior a 2 unidades de Wood, y se utiliza para diferenciar tipos de hipertensión pulmonar.

nodos.label: Prueba de vasoreactividad
nodos.desc: Evaluación matemática de la respuesta inmediata del sistema vascular a agentes como óxido nítrico o adenosina, basada en cambios en presión media pulmonar y gasto cardíaco.

nodos.label: Evaluación hemodinámica
nodos.desc: Proceso que incluye mediciones directas de presión y gasto cardíaco para analizar el funcionamiento del sistema cardiovascular.

nodos.label: Diagnóstico de hipertensión pulmonar
nodos.desc: Proceso que utiliza herramientas como ecocardiografía (no invasiva) y cateterización de la cavidad derecha (estándar) para identificar y clasificar la enfermedad.

nodos.label: Pleural Effusion
nodos.desc: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in the pleural space between the visceral and parietal pleura, which under normal conditions contains only a small amount of lubricating fluid to reduce friction during respiration.

nodos.label: Pleural Space
nodos.desc: The potential space between the visceral and parietal pleura, lined by serous membranes, normally containing a thin film of lubricating fluid secreted by mesothelial cells to facilitate smooth lung movement during respiration.

nodos.label: Visceral Pleura
nodos.desc: The serous membrane that closely adheres to the surface of the lungs, forming part of the pleural cavity.

nodos.label: Parietal Pleura
nodos.desc: The serous membrane that lines the inner aspect of the thoracic cage and mediastinal structures, forming part of the pleural cavity.

nodos.label: Mesothelial Cells
nodos.desc: Specialized cells lining the pleural membranes that secrete a lubricating fluid to reduce friction during respiration.

nodos.label: Lubricating Fluid
nodos.desc: A thin film of fluid produced by mesothelial cells in the pleural space to minimize friction and enable smooth lung expansion and contraction during breathing.

nodos.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms
nodos.desc: Biological processes underlying disease states, such as fluid accumulation in the pleural space, which result from disruptions in normal physiological functions.

nodos.label: Diagnostic Criteria
nodos.desc: Standardized conditions or measurements used to identify and confirm the presence of a medical condition, such as pleural effusion, through imaging or laboratory tests.

nodos.label: Treatment Options
nodos.desc: Therapeutic interventions used to manage a medical condition, including supportive care, pharmacological treatments, and avoidance measures.

nodos.label: TNM system
nodos.desc: A staging system used in lung cancer to describe the extent of cancer based on tumor size (T), lymph node involvement (N), and metastasis (M).

nodos.label: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
nodos.desc: The most common type of lung cancer, accounting for 80-85% of cases, subdivided into adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and large cell carcinoma.

nodos.label: Small Cell Lung Cancer
nodos.desc: A less common type of lung cancer, making up 10-15% of all cases, typically more aggressive and requiring different treatment approaches.

nodos.label: Adenocarcinoma
nodos.desc: A subtype of NSCLC commonly found in the outer parts of the lungs, growing slowly and often diagnosed in peripheral regions.

nodos.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
nodos.desc: A subtype of NSCLC typically located in the bronchi, growing slowly and associated with smoking history.

nodos.label: Large Cell Carcinoma
nodos.desc: A rare subtype of NSCLC that can develop in any part of the lung and is known for rapid growth and poor prognosis.

nodos.label: Staging
nodos.desc: A system that determines how far cancer has spread, essential for treatment planning and prognosis prediction.

nodos.label: Diagnosis
nodos.desc: The process of identifying the type of lung cancer, its stage, and molecular mutation status to guide treatment decisions.

nodos.label: Molecular Mutation Status
nodos.desc: Information about genetic mutations in cancer cells that can influence treatment options and disease progression.

nodos.label: Metastasis
nodos.desc: The spread of cancer cells from the primary site to distant organs, a key factor in determining disease severity and prognosis.

nodos.label: Biomarkers
nodos.desc: Measurable indicators of biological processes, used to predict metastatic potential and guide treatment decisions in lung cancer.

nodos.label: Performance Status
nodos.desc: A clinical measure of a patient's ability to perform ordinary activities, used to assess overall health and suitability for treatment.

nodos.label: Molecular Profiling
nodos.desc: A diagnostic technique that analyzes genetic and molecular characteristics of tumors to identify targets for therapy and predict response to treatment.

nodos.label: Upper Respiratory Infection (URI)
nodos.desc: Inflammation or infection of the nose, throat, sinuses, and voice box (larynx) caused by viruses, most commonly rhinovirus, affecting only the upper parts of the respiratory tract.

nodos.label: Virus Transmission
nodos.desc: Spread of viruses through airborne droplets when infected individuals cough, sneeze, talk, or touch contaminated surfaces.

nodos.label: Respiratory Tract
nodos.desc: The anatomical pathway of the respiratory system, including the nose, throat, sinuses, and voice box, which can be affected by infections such as URIs.

nodos.label: Infection Causation
nodos.desc: The process by which viruses, such as rhinovirus, initiate and propagate infection in the upper respiratory tract.

nodos.label: Enrollment Criteria
nodos.desc: Conditions that participants must meet to join a clinical trial, typically including age, performance status, histology, and disease stage.

nodos.label: Randomized Controlled Study
nodos.desc: A type of clinical trial that compares an experimental treatment against a standard treatment to assess efficacy and safety through random assignment.

nodos.label: Palliative Care
nodos.desc: A medical approach focused on relieving symptoms such as cough, dyspnea, chest pain, fatigue, depression, and anxiety, improving psychological wellbeing, and enhancing quality of life during lung cancer treatment.

nodos.label: Symptom Management
nodos.desc: The process of identifying, assessing, and treating distressing symptoms associated with diseases like lung cancer to improve patient comfort and outcomes.

nodos.label: Multidisciplinary Treatment
nodos.desc: A coordinated approach to cancer care involving surgical, radiation, and systemic therapies tailored to individual patient needs.

nodos.label: Targeted Therapy
nodos.desc: A treatment strategy that specifically targets molecular or genetic abnormalities in cancer cells, offering improved outcomes with fewer side effects.

nodos.label: Immunotherapy
nodos.desc: A therapeutic approach that enhances the body's immune system to recognize and destroy cancer cells, representing an emerging frontier in oncology.

nodos.label: End-of-Life Care
nodos.desc: Supportive care provided during the final stages of life, including hospice care, which focuses on comfort, dignity, and holistic well-being.

nodos.label: Pharyngitis
nodos.desc: Inflammation of the pharynx, which can be viral or bacterial in origin; typically resolves within 7-10 days, with supportive care such as hydration and rest.

nodos.label: Bacterial Pharyngitis
nodos.desc: A form of pharyngitis caused by bacteria, particularly group A streptococcus; requires targeted antibiotic therapy to prevent complications like rheumatic fever or glomerulonephritis.

nodos.label: Viral Pharyngitis
nodos.desc: A form of pharyngitis caused by viruses; does not require antibiotics, as viral infections are self-limiting and treated with supportive measures.

nodos.label: Antibiotic Therapy
nodos.desc: Treatment with antibiotics such as penicillin V, amoxicillin, azithromycin, clarithromycin, clindamycin, or ceftriaxone for bacterial pharyngitis; duration typically 5-10 days.

nodos.label: Supportive Measures
nodos.desc: Non-pharmacological interventions including hydration, rest, and over-the-counter analgesics to alleviate symptoms of pharyngitis.

nodos.label: Prevention
nodos.desc: Strategies to reduce the spread of pharyngitis, including handwashing, covering coughs, avoiding contact with sick individuals, and vaccination against influenza, Haemophilus influenzae, and pneumococcal disease.

nodos.label: Tonsillopharyngitis
nodos.desc: Inflammation affecting both tonsils and pharynx; commonly resolves within 7-10 days, but may require medical attention if complications arise.

nodos.label: Hydration
nodos.desc: Maintaining fluid intake to prevent dehydration and soothe throat irritation.

nodos.label: Soft Diet
nodos.desc: Consuming soft foods like yogurt, pudding, and soup to minimize irritation to surgical sites.

nodos.label: Physical Activity Restriction
nodos.desc: Limiting strenuous activity to prevent bleeding and support healing.

nodos.label: Pain Management
nodos.desc: Use of over-the-counter or prescription medications to alleviate postoperative pain.

nodos.label: Symptom Monitoring
nodos.desc: Tracking signs such as fever or increased respiratory effort to detect complications early.

nodos.label: Epiglottis
nodos.desc: A flap of tissue at the base of the tongue that covers the windpipe during swallowing to prevent aspiration.

nodos.label: Airway Obstruction
nodos.desc: Swelling of the epiglottis can block the airway, leading to breathing difficulties and potential suffocation.

nodos.label: Larynx
nodos.desc: The voice box that protects the lower respiratory tract from foreign matter during swallowing.

nodos.label: Infectious Agents
nodos.desc: Pathogens such as Haemophilus influenzae type b, Group A Streptococcus, and Staphylococcus aureus that can cause rapid inflammation of the epiglottis.

nodos.label: Diagnostic Methods
nodos.desc: Imaging and endoscopic techniques such as lateral neck X-ray, fiberoptic nasopharyngoscopy, and CT/MRI scans used to visualize and assess epiglottitis.

nodos.label: Identificación viral
nodos.desc: Uso de pruebas rápidas de antígenos o PCR para detectar virus causantes de bronquiolitis, crucial para tratamiento y control de infecciones.

nodos.label: Estudios de imagen
nodos.desc: Técnicas como radiografía torácica que ayudan a evaluar la gravedad de la enfermedad.

nodos.label: Pruebas funcionales
nodos.desc: Ejemplos como oximetría de pulso y análisis de gases sanguíneos para medir la función respiratoria y determinar necesidad de intervención.

nodos.label: Cuidado de apoyo
nodos.desc: Enfoque principal en la gestión de síntomas y mejora del confort respiratorio en pacientes con bronquiolitis.

nodos.label: Broncodilatadores
nodos.desc: Medicamentos como albuterol que, aunque usados en otras enfermedades, no han demostrado beneficios claros en bronquiolitis y se usan solo en casos seleccionados.

nodos.label: Agentes antivirales
nodos.desc: Medicamentos como ribavirin para RSV, con baja eficacia y usados solo en pacientes de alto riesgo con condiciones subyacentes.

nodos.label: Salina hipertónica nebulizada
nodos.desc: Tratamiento que ha mostrado mejoras en estudios aleatorizados frente a salina normal, mejorando los resultados clínicos en algunos casos.

nodos.label: Terapia con oxígeno
nodos.desc: Intervención utilizada para mantener niveles adecuados de oxígeno en pacientes con dificultad respiratoria.

nodos.label: Ventilación mecánica
nodos.desc: Terapia avanzada para pacientes con insuficiencia respiratoria grave, que requiere monitoreo intensivo.

nodos.label: Erythropoiesis
nodos.desc: Proceso biológico por el cual se producen glóbulos rojos a partir de células madre pluripotentes en el hueso largo.

nodos.label: Myeloid Cells
nodos.desc: A lineage of white blood cells that includes granulocytes (neutrophils, basophils, eosinophils), monocytes, and megakaryocytes, which give rise to platelets.

nodos.label: Lymphoid Cells
nodos.desc: A lineage of white blood cells that includes T cells, B cells, and natural killer (NK) cells, derived from common lymphoid progenitors.

nodos.label: Basophils
nodos.desc: Rare white blood cells (<1%) that release histamine and other mediators during allergic responses, contributing to inflammation.

nodos.label: Eosinophils
nodos.desc: Granulocytes involved in defense against parasites and implicated in inflammatory conditions such as asthma and allergic disorders.

nodos.label: Monocytes
nodos.desc: Large phagocytic cells that migrate from bone marrow to tissues and differentiate into macrophages, playing roles in immune surveillance, debris clearance, and antigen presentation.

nodos.label: Megakaryocytes
nodos.desc: Large polyploid cells in bone marrow that fragment to produce platelets, essential for hemostasis and thrombosis.

nodos.label: Platelets
nodos.desc: Small cytoplasmic fragments derived from megakaryocytes that adhere to vascular injury sites and initiate clot formation to prevent bleeding.

nodos.label: T Cells
nodos.desc: Lymphoid cells that differentiate into CD4+ or CD8+ subtypes and play central roles in adaptive immune responses, including cell-mediated immunity and immune regulation.

nodos.label: PU.1
nodos.desc: A specific transcription factor critical for hematopoiesis that promotes myeloid lineage development at the expense of lymphoid specification.

nodos.label: Ikaros
nodos.desc: A transcription factor that governs early lymphoid commitment by suppressing alternative cell fates, ensuring proper lineage allocation in hematopoietic development.

nodos.label: Ikaros and Aiolos
nodos.desc: A pair of transcription factors that regulate early lymphoid commitment by suppressing alternative developmental fates, demonstrating precise control in gene regulatory networks.

nodos.label: Growth Factors
nodos.desc: Extracellular signaling molecules that promote cell proliferation, survival, and differentiation in hematopoietic cells.

nodos.label: Cytokines
nodos.desc: Signaling proteins secreted by stromal cells that regulate hematopoietic cell behavior, including survival, proliferation, and differentiation.

nodos.label: Colony-Stimulating Factors (CSFs)
nodos.desc: A class of growth factors that promote the proliferation and differentiation of myeloid progenitor cells.

nodos.label: Interleukins (ILs)
nodos.desc: Cytokines that support the growth and functional activity of multiple hematopoietic lineages.

nodos.label: Hematopoiesis
nodos.desc: The process of blood cell formation and differentiation, regulated by intrinsic transcription factors and extracellular signals within the bone marrow microenvironment.

nodos.label: Gene Regulatory Networks
nodos.desc: Complex systems of interactions between genes, transcription factors, and regulatory elements that control cell fate decisions during development.

nodos.label: Neutropenia
nodos.desc: A reduction in neutrophil count, increasing susceptibility to bacterial infections.

nodos.label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
nodos.desc: A life-threatening hematological malignancy characterized by uncontrolled proliferation of myeloid precursors, disrupting normal hematopoiesis.

nodos.label: Aplastic Anemia
nodos.desc: A severe disorder in which the bone marrow fails to produce sufficient blood cells, leading to pancytopenia.

nodos.label: Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT)
nodos.desc: A therapeutic approach where donor-derived hematopoietic stem cells are transplanted to reconstitute healthy blood cell production in patients with hematological disorders.

nodos.label: Ex Vivo Expansion
nodos.desc: A technique that involves culturing autologous hematopoietic stem cells in defined media enriched with cytokines to increase cell yield before transplantation.

nodos.label: Carbonic Acid
nodos.desc: A compound formed by the reaction of carbon dioxide and water, which dissociates into hydrogen and bicarbonate ions.

nodos.label: Bicarbonate Ion
nodos.desc: A negatively charged ion formed when carbonic acid dissociates, involved in buffering and pH regulation in blood.

nodos.label: Red Blood Cell
nodos.desc: A cell type in the blood responsible for oxygen transport and carbon dioxide removal, playing a key role in gas exchange and pH regulation.

nodos.label: Chloride Shift
nodos.desc: A physiological process where chloride ions move out of red blood cells in exchange for bicarbonate ions entering, maintaining electrical neutrality and aiding in CO2 transport.

nodos.label: Hemoglobin
nodos.desc: A protein in red blood cells that binds oxygen and facilitates its transport, also involved in CO2 transport via bicarbonate formation and chloride shift.

nodos.label: Fetal Hemoglobin
nodos.desc: A type of hemoglobin found in fetal red blood cells, composed of two alpha and two gamma chains, with higher oxygen affinity than adult hemoglobin.

nodos.label: Hematocrit
nodos.desc: The volume percentage of red blood cells in whole blood, used as a measure of blood composition and oxygen-carrying capacity.

nodos.label: Concentration Gradient
nodos.desc: A difference in concentration of a substance between two regions, driving the movement of ions or molecules from high to low concentration.

nodos.label: 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate
nodos.desc: A molecule that modulates hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, reducing it under low oxygen conditions to facilitate oxygen release in tissues.

nodos.label: Partial Pressure of Carbon Dioxide
nodos.desc: A measure of the pressure exerted by carbon dioxide gas in a mixture of gases, indicating the concentration of CO2 in a given environment.

nodos.label: Oxygen Saturation of Hemoglobin
nodos.desc: The percentage of hemoglobin molecules in the blood that are bound to oxygen, indicating the amount of oxygen available for delivery to tissues.

nodos.label: Heme Group
nodos.desc: A porphyrin ring structure within hemoglobin that contains iron and is responsible for binding oxygen molecules.

nodos.label: Conformational Shift
nodos.desc: A change in the three-dimensional shape of a molecule, such as hemoglobin, which can affect its functional properties like oxygen binding affinity.

nodos.label: Affinity for Oxygen
nodos.desc: The strength with which hemoglobin binds to oxygen; reduced affinity facilitates oxygen release to tissues under specific conditions.

nodos.label: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
nodos.desc: A chronic respiratory condition characterized by airflow obstruction, leading to impaired gas exchange and elevated CO2 levels in the blood.

nodos.label: Haldane Effect
nodos.desc: The phenomenon where hemoglobin releases oxygen in tissues, increasing its capacity to bind carbon dioxide, thus enhancing CO2 transport back to the lungs.

nodos.label: Oxygen Release
nodos.desc: The process by which hemoglobin releases oxygen to peripheral tissues, especially under conditions of high CO2 or low pH.

nodos.label: Carbon Dioxide Binding
nodos.desc: The ability of hemoglobin to bind carbon dioxide molecules, which increases when oxygen is released from hemoglobin in tissues.

nodos.label: Thrombin
nodos.desc: A serine protease that plays a central role in coagulation by activating various coagulation factors and promoting fibrin polymerization.

nodos.label: Ionized Calcium
nodos.desc: A divalent cation essential for the activation of factor XIII, highlighting the role of divalent cations in coagulation regulation.

nodos.label: Antithrombin III (ATIII)
nodos.desc: A natural inhibitor of serine proteases such as thrombin, FXa, and FIXa; functions as a suicide inhibitor and is potentiated by heparin or its mimics.

nodos.label: Heparin
nodos.desc: A highly sulfated polysaccharide that enhances the affinity of antithrombin III for its target proteases via a pentasaccharide motif.

nodos.label: Fondaparinux
nodos.desc: A non-heparin anticoagulant that mimics the pentasaccharide structure of heparin to augment antithrombin III activity without the risks of traditional heparin.

nodos.label: Protein C
nodos.desc: A vitamin K-dependent protein activated by thrombin-thrombomodulin interaction, which then becomes active protein C (APC) and inactivates FVa and FVIIIa.

nodos.label: Thrombomodulin
nodos.desc: A membrane glycoprotein on endothelial cells that binds thrombin and redirects it from procoagulant to anticoagulant function.

nodos.label: Protein S
nodos.desc: A cofactor that enhances the activity of activated protein C (APC) in the inactivation of FVa and FVIIIa.

nodos.label: Coagulation Hierarchy
nodos.desc: A sequential cascade of enzymatic reactions involving multiple factors, with each step regulated by inhibitors to prevent excessive clot formation.

nodos.label: Termination Mechanisms
nodos.desc: Control processes that halt coagulation cascade activity, primarily mediated by antithrombin III, protein C, and tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI).

nodos.label: Hemoglobina
nodos.desc: Proteína presente en los glóbulos rojos que transporta oxígeno desde los pulmones a las células del cuerpo.

nodos.label: Glóbulos Rojos (RBCs)
nodos.desc: Células sanguíneas que contienen hemoglobina y son responsables de transportar oxígeno a las células del cuerpo.

nodos.label: Oxigenación
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual el oxígeno se transporta desde los pulmones a las células del cuerpo por medio de la hemoglobina en los glóbulos rojos.

nodos.label: Deficiencia de Hierro
nodos.desc: Tipo de anemia causado por una falta de hierro en el cuerpo, necesario para la síntesis de hemoglobina.

nodos.label: Reticulocitos
nodos.desc: Glóbulos rojos inmaduros liberados desde la médula ósea durante la recuperación de anemias, indicando una respuesta compensatoria al déficit de glóbulos rojos.

nodos.label: Volumen Sanguíneo
nodos.desc: Cantidad total de sangre en el cuerpo, que puede reducirse en casos de pérdida sanguínea, afectando la capacidad de transporte de oxígeno.

nodos.label: Hemólisis
nodos.desc: Proceso de destrucción de glóbulos rojos, que puede aumentar la susceptibilidad a la anemia y a complicaciones como la vaso-occlusión.

nodos.label: Vaso-Occlusión
nodos.desc: Bloqueo de vasos sanguíneos por glóbulos rojos deformados, que puede provocar isquemia y daño tisular.

nodos.label: Hematocrito
nodos.desc: Porcentaje de volumen de la sangre ocupado por glóbulos rojos, utilizado como indicador de la concentración de RBCs en la sangre.

nodos.label: Hemoglobina Total
nodos.desc: Cantidad total de hemoglobina en la sangre, que se mide en g/dL y es un parámetro clave para el diagnóstico de anemias.

nodos.label: Carga de Oxígeno
nodos.desc: Capacidad de la sangre para transportar oxígeno, que depende de la concentración de hemoglobina y el número de glóbulos rojos.

nodos.label: MCV (Mean Corpuscular Volume)
nodos.desc: Measure of the average size of red blood cells; used to classify anemia types, with normocytic anemia having MCV within normal range.

nodos.label: Normocytic Anemia
nodos.desc: Anemia characterized by normal red blood cell size, with MCV within the normal range, often resulting from bone marrow suppression by drugs or other factors.

nodos.label: Megaloblastic Anemia
nodos.desc: Anemia with large but immature red blood cell precursors, caused by deficiencies in vitamin B12 or folate, leading to impaired DNA replication and erythropoiesis.

nodos.label: Macrocytic Anemia
nodos.desc: Anemia defined by enlarged red blood cells, with MCV values above 100 fL, arising from delayed RBC maturation or defective nuclear development during erythropoiesis.

nodos.label: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
nodos.desc: Deficiency leading to megaloblastic anemia, with clinical signs like neurological symptoms (numbness, tingling, memory issues), and diagnosed via serum and methylmalonic acid levels.

nodos.label: Folate Deficiency
nodos.desc: Deficiency causing megaloblastic anemia, treated with oral supplementation, and responsive to therapy with improvement in symptoms within weeks.

nodos.label: Reticulocyte Count
nodos.desc: Laboratory test measuring the number of immature red blood cells, used to assess bone marrow activity and erythropoietic function in anemia evaluation.

nodos.label: Iron Studies
nodos.desc: A set of laboratory tests assessing iron metabolism, including serum iron, ferritin, and transferrin, to evaluate iron status in anemia.

nodos.label: Bone Marrow Aspiration and Biopsy
nodos.desc: Diagnostic procedure to examine bone marrow cells and assess the nature of erythropoiesis and potential abnormalities in cell development.

nodos.label: Methylmalonic Acid
nodos.desc: A biomarker used to detect vitamin B12 deficiency, elevated levels indicating deficiency even when serum B12 appears normal.

nodos.label: Homocysteine
nodos.desc: A metabolite whose elevated levels can indicate vitamin B12 deficiency, used as a supplementary diagnostic marker in megaloblastic anemia.

nodos.label: Drug-Induced Bone Marrow Suppression
nodos.desc: Condition where chemotherapy, antiretroviral therapies, or antibiotics impair bone marrow function, leading to normocytic anemia.

nodos.label: Alcohol Abuse
nodos.desc: A cause of nonmegaloblastic macrocytic anemia due to direct toxic effects on bone marrow cells and impaired liver function.

nodos.label: Cromosómica Nueva Variación
nodos.desc: Duplicaciones o deletaciones que involucran grandes tramos de ADN conteniendo múltiples genes, que pueden aumentar la dosis de proto-oncogenes o provocar pérdida de supresores tumorales.

nodos.label: Gene MECOM
nodos.desc: Un gen amplificado en el cromosoma 3q26.2, asociado con neoplasias mieloides relacionadas con terapia y algunos AML de origen de novo.

nodos.label: Delección del brazo largo del cromosoma 5
nodos.desc: Una alteración genética característica en pacientes con síndrome de 5q, que presenta anemia macrocítica, trombocitopenia y posible progresión a AML.

nodos.label: Variante Única de Nucleótido
nodos.desc: Sustitución de un solo nucleótido que puede activar oncogenes o inactivar supresores tumorales al alterar estructura, estabilidad o regulación posttranslacional de proteínas.

nodos.label: Proteína FLT3
nodos.desc: Un receptor de tirosina quinasa cuya mutación activa puede provocar activación independiente de ligando y señalización pro-proliferativa.

nodos.label: Transcripción GATA2
nodos.desc: Un factor de transcripción clave en la especificación de linajes hematopoyéticos; mutaciones que lo inactivan perturban el programa de diferenciación y favorecen la aparición de blastos leucémicos.

nodos.label: Proteína IKZF1
nodos.desc: Factor de transcripción involucrado en la regulación de linajes hematopoyéticos; mutaciones de pérdida de función contribuyen a la leucemia.

nodos.label: Proteína ETV6
nodos.desc: Factor de transcripción importante en la diferenciación hematopoyética; mutaciones afectan el desarrollo normal y pueden inducir leucemia.

nodos.label: Proteína SF3B1
nodos.desc: Componente del mecanismo de splicing; mutaciones en este gen están asociadas a enfermedades mieloides, especialmente MDS y AML.

nodos.label: Proteína SRSF2
nodos.desc: Un componente del sistema de splicing que, cuando muta, contribuye a alteraciones en la expresión génica y a la patogénesis de leucemias mieloides.

nodos.label: Proteína U2AF1
nodos.desc: Componente del mecanismo de splicing que, cuando se muta, puede alterar la maduración de ARN y contribuir a la leucemia mielóidea.

nodos.label: Proteína ZRSR2
nodos.desc: Componente del sistema de splicing; mutaciones en este gen están vinculadas a la aparición de enfermedades mieloides.

nodos.label: Modulación Epigenética
nodos.desc: Cambios en la expresión génica sin alterar la secuencia del ADN, incluyendo remodelación del cromatina y modificaciones de histonas, que influyen en la patogénesis de la leucemia.

nodos.label: Blast Count
nodos.desc: The percentage of blast cells in bone marrow and peripheral blood, used to classify phases of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML).

nodos.label: Chronic Phase
nodos.desc: The initial stage of CML characterized by minimal symptoms, low blast count (<5%), and minimal impact on health.

nodos.label: Accelerated Phase
nodos.desc: An intermediate stage of CML with increasing symptoms like fatigue, weight loss, and splenomegaly, and blast count between 5% and 15%.

nodos.label: Blastic Crisis
nodos.desc: The terminal stage of CML where blast count exceeds 15%, leading to bone marrow failure and severe clinical deterioration.

nodos.label: Chemotherapy
nodos.desc: Treatment using drugs that target rapidly dividing cells, effective initially but often leading to relapse due to drug resistance.

nodos.label: Stem Cell Transplantation
nodos.desc: A curative option for advanced CML cases, involving replacement of diseased bone marrow with healthy stem cells from a donor.

nodos.label: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
nodos.desc: Mide el número de glóbulos rojos, blancos, plaquetas y proporciona información sobre su tamaño, forma y concentración de hemoglobina. En la anemia ferropénica, se observan valores bajos de hemoglobina, hematocrito, volumen medio de glóbulo rojo (MCV) y hemoglobina media (MCH).

nodos.label: Peripheral Smear Review
nodos.desc: Permite observar morfología de glóbulos rojos, revelando anomalías como microcitos (glóbulos rojos pequeños) y hipocromia (color pálido por baja hemoglobina). También puede detectar células con forma de diana, estippling basófilo o glóbulos rojos con núcleo, indicando diagnósticos alternativos.

nodos.label: Serum Ferritin
nodos.desc: Indica los niveles de reservas de hierro en el cuerpo. Es un reactivo agudo, por lo que aumenta en inflamación. Niveles bajos (<15 ng/mL en adultos) sugieren deficiencia de hierro, aunque niveles altos pueden indicar enfermedad crónica con anemia por enfermedad crónica (ACD).

nodos.label: Total Iron Binding Capacity (TIBC)
nodos.desc: Mide la cantidad de hierro necesario para saturar completamente la transferrina, una proteína que transporta hierro en la sangre.

nodos.label: Transferrin Saturation Percentage (TS%)
nodos.desc: Indica el porcentaje de transferrina que está saturada con hierro. En anemia ferropénica, este valor es bajo, lo que sugiere deficiencia de hierro.

nodos.label: Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV)
nodos.desc: Mide el volumen promedio de los glóbulos rojos. En la anemia ferropénica, el MCV es bajo debido a la disminución del tamaño de los glóbulos rojos.

nodos.label: Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin (MCH)
nodos.desc: Mide la cantidad promedio de hemoglobina por glóbulo rojo. En anemia ferropénica, el MCH es bajo debido a la deficiencia de hierro en los glóbulos rojos.

nodos.label: C-Reactive Protein (CRP)
nodos.desc: Una proteína inflamatoria cuya concentración aumenta en condiciones inflamatorias. Puede interferir en la interpretación de ferritina y otros marcadores de hierro.

nodos.label: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR)
nodos.desc: Una prueba de inflamación que mide la velocidad a la que se sedimentan los glóbulos rojos en un tubo. Aumenta en condiciones inflamatorias y puede confundir el diagnóstico de anemia ferropénica.

nodos.label: Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin
nodos.desc: Average hemoglobin content per red blood cell; low MCH indicates hypochromasia, commonly seen in iron deficiency anemia.

nodos.label: Poikilocytosis
nodos.desc: Variation in the size and shape of red blood cells, observed in iron deficiency anemia.

nodos.label: Transferrin Saturation
nodos.desc: Ratio of iron bound to transferrin to total transferrin; low values suggest iron deficiency, while high values may indicate acute phase reactions.

nodos.label: C-Reactive Protein
nodos.desc: Inflammatory marker; elevated levels in acute phase reactions, used to differentiate acute from chronic iron deficiency.

nodos.label: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate
nodos.desc: Non-specific marker of inflammation; increased in acute phase reactions, useful in distinguishing anemia of chronic disease from iron deficiency.

nodos.label: Oral Iron Supplementation
nodos.desc: First-line treatment for iron deficiency anemia, using ferrous sulfate or other forms for iron replenishment.

nodos.label: Parenteral Iron Administration
nodos.desc: Intravenous iron therapy used when oral iron is ineffective or contraindicated, to directly replenish iron stores.

nodos.label: Anemia of Chronic Disease
nodos.desc: Anemia caused by chronic inflammation, with preserved or elevated ferritin and normal or high transferrin saturation.

nodos.label: JAK2 mutation
nodos.desc: An activating mutation in the JAK2 gene that is present in approximately 95% of polycythemia vera cases, leading to constitutive activation of signaling pathways that promote cell proliferation.

nodos.label: CALR mutation
nodos.desc: A mutation in the calreticulin gene associated with myeloproliferative disorders, particularly essential thrombocythemia, which disrupts normal protein function and contributes to uncontrolled cell growth.

nodos.label: MPL mutation
nodos.desc: A mutation in the myeloproliferative leukemia virus oncogene (MPL) that activates signaling pathways involved in hematopoiesis, leading to clonal expansion of blood cells.

nodos.label: Tyrosine kinase activity
nodos.desc: A key enzymatic mechanism in cell signaling that regulates cell growth and division; mutations in tyrosine kinase genes can lead to uncontrolled proliferation in myeloproliferative disorders.

nodos.label: Epigenetic regulation
nodos.desc: The control of gene expression without altering DNA sequence; mutations affecting epigenetic machinery can lead to aberrant cell growth in myeloproliferative disorders.

nodos.label: Splicing machinery
nodos.desc: A cellular system responsible for processing pre-mRNA into mature mRNA; mutations in splicing factors can result in abnormal protein expression and contribute to MPDs.

nodos.label: BCR-ABL fusion protein
nodos.desc: A chimeric protein formed by the Philadelphia chromosome translocation t(9;22), which drives uncontrolled proliferation of granulocytic cells in chronic myeloid leukemia.

nodos.label: Cytopenias
nodos.desc: A reduction in the number of blood cells; commonly observed in primary myelofibrosis due to bone marrow fibrosis and impaired hematopoiesis.

nodos.label: Hyperviscosity
nodos.desc: Increased viscosity of blood due to elevated red blood cell mass, leading to impaired circulation and increased risk of thrombotic events in polycythemia vera.

nodos.label: Thromboembolism
nodos.desc: A condition where a blood clot travels to a vessel and blocks it; patients with ET and PV have an increased risk due to hypercoagulable states.

nodos.label: Megakaryocyte progenitors
nodos.desc: Precursor cells in the bone marrow that give rise to platelets; clonal expansion of these cells is central to essential thrombocythemia.

nodos.label: Erythroid cells
nodos.desc: Cells responsible for red blood cell production; abnormal proliferation in polycythemia vera leads to elevated red blood cell mass.

nodos.label: Neutrophilia
nodos.desc: An increased number of neutrophils in the peripheral blood; a defining feature of chronic neutrophilic leukemia with persistent neutrophilia above 25 x 10^9/L.

nodos.label: Eosinophilia
nodos.desc: An elevated number of eosinophils in the blood; a key feature of chronic eosinophilic leukemia and hypereosinophilic syndrome, often associated with organ damage.

nodos.label: JAK inhibitors
nodos.desc: Therapeutic agents that inhibit JAK signaling pathways, used in myeloproliferative disorders like essential thrombocytopenia and myelofibrosis, showing potential benefits in polycythemia vera by reducing disease progression.

nodos.label: Thrombocytosis
nodos.desc: Condition characterized by elevated platelet counts, a hallmark of essential thrombocythemia, which can lead to both bleeding and thrombotic complications due to abnormal platelet activity.

nodos.label: Myeloproliferative disorders
nodos.desc: A group of hematologic conditions involving overproduction of blood cells, including essential thrombocytopenia and polycythemia vera, driven by genetic mutations and dysregulated signaling pathways.

nodos.label: Adverse reactions
nodos.desc: Side effects associated with therapies like interferon alpha, which are more severe than those of hydroxyurea, affecting patient tolerability and long-term use.

nodos.label: Long-term risks
nodos.desc: Persistent health threats such as leukemic transformation or secondary myelofibrosis, which may occur in patients with untreated or poorly managed myeloproliferative disorders.

nodos.label: Regulación de concentración hormonal
nodos.desc: Proceso que implica biosíntesis, transporte, interacción con receptores y mecanismos de retroalimentación negativa para mantener niveles hormonales estables.

nodos.label: Eje hipotálamo-pituitario-tiroideo
nodos.desc: Sistema endocrino que regula el crecimiento, desarrollo y tasa metabólica mediante la liberación de TRH y TSH, con retroalimentación negativa de T3 y T4.

nodos.label: Eje hipotálamo-pituitario-adrenal
nodos.desc: Sistema que regula respuestas al estrés y la regulación de glucocorticoides mediante retroalimentación negativa de cortisol.

nodos.label: Retroalimentación negativa autocrina
nodos.desc: Mecanismo en el que las células secretan una sustancia que inhibe su propia producción, como ocurre con la insulina en células beta del páncreas.

nodos.label: Clasificación de hormonas
nodos.desc: Categorización de hormonas según su estructura química y función, incluyendo hormonas derivadas de aminoácidos, péptidos, esteroideas, eicosanoides.

nodos.label: Punto de referencia
nodos.desc: Valor óptimo o nivel estable que un sistema biológico busca mantener, y que sirve como punto de comparación para detectar desviaciones en la regulación hormonal.

nodos.label: Control homeostático
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual los sistemas biológicos mantienen condiciones internas estables a pesar de cambios externos, utilizando mecanismos como la retroalimentación negativa.

nodos.label: Effector Response
nodos.desc: The final biological outcome of hormone action, resulting in measurable changes in cell or tissue function, such as altered metabolism or gene expression.

nodos.label: Mevalonate Pathway
nodos.desc: A metabolic pathway that converts acetyl coenzyme A into isopentenyl pyrophosphate (IPP), a key building block for terpene hormones.

nodos.label: Isopentenyl Pyrophosphate (IPP)
nodos.desc: A five-carbon molecule that serves as a fundamental precursor in the biosynthesis of terpene hormones.

nodos.label: Terpene Classification
nodos.desc: A system that categorizes terpene hormones based on the number of IPP units they contain: monoterpenes (2), sesquiterpenes (3), diterpenes (4), triterpenes (6), tetraterpenes (8).

nodos.label: Cellular Mechanism of Hormone Action
nodos.desc: A three-stage process involving hormone-receptor binding, signal transduction, and effector response, which regulates physiological functions like metabolism and growth.

nodos.label: Hypothalamus
nodos.desc: Un núcleo en el cerebro que integra señales del sistema nervioso y del sistema endocrino, regulando funciones como el estado de ánimo, la motivación, el apetito, el sueño y las funciones reproductivas.

nodos.label: Cortisol
nodos.desc: Hormona producida por las glándulas suprarrenales que aumenta la alerta, libera energía y mejora la recuerdo, pero niveles crónicos pueden causar problemas de salud física y mental como hipertensión, diabetes y depresión.

nodos.label: Adrenaline
nodos.desc: Hormona liberada por las glándulas suprarrenales que activa la respuesta de lucha o huida, aumentando la frecuencia cardíaca, la presión arterial y la atención.

nodos.label: Sistema endocrino
nodos.desc: Red de glándulas que producen hormonas que regulan funciones fisiológicas y comportamentales, integradas con el sistema nervioso para responder a estímulos internos y externos.

nodos.label: Sistema nervioso
nodos.desc: Red de neuronas que procesa estímulos externos e internos y coordina respuestas fisiológicas y conductuales mediante señales eléctricas y químicas.

nodos.label: Hyperglycemia
nodos.desc: Estado de elevación de los niveles de glucosa en la sangre.

nodos.label: Blood Glucose
nodos.desc: Nivel de glucosa en la sangre, un indicador clave de la función metabólica y del control glucémico.

nodos.label: Glucose Levels
nodos.desc: Medición de la concentración de glucosa en la sangre, utilizada para diagnosticar y monitorear diabetes.

nodos.label: Metabolic Disorder
nodos.desc: Trastorno en los procesos metabólicos del cuerpo, como la regulación de la glucosa.

nodos.label: Insulin Deficiency
nodos.desc: Condition where the body does not produce enough insulin, leading to elevated blood glucose levels.

nodos.label: Type 2 Diabetes
nodos.desc: A chronic condition characterized by insulin resistance and relative insulin deficiency, often associated with obesity and sedentary lifestyle.

nodos.label: Gestational Diabetes
nodos.desc: A form of diabetes that develops during pregnancy due to hormonal changes that impair insulin action, typically resolving after childbirth.

nodos.label: Beta Cells
nodos.desc: Cells in the pancreas that produce and secrete insulin; their destruction in Type 1 diabetes leads to insulin deficiency.

nodos.label: Autoimmune Disease
nodos.desc: A condition where the body's immune system attacks its own tissues, such as the beta cells in the pancreas in Type 1 diabetes.

nodos.label: Milligrams per deciliter
nodos.desc: Unit of measurement for blood glucose concentration, commonly used in diabetes diagnostics.

nodos.label: Fasting Glucose
nodos.desc: Blood glucose level measured after an overnight fast; impaired fasting glucose (100–125 mg/dL) indicates prediabetes.

nodos.label: Oral Glucose Tolerance Test
nodos.desc: A diagnostic test involving consumption of a 75-gram glucose solution, followed by serial plasma glucose measurements over two hours.

nodos.label: Biphasic Glucose Response
nodos.desc: A normal glucose response pattern showing an initial peak within the first hour followed by a rapid decline due to insulin release.

nodos.label: Impaired Glucose Tolerance
nodos.desc: A prediabetic state characterized by delayed glucose clearance, with values below diabetic thresholds.

nodos.label: Hemoglobin A1c
nodos.desc: A biomarker reflecting average blood glucose levels over the past 8–12 weeks, based on glucose binding to hemoglobin.

nodos.label: Insulin Therapy
nodos.desc: Treatment approach for Type I diabetes, involving exogenous insulin administration due to the body's inability to produce insulin naturally.

nodos.label: Hepatic Gluconeogenesis
nodos.desc: The metabolic process in the liver where glucose is synthesized from non-carbohydrate precursors, relevant to basal glucose regulation.

nodos.label: Postprandial Hyperglycemia
nodos.desc: Elevated blood glucose levels after meals, more commonly associated with type 2 diabetes and a limitation of fasting glucose tests.

nodos.label: Red Blood Cell Turnover
nodos.desc: The rate at which red blood cells are produced and replaced; affects HbA1c accuracy due to variations in hemoglobin lifespan.

nodos.label: Insulin Resistance
nodos.desc: A condition in which cells do not respond effectively to insulin, leading to elevated blood glucose levels.

nodos.label: Glycemic Control
nodos.desc: The management of blood glucose levels to prevent complications in diabetes, often measured by HbA1c.

nodos.label: Dyslipidemia
nodos.desc: Abnormal levels of lipids (fats) in the blood, such as high cholesterol or triglycerides, which increase cardiovascular risk.

nodos.label: Cardiovascular Risk
nodos.desc: The probability of developing heart disease or stroke, which is elevated in individuals with type II diabetes.

nodos.label: Tobacco Use
nodos.desc: A modifiable risk factor that increases cardiovascular and metabolic complications in diabetes patients.

nodos.label: Medication Classes
nodos.desc: Categories of drugs used to treat type II diabetes, such as SGLT-2 inhibitors and thiazolidinediones, each with distinct mechanisms and risks.

nodos.label: Basal Insulin
nodos.desc: A type of insulin that provides a background level of insulin throughout the day to manage fasting glucose levels.

nodos.label: Prandial Insulin
nodos.desc: Insulin administered before meals to manage postprandial (after-meal) blood glucose spikes.

nodos.label: Self-Monitoring of Blood Glucose
nodos.desc: A practice where patients measure their own blood glucose levels to adjust medication and lifestyle interventions.

nodos.label: Hypoglycemia
nodos.desc: A condition of abnormally low blood glucose levels, which can be dangerous and requires prompt recognition and treatment.

nodos.label: Blood Glucose Level
nodos.desc: A measure of the amount of glucose in the blood, typically expressed in mg/dL; extremely high levels are a key feature of Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic Nonketotic State (HHNS).

nodos.label: Hyperosmolar State
nodos.desc: A condition characterized by extremely high blood sugar levels and significant dehydration, resulting in elevated osmotic pressure in the blood, commonly seen in HHNS.

nodos.label: Counterregulatory Hormones
nodos.desc: Hormones such as cortisol and glucagon that oppose insulin action and increase blood glucose levels during stress, such as illness or infection.

nodos.label: Liver Glucose Production
nodos.desc: The process by which the liver releases stored glucose into the bloodstream in response to hormonal signals, contributing to hyperglycemia in HHNS.

nodos.label: Vital Signs
nodos.desc: Basic physiological measurements such as temperature, heart rate, respiration rate, and blood pressure, used to monitor the body's response to therapy and detect complications early.

nodos.label: Neurologic Status
nodos.desc: The assessment of brain function and neurological health, including mental status, reflexes, and consciousness, critical for detecting complications in diabetes-related conditions.

nodos.label: Laboratory Evaluations
nodos.desc: Serial blood tests used to monitor glucose, electrolyte, and other biomarkers to assess disease progression and treatment response.

nodos.label: Acute Complication
nodos.desc: A sudden and severe medical condition that can rapidly progress and threaten life, such as diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or HHNS, requiring immediate intervention.

nodos.label: Sick Day Guidelines
nodos.desc: Protocols for managing diabetes during illness, including adjustments to diet, medication, and monitoring frequency to prevent complications like HHNS or DKA.

nodos.label: Renal Failure
nodos.desc: Etapa final de la diabetes nefrótica, caracterizada por una disminución significativa de la tasa de filtración glomerular (GFR).

nodos.label: Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)
nodos.desc: Métrica que indica la eficacia de los riñones para filtrar desechos del sangre; un GFR bajo indica función renal comprometida.

nodos.label: ACE Inhibitors
nodos.desc: Medicamentos que bloquean la acción de angiotensina II, dilatando vasos sanguíneos y reduciendo la pérdida de proteínas en orina y la presión arterial.

nodos.label: ARBs
nodos.desc: Inhibidores de receptores de angiotensina que actúan de forma similar a los ACE inhibitors, reduciendo la presión arterial y la pérdida de proteínas urinarias.

nodos.label: Kidney Transplantation
nodos.desc: Procedimiento quirúrgico que consiste en reemplazar el riñón dañado por un riñón donado, mejorando la supervivencia y calidad de vida en pacientes con DN severa.

nodos.label: Percutaneous Transluminal Renal Angioplasty (PTRA)
nodos.desc: Procedimiento quirúrgico percutáneo que dilata arterias bloqueadas en los riñones para mejorar la función renal, aunque con riesgos como hemorragia e infección.

nodos.label: Fibra aferente
nodos.desc: Fibra nerviosa que transmite información sensorial desde el periférico al sistema nervioso central.

nodos.label: Fibra eferente
nodos.desc: Fibra nerviosa que transmite órdenes motoras desde el sistema nervioso central a músculos y glándulas.

nodos.label: Neurona intermedia
nodos.desc: Neurona que se encuentra dentro del sistema nervioso central y que integra y modula la información entre fibras aferentes y eferentes.

nodos.label: Tracto de la columna dorsal
nodos.desc: Bucle de fibras nerviosas que transporta información sensorial fina, vibración y propiosensación desde el tronco y extremidades hacia el cerebro.

nodos.label: Medial lemniscus
nodos.desc: Parte del tracto de la columna dorsal que transmite información sensorial de los miembros superiores y tórax.

nodos.label: Fasciculus gracilis
nodos.desc: Parte del tracto de la columna dorsal que transmite información sensorial de las extremidades inferiores y tórax.

nodos.label: Decusación
nodos.desc: Cruce de fibras nerviosas en el sistema nervioso central, que ocurre en el nivel de la médula espinal y permite la proyección de señales hacia el cerebro.

nodos.label: Ependymal Cell
nodos.desc: Cell type that lines the ventricles of the brain and spinal cord, secreting cerebrospinal fluid and aiding in its circulation via ciliary motion.

nodos.label: Cerebrospinal Fluid
nodos.desc: Protective fluid in the CNS that cushions the brain and spinal cord, provides buoyancy, and aids in nutrient distribution and waste removal.

nodos.label: Myelin Sheath
nodos.desc: Insulating layer around axons produced by oligodendrocytes that enhances the speed and efficiency of neural signal transmission.

nodos.label: Calcium Wave
nodos.desc: A signaling mechanism in astrocytes that facilitates coordination of neuronal activity through intercellular calcium propagation.

nodos.label: Extracellular Environment
nodos.desc: The space outside neurons where ion concentrations, neurotransmitters, and metabolic factors are regulated by glial cells.

nodos.label: Neurological Dysfunction
