nodos.desc: Impaired function of the nervous system resulting from damage to glial cells or myelin sheaths, as seen in diseases like Multiple Sclerosis.

nodos.label: Intracranial Pressure
nodos.desc: Pressure within the skull, maintained by cerebrospinal fluid circulation, which is critical for brain stability and function.

nodos.label: Cerebrospinal Fluid
nodos.desc: A clear, colorless fluid that surrounds the brain and spinal cord, providing buoyancy, protection, and a medium for molecular exchange.

nodos.label: Ependymal Cells
nodos.desc: Glial cells lining the ventricles of the brain that produce and regulate cerebrospinal fluid, and facilitate its flow through ciliary motility.

nodos.label: Hydrocephalus
nodos.desc: A pathological condition characterized by the abnormal accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid in the brain ventricles, leading to increased intracranial pressure and neurological impairment.

nodos.label: Meningitis
nodos.desc: An inflammatory condition of the meninges, often caused by infection, which can damage ependymal cells and disrupt the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier.

nodos.label: Myelin
nodos.desc: A fatty substance that insulates axons of neurons, enabling rapid transmission of nerve impulses; produced by oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system.

nodos.label: Oligodendrocytes
nodos.desc: Glial cells in the central nervous system that produce myelin sheaths to insulate axons and enhance the speed of neural signal conduction.

nodos.label: Blood-Cerebrospinal Fluid Barrier
nodos.desc: A selective barrier formed by ependymal cells and capillary endothelial cells that regulates the passage of substances between the bloodstream and cerebrospinal fluid.

nodos.label: Nerve Growth Factor
nodos.desc: A protein released by Schwann cells that supports the survival, differentiation, maturation, and functional maintenance of neurons.

nodos.label: Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor
nodos.desc: A neurotrophic factor released by Schwann cells that promotes neuronal survival and function.

nodos.label: Ciliary Neurotrophic Factor
nodos.desc: A growth factor released by Schwann cells that contributes to neuronal survival and development.

nodos.label: Major Histocompatibility Complex Class II
nodos.desc: Molecules expressed by Schwann cells that enable antigen presentation and immune modulation during inflammation.

nodos.label: Dedifferentiation
nodos.desc: A process where Schwann cells revert to a progenitor-like state after injury, enabling proliferation and migration to repair sites.

nodos.label: Regenerative Capacity
nodos.desc: The ability of Schwann cells to divide, migrate, and redifferentiate to reform myelin sheaths following nerve damage.

nodos.label: Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease
nodos.desc: An inherited peripheral neuropathy caused by mutations in genes affecting myelinating or non-myelinating Schwann cells, leading to demyelination and impaired nerve conduction.

nodos.label: Guillain-Barré Syndrome
nodos.desc: An autoimmune disorder triggered by infections, where antibodies attack gangliosides on Schwann cells, leading to demyelination and acute polyneuropathy.

nodos.label: Schwannoma
nodos.desc: A benign tumor arising from Schwann cells, often visible on imaging with heterogeneous enhancement due to cystic, hemorrhagic, or calcified components.

nodos.label: Demyelination
nodos.desc: Loss of the myelin sheath around axons, impairing nerve conduction and leading to neurological deficits in conditions like CMT and GBS.

nodos.label: Nerve Conduction Velocity
nodos.desc: A measure of how fast nerve impulses travel; reduced in CMT due to demyelination or impaired remyelination.

nodos.label: Gangliosides
nodos.desc: Glycolipids concentrated in peripheral nerves that are targeted by autoantibodies in GBS, leading to Schwann cell damage and demyelination.

nodos.label: Complement Cascade
nodos.desc: A series of immune reactions triggered by antibody-ganglioside interactions in GBS, resulting in destruction of the myelin sheath.

nodos.label: Synapse
nodos.desc: The junction where two neurons communicate, consisting of a synaptic cleft that separates the presynaptic terminal from the postsynaptic membrane.

nodos.label: Synaptic Cleft
nodos.desc: The small gap between the presynaptic and postsynaptic neurons, typically 20 nanometers wide at rest and narrowing to as little as 5 nanometers during transmission.

nodos.label: Receptor
nodos.desc: A protein on the postsynaptic membrane that binds to neurotransmitters, modulating the generation of action potentials in the postsynaptic neuron.

nodos.label: Excitatory Neurotransmitter
nodos.desc: A neurotransmitter that increases the likelihood of an action potential in the postsynaptic neuron, such as glutamate.

nodos.label: Inhibitory Neurotransmitter
nodos.desc: A neurotransmitter that decreases the likelihood of an action potential in the postsynaptic neuron, such as GABA.

nodos.label: Neural Signaling
nodos.desc: The process by which neurons communicate via electrical and chemical signals across synapses.

nodos.label: Neurological Disorder
nodos.desc: A condition resulting from dysregulation of neuronal signaling, such as epilepsy, Parkinson's disease, or Alzheimer's disease.

nodos.label: Nanometer
nodos.desc: A unit of length equal to 10^-9 meters, used to measure the width of the synaptic cleft.

nodos.label: Transportador
nodos.desc: Proteína transmembrana que facilita el movimiento activo de molé- culas o iones contra su gradiente de concentración, como en el caso de la reuptake de neurotransmisores.

nodos.label: Distribución espacial
nodos.desc: Forma en que una sustancia se distribuye en el espacio, como el neurotransmisor en el espacio sináptico, que afecta la eficacia de la señal neuronal.

nodos.label: Selección de substrato
nodos.desc: Capacidad de los transportadores para reconocer y transportar específicamente ciertas clases de neurotransmisores, según sus estructuras químicas.

nodos.label: Diferencia de concentración
nodos.desc: Variación en la cantidad de una sustancia en diferentes regiones, que impulsa el movimiento por difusión en el espacio sináptico.

nodos.label: Degradación enzimática
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que enzimas descomponen los neurotransmisores en el espacio sináptico, eliminándolos de forma activa y específica.

nodos.label: Terminación de la transmisión
nodos.desc: Mecanismo que asegura que la señal neuronal se detenga después de su activación, evitando una respuesta prolongada en el neuronas postsinápticas.

nodos.label: Mecanismo orquestado
nodos.desc: Serie de interacciones moleculares coordinadas que regulan la liberación, acción y eliminación de neurotransmisores para garantizar la precisión del proceso de comunicación neuronal.

nodos.label: Firing Rates
nodos.desc: The rate at which neurons generate action potentials, influencing network dynamics and overall brain function.

nodos.label: GABAergic Transmission
nodos.desc: Neurotransmission mediated by gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system.

nodos.label: Glutamatergic Neurons
nodos.desc: Neurons that use glutamate as their primary neurotransmitter, typically associated with excitatory signaling.

nodos.label: Cytoplasmic Cl⁻ Concentration
nodos.desc: The concentration of chloride ions inside neurons, which determines the polarity of GABAergic responses.

nodos.label: Na⁺-K⁺-Cl⁻ Cotransporter
nodos.desc: A membrane protein that regulates intracellular chloride concentration by transporting Cl⁻ into the cell.

nodos.label: K⁺-Cl⁻ Symporter
nodos.desc: A transporter that moves K⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in equal amounts, contributing to the reduction of intracellular Cl⁻ levels.

nodos.label: Neuronal Polarity
nodos.desc: The direction of neuronal response to neurotransmitters (excitatory or inhibitory) based on ion gradients and receptor properties.

nodos.label: Monoamines
nodos.desc: A class of small-molecule neurotransmitters including dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine, histamine, and melatonin.

nodos.label: Dopamine Receptors
nodos.desc: Five distinct receptor subtypes that bind dopamine and mediate its effects on neuronal activity, involved in reward, motivation, and learning.

nodos.label: Neurotransmitter Homeostasis
nodos.desc: The balanced regulation of neurotransmitter levels and activity in the brain to maintain normal physiological function.

nodos.label: Voltage-Gated Ca²⁺ Channels
nodos.desc: Ion channels that open in response to membrane depolarization, allowing Ca²⁺ influx to trigger neurotransmitter release.

nodos.label: Vesicular Release
nodos.desc: The process by which neurotransmitters are released from synaptic vesicles into the synaptic cleft via exocytosis.

nodos.label: Neuronal Connectivity
nodos.desc: The pattern of connections between neurons, which influences information processing and network stability in the brain.

nodos.label: N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor
nodos.desc: A type of ionotropic glutamate receptor that requires simultaneous binding of glutamate and glycine, along with membrane depolarization, to open its channel. It plays a key role in synaptic plasticity, long-term potentiation (LTP), and long-term depression (LTD), and is involved in learning and memory.

nodos.label: Gamma-aminobutyric Acid Type B Receptor
nodos.desc: A G protein-coupled receptor that mediates inhibitory neurotransmission in the brain, distinct from GABA_A receptors which are ligand-gated ion channels.

nodos.label: Ionotropic receptor
nodos.desc: A receptor that forms ion channels and allows rapid ion flux upon neurotransmitter binding, such as AMPA, kainate, and NMDARs.

nodos.label: Anionic ion channel
nodos.desc: An ion channel that conducts chloride ions (Cl^-) instead of cations, primarily involved in neural inhibition and regulation of neuronal excitability.

nodos.label: Neurological disorders
nodos.desc: Conditions such as epilepsy, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, and stroke that are linked to dysregulation of neurotransmitter systems like NMDARs and GABA_B receptors.

nodos.label: Resting Potential
nodos.desc: The electrical potential difference across the neuronal membrane when the neuron is at rest, typically around -70 mV, determined by ion permeabilities and concentrations.

nodos.label: Potassium Permeability Coefficient
nodos.desc: A measure of how easily potassium ions pass through the membrane, influencing the resting potential.

nodos.label: Sodium Permeability Coefficient
nodos.desc: A measure of how easily sodium ions pass through the membrane, contributing to the resting potential.

nodos.label: Chloride Permeability Coefficient
nodos.desc: A measure of how easily chloride ions pass through the membrane, affecting the resting potential.

nodos.label: Extracellular Potassium Concentration
nodos.desc: The concentration of potassium ions outside the cell, typically around 5 mM.

nodos.label: Intracellular Potassium Concentration
nodos.desc: The concentration of potassium ions inside the cell, typically around 140 mM.

nodos.label: Extracellular Sodium Concentration
nodos.desc: The concentration of sodium ions outside the cell, influencing the resting potential.

nodos.label: Intracellular Sodium Concentration
nodos.desc: The concentration of sodium ions inside the cell, contributing to ion gradients.

nodos.label: Intracellular Chloride Concentration
nodos.desc: The concentration of chloride ions inside the cell, affecting membrane potential.

nodos.label: Extracellular Chloride Concentration
nodos.desc: The concentration of chloride ions outside the cell, influencing ion balance.

nodos.label: Nernst Potential for Potassium
nodos.desc: The equilibrium potential for potassium ions, calculated using the Nernst equation, approximately -90 mV at room temperature.

nodos.label: Nernst Equation
nodos.desc: A mathematical equation that calculates the equilibrium potential of an ion based on concentration gradients and temperature.

nodos.label: Goldman Equation
nodos.desc: A mathematical model that calculates the resting potential based on ion permeabilities and concentrations.

nodos.label: Electrochemical Gradient
nodos.desc: The combined effect of concentration and electrical potential differences that drive ion movement across the membrane.

nodos.label: Passive Diffusion
nodos.desc: The movement of ions across the membrane due to concentration and electrical gradients without energy input.

nodos.label: Active Transport
nodos.desc: The energy-dependent movement of ions across the membrane, primarily mediated by ion pumps like the Na+/K+ ATPase.

nodos.label: Leak Channels
nodos.desc: Ion channels that allow passive ion flow through the membrane, contributing to the resting potential.

nodos.label: Dynamic Steady State
nodos.desc: A state where ion fluxes are balanced over time, resulting in a stable resting potential despite continuous ion exchange.

nodos.label: Bursting
nodos.desc: Activación repetida de potenciales de acción en clusters de alta frecuencia separados por periodos silenciosos, que puede representar unidades de codificación distintas a los spikes individuales y está asociado con funciones como la regulación respiratoria y condiciones patológicas como el epilépsia.

nodos.label: Oscillations
nodos.desc: Ritmos coherentes de actividad en poblaciones de neuronas interconectadas, generados por interacciones recurrentes entre neuronas excitatorias e inhibitorias, manifestándose en frecuencias específicas como gamma (30–80 Hz), beta (15–30 Hz), alpha (8–15 Hz), theta (4–7 Hz), y delta (<4 Hz), y que subyacen a funciones cognitivas como la atención, la memoria y el sueño.

nodos.label: Plasticidad
nodos.desc: Modificación de la fuerza sináptica y la conectividad basada en experiencias, incluyendo el aprendizaje hebbiano, en el que las neuronas que se activan juntas tienden a conectarse más fuertemente.

nodos.label: Weber's Law
nodos.desc: A principle in sensory perception stating that the just-noticeable difference (JND) of a stimulus is a constant proportion of the original stimulus intensity, expressed as ΔI/I = k, where k is a constant specific to each sense.

nodos.label: Rhodopsin
nodos.desc: A photopigment in the retina of the eye that absorbs light and initiates the visual signal cascade; its regeneration during dark adaptation is essential for restoring vision in low-light conditions.

nodos.label: Sensory Adaptation
nodos.desc: The process by which sensory receptors reduce their response to a constant stimulus over time, allowing the nervous system to focus on changes rather than static inputs.

nodos.label: Mechanoreceptors
nodos.desc: Sensory receptors that respond to mechanical forces such as pressure, vibration, or deformation; examples include Merkel cells and Pacinian corpuscles.

nodos.label: Hair Bundles
nodos.desc: Structures in auditory hair cells composed of stereocilia arranged in rows of decreasing height; their bending in response to sound waves triggers ion channel activation and neurotransmitter release.

nodos.label: Neurotransmitter Release
nodos.desc: The process by which neurons release chemical messengers at synapses to transmit signals; in sensory systems, this occurs in response to receptor activation and is modulated by adaptation.

nodos.label: Hit Rate (HR)
nodos.desc: The proportion of actual signals that were correctly detected out of all signals presented.

nodos.label: False Alarm Rate (FAR)
nodos.desc: The proportion of times a signal was incorrectly reported when no signal existed.

nodos.label: Criterion (β)
nodos.desc: The level of evidence required before concluding that a signal is present; higher values indicate more conservative responses, lower values indicate liberal responding.

nodos.label: Signal Detection Theory (SDT)
nodos.desc: A mathematical framework for analyzing the ability to detect a signal in the presence of noise, based on outcomes like hits, false alarms, correct rejections, and misses.

nodos.label: Bottom-up Processing
nodos.desc: A process in which raw sensory data from the environment is converted into neural signals, forming the basis of perception.

nodos.label: Top-down Processing
nodos.desc: A cognitive process that uses higher-level knowledge and expectations to interpret sensory signals, influencing perception.

nodos.label: Principle of Similarity
nodos.desc: The tendency of the brain to group objects that share common features such as color, shape, or size to form coherent patterns.

nodos.label: Principle of Proximity
nodos.desc: The perception that objects close to each other are grouped together, even without shared features, aiding in organizing visual clutter.

nodos.label: Principle of Continuity
nodos.desc: The brain's tendency to perceive lines or curves as continuing smoothly beyond their actual endpoints, facilitating the tracking of motion and prediction of trajectories.

nodos.label: Principle of Closure
nodos.desc: The brain's ability to fill in missing parts of a shape or pattern, perceiving complete forms even when elements are absent.

nodos.label: Phototransduction
nodos.desc: El proceso mediante el cual la energía luminosa se convierte en señales eléctricas en la retina del ojo, permitiendo la percepción de estímulos visuales.

nodos.label: Opsin
nodos.desc: Una proteína transmembrana que actúa como receptor G proteína acoplado (GPCR) en la rhodopsina.

nodos.label: Retinal
nodos.desc: Un cofactor derivado de la vitamina A que, al absorber una fotón, se isomeriza y desencadena una cascada de reacciones.

nodos.label: Transducin
nodos.desc: Proteína G que se activa al ser liberada de la rhodopsina y que regula la actividad de la fosfodiesterasa.

nodos.label: cGMP
nodos.desc: Un segundo mensajero que se hidroliza a GMP cuando se activa la fosfodiesterasa, lo que lleva a la apertura o cierre de canales iónicos.

nodos.label: PDE6
nodos.desc: Fosfodiesterasa que se activa por transducin y que hidroliza cGMP a GMP, reduciendo así los niveles de cGMP en la célula.

nodos.label: Hyperpolarization
nodos.desc: Cambio en el potencial de membrana de la célula rodas que ocurre cuando los canales iónicos se cierran, reduciendo el flujo de sodio.

nodos.label: Molecular Cascade
nodos.desc: Secuencia de reacciones bioquímicas que comienza con la absorción de luz y termina en la generación de una señal eléctrica en la retina.

nodos.label: Lateral Inhibition
nodos.desc: A neural process where neighboring neurons suppress each other's output, enhancing contrast and salience in sensory perception, particularly in visual and tactile processing.

nodos.label: Edge Enhancement
nodos.desc: A sensory phenomenon where lateral inhibition sharpens boundaries between different regions, improving the detection of edges in visual stimuli.

nodos.label: Tactile Acuity
nodos.desc: The ability to detect fine differences in texture or surface patterns through touch, refined by lateral inhibition in peripheral tissues.

nodos.label: Somatosensory Homunculus
nodos.desc: A neural map representing the relative size of brain areas dedicated to processing sensory inputs from different body regions, with size reflecting sensory importance.

nodos.label: Neural Threshold
nodos.desc: The minimum level of stimulation required to trigger a neuron's response; lateral inhibition modulates this threshold in neighboring neurons.

nodos.label: Homeostatic Balance
nodos.desc: The stable internal condition maintained by the nervous system, crucial for proper sensory processing and preventing pathological conditions.

nodos.label: Dopamine
nodos.desc: A neurotransmitter that plays a key role in motor control and coordination, whose reduced levels are associated with Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Substantia Nigra
nodos.desc: A region in the midbrain responsible for regulating motor control and coordination, where dopamine-producing cells are located.

nodos.label: Neurodegenerative Disorder
nodos.desc: A condition characterized by the progressive loss of neurons, leading to deterioration of neurological functions, as seen in Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Aging
nodos.desc: A significant risk factor for Parkinson's disease, with the majority of cases diagnosed in individuals over the age of 60.

nodos.label: Progressive Disease
nodos.desc: A condition that worsens over time, with symptoms starting mildly and gradually intensifying over several years.

nodos.label: Basal Ganglia
nodos.desc: A group of interconnected nuclei located deep within the forebrain that play a crucial role in regulating movement and coordination through connections with the cerebral cortex and thalamus.

nodos.label: Direct Pathway
nodos.desc: A neural circuit within the basal ganglia that contributes to the facilitation of movement by transmitting signals from the cerebral cortex to the thalamus.

nodos.label: Musculoskeletal Pain
nodos.desc: Pain arising from muscle stiffness or cramping, commonly reported by Parkinson's disease patients.

nodos.label: Radicular Pain
nodos.desc: Pain that radiates from the spine down the limbs, often due to nerve compression or irritation.

nodos.label: Central Neuropathic Pain
nodos.desc: Pain originating from damage to the brain or spinal cord, a non-motor symptom in Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Akathisia
nodos.desc: An intense inner restlessness causing discomfort and distress when sitting or lying down, a unique symptom in Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Olfactory Hallucinations
nodos.desc: The perception of smells that are not present, a sensory disturbance observed in some Parkinson's patients.

nodos.label: Tactile Hallucinations
nodos.desc: The sensation of feeling things crawling on the skin, a sensory disturbance in Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Formication
nodos.desc: The sensation of bugs burrowing under the skin, a common sensory disturbance in Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Insomnia
nodos.desc: Difficulty falling or staying asleep, a common sleep disorder in Parkinson's disease patients.

nodos.label: Excessive Daytime Sleepiness
nodos.desc: A state of prolonged drowsiness during the day, frequently reported in Parkinson's disease patients.

nodos.label: REM Sleep Behavior Disorder
nodos.desc: A condition where individuals act out their dreams during REM sleep, linked to increased risk of synucleinopathies like Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Periodic Leg Movements
nodos.desc: Repetitive movements of the legs during sleep, a common sleep disturbance in Parkinson's patients.

nodos.label: Restless Legs Syndrome
nodos.desc: An uncomfortable sensation in the legs that causes an irresistible urge to move, often disrupting sleep in Parkinson's patients.

nodos.label: Striatum
nodos.desc: A region of the basal ganglia that receives inputs from the cortex and sends GABAergic projections to the globus pallidus externa (GPe).

nodos.label: Globus Pallidus Externa
nodos.desc: A structure that receives inhibitory GABAergic input from the striatum and provides excitatory glutamatergic input to the subthalamic nucleus (STN).

nodos.label: Subthalamic Nucleus
nodos.desc: A nucleus that receives excitatory glutamatergic input from the GPe and projects to the globus pallidus pars interna (GPi), playing a key role in motor control regulation.

nodos.label: Globus Pallidus Pars Interna
nodos.desc: A major output nucleus of the basal ganglia that receives excitatory input from the STN and inhibits thalamocortical circuits, modulating motor output.

nodos.label: GABAergic Projections
nodos.desc: Neural pathways that use gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) as a neurotransmitter to provide inhibitory control in the basal ganglia.

nodos.label: Glutamatergic Projections
nodos.desc: Neural pathways that use glutamate as a neurotransmitter to provide excitatory control in the basal ganglia.

nodos.label: Thalamocortical Network
nodos.desc: A network connecting the thalamus to the cerebral cortex, which is modulated by basal ganglia output to regulate motor coordination.

nodos.label: Motor Impairment
nodos.desc: A pathological outcome resulting from dysregulation of the indirect pathway, particularly in Parkinson's disease, leading to abnormal motor function.

nodos.label: Alpha-synuclein
nodos.desc: A protein that, when misfolded or aggregated, forms Lewy bodies, which are pathological hallmarks in Parkinson's disease and are associated with the degeneration of dopamine-producing neurons.

nodos.label: SNCA gene
nodos.desc: The gene encoding alpha-synuclein; mutations such as point mutations, duplications, and triplications increase alpha-synuclein levels and elevate the risk of developing Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: LRRK2 gene
nodos.desc: A gene encoding a kinase protein involved in autophagy, vesicle trafficking, and cytoskeleton dynamics; mutations disrupt cellular functions and increase oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction.

nodos.label: PRKN gene
nodos.desc: Encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase that facilitates protein degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome system; loss-of-function mutations lead to protein accumulation and dopaminergic neuron degeneration.

nodos.label: PINK1 gene
nodos.desc: Involved in mitochondrial quality control and the mitophagy pathway; mutations impair mitochondrial function and contribute to neuronal death.

nodos.label: DJ-1 gene
nodos.desc: Encodes a protein that acts as an antioxidant and protects against oxidative stress; mutations increase susceptibility to Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: ATP13A2 gene
nodos.desc: Encodes a protein involved in lysosomal function; mutations impair lysosomal activity and contribute to protein aggregation and neuronal death.

nodos.label: FBXO7 gene
nodos.desc: Part of the ubiquitin-proteasome system; mutations affect protein degradation and are linked to Parkinson's disease pathogenesis.

nodos.label: VPS35 gene
nodos.desc: Involved in vesicle trafficking and endosomal sorting; mutations disrupt cellular transport and are associated with Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: CHCHD2 gene
nodos.desc: Encodes a mitochondrial protein involved in mitochondrial dynamics and function; mutations are linked to Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: DNAJC13 gene
nodos.desc: Regulates protein folding and quality control; mutations may disrupt cellular homeostasis and contribute to Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: SYNJ1 gene
nodos.desc: Encodes a protein involved in synaptic vesicle trafficking; mutations affect synaptic transmission and are associated with Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: GBA gene
nodos.desc: Encodes glucocerebrosidase, an enzyme involved in lysosomal function; variants increase risk of both sporadic and familial Parkinson's disease, especially in Ashkenazi Jewish populations.

nodos.label: Ubiquitin-proteasome system
nodos.desc: A cellular pathway that tags proteins for degradation; dysfunction in this system leads to accumulation of damaged proteins and neurodegeneration.

nodos.label: Mitochondrial dysfunction
nodos.desc: Impaired mitochondrial function reduces energy production and increases oxidative stress, contributing to dopaminergic neuron death in Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Oxidative stress
nodos.desc: An imbalance between reactive oxygen species and antioxidant defenses; elevated oxidative stress damages cellular components and is a key factor in Parkinson's disease pathogenesis.

nodos.label: Synaptic transmission
nodos.desc: The process by which neurons communicate via neurotransmitters; impaired synaptic transmission is a consequence of genetic mutations in Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Dopamine-producing neurons
nodos.desc: Neurons in the substantia nigra that produce dopamine; their degeneration is the primary pathological feature of Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Gene mutation
nodos.desc: A change in the DNA sequence of a gene that can disrupt normal protein function; various mutations in PD-related genes increase disease risk.

nodos.label: Loss-of-function mutation
nodos.desc: A mutation that reduces or eliminates the function of a protein; such mutations in PRKN and other genes lead to impaired cellular processes and increased disease risk.

nodos.label: Unfolded protein response
nodos.desc: A cellular stress response that manages misfolded proteins; disruption of this pathway contributes to protein aggregation and neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Levodopa
nodos.desc: Precursor of dopamine; used to treat Parkinson's disease by increasing dopamine levels in the brain.

nodos.label: COMT Inhibitors
nodos.desc: Medications that inhibit the enzyme catechol-O-methyltransferase, thereby prolonging the effect of levodopa in the body.

nodos.label: Entacapone
nodos.desc: FDA-approved COMT inhibitor used in Parkinson's disease to extend levodopa's therapeutic effect.

nodos.label: Tolcapone
nodos.desc: FDA-approved COMT inhibitor for Parkinson's disease, requiring regular liver function monitoring due to toxicity risk.

nodos.label: Opicapone
nodos.desc: FDA-approved COMT inhibitor used to enhance and prolong levodopa's effect in Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Anticholinergics
nodos.desc: Drugs that reduce acetylcholine activity in the brain to balance dopamine deficiency in Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Trihexyphenidyl
nodos.desc: An anticholinergic drug used in Parkinson's disease, though limited by side effects such as confusion and memory issues.

nodos.label: Benztropine
nodos.desc: An anticholinergic medication used to manage Parkinson's symptoms, with potential side effects including dry mouth and constipation.

nodos.label: Amantadine
nodos.desc: A medication with multiple CNS effects, including weak dopamine reuptake inhibition and anti-glutamatergic properties, primarily used to reduce dyskinesias in Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS)
nodos.desc: Surgical intervention involving implantation of electrodes in specific brain regions to modulate abnormal neural activity in Parkinson's disease.

nodos.label: Subthalamic Nucleus (STN)
nodos.desc: A brain target for DBS in Parkinson's disease, involved in motor control regulation.

nodos.label: Globus Pallidus Internus (GPi)
nodos.desc: A brain region targeted in DBS for Parkinson's disease to reduce motor symptoms.

nodos.label: Ventral Intermediate Thalamus (VIM)
nodos.desc: A brain target for DBS in Parkinson's disease, involved in motor pathway modulation.

nodos.label: Stereotactic Planning
nodos.desc: Precision imaging-guided technique used to plan and position electrodes during DBS surgery.

nodos.label: Neural Activity
nodos.desc: Abnormal patterns of brain activity associated with Parkinson's disease, modulated by DBS to improve motor function.

nodos.label: Central Nervous System (CNS)
nodos.desc: Sistema nervioso central que incluye el cerebro y la médula espinal, afectado en la enfermedad de múltiples sclerosis.

nodos.label: McDonald Criteria
nodos.desc: Conjunto de criterios basados en evidencia para diagnosticar múltiples sclerosis, que busca estandarizar la detección de lesiones dispersas en el sistema nervioso central.

nodos.label: Blood-Brain Barrier
nodos.desc: Estructura que regula el paso de sustancias del torrente sanguíneo al sistema nervioso central, cuya integridad puede ser comprometida en la MS, facilitando la entrada de células inmunes.

nodos.label: Immune Functions
nodos.desc: Procesos regulados por el sistema inmune que pueden ser alterados en la MS, contribuyendo a la inflamación y a la destrucción de la mielina.

nodos.label: Anti-spasticity agents
nodos.desc: Medications such as baclofen, tizanidine, gabapentin, and dantrolene used to relieve muscle spasticity, stiffness, and cramping; botulinum toxin A (Botox) provides temporary relief in localized areas.

nodos.label: Analgesics
nodos.desc: Drugs used to manage pain in MS, including NSAIDs, anticonvulsants, antidepressants, opioids, and topical creams with capsaicin or lidocaine.

nodos.label: Antidepressants
nodos.desc: Used to treat depression in MS patients, with SSRIs, SNRIs, and TCAs being common choices to improve mood and quality of life.

nodos.label: Fatigue management
nodos.desc: Involves pharmacological options like modafinil, amantadine, and stimulants, as well as non-pharmacological strategies such as exercise, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), energy conservation, and sleep hygiene.

nodos.label: Lifestyle modifications
nodos.desc: Includes regular aerobic exercise to improve cardiovascular fitness, strength, balance, mobility, fatigue, depression, and cognition in individuals with MS.

nodos.label: Personalized management
nodos.desc: Symptom management in MS varies widely among individuals, requiring tailored treatment strategies based on specific symptoms and patient profiles.

nodos.label: Head Positioning
nodos.desc: The technique of positioning the head during laryngoscopy and intubation, traditionally using the 'sniffing position' with neck extension, which has been found to increase cervical spine injury risk; modern approaches advocate for neutral or slightly flexed positions to minimize cervical stress.

nodos.label: External Immobilization Devices
nodos.desc: Devices such as cervical collars or rigid boards provide support during airway procedures, but must be applied appropriately to avoid exacerbating cervical spine injury or impairing intubation efficiency.

nodos.label: Manual Inline Stabilization
nodos.desc: A technique involving gentle traction along the spinal axis to maintain cervical alignment during intubation, typically performed by two providers or via self-stabilization with a non-dominant hand.

nodos.label: Video Laryngoscopy
nodos.desc: A technology that uses indirect visualization to improve glottic view and reduce neck extension, thereby decreasing the risk of cervical spine injury during intubation.

nodos.label: Concepto
nodos.desc: Un concepto es una unidad básica de pensamiento que representa una idea o entidad en el sistema cognitivo.

nodos.label: Red semántica
nodos.desc: Una red semántica es un modelo que representa las relaciones entre conceptos en la memoria, donde los nodos son conceptos y las aristas son relaciones.

nodos.label: Asociación
nodos.desc: La asociación es la conexión mental entre dos conceptos que se activan simultáneamente o de forma secuencial en el pensamiento.

nodos.label: Conexión
nodos.desc: Una conexión es una relación matemática o estructural que une dos elementos en un sistema, como nodos en una red.

nodos.label: Memory
nodos.desc: A cognitive function that stores and retrieves information; includes sensory, short-term (working), and long-term memory types.

nodos.label: Executive Functions
nodos.desc: Higher-order cognitive processes that regulate attention, reasoning, planning, and decision-making; can be affected by aging.

nodos.label: Cognitive Abilities
nodos.desc: Broad mental skills such as memory, attention, reasoning, and problem-solving that are influenced by age and culture.

nodos.label: Intelligence
nodos.desc: A complex construct encompassing various forms of intellectual functioning, shaped by both biological and sociocultural factors.

nodos.label: Assessment Methods
nodos.desc: Techniques used to evaluate cognitive performance, such as dynamic assessment and portfolio-based evaluation, which provide nuanced insights into learning and development.

nodos.label: Cultural Influence
nodos.desc: The role of cultural context in shaping cognitive processing styles and the interpretation of intelligence and problem-solving behaviors.

nodos.label: Effects of Aging on Cognition
nodos.desc: Age-related changes in cognitive functions such as memory, attention, and executive functions, which impact mental health and well-being in older adults.

nodos.label: Selective Attention
nodos.desc: La capacidad de enfocarse en ciertos estímulos mientras se ignoran otros, permitiendo filtrar información irrelevante y concentrarse en lo importante en el entorno.

nodos.label: Spotlight Model
nodos.desc: Teoría que sugiere que la atención actúa como un haz de luz que ilumina una región específica del espacio, permitiendo procesar mejor estímulos en esa zona en comparación con los no atendidos.

nodos.label: Multiple Resources Model
nodos.desc: Teoría que propone que la atención está compuesta por múltiples recursos distintos, lo que permite una distribución más compleja y flexible de la atención en diferentes tareas o estímulos.

nodos.label: Attentional Capacity
nodos.desc: La capacidad limitada de los usuarios para mantenerse atentos, que influye en el diseño de interfaces y la eficiencia de las interacciones humanas con tecnología.

nodos.label: Cognitive Load
nodos.desc: La cantidad total de información que el cerebro debe procesar en un momento dado; cuando es excesiva, puede afectar la atención y el rendimiento cognitivo.

nodos.label: Active Engagement
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual los aprendices participan activamente en el contenido, lo que mejora la retención y comprensión de conceptos matemáticos.

nodos.label: Multisensory Elements
nodos.desc: Uso de múltiples modos sensoriales (visuales, auditivos, táctiles) para facilitar la comprensión y retención de información, especialmente en contextos educativos.

nodos.label: Innate Capacity
nodos.desc: The inherent, pre-existing ability in humans to acquire language without explicit instruction, suggesting a biological or cognitive mechanism that enables children to infer grammatical rules from environmental input.

nodos.label: Grammatical Rules
nodos.desc: Structural principles that govern the formation of sentences in a language, which children are believed to acquire through an innate mechanism according to nativist theory.

nodos.label: Cultural Practices
nodos.desc: Shared activities and conventions within a community that shape communicative behavior and influence how language is used and developed in social contexts.

nodos.label: Discursive Norms
nodos.desc: The established patterns and rules of communication within a community of practice, which guide how language is produced and interpreted in specific social settings.

nodos.label: Sociocultural Factors
nodos.desc: Environmental and social influences that determine the development and usage of language, emphasizing the role of community and shared experiences in learning.

nodos.label: Interplay between Language and Cognition
nodos.desc: The dynamic relationship between language development and cognitive processes, where language is seen as both a product and a driver of mental functions.

nodos.label: Arcuate Fasciculus
nodos.desc: A white matter tract that connects Broca's and Wernicke's areas, facilitating information transfer between them; disruption leads to conduction aphasia.

nodos.label: Broca's Area
nodos.desc: A brain region involved in speech production and language expression; typically dominant in the left hemisphere.

nodos.label: Wernicke's Area
nodos.desc: A brain region responsible for language comprehension; typically dominant in the left hemisphere.

nodos.label: Conduction Aphasia
nodos.desc: A language disorder characterized by impaired repetition of words or sentences, while comprehension and production remain largely intact.

nodos.label: Corpus Callosum
nodos.desc: The largest bundle of nerve fibers connecting the two cerebral hemispheres; its sectioning in split-brain surgery disrupts interhemispheric communication.

nodos.label: Lateralization of Function
nodos.desc: The specialization of functions, such as language, to one hemisphere of the brain, with the left hemisphere typically dominating language in right-handers and most left-handers.

nodos.label: Visual Field Projection
nodos.desc: The phenomenon where visual stimuli presented to one visual field are processed primarily by the opposite hemisphere of the brain.

nodos.label: Hemispheric Dissociation
nodos.desc: The separation of cognitive functions between the two hemispheres, demonstrated in split-brain patients, showing distinct capabilities in language and nonverbal tasks.

nodos.label: REM Sleep
nodos.desc: A stage of sleep characterized by rapid eye movements, heightened brain activity, and vivid dreaming, primarily occurring during the night cycle.

nodos.label: Cerebral Cortex
nodos.desc: The outer layer of the brain responsible for higher cognitive functions such as thought, memory, and perception, which becomes active during REM sleep.

nodos.label: Circadian Rhythm
nodos.desc: An internal biological process that follows a roughly 24-hour cycle, regulating sleep-wake cycles, hormone release, and other physiological functions, primarily controlled by the suprachiasmatic nucleus in the hypothalamus.

nodos.label: Sleep Stages
nodos.desc: The different phases of sleep, including REM and non-REM stages, which contribute to brain function, memory consolidation, and emotional regulation.

nodos.label: Brain Activity
nodos.desc: The electrical and metabolic processes occurring in the brain during sleep, particularly during REM sleep, which resemble wakefulness in terms of neural activation.

nodos.label: Sleep-Wake Disorders
nodos.desc: A group of conditions where the internal circadian rhythm is misaligned with external environmental demands, affecting sleep patterns and daily functioning.

nodos.label: Delayed Sleep Phase Disorder
nodos.desc: A sleep-wake disorder characterized by a delay in the timing of the sleep-wake cycle, making it difficult to fall asleep and wake up at conventional times.

nodos.label: Advanced Sleep Phase Disorder
nodos.desc: A sleep-wake disorder where individuals fall asleep and wake up earlier than usual, often before dawn.

nodos.label: Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Rhythm Disorder
nodos.desc: A condition where the circadian rhythm does not align with a 24-hour day, resulting in a gradual shift of the sleep-wake cycle over time.

nodos.label: Shift Work Disorder
nodos.desc: A sleep-wake disorder affecting individuals who work irregular or night shifts, leading to difficulties in maintaining a consistent sleep schedule.

nodos.label: Jet Lag Disorder
nodos.desc: A temporary disruption of the circadian rhythm caused by rapid travel across multiple time zones, leading to sleep and alertness disturbances.

nodos.label: Bright Light Exposure
nodos.desc: A non-pharmacological intervention used to reset circadian rhythms by exposing individuals to bright light, typically in the morning to advance or in the evening to delay the sleep-wake cycle.

nodos.label: Melatonin
nodos.desc: A hormone naturally produced by the body that regulates sleep-wake cycles; supplementation is used to help align circadian rhythms in sleep disorders.

nodos.label: Chronobiotics
nodos.desc: Pharmaceutical agents designed to modulate circadian rhythms, often used in the management of sleep-wake disorders.

nodos.label: Lifestyle Adjustments
nodos.desc: Behavioral modifications such as regular sleep schedules, physical activity, and environmental control to support circadian rhythm stability.

nodos.label: Hypnosis
nodos.desc: A state of focused attention and heightened suggestibility induced by verbal cues, leading to changes in perception, memory, and voluntary control, used in therapeutic contexts.

nodos.label: Meditation
nodos.desc: A mental training technique involving focused attention and mindfulness, aimed at improving emotional regulation, cognitive function, and mental well-being.

nodos.label: Neurobiological Research
nodos.desc: Scientific study of the brain and nervous system, providing evidence for the mechanisms underlying hypnosis and meditation in mental health.

nodos.label: Cognitive Function
nodos.desc: The mental processes involved in acquiring knowledge and understanding through thought, experience, and the processing of information.

nodos.label: Emotional Wellbeing
nodos.desc: A state of mental health characterized by the ability to manage emotions effectively and maintain positive psychological states.

nodos.label: Prefrontal Cortex
nodos.desc: Regulatory region of the brain involved in self-referential processing, decision making, and emotional appraisals; shows increased gray matter density after meditation.

nodos.label: Insula
nodos.desc: Region associated with viscerosensory precision, interoceptive accuracy, and embodied presence; hypertrophy improves homeostatic balance and affect tolerance.

nodos.label: Hippocampus
nodos.desc: Critical for declarative memory, episodic retrieval, pattern separation, and context discrimination; volume expansion supports autobiographical memory encoding and skill acquisition.

nodos.label: Amygdala
nodos.desc: Involved in threat detection and emotional reactivity; reduced dimensions correlate with diminished fear responses and improved anxiety reduction.

nodos.label: Thalamus
nodos.desc: Acts as a sensory relay; plasticity improves filtering of ascending sensory input, enhancing attention and information processing efficiency.

nodos.label: Elaborative Encoding
nodos.desc: Proceso de conectar nueva información con conocimientos existentes para crear representaciones más ricas y profundas, lo que facilita el almacenamiento y recuperación de la memoria.

nodos.label: Self-Explanation
nodos.desc: Técnica que consiste en explicar un concepto en propias palabras, lo que promueve una comprensión más profunda y mejora la retención de la información.

nodos.label: Mnemonic Devices
nodos.desc: Herramientas de memoria que establecen asociaciones entre elementos aparentemente no relacionados, como acrónimos o palabras que suenan similares, para facilitar la recuerdo.

nodos.label: Keyword Method
nodos.desc: Técnica de mnemotécnica que asocia una palabra en un idioma extranjero con una palabra en inglés que suene similar o tenga un significado relacionado, para facilitar la memorización.

nodos.label: Mental Rehearsal
nodos.desc: Técnica de visualización que implica imaginar paso a paso una tarea o movimiento, detallando cada acción mentalmente, comúnmente usada por atletas para entrenamiento.

nodos.label: Abstract to Concrete
nodos.desc: Proceso de transformar conceptos abstractos en imágenes concretas para facilitar su comprensión y memorización mediante representaciones visuales.

nodos.label: Recognition Memory
nodos.desc: A type of retrieval where participants identify whether a stimulus was encountered before, using both the item and its contextual information to facilitate correct identification. It is generally easier than free recall due to contextual support and is less prone to intrusion errors.

nodos.label: False Alarm
nodos.desc: An error in recognition memory where participants incorrectly identify a novel item as familiar, often exacerbated by high response bias, such as endorsing all test items regardless of their actual status.

nodos.label: Contextual Support
nodos.desc: The use of surrounding information and context during retrieval to aid in the identification of previously encountered stimuli, enhancing accuracy in recognition memory.

nodos.label: Memory Reconstruction
nodos.desc: The cognitive process by which the brain reassembles stored memories, often incorporating current knowledge and expectations, leading to potential distortions or inaccuracies in recalled information.

nodos.label: Retrieval Process
nodos.desc: The cognitive mechanism by which stored information is accessed from memory, including free recall, cued recall, and recognition, each with distinct characteristics and error profiles.

nodos.label: Intrusion Error
nodos.desc: A memory error in which participants incorrectly recall a non-studied item as having been studied, more common in free recall than in recognition.

nodos.label: Cued Recall
nodos.desc: A retrieval method where cues are provided to assist in the recall of information, helping to disambiguate between similar memories and improve retrieval accuracy.

nodos.label: Long-Term Potentiation
nodos.desc: A form of synaptic plasticity where repeated stimulation of a neural pathway leads to a long-lasting increase in synaptic strength, enhancing communication between neurons and serving as a cellular mechanism for memory formation.

nodos.label: Homosynaptic LTP
nodos.desc: A type of LTP where only the stimulated pathway undergoes strengthening, resulting in input-specific changes within a single synaptic connection.

nodos.label: Heterosynaptic LTP
nodos.desc: A type of LTP where unstimulated neighboring pathways also show increased connectivity, indicating broader, network-level changes in synaptic strength.

nodos.label: Associative LTP
nodos.desc: A form of LTP where weakly stimulated synapses are strengthened due to association with strongly activated neighboring pathways, reflecting cooperative mechanisms in memory encoding.

nodos.label: Homeostatic Scaling
nodos.desc: A mechanism that adjusts the sensitivity of all synapses proportionally to maintain network stability and balance between excitation and inhibition.

nodos.label: Synaptic Decay
nodos.desc: The gradual weakening of neural connections over time, leading to the loss of stored memories.

nodos.label: Interference
nodos.desc: A process where new information disrupts the retrieval of previously learned information, contributing to forgetting.

nodos.label: Spine Volume
nodos.desc: The size of dendritic spines, which increases during actin polymerization and reflects synaptic strengthening, contributing to enhanced neuronal connectivity.

nodos.label: Actin Polymerization
nodos.desc: The process by which actin filaments grow and form structures within neurons, promoting spine enlargement and facilitating synaptic strengthening.

nodos.label: Cognitive Decline
nodos.desc: A gradual reduction in cognitive abilities such as memory, attention, and executive functioning, often associated with aging.

nodos.label: Cardiovascular Disease
nodos.desc: A group of conditions affecting the heart and blood vessels, which can contribute to cognitive decline through reduced blood flow to the brain.

nodos.label: Depression
nodos.desc: A mental health condition that has been linked to increased risk of cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease.

nodos.label: Chronic Stress
nodos.desc: Prolonged exposure to stress, which can negatively affect brain function and contribute to memory impairments.

nodos.label: Vascular Causes
nodos.desc: Conditions related to blood vessel function that can lead to dementia, with up to 50% of dementias attributed to such causes.

nodos.label: Alzheimer's Disease
nodos.desc: A progressive neurological disorder that leads to memory loss, cognitive decline, and eventual loss of the ability to perform daily activities.

nodos.label: Korsakoff's Syndrome
nodos.desc: A neurological disorder characterized by severe memory loss, typically caused by thiamine deficiency, often associated with chronic alcoholism.

nodos.label: Amnesia
nodos.desc: A condition involving memory impairment, where individuals experience gaps in recalling personal experiences or information.

nodos.label: Memory Loss
nodos.desc: The inability to retain or recall information, a core symptom in both Alzheimer's disease and Korsakoff's syndrome.

nodos.label: Executive Functioning
nodos.desc: A set of cognitive processes that include planning, decision-making, and problem-solving, which are affected in aging and neurological disorders.

nodos.label: Cognitive Training
nodos.desc: Structured programs designed to improve and maintain cognitive abilities such as memory and attention.

nodos.label: Septal Nuclei
nodos.desc: A group of neurons beneath the corpus callosum involved in reward processing, pleasure sensation, motivation, and modulation of learning and memory through connections with the hippocampus.

nodos.label: Anterior Cingulate Cortex
nodos.desc: A part of the prefrontal region that contributes to emotional regulation and the appraisal of emotional stimuli, forming functional loops with the amygdala and prefrontal cortex.

nodos.label: Subjective Experience
nodos.desc: The conscious awareness of feeling a particular emotion, such as happiness or sadness, involving introspection and self-reporting, which is difficult to quantify but studied through cognitive neuroscience.

nodos.label: Physiological Response
nodos.desc: The body's automatic physical reactions to emotions, such as changes in heart rate or hormone levels, which are measurable and form part of the emotional response system.

nodos.label: Expressive Behavior
nodos.desc: The outward manifestation of emotions through facial expressions, gestures, or vocal tone, which serves as a communicative signal of internal emotional states.

nodos.label: Anterior Insula
nodos.desc: A brain region involved in representing bodily sensations associated with emotional states, enabling conscious awareness of emotions through interoception.

nodos.label: Orbitofrontal Cortex
nodos.desc: A brain region linked to the processing of affective information and contributing to the regulation of emotional experiences.

nodos.label: Medial Prefrontal Cortex
nodos.desc: A brain region associated with emotional regulation and the integration of emotional and cognitive processes.

nodos.label: Biofeedback Training
nodos.desc: A technique that enables individuals to learn and control physiological processes through real-time feedback, used effectively in treating anxiety, depression, and chronic pain.

nodos.label: Self-Regulation
nodos.desc: The ability to manage and modulate one's emotional and physiological responses, enhanced through awareness of internal bodily reactions.

nodos.label: Neurona espejo
nodos.desc: Células especializadas en áreas del cerebro relacionadas con la planificación y ejecución motriz que se activan tanto al realizar una acción como al observar a otro realizarla.

nodos.label: Noradrenalina
nodos.desc: Neurotransmisor involucrado en la respuesta fisiológica al estrés, la alerta y la atención.

nodos.label: Estimulante
nodos.desc: Clase de drogas que aumentan la actividad del sistema nervioso central, mejorando la alerta, la energía y la atención.

nodos.label: Depresor
nodos.desc: Clase de drogas que disminuyen la actividad del sistema nervioso central, produciendo efectos de relajación y sedación.

nodos.label: Hallucinógeno
nodos.desc: Clase de drogas que alteran la percepción y la conciencia, provocando sensaciones visuales o auditivas no reales.

nodos.label: Procesamiento emocional
nodos.desc: Mecanismos cerebrales que permiten la generación, regulación y expresión de emociones.

nodos.label: Cognición social
nodos.desc: Capacidad del cerebro para entender y responder a las acciones y emociones de otros individuos.

nodos.label: Trastorno psiquiátrico
nodos.desc: Afecciones mentales caracterizadas por alteraciones en el funcionamiento social, como el trastorno del espectro autista o la esquizofrenia.

nodos.label: Kappa receptor
nodos.desc: A type of opioid receptor located in the brain and spinal cord, involved in pain modulation and other physiological responses.

nodos.label: Mu receptor
nodos.desc: A type of opioid receptor located in the brain and spinal cord, involved in pain relief, euphoria, and respiratory depression.

nodos.label: Analgesia
nodos.desc: The reduction or elimination of pain sensation, mediated by opioid receptor activation.

nodos.label: Euphoria
nodos.desc: A state of intense pleasure or happiness, induced by activation of opioid receptors in the brain.

nodos.label: Respiratory depression
nodos.desc: A decrease in respiratory rate and depth, a potentially life-threatening side effect of opioid receptor activation.

nodos.label: Constipation
nodos.desc: A gastrointestinal side effect caused by opioid receptor activation in the enteric nervous system.

nodos.label: Physical dependence
nodos.desc: A state where the body adapts to the presence of a drug, leading to withdrawal symptoms upon discontinuation.

nodos.label: Tolerance
nodos.desc: A physiological adaptation where increasing doses of a drug are required to achieve the same effect.

nodos.label: Withdrawal syndrome
nodos.desc: A set of physiological and psychological symptoms that occur when a person stops using a drug after prolonged use.

nodos.label: G proteins
nodos.desc: Molecular signaling proteins that mediate the effects of opioid receptor activation by transmitting signals from the receptor to intracellular pathways.

nodos.label: Second messengers
nodos.desc: Intracellular molecules that relay signals from activated receptors to downstream effectors, such as cAMP or IP3.

nodos.label: Kinases
nodos.desc: Enzymes that phosphorylate proteins, playing a key role in intracellular signaling cascades triggered by opioid receptors.

nodos.label: Transcription factors
nodos.desc: Proteins that regulate gene expression by binding to DNA and modulating transcription, influenced by opioid receptor signaling.

nodos.label: Membrane excitability
nodos.desc: The ability of neurons to generate action potentials, which can be modulated by opioid receptor activity at the cellular level.

nodos.label: Neural circuitry dynamics
nodos.desc: The patterns of activity and connectivity among neurons that are altered by chronic opioid exposure, affecting behavior and cognition.

nodos.label: Functional connectivity
nodos.desc: The statistical dependence between neural signals in different brain regions, which is disrupted by chronic opioid use.

nodos.label: Network organization
nodos.desc: The structural and functional architecture of brain networks, which is impaired by long-term opioid exposure.

nodos.label: Decision making
nodos.desc: A cognitive function that is impaired by chronic opioid exposure due to disrupted brain network dynamics.

nodos.label: Emotion regulation
nodos.desc: The ability to manage emotional responses, which is compromised by opioid-induced neural changes.

nodos.label: Executive control
nodos.desc: Cognitive functions such as planning, inhibition, and goal-directed behavior, which are impaired by chronic opioid use.

nodos.label: Stimulant drugs
nodos.desc: A class of psychoactive substances that increase central nervous system activity, leading to heightened alertness and energy.

nodos.label: Alertness
nodos.desc: A state of heightened awareness and responsiveness, induced by stimulant drugs through increased neurotransmitter activity.

nodos.label: Attention
nodos.desc: The cognitive ability to focus on specific stimuli, improved by low-dose stimulant drug use.

nodos.label: Bioavailability
nodos.desc: La fracción de fármaco no alterado que llega a la circulación sistémica después de la administración de un medicamento.

nodos.label: First-Pass Metabolism
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que los fármacos son metabolizados por el hígado antes de alcanzar la circulación sistémica, reduciendo su biodisponibilidad.

nodos.label: Oral Administration
nodos.desc: Administración por vía oral, donde el fármaco es absorbido en el intestino delgado y pasa por el hígado antes de entrar en la circulación sistémica.

nodos.label: Intravenous Administration
nodos.desc: Inyección directa en una vena que permite una absorción rápida y alta bioavailability, sin pasos de metabolismo previo.

nodos.label: Intramuscular Administration
nodos.desc: Inyección en músculo que permite una absorción gradual y sostenida debido a la vascularización muscular.

nodos.label: Transdermal Administration
nodos.desc: Aplicación tópica de fármacos a través de la piel, que permite una liberación continua y baja dosis, ideal para terapias prolongadas.

nodos.label: Molecular Size
nodos.desc: El tamaño molecular de un fármaco influye en su capacidad para penetrar a través de barreras como la capa corneosa de la piel.

nodos.label: Vascularization
nodos.desc: Proceso de formación de vasos sanguíneos en tejidos, que facilita la absorción de fármacos como en el músculo o en la piel.

nodos.label: Genetic Vulnerability
nodos.desc: The contribution of genetic factors to the development of substance use disorders, with estimates suggesting up to 60% of individual vulnerability is attributable to genetics, particularly through genes like DRD2 related to dopamine receptor function.

nodos.label: Environmental Influences
nodos.desc: External factors such as trauma, stress, peer pressure, cultural attitudes, and drug availability that increase the risk of substance use disorders, especially when experienced during critical developmental periods.

nodos.label: Interplay of Factors
nodos.desc: The complex interaction between genetic predisposition and environmental exposures that collectively determine an individual's risk of developing a substance use disorder, rather than any single factor being decisive.

nodos.label: Manic Episode
nodos.desc: A distinct period of abnormally elevated, expansive, or irritable mood lasting at least one week, characterized by increased activity, racing thoughts, decreased sleep need, grandiosity, distractibility, and impulsivity, interfering with daily functioning.

nodos.label: Major Depressive Episode
nodos.desc: A period of at least two weeks with symptoms such as low mood, anhedonia, changes in appetite or weight, insomnia or hypersomnia, psychomotor agitation or retardation, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, difficulty concentrating, and recurrent suicidal thoughts.

nodos.label: Hypomanic Episode
nodos.desc: A milder form of mania, lasting at least four consecutive days, with symptoms like elevated mood, increased activity, and decreased need for sleep, but without severe impairment or psychotic features.

nodos.label: Bipolar I Disorder
nodos.desc: Diagnosed when an individual has at least one manic episode, which may be preceded or followed by hypomanic or major depressive episodes.

nodos.label: Bipolar II Disorder
nodos.desc: Diagnosed when an individual has at least one major depressive episode and at least one hypomanic episode, but no full manic episode.

nodos.label: Cyclothymic Disorder
nodos.desc: Involves numerous periods of hypomanic and depressive symptoms over at least two years (one year in children and adolescents), without meeting full criteria for manic or major depressive episodes.

nodos.label: Multifactorial Causes
nodos.desc: Bipolar disorder arises from a combination of genetic, environmental, and neurochemical factors, with a strong genetic component observed in familial cases.

nodos.label: Depressive Episode
nodos.desc: A period of at least two weeks with depressed mood or loss of interest, accompanied by at least five of the following symptoms: low energy, poor self-esteem, difficulty concentrating, irritability, insomnia, hypersomnia, appetite changes, fatigue, and feelings of worthlessness or guilt.

nodos.label: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD)
nodos.desc: A severe form of premenstrual syndrome affecting 3%-8% of menstruating women, characterized by emotional and physical symptoms during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle that significantly interfere with daily functioning.

nodos.label: Substance/Medication-Induced Depressive Disorder
nodos.desc: Depressive symptoms caused by substance intoxication, withdrawal, or medication exposure, not better explained by another medical condition or preexisting depression unrelated to substance use.

nodos.label: Depressive Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition
nodos.desc: Depressive symptoms resulting from an underlying medical illness such as Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, multiple sclerosis, stroke, cancer, HIV, or autoimmune diseases, with symptoms not attributable to other causes.

nodos.label: HPA axis
nodos.desc: A hormonal system regulating stress response, involving the hypothalamus, pituitary, and adrenal glands.

nodos.label: Thyroid hormones
nodos.desc: Hormones that regulate metabolism, growth, development, and neurological function; imbalances linked to mood disturbances.

nodos.label: Hypothyroidism
nodos.desc: A condition of reduced thyroid hormone levels, associated with mood disturbances and emotional instability.

nodos.label: TSH response
nodos.desc: The body's response to thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH), measured via challenge tests; blunted responses observed in some depressed patients.

nodos.label: Free thyroxine (FT4) response
nodos.desc: A biomarker of thyroid function; reduced response to TRH in depressed individuals suggests possible thyroid dysfunction.

nodos.label: Sex steroid hormones
nodos.desc: Hormones including estrogens and androgens that influence mood regulation and are linked to mood disturbances in women and men.

nodos.label: Estrogens
nodos.desc: Female sex hormones whose fluctuations during menstrual cycles, pregnancy, and menopause are associated with mood changes.

nodos.label: Androgens
nodos.desc: Male sex hormones, with testosterone playing a role in mood regulation and vulnerability to depression.

nodos.label: Testosterone
nodos.desc: Primary male sex hormone; low levels may increase vulnerability to depression in men.

nodos.label: Functional MRI
nodos.desc: Imaging technique that measures brain activity by detecting changes in blood flow, used to study emotion processing in depression.

nodos.label: Positron Emission Tomography
nodos.desc: Imaging technique that visualizes metabolic and molecular processes in the brain, useful for studying neurochemical changes in depression.

nodos.label: Electroencephalography and Magnetoencephalography
nodos.desc: Neuroimaging methods that measure electrical and magnetic activity in the brain, offering high temporal resolution for studying brain dynamics.

nodos.label: Fronto-limbic network
nodos.desc: A neural circuit involving the prefrontal cortex and limbic structures, responsible for regulating emotions; dysfunction is linked to depression.

nodos.label: Top-down regulation
nodos.desc: A cognitive and neural process that modulates emotional states through higher-order brain regions; disruptions are associated with depression.

nodos.label: Emotional homeostasis
nodos.desc: The stable regulation of emotional states; optimal hormone levels are necessary for maintaining this balance.

nodos.label: Serotonin
nodos.desc: A neurotransmitter involved in regulating mood, appetite, sleep, and other functions; increased levels are associated with improved mood and reduced anxiety.

nodos.label: Reuptake
nodos.desc: The process by which neurotransmitters are reabsorbed by the presynaptic neuron after releasing into the synaptic cleft, reducing their availability in the synapse.

nodos.label: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor (SSRI)
nodos.desc: A class of antidepressants that selectively inhibit the reuptake of serotonin, increasing its availability in the synapse to improve mood.

nodos.label: Serotonin and Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitor (SNRI)
nodos.desc: A class of antidepressants that inhibit the reuptake of both serotonin and norepinephrine, increasing the availability of both neurotransmitters in the synapse.

nodos.label: Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA)
nodos.desc: An older class of antidepressants that increase serotonin and norepinephrine levels but also affect other neurotransmitters, leading to a higher risk of side effects.

nodos.label: Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitor (MAOI)
nodos.desc: An older class of antidepressants that block the breakdown of neurotransmitters, increasing their levels in the synapse, but with significant dietary and interaction risks.

nodos.label: Neurochemical Balance
nodos.desc: The equilibrium of neurotransmitter levels in the brain, which is critical for regulating mood and emotional well-being.

nodos.label: Panic Attack
nodos.desc: Unsudden surge of intense fear or discomfort that reaches its peak within minutes, accompanied by physical symptoms like palpitations, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, chest pain, and nausea.

nodos.label: Obsession
nodos.desc: Uncontrollable, unwanted thoughts, images, or urges that cause significant distress and interfere with daily functioning in individuals with Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD).

nodos.label: Compulsion
nodos.desc: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed to reduce anxiety caused by obsessions, often serving as a temporary relief, such as handwashing, checking, or mental rituals.

nodos.label: Etiology
nodos.desc: The study of the causes of OCD, which may include genetic, neurological, environmental, and infectious factors such as Streptococcus bacteria in PANDAS.

nodos.label: Prevalence
nodos.desc: The frequency or distribution of OCD in the population, with the World Health Organization indicating it is among the top ten causes of disability worldwide.

nodos.label: Age of Onset
nodos.desc: The age at which OCD typically begins, which can occur in childhood or adolescence, though it may also start in adulthood.

nodos.label: Neurobiological Factors
nodos.desc: Structural and functional differences in the brain observed in individuals with OCD compared to those without the disorder.

nodos.label: Environmental Stressors
nodos.desc: Traumatic or chronic stress events, such as abuse, neglect, loss, or ongoing personal difficulties, can trigger or exacerbate psychotic symptoms in vulnerable individuals.

nodos.label: Substance Abuse
nodos.desc: Use of certain drugs like amphetamines, cocaine, LSD, and PCP can induce temporary or persistent psychotic states, and may worsen existing symptoms.

nodos.label: Neurological Abnormalities
nodos.desc: Structural and functional brain differences, including gray and white matter alterations and disrupted connectivity, are observed in individuals with psychosis, along with neurochemical imbalances in dopamine and serotonin systems.

nodos.label: Hallucinations
nodos.desc: Perception-like experiences occurring without external stimuli, commonly auditory, but can also be visual, tactile, olfactory, or gustatory.

nodos.label: Delusions
nodos.desc: Fixed, irrational beliefs that persist despite contradictory evidence, often involving themes of persecution, grandiosity, jealousy, or somatization.

nodos.label: Disorganized Thinking and Speech
nodos.desc: Loose associations and incoherent thought patterns that manifest in speech, reflecting impaired cognitive functioning in psychosis.

nodos.label: Mood Episode
nodos.desc: A period of significant emotional disturbance, either depressive or manic, meeting diagnostic criteria for major depressive or manic episodes.

nodos.label: Concurrent Symptoms
nodos.desc: The presence of both psychotic and mood symptoms occurring simultaneously during illness episodes.

nodos.label: Exclusion Criteria
nodos.desc: Conditions under which the disorder is not attributed to substance use or medical conditions, ensuring the diagnosis is based on psychiatric rather than physiological causes.

nodos.label: Autism Spectrum Disorder
nodos.desc: A neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by challenges in social interaction, communication, and repetitive behaviors, which may influence diagnostic considerations in schizoaffective disorder.

nodos.label: Communication Disorder of Childhood Onset
nodos.desc: A developmental condition affecting language and communication skills, potentially impacting the clinical presentation and diagnosis of schizoaffective disorder.

nodos.label: Clinical Presentation
nodos.desc: The observable pattern of symptoms and behaviors exhibited by individuals, which can vary significantly between patients due to the combination of psychotic and mood symptoms.

nodos.label: DSM-5
nodos.desc: The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, which provides standardized criteria for diagnosing psychiatric disorders, including schizoaffective disorder.

nodos.label: Clinical Features
nodos.desc: Symptoms and functional impairments such as social isolation, loneliness, awkward interpersonal behavior, unusual nonverbal cues, eccentric dress, and difficulties in forming meaningful relationships.

nodos.label: Assessment
nodos.desc: A multi-source evaluation process, including interviews with the patient, to determine the presence and severity of SPD symptoms.

nodos.label: Beta-amyloid plaques
nodos.desc: Clumps of protein fragments called amyloid-beta peptides that accumulate outside and around neurons, disrupting cell-to-cell communication and activating immune system response.

nodos.label: Tau tangles
nodos.desc: Twisted fibers of the protein tau that collect inside neurons, blocking the transport of nutrients and essential molecules within cells.

nodos.label: Neurological assessment
nodos.desc: A medical evaluation that assesses brain function and cognitive abilities to detect signs of neurological disorders like Alzheimer's.

nodos.label: Neuropsychological testing
nodos.desc: A set of cognitive tests used to evaluate memory, reasoning, language, and other mental functions to diagnose dementia or cognitive decline.

nodos.label: Attention and awareness
nodos.desc: Core cognitive domains affected in delirium, which is characterized by a sudden disturbance in these functions.

nodos.label: Brain tissue destruction
nodos.desc: Gradual loss of brain tissue due to the accumulation of beta-amyloid plaques and tau tangles, leading to brain shrinkage over time.

nodos.label: Diagnosis process
nodos.desc: A comprehensive evaluation involving physical examination, laboratory tests, and cognitive assessments to identify Alzheimer's or delirium.

nodos.label: Symptom progression
nodos.desc: The gradual worsening of symptoms over time in Alzheimer's, as opposed to the acute and fluctuating symptoms in delirium.

nodos.label: Reversibility
nodos.desc: The ability to reverse symptoms once the underlying cause is treated; delirium is generally reversible, while Alzheimer's is progressive and irreversible.

nodos.label: Aggregation
nodos.desc: The process by which molecules, such as proteins, come together to form larger structures, often leading to dysfunction or disease.

nodos.label: Misfolding
nodos.desc: The incorrect three-dimensional conformation of a protein, which can lead to loss of function and aggregation.

nodos.label: Neuronal Death
nodos.desc: The loss of structure and function of neurons, resulting in cognitive decline and neurological symptoms.

nodos.label: Vascular Dementia
nodos.desc: A type of dementia caused by damage to brain blood vessels, leading to reduced blood flow and neuronal death.

nodos.label: Lewy Bodies
nodos.desc: Abnormal protein deposits found in nerve cells, associated with Lewy body dementia and linked to cognitive and motor impairments.

nodos.label: Neuroimaging
nodos.desc: Diagnostic techniques used to visualize brain structure and function, aiding in the detection of dementia-related changes.

nodos.label: Symptom Variability
nodos.desc: The wide range of symptoms observed among individuals with the same neurological condition, such as Lewy body dementia.

nodos.label: Cognitive Functioning
nodos.desc: The ability to think, remember, learn, and process information, which is progressively impaired in dementia and Alzheimer's disease.

nodos.label: Daily Living Abilities
nodos.desc: The capacity to perform basic activities of daily life, which diminishes as dementia advances and affects independence.

nodos.label: Stages of Dementia
nodos.desc: A classification system that divides dementia progression into early (mild), middle (moderate), and late (severe) stages based on symptom severity and functional capacity.

nodos.label: Intervention Strategies
nodos.desc: Proactive measures such as social engagement, stress management, cognitive stimulation, and sleep hygiene that may reduce dementia risk or progression.

nodos.label: Pathogenesis
nodos.desc: The biological and physiological processes underlying the development and progression of dementia and Alzheimer's disease.

nodos.label: Proliferation
nodos.desc: El proceso de división celular que ocurre durante el desarrollo nervioso, donde las células se multiplican para formar la base de las estructuras del sistema nervioso.

nodos.label: Myelination
nodos.desc: El proceso de formación de la mielina alrededor de los axones de las neuronas, que mejora la transmisión eficiente de señales nerviosas y aumenta la velocidad de procesamiento.

nodos.label: Critical Period
nodos.desc: Un intervalo temporal durante el desarrollo en el que ciertas habilidades o funciones cerebrales se desarrollan de manera óptima con estímulos ambientales específicos; si no se presentan, puede haber un déficit en el nivel de dominio.

nodos.label: Neural Milestones
nodos.desc: Habilidades y logros cognitivos y comportamentales que se alcanzan en etapas específicas del desarrollo infantil, como el control de la cabeza, el reconocimiento visual o la comprensión de objetos.

nodos.label: Cortical Growth
nodos.desc: El crecimiento del neocortex desde el nacimiento hasta la infancia, que alcanza el 25% del tamaño adulto al nacer y se triplica en el tamaño de la superficie cortical por el año de edad dos, debido a la formación de conexiones neuronales y mielina.

nodos.label: Spastic Quadriplegia
nodos.desc: A form of cerebral palsy affecting all four limbs, the trunk, and facial muscles, resulting in significant motor impairments and communication difficulties due to oral muscle dysfunction.

nodos.label: Monoplegia
nodos.desc: A rare form of spastic cerebral palsy affecting only one limb, though it is not typically classified under spastic cerebral p-than due to lack of generalized increased muscle tone.

nodos.label: Mixed Cerebral Palsy
nodos.desc: A condition where both spasticity and other types of abnormal muscle tone (such as ataxic or dystonic) coexist in an individual.

nodos.label: Dyskinetic Cerebral Palsy
nodos.desc: A type of cerebral palsy affecting 10-20% of individuals, characterized by involuntary movements and abnormal postures due to impaired regulation of muscle tone.

nodos.label: Muscle Tone
nodos.desc: The tension or resistance of muscles when at rest, which is abnormally regulated in cerebral palsy types such as spastic and dyskinetic forms.

nodos.label: Early Intervention
nodos.desc: Therapeutic strategies like physical therapy, occupational therapy, and orthotics that improve functional outcomes and quality of life in individuals with cerebral palsy.

nodos.label: Tic
nodos.desc: Un tic es un movimiento o sonido involuntario y repetitivo que puede ser motor o vocal, que se manifiesta en individuos con síndrome de Tourette.

nodos.label: Tic motor
nodos.desc: Un tic motor es un movimiento involuntario y repetitivo, como el parpadeo, el temblor de la nariz o el encogimiento de los hombros.

nodos.label: Tic vocal
nodos.desc: Un tic vocal es un sonido involuntario y repetitivo, como el ronroneo, el tos o el gruñido.

nodos.label: Tic complejo
nodos.desc: Un tic complejo es una secuencia coordinada de movimientos o sonidos que pueden incluir acciones como saltar o repetir palabras de otros.

nodos.label: Edad de inicio
nodos.desc: El inicio de los tics debe ocurrir antes de los 18 años, lo que es un criterio diagnóstico clave para el síndrome de Tourette.

nodos.label: Co-morbilidad
nodos.desc: La presencia de otros trastornos como el trastorno obsesivo-compulsivo (TOC), trastorno de déficit de atención e hiperactividad (TDAH) o trastornos del estado de ánimo puede coexistir con el síndrome de Tourette.

nodos.label: Criterio de exclusión
nodos.desc: El trastorno no debe atribuirse a efectos fisiológicos de sustancias (como cocaína) ni a condiciones médicas específicas (como enfermedad de Huntington o encefalitis postviral).

nodos.label: Trastorno neurodesarrollado
nodos.desc: El síndrome de Tourette se asocia frecuentemente con otros trastornos neurodesarrollados, como el TOC, el TDAH o trastornos del aprendizaje.
