nodos.desc: The global sum of all ecosystems, encompassing all life on Earth and the environmental conditions that support it.

nodos.label: Neutro
nodos.desc: Partícula subatómica sin carga eléctrica (0) ubicada en el núcleo del átomo.

nodos.label: Electrón
nodos.desc: Partícula subatómica con carga negativa (-1) que orbita el núcleo en niveles de energía o capas electrónicas.

nodos.label: Núcleo
nodos.desc: Centro del átomo donde se encuentran los protones y neutrones, y que contiene la mayor parte de la masa del átomo.

nodos.label: Capa electrónica
nodos.desc: Rutas definidas en las que los electrones orbitan el núcleo, también conocidas como niveles de energía.

nodos.label: Ion
nodos.desc: Átomo que ha ganado o perdido electrones, resultando en una carga eléctrica neta positiva o negativa.

nodos.label: Ions
nodos.desc: Charged particles formed when atoms gain or lose electrons; cations are positively charged and anions are negatively charged.

nodos.label: Noble Gases
nodos.desc: Elements with completely filled outer electron shells, which makes them chemically inert and highly stable.

nodos.label: Transition Metals
nodos.desc: Elements that can exhibit multiple oxidation states and do not strictly follow the octet rule in their bonding behavior.

nodos.label: Duet Rule
nodos.desc: A rule applicable to some transition metals, stating that they aim to have two valence electrons in their outermost s orbital, resembling helium's stable configuration.

nodos.label: Bond Strength
nodos.desc: The measure of the energy required to break a covalent bond, which increases with the number of shared electron pairs and decreases with larger atomic radii.

nodos.label: Bond Length
nodos.desc: The distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms; longer bond lengths are associated with weaker bonds and larger atomic radii.

nodos.label: Bond Polarity
nodos.desc: The unequal sharing of electrons between two atoms in a bond due to differences in electronegativity, resulting in partial charges.

nodos.label: Molecular Polarity
nodos.desc: The overall polarity of a molecule, determined by the vector sum of bond dipoles and molecular geometry.

nodos.label: Symmetric Electron Distribution
nodos.desc: Even electron density across a molecule, leading to no net dipole moment and nonpolar character in homonuclear diatomic molecules.

nodos.label: Atom Conservation
nodos.desc: The principle that atoms are neither created nor destroyed during a chemical reaction, so the number of each type of atom must be equal on both sides of the equation.

nodos.label: Charge Conservation
nodos.desc: The total electric charge remains constant before and after a chemical reaction, although it is often omitted when all species are neutral.

nodos.label: Reaction Equilibrium
nodos.desc: A state in which the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are equal, resulting in no net change in the concentrations of reactants and products over time.

nodos.label: Balanced Equation
nodos.desc: A chemical equation in which the number of atoms and the total charge are equal on both sides, reflecting the actual proportions of reactants and products.

nodos.label: Cohesion
nodos.desc: Attractive forces between molecules of the same type, such as water molecules interacting with each other through hydrogen bonding.

nodos.label: Adhesion
nodos.desc: Attractive forces between molecules of different types, such as water molecules and the walls of a container.

nodos.label: Convection Current
nodos.desc: Circulación de fluidos causada por diferencias de densidad: el agua caliente se vuelve menos densa y asciende, mientras que el agua fría y densa desciende, generando corrientes que distribuyen nutrientes en el océano.

nodos.label: Thermal Stability
nodos.desc: Propiedad que permite que el agua mantenga una temperatura relativamente constante, lo que ayuda a estabilizar el clima terrestre y protege a los ecosistemas y a la vida en general.

nodos.label: Heat Absorption
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual el agua absorbe calor del entorno (como el sol) sin un aumento significativo de temperatura, lo que es clave para su uso en aplicaciones térmicas y naturales.

nodos.label: Cooling Application
nodos.desc: Uso de agua como refrigerante en plantas de energía, donde circula por alrededores de turbinas para absorber calor y prevenir el sobrecalentamiento.

nodos.label: Cantidades molares
nodos.desc: Cantidad de sustancia expresada en moles, utilizada para equilibrar reacciones químicas y determinar el punto de neutralización.

nodos.label: Ácido de Arrhenius
nodos.desc: Sustancia que al disolverse en agua produce iones H+.

nodos.label: Base de Arrhenius
nodos.desc: Sustancia que al disolverse en agua produce iones OH-.

nodos.label: Ácido de Brønsted-Lowry
nodos.desc: Sustancia que dona un protón (H+) en una reacción química.

nodos.label: Base de Brønsted-Lowry
nodos.desc: Sustancia que acepta un protón (H+) en una reacción química.

nodos.label: Buffer
nodos.desc: Sistema que mantiene una concentración constante de iones hidrógeno (H+) o hidroxilo (OH-), evitando cambios bruscos en el pH al añadir ácidos o bases fuertes.

nodos.label: Constante de disociación (Ka)
nodos.desc: Valor que cuantifica la tendencia de un ácido débil a disociarse en iones H+ y su conjugado base en solución acuosa.

nodos.label: Expresión de Ka
nodos.desc: Fórmula matemática que define la constante de disociación: Ka = [H3O+][A-]/[HA], donde [H3O+] es la concentración de iones hidronio, [A-] es la concentración de la base conjugada y [HA] es la concentración del ácido original.

nodos.label: Clasificación de buffers
nodos.desc: Categorización de los buffers según su composición (tipo de compuesto) o según su capacidad para resistir cambios de pH.

nodos.label: Sistema de bicarbonato
nodos.desc: Buffer biológico compuesto por ácido carbónico (H2CO3) y iones bicarbonato (HCO3-), que mantiene el pH del sangre humana alrededor de 7.4.

nodos.label: Double Bond Stability
nodos.desc: The stability of double bonds formed between oxygen and elements like carbon or silicon, with differences in reactivity and persistence of the resulting compounds.

nodos.label: Disproportionation
nodos.desc: A chemical reaction in which a single species is both oxidized and reduced, leading to the formation of two different products; silanones disproportionate into siloxanes and silanols under ambient conditions.

nodos.label: Tetrahedral Geometry
nodos.desc: A molecular geometry where four atoms or groups are arranged symmetrically around a central atom, commonly observed in both carbon and silicon compounds.

nodos.label: Rotational Barrier
nodos.desc: The energy required to rotate a bond or group around a central atom; silicon exhibits lower rotational barriers than carbon due to its larger atomic mass and increased vibrational freedom.

nodos.label: Conformational Flexibility
nodos.desc: The ability of a molecule to adopt multiple three-dimensional shapes; this property is more pronounced in silicon-based compounds and can hinder precise molecular recognition or catalysis.

nodos.label: Polymer Structure
nodos.desc: The three-dimensional arrangement of repeating units in polymers; poly(silane)s exhibit helical structures similar to proteins, indicating structural parallels between carbon and silicon-based systems.

nodos.label: Self-Assembly
nodos.desc: A process where molecules spontaneously organize into ordered structures without external direction; cyclic silsesquioxanes show self-assembly behavior analogous to lipid bilayers.

nodos.label: Catalytic Efficiency
nodos.desc: The ability of a catalyst to accelerate a chemical reaction effectively; silicon-based enzyme-like catalysts have demonstrated high efficiency in organic transformations.

nodos.label: Elemental Reactivity
nodos.desc: The tendency of an element to participate in redox reactions; silicon shows limited reactivity in redox processes compared to carbon, restricting its role in energy transduction.

nodos.label: Energy Transduction
nodos.desc: The conversion of energy from one form to another; carbon-based systems are central to metabolic energy transduction, while silicon lacks this capacity due to limited redox activity.

nodos.label: Periodic Table Properties
nodos.desc: The systematic arrangement of elements based on atomic structure and properties; understanding differences in bonding and reactivity across the periodic table informs insights into the suitability of elements for life-like systems.

nodos.label: Symmetrical Molecules
nodos.desc: Molecules with symmetric shapes that pack closely in crystal lattices, resulting in higher melting points.

nodos.label: Combustion
nodos.desc: A chemical reaction where hydrocarbons react with oxygen to release energy, commonly used in industrial and transportation applications.

nodos.label: Addition Reactions
nodos.desc: Reactions where atoms or molecules are added across double or triple bonds, such as halogenation, hydrogenation, and hydration.

nodos.label: Substitution Reactions
nodos.desc: Reactions in which a functional group replaces a hydrogen atom, common in saturated hydrocarbons like chlorination and nitration.

nodos.label: Alkanes
nodos.desc: Saturated hydrocarbons with only single carbon-carbon bonds, classified as normal (n-) or branched isomers.

nodos.label: Isomers
nodos.desc: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements.

nodos.label: Alkenes
nodos.desc: Unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon-carbon double bond, which can exhibit cis (Z) and trans (E) configurations.

nodos.label: Cycloalkenes
nodos.desc: Hydrocarbons with a ring structure and one or more double bonds within the ring.

nodos.label: Primary Alcohol
nodos.desc: An alcohol in which the hydroxyl group is bonded to a carbon atom that is directly attached to only one other carbon atom.

nodos.label: Secondary Alcohol
nodos.desc: An alcohol in which the hydroxyl group is bonded to a carbon atom that is directly attached to two other carbon atoms.

nodos.label: Tertiary Alcohol
nodos.desc: An alcohol in which the hydroxyl group is bonded to a carbon atom that is directly attached to three other carbon atoms.

nodos.label: Carboxyl Group
nodos.desc: A functional group (-COOH) found in carboxylic acids, capable of donating a proton (H+) and forming hydrogen bonds.

nodos.label: Asymmetric Carbon
nodos.desc: A carbon atom bonded to four different groups, leading to chirality and the possibility of stereoisomers.

nodos.label: Glycosidic Bond
nodos.desc: A covalent bond formed between two monosaccharide units through dehydration synthesis, linking them in polysaccharides.

nodos.label: Amylase
nodos.desc: An enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of starch into smaller sugars like maltose and glucose.

nodos.label: Cellulase
nodos.desc: An enzyme that breaks down cellulose in plant cell walls into simpler sugars, primarily found in bacteria and fungi.

nodos.label: Chitinase
nodos.desc: An enzyme that hydrolyzes chitin, a structural polysaccharide found in insect exoskeletons and fungal cell walls.

nodos.label: Molecular Machinery
nodos.desc: The complex systems of biomolecules that perform specific functions in cells, such as catalyzing reactions or facilitating transport.

nodos.label: Energy Expenditure
nodos.desc: The amount of energy an organism uses for metabolic processes, often supported by stored energy reserves like glycogen.

nodos.label: Post-Translational Modification
nodos.desc: A process where proteins are chemically modified after synthesis, such as the addition of oligosaccharides, affecting their function and stability.

nodos.label: Amphipathic
nodos.desc: A molecule possessing both hydrophilic (polar) and hydrophobic (nonpolar) regions; in triglycerides, the glycerol head is polar and the fatty acid tails are nonpolar.

nodos.label: Micelle
nodos.desc: A spherical aggregate formed by amphipathic molecules in aqueous environments, with hydrophilic heads facing water and hydrophobic tails clustered together.

nodos.label: Liposome
nodos.desc: A vesicular structure composed of lipid bilayers, where hydrophilic regions face outward and hydrophobic regions face inward, used to encapsulate substances in aqueous environments.

nodos.label: Oxidative Damage
nodos.desc: Degradation of fatty acids caused by reaction with oxygen, which is more likely in unsaturated fats due to the presence of double bonds.

nodos.label: Cholesterol
nodos.desc: A lipid molecule that is not directly discussed in the text but is mentioned in context of health risks related to dietary fats.

nodos.label: Amphiphilic Nature
nodos.desc: Propiedad de ciertos lípidos, como las fosfolípidos, que poseen regiones hidrofóbicas y hidrofílicas, permitiendo su autoensamblaje en estructuras ordenadas en entornos acuosos, formando membranas biológicas.

nodos.label: Membrane Formation and Function
nodos.desc: Formación de bilayers por fosfolípidos debido a su naturaleza amphiphílica, creando barreras selectivamente permeables en células y orgánulos, con proteínas integradas que facilitan transporte, gradientes iónicos y comunicación celular.

nodos.label: Lipid Signaling
nodos.desc: Acción de lípidos como moléculas de señalización en procesos fisiológicos como inflamación, inmunidad y crecimiento celular, ejemplos incluyen eicosanoides, endocannabinoides y esfingosina-1-fosfato.

nodos.label: DNA Structure
nodos.desc: Molécula larga y en forma de escalera torcida encontrada en el núcleo celular, compuesta por dos hebras complementarias unidas por pares de bases.

nodos.label: Ribosome
nodos.desc: A cellular structure composed of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins, where protein synthesis occurs through the formation of peptide bonds between amino acids.

nodos.label: RNA Polymerase
nodos.desc: An enzyme that catalyzes the synthesis of RNA from a DNA template during transcription, adding nucleotides to the growing RNA chain in a sequence complementary to the DNA template.

nodos.label: Formula general de hidratos de carbono
nodos.desc: Ecuación que representa la composición general de los hidratos de carbono, donde n es el número de átomos de carbono.

nodos.label: Monosaccharides
nodos.desc: Azúcares simples que contienen entre tres y siete átomos de carbono, como glucosa, fructosa y galactosa.

nodos.label: Disaccharides
nodos.desc: Compuestos formados por dos unidades de monosaccharides unidas por un enlace glicosídico, ejemplos: sacarosa, lactosa, maltosa.

nodos.label: Oligosaccharides
nodos.desc: Hidratos de carbono compuestos por entre tres y diez unidades de monosaccharides, que actúan como sitios de reconocimiento en interacciones celulares.

nodos.label: Polysacides
nodos.desc: Estructuras complejas formadas por muchas unidades de monosaccharides, utilizadas para almacenar energía y proporcionar soporte estructural.

nodos.label: Configuración D y L
nodos.desc: Clasificación de azúcares basada en la rotación del plano de la luz polarizada: D (giro horario) y L (giro antihorario).

nodos.label: Fructosa
nodos.desc: Azúcar de seis carbonos con estructura cíclica diferente a la de la glucosa, involucrada en la lipogénesis y asociada a problemas metabólicos.

nodos.label: Galactosa
nodos.desc: Azúcar de seis carbonos que se encuentra en la lactosa y participa en procesos metabólicos y estructurales.

nodos.label: Reacción de glicación
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que la glucosa se une a proteínas, modificando su estructura y función, relacionado con enfermedades como la diabetes.

nodos.label: Ruta de pentosa fosfato
nodos.desc: Ciclo metabólico que produce NADPH, ribosa y deoxiribosa, necesarios para la síntesis de nucleótidos.

nodos.label: Microestado
nodos.desc: Cada posible configuración detallada de las partículas en un sistema, que determina el número total de estados accesibles para una condición dada.

nodos.label: Segunda Ley de la Termodinámica
nodos.desc: Afirma que en cualquier transformación de energía, la entropía total de un sistema cerrado siempre aumenta con el tiempo.

nodos.label: Formación y ruptura de enlaces
nodos.desc: Procesos químicos que alteran la estructura molecular, influyendo en el número de microestados y, por tanto, en la entropía del sistema.

nodos.label: Molecular Mobility
nodos.desc: The ability of particles to move freely within a system, which increases with temperature and leads to greater dispersion and interaction among particles.

nodos.label: Endergonico
nodos.desc: Reacción que requiere energía para ocurrir, con cambio de energía libre de Gibbs positivo (ΔG > 0).

nodos.label: Exergónico
nodos.desc: Reacción que libera energía, con cambio de energía libre de Gibbs negativo (ΔG < 0).

nodos.label: Fosforilación de nivel de sustrato
nodos.desc: Mecanismo en el que se forma ATP directamente mediante reacciones químicas en el interior de las células, sin implicar el ciclo de Krebs o la cadena de transporte de electrones.

nodos.label: ATP Hydrolysis
nodos.desc: The enzymatic cleavage of ATP into ADP and inorganic phosphate, releasing free energy used to drive cellular processes.

nodos.label: ATPase
nodos.desc: An enzyme that catalyzes ATP hydrolysis, converting chemical energy into mechanical work, such as muscle contraction or flagellar rotation.

nodos.label: Mechanical Work
nodos.desc: Physical energy output performed by biomolecular machines, such as muscle contraction, driven by ATP hydrolysis.

nodos.label: Km
nodos.desc: La constante de Michaelis (Km) es la concentración de sustrato a la cual la velocidad inicial de la reacción es la mitad de Vmax. Indica la afinidad del enzima por su sustrato; un valor bajo indica alta afinidad.

nodos.label: Ecuación de Michaelis-Menten
nodos.desc: Ecuación matemática que describe la relación entre la velocidad inicial de una reacción enzimática y la concentración de sustrato: v = Vmax[S]/(Km + [S]).

nodos.label: Velocidad inicial
nodos.desc: Es la velocidad de reacción medida en condiciones de concentración de sustrato baja, donde el enzima no está saturado, y se utiliza para determinar Vmax y Km.

nodos.label: Concentración de sustrato
nodos.desc: Variable independiente en la cinética enzimática que se varía para obtener datos de velocidad inicial, y se utiliza en la ecuación de Michaelis-Menten.

nodos.label: Regresión no lineal
nodos.desc: Método matemático utilizado para ajustar datos experimentales a la ecuación de Michaelis-Menten, proporcionando estimaciones más precisas de Vmax y Km sin necesidad de extrapolación.

nodos.label: Gráficos linealizados
nodos.desc: Técnicas gráficas como el plot de Lineweaver-Burk o Eadie-Hofstee que transforman la ecuación de Michaelis-Menten en una forma lineal para facilitar el análisis, aunque introducen errores por extrapolación.

nodos.label: Energía de activación
nodos.desc: Energía mínima que debe ser superada para que una reacción ocurra; los enzimas reducen esta energía, acelerando la reacción sin ser consumidos.

nodos.label: Sitio activo
nodos.desc: Región específica en la estructura de un enzima donde se une el sustrato, permitiendo la conversión de sustrato en producto mediante una serie de pasos intermedios.

nodos.label: Dominio funcional
nodos.desc: Región de una proteína que tiene una función específica, como la unión al sustrato o la catalización, y que está conservada en estructuras similares de enzimas.

nodos.label: Enzyme Binding Sites
nodos.desc: The specific regions on an enzyme where substrates bind, limiting the maximum reaction rate when all sites are occupied.

nodos.label: Competitive Inhibitor
nodos.desc: A molecule that structurally resembles a substrate and competes for the same active site on an enzyme, reducing reaction velocity without covalently modifying the enzyme.

nodos.label: Apparent Dissociation Constant (Ki)
nodos.desc: A parameter in the modified Michaelis-Menten equation that represents the equilibrium constant for the binding of an inhibitor to the enzyme, indicating the inhibitor's affinity for the enzyme.

nodos.label: Michaelis-Menten Equation
nodos.desc: A mathematical model describing enzyme kinetics, relating reaction velocity to substrate concentration, with parameters Km and Vmax.

nodos.label: Michaelis Constant (Km)
nodos.desc: The substrate concentration at which the reaction velocity is half of its maximum value, reflecting the enzyme's affinity for the substrate.

nodos.label: Maximum Reaction Velocity (Vmax)
nodos.desc: The maximum rate of reaction achieved when all enzyme active sites are saturated with substrate.

nodos.label: Reciprocal Reaction Velocity
nodos.desc: The inverse of reaction velocity, used in graphical analysis (e.g., Lineweaver-Burk plot) to linearize the Michaelis-Menten equation.

nodos.label: Concentration Ratio
nodos.desc: The ratio of inhibitor to substrate concentrations, which determines the extent of competitive inhibition in the system.

nodos.label: Tamaño de la célula
nodos.desc: La dimensión física de una célula, que varía entre prokariotas y eucariotas, influye en su estructura y funcionalidad.

nodos.label: Sistema endomembrano
nodos.desc: Red de membranas internas que facilitan el transporte y clasificación de macromoléculas dentro de la célula eucariota.

nodos.label: Complejidad del genoma
nodos.desc: El tamaño y organización del ADN dentro de la célula, que influye en la necesidad de sistemas de transporte y compartimentación.

nodos.label: Estructura celular
nodos.desc: La organización interna de la célula, que determina su capacidad funcional y adaptabilidad a diferentes ambientes.

nodos.label: Surface Area to Volume Ratio
nodos.desc: A mathematical concept that describes the ratio of the surface area of a cell to its volume, influencing cellular functions such as nutrient uptake, waste removal, and gas exchange.

nodos.label: Cell Size and Function
nodos.desc: The relationship between the physical dimensions of a cell and its physiological performance, where smaller cells have higher surface area to volume ratios, enabling more efficient exchange with the environment.

nodos.label: Compartmentalization
nodos.desc: A mathematical and biological principle where internal structures within a cell divide its volume into distinct regions, allowing specialized functions and improving efficiency in material transport and processing.

nodos.label: Permeabilidad selectiva
nodos.desc: Propiedad de la membrana plasmática que permite el paso de ciertas moléculas mientras bloquea otras, basándose en el tamaño, carga y solubilidad de las moléculas.

nodos.label: Lipidos rafts
nodos.desc: Microdominios dinámicos y transitorios en la membrana que contienen altas concentraciones de esfingolípidos y colesterol, que organizan funciones específicas como señalización y endocitosis.

nodos.label: Modelo de mosaico fluido
nodos.desc: Teoría que describe la estructura de la membrana plasmática como una capa fluida y dinámica, compuesta por lípidos y proteínas que se organizan de forma flexible y selectiva.

nodos.label: Movimiento molecular
nodos.desc: Movimiento aleatorio de partículas a nivel molecular que es la base física del proceso de difusión en sistemas biológicos.

nodos.label: Soluto
nodos.desc: Sustancia que se disuelve en un disolvente para formar una solución, y cuya concentración influye en el comportamiento osmótico.

nodos.label: Disolvente
nodos.desc: Sustancia en la que se disuelve el soluto, generalmente agua, que actúa como medio para la difusión y osmosis.

nodos.label: Membrana semipermeable
nodos.desc: Estructura que permite el paso selectivo de moléculas, como el agua, pero rechaza otras sustancias, facilitando el proceso de osmosis.

nodos.label: Tonicidad
nodos.desc: Relación entre la concentración de solutos en una solución y la concentración dentro de una célula, que determina si el agua entra o sale de la célula.

nodos.label: Hipotónico
nodos.desc: Solución con menor concentración de solutos que el interior de la célula, provocando que el agua entre en la célula por osmosis.

nodos.label: Isotónico
nodos.desc: Solución con la misma concentración de solutos que el interior de la célula, resultando en equilibrio osmótico sin flujo neto de agua.

nodos.label: Hiperónico
nodos.desc: Solución con mayor concentración de solutos que el interior de la célula, provocando que el agua salga de la célula por osmosis.

nodos.label: Aquaporina
nodos.desc: Proteína transportadora especializada en facilitar el paso del agua a través de las membranas celulares, aumentando la eficiencia de la osmosis en plantas.

nodos.label: Xilema
nodos.desc: Tissue vegetal que transporta agua y nutrientes desde las raíces hacia las hojas, mediante el movimiento osmótico y por gravedad.

nodos.label: Gradiente osmótico
nodos.desc: Diferencia de concentración de solutos entre dos soluciones separadas por una membrana, que impulsa el movimiento del agua por osmosis.

nodos.label: Crenación
nodos.desc: Deformación y encogimiento de una célula debido a la pérdida de agua en un medio hiperónico, provocando que la célula se vuelva más redonda y delgada.

nodos.label: Tonicidad triángulo
nodos.desc: Representación gráfica que muestra las relaciones entre la presión osmótica, la concentración de solutos y el comportamiento celular en condiciones hipotónicas, isotónicas y hiperónicas.

nodos.label: Fosfolípidos en bilayer
nodos.desc: Estructura de la membrana formada por fosfolípidos con cabeza hidrofílica y colas hidrofóbicas, que se organizan en una capa doble con cabezas hacia el exterior y colas hacia el interior.

nodos.label: Transporte pasivo
nodos.desc: Movimiento de moléculas a través de la membrana sin consumo de energía, facilitado por gradientes de concentración, temperatura y propiedades de la membrana.

nodos.label: Proteínas de canal
nodos.desc: Proteínas que forman poros en la membrana para permitir el paso selectivo de iones, actuando como puertas reguladas.

nodos.label: Proteínas de transporte
nodos.desc: Proteínas que se unen a moléculas específicas en un lado de la membrana y cambian de forma para liberarlas en el otro lado.

nodos.label: Mecanismo de regulación (gating)
nodos.desc: Proceso por el cual los canales o transportadores se abren o cierran en respuesta a señales como cambios de voltaje, ligandos o estrés mecánico.

nodos.label: Solute Potential (Ψs)
nodos.desc: The component of water potential that reflects the effect of dissolved solutes on water movement; it decreases as solute concentration increases.

nodos.label: Membrane Curvature
nodos.desc: The shape of a membrane surface, influenced by proteins that sense and regulate curvature during cellular processes like endocytosis and exocytosis.

nodos.label: Scaffolding
nodos.desc: Structural organization of proteins that provide a framework for assembling signaling complexes and stabilizing membrane protein interactions.

nodos.label: Signaling Complex Assembly
nodos.desc: The formation of multi-protein complexes on membranes that facilitate intracellular communication and response to external stimuli.

nodos.label: Targeting
nodos.desc: The mechanism by which integral membrane proteins are directed to specific subcellular locations within the membrane.

nodos.label: BAR Domain
nodos.desc: A protein structural motif that senses and induces membrane curvature, playing a key role in membrane shaping during vesicle trafficking.

nodos.label: Molecular Dynamics
nodos.desc: A computational method simulating the physical movements of atoms and molecules over time to predict protein conformational changes and interactions.

nodos.label: Cryo-Electron Microscopy (Cryo-EM)
nodos.desc: A technique that captures high-resolution images of membrane proteins in near-native states by rapidly freezing samples.

nodos.label: X-ray Free Electron Laser (XFEL)
nodos.desc: An advanced imaging technique that uses intense X-ray pulses to determine the 3D structure of membrane proteins at atomic resolution.

nodos.label: Redox Reaction
nodos.desc: A chemical reaction in which oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously; involves transfer of electrons, crucial in cellular respiration for energy conversion.

nodos.label: Half-Reactions
nodos.desc: A method to separate redox reactions into oxidation and reduction components to analyze electron transfer individually.

nodos.label: Proton Gradient
nodos.desc: An electrochemical gradient of protons (H+) across a membrane, established by electron transport, used to generate ATP through ATP synthase.

nodos.label: Oxygen
nodos.desc: Final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration, reduced to form water during the electron transport chain.

nodos.label: Dephosphorylation
nodos.desc: The removal of a phosphate group from a molecule, such as in the conversion of 2-phosphoglycerate to phosphoenolpyruvate, which generates a high-energy intermediate.

nodos.label: Substrate-level phosphorylation
nodos.desc: A mechanism by which ATP is synthesized directly from the transfer of a phosphate group to ADP, occurring during specific enzymatic reactions in glycolysis.

nodos.label: Isomerization
nodos.desc: A chemical reaction that alters the structure of a molecule without changing its molecular formula, such as the conversion of glucose-6-phosphate to fructose-6-phosphate.

nodos.label: Energy yield
nodos.desc: The total amount of ATP and NADH produced per glucose molecule during glycolysis, with a net yield of two ATP molecules after accounting for initial ATP investment.

nodos.label: High-energy state
nodos.desc: A molecular state characterized by a high potential energy, such as in phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), which readily donates a phosphate group to ADP to form ATP.

nodos.label: Molecular formula
nodos.desc: The chemical composition of a molecule expressed in terms of the number of atoms of each element, which remains constant during isomerization reactions.

nodos.label: Cytochrome c
nodos.desc: A mobile protein that transfers electrons from Complex III to Complex IV in the electron transport chain.

nodos.label: Flavin mononucleotide
nodos.desc: A cofactor in Complex I that accepts electrons from NADH and is reduced to FMNH2.

nodos.label: Iron-sulfur clusters
nodos.desc: Protein-bound clusters that facilitate electron transfer within Complex I.

nodos.label: Heme groups
nodos.desc: Protein-bound porphyrin rings in cytochromes that mediate electron transfer in Complex III and cytochrome c.

nodos.label: Proton motive force
nodos.desc: The electrochemical gradient of protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane, generated by electron transport and used to drive ATP synthesis.

nodos.label: ATP synthase
nodos.desc: An enzyme complex (Complex V) that uses the flow of protons back into the matrix to synthesize ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate.

nodos.label: Chemiosmotic potential
nodos.desc: The energy stored in the proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane, which drives ATP synthesis via ATP synthase.

nodos.label: Complex I
nodos.desc: The first protein complex in the electron transport chain that accepts electrons from NADH and transfers them to ubiquinone.

nodos.label: Complex III
nodos.desc: A cytochrome complex that transfers electrons from ubiquinone to cytochrome c via heme groups and pumps protons across the membrane.

nodos.label: Complex IV
nodos.desc: The terminal complex in the electron transport chain that transfers electrons to oxygen, forming water and pumping additional protons.

nodos.label: Inorganic phosphate
nodos.desc: A phosphate group that combines with ADP to form ATP in the presence of energy from the proton motive force.

nodos.label: Inhibitors
nodos.desc: Molecules that bind to specific sites in the electron transport chain to block electron flow and regulate cellular respiration.

nodos.label: Antimycin A
nodos.desc: An inhibitor of Complex III that blocks electron transfer from ubiquinone to cytochrome c.

nodos.label: Feedback regulation
nodos.desc: A mechanism where high ATP levels inhibit electron entry into the ETC, reducing metabolic activity to prevent overproduction of energy.

nodos.label: Ethanol
nodos.desc: An alcohol produced during fermentation as a byproduct of the reduction of acetaldehyde, using NADH as a reducing agent.

nodos.label: Carbon Dioxide
nodos.desc: A gas released during the decarboxylation of pyruvate in the fermentation process.

nodos.label: NAD+
nodos.desc: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide in its oxidized form, essential for electron transport and used to regenerate during fermentation.

nodos.label: NADH
nodos.desc: Reduced form of NAD+, produced during glycolysis and used in the reduction of acetaldehyde to ethanol in fermentation.

nodos.label: Glyceraldehyde-3-Phosphate
nodos.desc: A three-carbon sugar phosphate intermediate in glycolysis and fermentation, involved in the production of NADH and subsequent energy generation.

nodos.label: Dihydroxyacetone Phosphate
nodos.desc: A three-carbon sugar phosphate intermediate that splits from fructose-1,6-bisphosphate and is converted to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate.

nodos.label: Fructose-1,6-Bisphosphate
nodos.desc: A key intermediate in glycolysis and fermentation, formed from glucose through a series of enzymatic reactions.

nodos.label: Acetaldehyde
nodos.desc: An intermediate in alcohol fermentation, produced from pyruvate decarboxylation and reduced to ethanol by alcohol dehydrogenase.

nodos.label: Anaerobic
nodos.desc: Conditions in which oxygen is absent, leading organisms to use fermentation instead of aerobic respiration to generate energy.

nodos.label: Aldolase
nodos.desc: An enzyme that catalyzes the cleavage of fructose-1,6-bisphosphate into dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate.

nodos.label: Alcohol Dehydrogenase
nodos.desc: An enzyme that reduces acetaldehyde to ethanol, using NADH as a cofactor to regenerate NAD+.

nodos.label: Electrical Potential (ΔΨ)
nodos.desc: Diferencia de potencial eléctrico entre dos regiones, que es una componente del gradiente de protones en el proceso de fotosíntesis.

nodos.label: pH Gradient (ΔpH)
nodos.desc: Diferencia de pH entre dos regiones, que es la otra componente del gradiente de protones en el proceso de fotosíntesis.

nodos.label: Rotación del anillo c
nodos.desc: Movimiento rotacional del anillo c dentro del dominio Fo, que transmite torque al dominio F1 a través del tallo central.

nodos.label: Síntesis de ATP
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual se forma ATP a partir de ADP y fosfato, impulsado por el gradiente de protones en la fotosíntesis.

nodos.label: Reacciones dependientes de luz
nodos.desc: Fase de la fotosíntesis que ocurre en la membrana tilacoidal y requiere luz para producir ATP, NADPH y oxígeno a partir del agua.

nodos.label: Ciclo de Calvin
nodos.desc: Fase de la fotosíntesis que no requiere luz y utiliza ATP y NADPH para convertir CO2 en glucosa.

nodos.label: Energía química
nodos.desc: Forma de energía almacenada en enlaces químicos, como en el ATP, que se utiliza para realizar trabajo celular.

nodos.label: Síntesis de glucosa
nodos.desc: Proceso mediante el cual se forma glucosa a partir de dióxido de carbono y agua, utilizando energía de la luz en la fotosíntesis.

nodos.label: ATP Synthesis
nodos.desc: The formation of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) from adenosine diphosphate (ADP) and inorganic phosphate (Pi) via ATP synthase enzyme complexes, powered by proton diffusion across membranes.

nodos.label: Carboxylation
nodos.desc: The first stage of the Calvin cycle where carbon dioxide is added to ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP) to form a six-carbon intermediate that immediately splits into two three-carbon molecules.

nodos.label: Regeneration of RuBP
nodos.desc: The third stage of the Calvin cycle where the G3P molecules are used to regenerate ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP), the starting molecule, to allow the cycle to continue.

nodos.label: Xanthophylls
nodos.desc: Pigments that help dissipate excess light energy as heat in plants, preventing photooxidative damage and protecting photosystems from overexposure.

nodos.label: Thylakoid Membranes
nodos.desc: Internal membrane structures within chloroplasts where light-dependent reactions occur, housing photosystems and ATP synthase complexes.

nodos.label: 3-Phosphoglycerate
nodos.desc: A three-carbon intermediate produced in the Calvin cycle during carbon fixation in C3 plants.

nodos.label: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase
nodos.desc: The enzyme responsible for carbon fixation in photosynthesis; it has both carboxylase and oxygenase activities, with the oxygenase activity leading to photorespiration.

nodos.label: Glycine
nodos.desc: An intermediate formed during the conversion of PG (pyruvate or glycolate) in peroxisomes, involved in the photorespiratory cycle.

nodos.label: Serine
nodos.desc: A molecule produced during transamination and decarboxylation in mitochondria, which is later transported back to the peroxisome and converted into glycerate.

nodos.label: Glycerate
nodos.desc: A compound derived from serine in peroxisomes, which can re-enter the Calvin cycle after transport into chloroplasts.

nodos.label: Ammonia (NH3)
nodos.desc: A byproduct of decarboxylation in mitochondria; must be reassimilated to prevent toxicity and requires energy for conversion to glutamine.

nodos.label: Glutamine
nodos.desc: An amino acid formed from ammonia via assimilation, which completes the photorespiratory cycle and recycles nitrogen.

nodos.label: Reducing power
nodos.desc: A form of energy (e.g., NADPH) used in metabolic reactions to drive redox processes, such as those in photorespiration.

nodos.label: C3 Photosynthesis
nodos.desc: A photosynthetic pathway in which CO2 is fixed into a three-carbon compound (3-PGA) via the Calvin cycle, common in most plants but prone to photorespiration.

nodos.label: C4 Photosynthesis
nodos.desc: A photosynthetic pathway that spatially separates CO2 fixation and the Calvin cycle to minimize photorespiration, especially under high temperature and low CO2 conditions.

nodos.label: Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM) Photosynthesis
nodos.desc: A photosynthetic strategy in which plants open stomata at night to fix CO2 into organic acids, minimizing photorespiration under high temperature and low CO2 conditions.

nodos.label: Oxygenase Activity
nodos.desc: The activity of Rubisco that catalyzes the reaction with O2 instead of CO2, leading to photorespiration and reduced carbon fixation efficiency.

nodos.label: Carboxylase Activity
nodos.desc: The activity of Rubisco that catalyzes the reaction with CO2 to fix carbon into organic molecules, which is favored under low oxygen and high CO2 conditions.

nodos.label: Estomatas
nodos.desc: Estructuras en las plantas que regulan el intercambio de gases, abriendo y cerrando para controlar la pérdida de agua y la absorción de CO₂.

nodos.label: Enzima PEP carboxilasa
nodos.desc: Enzima que cataliza la fijación de CO₂ en plantas CAM, utilizando fosfenolpiruvato (PEP) para formar oxalacetato.

nodos.label: Ácido málico
nodos.desc: Compuesto orgánico almacenado en plantas CAM que sirve como fuente de CO₂ durante la fase diurna para la fotosíntesis.

nodos.label: Carbonato anidro
nodos.desc: Enzima que convierte CO₂ en bicarbonato (HCO₃⁻), facilitando su uso en la fijación de carbono en plantas CAM.

nodos.label: Ciclo de Calvin
nodos.desc: Secuencia de reacciones que convierten CO₂ en triosas, que luego se transforman en azúcares como la sacarosa para el crecimiento.

nodos.label: Triosas
nodos.desc: Productos de la fotosíntesis que se forman en el ciclo de Calvin y se utilizan para producir azúcares como la sacarosa.

nodos.label: Vacuola
nodos.desc: Orgánulo celular donde se almacena el ácido málico en plantas CAM para su posterior liberación durante el día.

nodos.label: Metabotropic Receptor
nodos.desc: A type of receptor that activates intracellular signaling pathways via G-proteins, resulting in slower, biochemical responses in the postsynaptic neuron.

nodos.label: Cellular Communication
nodos.desc: The process by which cells transmit signals to one another to coordinate functions, enabling complex biological processes in multicellular organisms.

nodos.label: Paracrine Signaling
nodos.desc: A mode of communication where signaling molecules are released and act on nearby cells, not through a long-distance medium.

nodos.label: Autocrine Signaling
nodos.desc: A signaling mechanism in which a cell produces and responds to its own signaling molecules.

nodos.label: Juxtacrine Signaling
nodos.desc: A form of cell-to-cell communication where signaling occurs through direct contact between adjacent cells, often via membrane-bound ligands.

nodos.label: Hormone
nodos.desc: A chemical messenger that travels through the bloodstream to target tissues and organs, regulating physiological processes such as metabolism and growth.

nodos.label: Hormone Classes
nodos.desc: Categorization of hormones based on chemical structure: amines, peptides/proteins, and steroids, each with distinct solubility, transport, and action mechanisms.

nodos.label: Catecholamines
nodos.desc: A class of hormones derived from tyrosine, including adrenaline, which play roles in stress response and metabolic regulation.

nodos.label: Peptide Hormones
nodos.desc: Hormones composed of short to long chains of amino acids, such as insulin and glucagon, which act via receptor binding and intracellular signaling.

nodos.label: Steroid Hormones
nodos.desc: Hormones derived from cholesterol and sharing a common ring structure, such as cortisol and testosterone, which are lipid-soluble and diffuse through membranes.

nodos.label: Downstream Signaling
nodos.desc: A cascade of intracellular events initiated by hormone-receptor binding, leading to changes in gene expression, protein activity, and cell behavior.

nodos.label: Hyperinsulinemia
nodos.desc: Condición caracterizada por niveles anormalmente altos de insulina en la sangre, que puede llevar a complicaciones como diabetes tipo 2 y enfermedades cardiovasculares.

nodos.label: Thyroxine (T4)
nodos.desc: Hormona tiroidea producida por la glándula tiroides, que actúa como prohormona y se convierte en T3 en tejidos periféricos.

nodos.label: Triiodothyronine (T3)
nodos.desc: Forma biológicamente activa de la hormona tiroidea, responsable de mediar efectos fisiológicos de la hormona tiroidea en diversos tejidos.

nodos.label: Deiodination
nodos.desc: Proceso en el que se elimina un ión de la hormona tiroidea (T4) para convertirla en T3, regulando la disponibilidad activa de la hormona.

nodos.label: Número cromosómico
nodos.desc: Cantidad de cromosomas en una célula. En mitosis se mantiene constante (diploide, 2n), mientras que en meiosis se reduce a la mitad (haploide, n).

nodos.label: Citosquesis
nodos.desc: Proceso que sigue a la división nuclear, en el cual el citoplasma se divide, resultando en células hijas separadas.

nodos.label: Fibras de huso
nodos.desc: Estructuras que se forman a partir de centrosomas o cuerpos polares y se unen a los cromatidas hermanas en los cromosomas, permitiendo su movimiento durante las fases de metafase, anafase y telofase.

nodos.label: Puntos de control
nodos.desc: Mecanismos que supervisan la replicación y separación correcta del ADN durante mitosis y meiosis, evitando errores que podrían causar mutaciones o enfermedades.

nodos.label: Diploid cell
nodos.desc: A cell containing two sets of chromosomes, one from each parent, typically found in somatic cells.

nodos.label: Meiosis II
nodos.desc: The second division of meiosis that separates sister chromatids, resulting in four haploid gametes from a single diploid cell.

nodos.label: Sister Chromatids
nodos.desc: Identical copies of a chromosome formed during DNA replication, joined at the centromere and separated during meiosis II.

nodos.label: Cohesin Proteins
nodos.desc: Proteins that hold sister chromatids together, preventing their separation until anaphase of meiosis II.

nodos.label: Metaphase Plate
nodos.desc: An imaginary plane in the cell during metaphase where chromosomes align at the equator of the cell during meiosis II.

nodos.label: Kinetochores
nodos.desc: Structures at the centromere of chromosomes that attach to microtubules during cell division, ensuring proper chromosome segregation.

nodos.label: Spindle Apparatus
nodos.desc: A structure composed of microtubules that forms during prophase and facilitates chromosome movement during cell division.

nodos.label: Hemato-lymphoid homeostasis
nodos.desc: The balanced state of hematopoietic and lymphoid cell production, maintenance, and regulation in the body.

nodos.label: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL)
nodos.desc: A type of leukemia characterized by the rapid proliferation of immature lymphoid cells, affecting both children and adults.

nodos.label: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)
nodos.desc: A slow-progressing leukemia primarily affecting older individuals, typically beyond the sixth decade of life.

nodos.label: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML)
nodos.desc: A chronic form of leukemia with a median age of onset between the fifth and seventh decades, involving myeloid cells.

nodos.label: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL)
nodos.desc: A subtype of AML defined by a specific translocation t(15;17) leading to PML-RARA fusion protein, disrupting differentiation and causing blast accumulation.

nodos.label: Translocation t(15;17)(q24;q21)
nodos.desc: A reciprocal balanced chromosomal translocation that results in the formation of the PML-RARA fusion oncoprotein.

nodos.label: PML-RARA Fusion Protein
nodos.desc: A chimeric oncoprotein formed by the t(15;17) translocation, which interferes with normal granulocytic differentiation.

nodos.label: Blast Accumulation
nodos.desc: The abnormal buildup of immature, undifferentiated cells in the bone marrow and blood, a hallmark of acute leukemias.

nodos.label: Coagulopathy
nodos.desc: A disorder of blood clotting, in this context caused by fibrinolysis activation due to elevated plasmin levels in APL.

nodos.label: All-Trans Retinoic Acid (ATRA)
nodos.desc: A retinoid derivative used in therapy to restore granulocytic differentiation in APL.

nodos.label: Arsenic Trioxide
nodos.desc: A chemotherapeutic agent used in combination with ATRA to eliminate residual leukemic clones in APL.

nodos.label: Hodgkin Lymphoma (HL)
nodos.desc: A lymphoma characterized by the presence of Reed-Sternberg cells, arising from transformed lymphocytes in lymph nodes or bone marrow.

nodos.label: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL)
nodos.desc: A broad category of lymphomas originating from transformed lymphocytes, including B-cell, T-cell, and natural killer cell derivatives.

nodos.label: B-cell Lymphoma
nodos.desc: The most common type of NHL, derived from B-lymphocytes, accounting for over 90% of cases.

nodos.label: T-cell Lymphoma
nodos.desc: A less common form of NHL derived from T-lymphocytes, representing about 5% of cases.

nodos.label: Natural Killer Cell Lymphoma
nodos.desc: A rare subtype of NHL derived from natural killer cells, accounting for approximately 1% of cases.

nodos.label: Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma (DLBCL)
nodos.desc: The most common form of NHL, exhibiting heterogeneous clinical and biological behavior with distinct subtypes.

nodos.label: Activated B-cell–like DLBCL (ABC-DLBCL)
nodos.desc: A molecular subtype of DLBCL with inferior prognosis due to distinct signaling pathways and resistance to therapy.

nodos.label: Germinal Center B-cell–like DLBCL (GCB-DLBCL)
nodos.desc: A molecular subtype of DLBCL with favorable response to standard chemotherapy regimens like R-CHOP.

nodos.label: R-CHOP Regimen
nodos.desc: A standard chemotherapy protocol for GCB-DLBCL, consisting of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone.

nodos.label: Carcinogenesis
nodos.desc: The process by which normal cells transform into cancer cells through genetic and epigenetic alterations.

nodos.label: Signal Transduction Cascade
nodos.desc: A series of molecular events that transmit signals from the cell surface to the nucleus, often perturbed in cancer development.

nodos.label: Intracellular Signal Perturbation
nodos.desc: Abnormal regulation of intracellular signaling pathways that contribute to uncontrolled cell growth and survival in cancer.

nodos.label: DNA
nodos.desc: Molécula que contiene las instrucciones para el desarrollo y funcionamiento de todos los organismos vivos.

nodos.label: Cromosomas
nodos.desc: Estructuras que organizan el ADN en las células; en humanos, hay 46 cromosomas en 23 pares, uno de cada par proveniente de cada padre.

nodos.label: Alelos
nodos.desc: Formas diferentes de un mismo gen que pueden ser heredados y que determinan variaciones en características fenotípicas.

nodos.label: Homozygote
nodos.desc: Individuo que posee dos copias idénticas de un gen (por ejemplo, AA o aa).

nodos.label: Heterozygote
nodos.desc: Individuo que posee dos copias diferentes de un gen (por ejemplo, Aa).

nodos.label: Genotipo
nodos.desc: Combinación de alelos que un individuo hereda para un gen específico.

nodos.label: Recesivo
nodos.desc: Alelo que solo se expresa en el fenotipo cuando no hay un alelo dominante presente.

nodos.label: F1 (primera generación filial)
nodos.desc: Generación de descendientes obtenida al cruzar dos individuos con características distintas, como en el experimento de Mendel con plantas de guisantes.

nodos.label: Reorganización cromosómica
nodos.desc: Cambio en la estructura de un cromosoma, como translocaciones o inversiones, que puede afectar el genotipo y fenotipo.

nodos.label: Cromosoma X
nodos.desc: Cromosoma sexual que determina el sexo en muchos organismos y que contiene genes relacionados con rasgos como el color del ojo.

nodos.label: Cromosoma Y
nodos.desc: Cromosoma sexual que se encuentra en los machos y que contribuye a la determinación del sexo en muchos organismos.

nodos.label: Radiación ionizante
nodos.desc: Tipo de radiación que puede dañar el ADN y provocar mutaciones en los cromosomas.

nodos.label: Pair of chromosomes
nodos.desc: A set of two chromosomes that carry genetic information; humans have 23 pairs.

nodos.label: DNA base sequence
nodos.desc: The order of nucleotide bases (A, T, C, G) in DNA that encodes genetic information.

nodos.label: Messenger RNA (mRNA)
nodos.desc: An RNA molecule that carries genetic information from DNA to the ribosome for protein synthesis.

nodos.label: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)
nodos.desc: A technique that amplifies specific DNA regions, allowing for detailed analysis of small DNA samples.

nodos.label: DNA sequencing
nodos.desc: The process of determining the precise order of nucleotide bases in a DNA molecule.

nodos.label: Genetic information
nodos.desc: The data encoded in the DNA base sequence that determines the traits and functions of an organism.

nodos.label: Genetic inheritance
nodos.desc: The transmission of genetic information from one generation to the next through DNA.

nodos.label: Sugar-Phosphate Backbone
nodos.desc: The structural framework of DNA formed by alternating sugar and phosphate groups, located on the outside of the double helix and providing stability and directionality.

nodos.label: X-ray crystallography
nodos.desc: A technique used to determine the three-dimensional atomic structure of a crystal by analyzing the diffraction patterns produced when high-energy radiation is passed through the material.

nodos.label: Diffraction patterns
nodos.desc: Visual representations of how radiation waves scatter when interacting with a material, used to infer structural details of molecules such as DNA.

nodos.label: Helical structure
nodos.desc: A three-dimensional structure in which components are arranged in a spiral or coil, as seen in DNA, where the molecule forms a double helix with two strands winding around each other.

nodos.label: Hydrogen bonds
nodos.desc: Intermolecular forces that occur when a hydrogen atom is covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom and is attracted to another electronegative atom, providing stability to the double helix structure of DNA.

nodos.label: Double helix model
nodos.desc: A mathematical and structural model of DNA that consists of two antiparallel strands coiled around a central axis, with base pairs forming the rungs of the helix, stabilized by hydrogen bonds.

nodos.label: 5' to 3' direction
nodos.desc: A directional constraint in DNA synthesis where nucleotides are added only from the 5' end to the 3' end of a growing DNA strand.

nodos.label: Leading strand
nodos.desc: The DNA strand synthesized continuously in the 5' to 3' direction, parallel to the replication fork movement, allowing uninterrupted elongation.

nodos.label: Lagging strand
nodos.desc: The DNA strand synthesized discontinuously in short segments called Okazaki fragments, antiparallel to the replication fork, due to the 5' to 3' synthesis constraint.

nodos.label: Okazaki fragments
nodos.desc: Short segments of DNA synthesized on the lagging strand, each initiated by an RNA primer and later joined by DNA ligase to form a continuous strand.

nodos.label: RNA primer
nodos.desc: A short sequence of RNA nucleotides added by primase to provide a free 3' hydroxyl group for DNA polymerase to initiate DNA synthesis.

nodos.label: Discontinuous synthesis
nodos.desc: A process in which DNA is synthesized in short, non-continuous segments, as opposed to a single continuous chain, due to the 5' to 3' directionality of DNA polymerase.

nodos.label: DNA ligation
nodos.desc: The enzymatic joining of adjacent DNA fragments, such as Okazaki fragments, to form a continuous DNA strand.

nodos.label: Mutation accumulation
nodos.desc: The increased likelihood of errors in DNA replication on the lagging strand due to repeated initiation and termination cycles of fragment synthesis.

nodos.label: G-quadruplex
nodos.desc: Estructura formada por arreglos apilados de guaninas unidas por iones metálicos, comúnmente encontrada cerca de promotores de genes y telomerias.

nodos.label: Kissing loop
nodos.desc: Emparejamiento de segmentos de RNA distantes que se acercan debido a la conformación general de la molécula de RNA.

nodos.label: A-minor interaction
nodos.desc: Emparejamiento no canónico que involucra adeninas que se encajan estrechamente en las zonas menores formadas por otros elementos helicoidales.

nodos.label: transfer RNA (tRNA)
nodos.desc: ARN que actúa como adaptador, vinculando aminoácidos específicos a codones durante la traducción, con estructuras secundarias en forma de hoja de clover compuesta por bucles de aceptación, D, anticodón y TΨC.

nodos.label: ribosomal RNA (rRNA)
nodos.desc: ARN que forma parte integral de los ribosomas, mediando reacciones de transferencia peptídica y facilitando la escaneo de ARN mensajero, con estructuras terciarias complejas basadas en pares de bases intramoleculares y interacciones con proteínas ribosómicas.

nodos.label: small nuclear RNA (snRNA)
nodos.desc: ARN que participa en la splicing de ARN pre-mRNA, funcionando junto con proteínas en la formación y catalización del spliceosoma, reconociendo secuencias de consenso en los límites intrónicos.

nodos.label: small nucleolar RNA (snoRNA)
nodos.desc: ARN que guía modificaciones posttranscripcionales de ARN ribosómico y transferente, actuando con cofactores enzimáticos para facilitar metilación o modificaciones pseudouridínicas.

nodos.label: EF-Tu release
nodos.desc: The dissociation of the tRNA•amino acid complex from EF-Tu after GTP hydrolysis, enabling the tRNA to enter the ribosomal A-site.

nodos.label: Peptidyl transferase activity
nodos.desc: An intrinsic ribosomal function that catalyzes the formation of a peptide bond between the growing polypeptide chain and the new amino acid.

nodos.label: Elongation factor (EF-G or eEF2)
nodos.desc: A protein that facilitates conformational changes in the ribosome during translocation, ensuring accurate movement of the ribosome along the mRNA.

nodos.label: Stop codon
nodos.desc: A sequence in mRNA that signals the end of translation; recognized by release factors to terminate protein synthesis.

nodos.label: Release factors (RF1, RF2)
nodos.desc: Proteins that bind to stop codons and catalyze the cleavage of the polypeptide chain from the tRNA in the P-site.

nodos.label: Ribosome recycling
nodos.desc: The process by which the ribosome is disassembled and reassembled for subsequent rounds of translation, facilitated by RF3.

nodos.label: Misincorporation
nodos.desc: The erroneous insertion of an incorrect amino acid during translation, which can lead to nonfunctional or harmful proteins.

nodos.label: Peptidyl-tRNA hydrolase
nodos.desc: An enzyme that recognizes and removes misincorporated amino acids from the tRNA, preventing the formation of defective proteins.

nodos.label: Nonsense-mediated decay (NMD)
nodos.desc: A cellular surveillance mechanism that degrades mRNAs containing premature stop codons to prevent production of truncated proteins.

nodos.label: Operon
nodos.desc: A cluster of genes in bacterial DNA that are transcribed together as a single mRNA molecule, enabling coordinated gene expression.

nodos.label: Operator region
nodos.desc: A DNA segment that serves as a binding site for regulatory proteins, such as repressors or activators, to control gene expression in operons.

nodos.label: Ribose Sugar
nodos.desc: A five-carbon sugar found in RNA, with a hydroxyl group at the second carbon (C2'), which contributes to its reactivity and structural differences from DNA's deoxyribose.

nodos.label: Deoxyribose Sugar
nodos.desc: A five-carbon sugar found in DNA, lacking a hydroxyl group at the second carbon (C2'), making it more stable than ribose-containing RNA.

nodos.label: Uracil
nodos.desc: A nitrogenous base in RNA that pairs with adenine via two hydrogen bonds, replacing thymine in DNA.

nodos.label: Adenine, Guanine, Cytosine
nodos.desc: Nitrogenous bases in DNA that participate in Watson-Crick base pairing, with adenine pairing with thymine and guanine with cytosine.

nodos.label: Primary Structure
nodos.desc: The linear sequence of nucleotides in a nucleic acid, which encodes genetic information and determines the molecule's function and stability.

nodos.label: Sense strand
nodos.desc: The DNA strand that contains the same sequence as the mRNA transcript, except for T instead of U, and is used as a reference for the coding sequence.

nodos.label: Antisense strand
nodos.desc: The DNA strand that serves as a template for RNA synthesis and contains a sequence complementary to the mRNA transcript.

nodos.label: mRNA codon
nodos.desc: A triplet sequence of nucleotides in mRNA that specifies a particular amino acid during protein synthesis.

nodos.label: tRNA anticodon
nodos.desc: A triplet sequence in the tRNA that is complementary to an mRNA codon and ensures correct amino acid pairing during translation.

nodos.label: Semiconservative replication
nodos.desc: A mechanism in which each new DNA double helix consists of one original parental strand and one newly synthesized complementary strand, preserving genetic information across generations.

nodos.label: Directionality
nodos.desc: The inherent orientation of DNA strands (5' to 3') that governs the sequence and alignment of nucleotides during replication, transcription, and translation.

nodos.label: RNA Polimerase II
nodos.desc: Enzima responsable de la transcripción de genes que codifican proteínas, que se une a regiones promotoras del ADN.

nodos.label: Enhancer
nodos.desc: Elemento regulador del ADN que puede estar a kilómetros de distancia del promotor y que, mediante interacciones de bucle, activa la transcripción de genes.

nodos.label: Lineage-Specific Transcription Factor
nodos.desc: Factores de transcripción cuya expresión está restringida a tipos celulares específicos y que definen la identidad celular.

nodos.label: Basal Transcription Machinery
nodos.desc: Conjunto de factores de transcripción generales (GTFs) esenciales para la reconocimiento del promotor y la iniciación precisa de la transcripción, incluyendo TFIIA, TFIIB, TFIID, TFIIE, TFIIF y TFIIH, que recrutan a la polimerasa II para formar el complejo preinicial (PIC).

nodos.label: Core Promoter
nodos.desc: Promotor básico que contiene elementos conservados como el box TATA (TATAAA), el iniciador (INR), el elemento de promotor descendente (DPE) y el elemento Motif Ten (MTE), que determinan el sitio de inicio de transcripción.

nodos.label: Proximal Promoter
nodos.desc: Promotor proximal que contiene elementos de regulación en el cromatina, como promotores de activación (enhancers) y silenciadores, reconocidos por factores de transcripción específicos o dependientes de señales, que pueden estar a kilómetros de distancia del gen objetivo y requieren interacciones a largo alcance mediadas por proteínas como CTCF y Cohesin.

nodos.label: Transcription Factor Classification
nodos.desc: Clasificación de factores de transcripción eucarióticos basada en sus dominios de reconocimiento de ADN: Helix-Turn-Helix (HTH) y proteínas de zinc. Los HTH incluyen homeodominio, dominio forkhead, bZIP y tipo winged-helix; los de zinc incluyen Cys2His2, GLI-type zinc knuckle, PHD-finger, entre otros. Muchos factores poseen dominios de activación y reprimición modulares que confieren actividad contextual al interactuar con coreguladores.

nodos.label: Chromatin Modifications
nodos.desc: Modificaciones posttranslacionales de histonas como metilación, acetilación, fosforilación, ubiquitinación y sumoylación que determinan el estado local del cromatina y su accesibilidad para el equipo de transcripción.

nodos.label: Post-transcriptional Regulation
nodos.desc: Mecanismos por los cuales las células controlan la expresión génica después de la transcripción inicial de ADN en ARN.

nodos.label: RNA Processing
nodos.desc: Modificaciones que sufre el ARN primario antes de convertirse en ARN mensajero maduro, incluyendo capping, splicing y polyadenylation.

nodos.label: Capping
nodos.desc: Adición de una capa de 7-metilguanina al extremo 5' del ARN que protege al ARN de la degradación y facilita su reconocimiento por la maquinaria de traducción.

nodos.label: Polyadenylation
nodos.desc: Adición de una cadena de adeninas al extremo 3' del ARN que protege al ARN de la degradación y facilita su exportación del núcleo.

nodos.label: RNA Stability
nodos.desc: Duración promedio del ARN mensajero antes de su degradación, que varía según el tipo celular y condiciones ambientales.

nodos.label: MicroRNAs (miRNAs)
nodos.desc: ARNs no codificantes pequeños que se unen a secuencias complementarias en ARN mensajero, induciendo su inestabilidad y degradación.

nodos.label: AU-Rich Elements (AREs)
nodos.desc: Secuencias ricas en adenina que influyen en la estabilidad del ARN mensajero y pueden regular su degradación.

nodos.label: Reverse Transcriptase
nodos.desc: Enzyma virales que convierte el ARN viral en ADN complementario (cDNA).

nodos.label: cDNA
nodos.desc: ADN complementario sintetizado a partir del ARN viral por la enzima reverse transcriptase.

nodos.label: Double-Stranded Viral DNA
nodos.desc: Molécula de ADN viral doble cadena formada por la replicación de la cDNA.

nodos.label: Long Terminal Repeats (LTRs)
nodos.desc: Secuencias repetitivas en los extremos del ADN viral que actúan como promotores y reguladores de transcripción.

nodos.label: Preintegration Complex (PIC)
nodos.desc: Complejo formado por el ADN viral y proteínas virales y de host que se mueve hacia el núcleo para la integración.

nodos.label: Host Cell Genome
nodos.desc: Genoma del hospedador en el que se integra el ADN viral, convirtiéndose así parte del código genético del hospedador.

nodos.label: Latent Virus
nodos.desc: Virus integrado que permanece inactivo durante largos períodos hasta que se activa por un estímulo ambiental.

nodos.label: Cromosoma autosómico
nodos.desc: Cromosoma no relacionado con el sexo, que incluye los cromosomas 1 a 22 en humanos.

nodos.label: Cromosoma X
nodos.desc: Cromosoma sexual que las mujeres tienen dos copias (XX) y los hombres una copia (XY).

nodos.label: Cromosoma Y
nodos.desc: Cromosoma sexual presente en los hombres, que no lleva genes de muchas características hereditarias.

nodos.label: Trastorno recesivo
nodos.desc: Un rasgo que solo se expresa cuando un individuo hereda dos alelos recesivos, uno de cada padre.

nodos.label: Patrón de herencia
nodos.desc: Forma en que se transmite un rasgo o enfermedad de generación en generación.

nodos.label: Portador
nodos.desc: Individuo que tiene un alelo recesivo pero no muestra el rasgo, ya que necesita dos copias para expresarlo.

nodos.label: Genetic Expression
nodos.desc: The process by which information from a gene is used in a cell to synthesize a functional product, such as a protein.

nodos.label: Epigenetic Modification
nodos.desc: Heritable changes in gene expression that do not involve changes to the underlying DNA sequence, such as DNA methylation and histone acetylation.

nodos.label: Probabilistic Model
nodos.desc: A mathematical framework that accounts for the likelihood of multiple genotypes producing similar phenotypes due to shared biological pathways.

nodos.label: Interactive Model
nodos.desc: A model that integrates both genetic and environmental factors to predict phenotypic outcomes, emphasizing their combined influence.

nodos.label: Signaling Molecules
nodos.desc: Molecules that transmit signals within and between cells, often regulating gene expression in response to environmental stimuli.

nodos.label: Metabolic Enzymes
nodos.desc: Enzymes that catalyze biochemical reactions in metabolic pathways, influencing gene expression and phenotypic outcomes.

nodos.label: Gene Expression Rate
nodos.desc: The level at which a gene is transcribed and translated into protein, influencing the final phenotype.

nodos.label: Stress Response
nodos.desc: Biological mechanisms activated in response to adverse environmental conditions, such as those studied in the 5-HTTLPR polymorphism research.

nodos.label: Polygenic Trait
nodos.desc: A trait influenced by multiple genes, often with complex interactions between genetic and environmental factors.

nodos.label: Insertion or Deletion (Indel)
nodos.desc: Adición o eliminación de uno o más nucleótidos en la secuencia del ADN, que puede causar desplazamiento del marco de lectura y alterar la estructura y función de proteínas.

nodos.label: Duplication
nodos.desc: Replicación de un segmento del ADN, que puede provocar aberraciones cromosómicas y enfermedades durante la meiosis.

nodos.label: Amplification
nodos.desc: Replicación de múltiples copias de un gen o región cromosómica, asociada con un aumento en la producción de proteínas, especialmente en el desarrollo del cáncer.

nodos.label: Deletion
nodos.desc: Eliminación de una secuencia de nucleótidos en el ADN, que puede alterar la función de un gen.

nodos.label: Transversión
nodos.desc: Cambio de un purina por una pirimidina o viceversa en la secuencia del ADN.

nodos.label: Inserción o delección
nodos.desc: Adición o eliminación de uno o más nucleótidos en la secuencia del ADN, que puede causar mutaciones de desplazamiento (frameshift) si ocurre en regiones codificantes.

nodos.label: Receptor de estrógeno
nodos.desc: Proteína en las células que recibe señales de estrógeno; mutaciones en este gen pueden alterar la regulación de estrógeno y promover el desarrollo de cáncer.

nodos.label: Mutación genética
nodos.desc: Alteración en la secuencia de nucleótidos de un gen que puede afectar la función de un proteína o el fenotipo del organismo.

nodos.label: Mutación cromosómica
nodos.desc: Cambio en la estructura o número de cromosomas, que puede tener efectos significativos en el desarrollo y función celular.

nodos.label: Mutación germlinal
nodos.desc: Mutación que ocurre durante la formación de gametos y se transmite a las generaciones siguientes.

nodos.label: Mutación somática
nodos.desc: Mutación que ocurre después de la fertilización en tejidos y órganos, no se hereda.

nodos.label: Mutación de desplazamiento de marco
nodos.desc: Mutación que altera el marco de lectura del ADN, cambiando la secuencia de aminoácidos en la proteína.

nodos.label: Marco de lectura
nodos.desc: Secuencia de tres nucleótidos que determina cuál aminoácido se incorpora durante la síntesis de proteínas.

nodos.label: Oncogénesis
nodos.desc: Proceso por el cual las células se convierten en células cancerosas debido a mutaciones en genes reguladores.

nodos.label: Lesión genética
nodos.desc: Alteración en el ADN que puede afectar la función de proteínas y conducir a enfermedades o cambios evolutivos.

nodos.label: Condición patológica
nodos.desc: Estado anormal del organismo que puede ser causado por mutaciones genéticas.

nodos.label: Anabolism
nodos.desc: Process by which cells synthesize complex molecules from simpler precursors using energy from ATP, forming covalent bonds to create macromolecules like proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and carbohydrates.

nodos.label: Catabolism
nodos.desc: Process involving the breakdown of complex molecules into simpler ones, releasing energy in the form of heat or ATP, such as in protein turnover, cellular respiration, and autophagy.

nodos.label: Gluconeogenesis
nodos.desc: An anabolic pathway in which the body converts stored glycogen or intermediates like pyruvate into glucose, primarily in the liver and kidneys, during fasting or starvation.

nodos.label: Single Nucleotide Polymorphism
nodos.desc: A variation at a single position in the DNA sequence among individuals, representing a difference in a single nucleotide base.

nodos.label: Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism
nodos.desc: A genetic technique that detects variations in DNA sequences by analyzing differences in fragment lengths after restriction enzyme digestion.

nodos.label: Cleaved Amplified Polymorphic Sequences
nodos.desc: A method that uses PCR amplification and restriction digestion to detect molecular variation, particularly at exonic SNPs, to infer haplotypes.

nodos.label: Next-Generation Sequencing
nodos.desc: A high-throughput sequencing technology that enables the rapid and accurate identification of genetic variants across entire genomes.

nodos.label: Genome
nodos.desc: The complete set of genetic material in an organism, including all of its DNA sequences, which can vary among individuals.

nodos.label: Bioinformatics
nodos.desc: The application of computational tools and algorithms to analyze and interpret biological data, such as DNA sequences and genetic variants.

nodos.label: Genetic Variant
nodos.desc: A difference in the DNA sequence among individuals, including single nucleotide variants (SNVs), insertions, deletions, and structural variations.

nodos.label: Multiplexity
nodos.desc: The ability to detect multiple genetic markers or variants simultaneously in a single assay or experiment.

nodos.label: Throughput
nodos.desc: The number of samples or sequences that can be processed in a given time, indicating the efficiency and scalability of a method.

nodos.label: Resolution
nodos.desc: The level of detail or precision with which a method can detect genetic variation, affecting the accuracy of genotype calls.

nodos.label: Cyclin-Dependent Kinases (CDKs)
nodos.desc: Enzymes that regulate the cell cycle by phosphorylating target proteins; activated by binding to cyclin partners.

nodos.label: Cyclins
nodos.desc: Proteins that bind to CDKs to activate them; synthesized and degraded at specific cell cycle phases to ensure timely progression.

nodos.label: CDK Inhibitors
nodos.desc: Molecules that prevent premature activation of CDKs and maintain cell cycle arrest under specific conditions.

nodos.label: CDKN2A Gene
nodos.desc: Gene encoding the p16INK4a protein, a CDK inhibitor; mutations in this gene are commonly found in human cancers and impair cell cycle arrest.

nodos.label: Retinoblastoma Protein (pRb)
nodos.desc: A tumor suppressor protein that sequesters E2F transcription factors, preventing S phase entry; its dysfunction leads to uncontrolled cell proliferation.

nodos.label: G2/M Transition
nodos.desc: A critical checkpoint in the cell cycle where cells must ensure DNA replication is complete before entering mitosis; dysregulation can lead to genomic instability and cancer.

nodos.label: Tumor Suppression
nodos.desc: Biological mechanisms that prevent uncontrolled cell growth; loss of function in key regulators like pRb or CDK inhibitors contributes to cancer development.

nodos.label: Aberrant Cell Cycle Progression
nodos.desc: Uncontrolled or incorrect progression through the cell cycle phases, often due to mutations or dysregulation of key regulatory proteins, leading to tumorigenesis.

nodos.label: Cloning
nodos.desc: The process of creating identical copies of a gene or DNA segment, often used in genetic engineering to produce multiple copies of a target sequence.

nodos.label: Transfection
nodos.desc: A method of introducing foreign DNA into cells using chemical agents or electrical pulses, enabling gene expression in the host cells.

nodos.label: Electroporation
nodos.desc: A technique that uses high-voltage electrical pulses to create temporary pores in cell membranes, allowing the entry of exogenous DNA into cells.

nodos.label: Viral Vectors
nodos.desc: Engineered viruses used as delivery systems to introduce foreign genes into host organisms, leveraging viral mechanisms for efficient gene transfer.

nodos.label: Endogenous Gene
nodos.desc: A gene that is naturally present in an organism's genome and is involved in its normal biological functions.

nodos.label: Bt Corn
nodos.desc: A genetically modified crop that contains a gene from Bacillus thuringiensis, producing a protein toxic to certain insect pests, reducing pesticide use.

nodos.label: Golden Rice
nodos.desc: A genetically engineered rice variety that produces beta-carotene, a precursor of vitamin A, to combat vitamin A deficiency in developing regions.

nodos.label: Gene Therapy
nodos.desc: A medical treatment that involves introducing functional genes into patient cells to correct or compensate for defective genes causing disease.

nodos.label: Cell Fate Determination
nodos.desc: The process by which cells adopt specific identities through molecular interactions and positional cues during development.

nodos.label: Pluripotency
nodos.desc: The ability of a single cell to differentiate into multiple cell types, a property exhibited by embryonic stem cells (ESCs).

nodos.label: Embryonic Stem Cells (ESCs)
nodos.desc: Cells derived from the inner cell mass of a blastocyst that can differentiate into any cell type in the human body.

nodos.label: Nanog
nodos.desc: A transcription factor that maintains the undifferentiated state of embryonic stem cells; its reduction triggers differentiation.

nodos.label: Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells (iPSCs)
nodos.desc: Somatic cells reprogrammed using transcription factors to acquire pluripotency and differentiate into various cell types.

nodos.label: Caspase-8
nodos.desc: An initiator caspase activated by adaptor proteins, which subsequently cleaves and activates effector caspases like Caspase-3.

nodos.label: Caspase-3
nodos.desc: An effector caspase activated by Caspase-8, responsible for degrading cellular substrates and triggering DNA fragmentation in apoptosis.

nodos.label: Apoptosome
nodos.desc: A complex formed by cytochrome c, Apaf-1, and procaspase-9, which activates Caspase-9 through autocatalytic processing.

nodos.label: Caspase-9
nodos.desc: An initiator caspase activated by the apoptosome, which then activates downstream effector caspases in the intrinsic pathway.

nodos.label: Effector Caspases
nodos.desc: Caspases that are activated in both intrinsic and extrinsic pathways and mediate the degradation of cellular substrates and DNA fragmentation.

nodos.label: Cytochrome c
nodos.desc: A mitochondrial protein released into the cytosol during stress, where it forms the apoptosome with Apaf-1 and procaspase-9.

nodos.label: DNA Fragmentation
nodos.desc: A hallmark feature of apoptosis, mediated by endogenous nucleases activated by effector caspases, resulting in internucleosomal cleavage of DNA.

nodos.label: Intrinsic Pathway
nodos.desc: A stress-induced pathway activated by DNA damage, oxidative stress, or growth factor withdrawal, leading to mitochondrial cytochrome c release and apoptosome formation.

nodos.label: Extrinsic Pathway
nodos.desc: A pathway initiated by extracellular signals via adaptor proteins and Caspase-8 activation, leading to effector caspase activation.

nodos.label: Cell Homeostasis
nodos.desc: The maintenance of a stable internal environment in cells, achieved through regulated apoptosis in adult tissues.

nodos.label: Tissue Replacement
nodos.desc: A process in which apoptosis enables the shedding and replacement of cells in epithelial tissues like skin and gut.

nodos.label: Dysregulated Apoptosis
nodos.desc: Abnormal apoptosis levels linked to diseases such as neurodegenerative disorders, cancer, and autoimmune conditions.

nodos.label: Autocatalytic Processing
nodos.desc: A self-amplifying mechanism in which activated caspases cleave and activate more caspases, leading to a cascade of cell death.

nodos.label: Substrate Degradation
nodos.desc: The breakdown of cellular components by effector caspases during apoptosis, leading to loss of cell structure and function.

nodos.label: Binary Fission
nodos.desc: A form of asexual reproduction in prokaryotes where a parent cell elongates and divides into two genetically identical daughter cells.

nodos.label: Dynein
nodos.desc: A motor protein that facilitates movement in eukaryotic flagella by generating sliding forces between microtubules, resulting in wave-like bending.

nodos.label: Cytoplasm
nodos.desc: The gel-like substance within a cell that contains organelles and is the medium in which cellular processes occur, including the floating of prokaryotic chromosomes.

nodos.label: Behavioral Divergence
nodos.desc: Changes in behavior among populations that reduce interbreeding, contributing to speciation.

nodos.label: Infraorder Simiiformes
nodos.desc: A taxonomic group that includes Old World monkeys, New World monkeys, apes, and humans.

nodos.label: Parvorder Catarrhini
nodos.desc: A subgroup within Simiiformes characterized by downward-facing nostrils and shared ancestry with apes and humans.

nodos.label: Superfamily Hominoidea
nodos.desc: A taxonomic group that includes apes and humans, encompassing both gibbons and hominids.

nodos.label: Hylobatidae
nodos.desc: The family of gibbons, known as lesser apes, with adaptations for brachiation in Southeast Asian forests.

nodos.label: Hominidae
nodos.desc: The family of great apes, including humans, chimpanzees, and orangutans, sharing a common ancestor with humans.

nodos.label: Brachiation
nodos.desc: A form of locomotion in which movement is primarily achieved using the arms, common in gibbons.

nodos.label: Adaptive Traits
nodos.desc: Characteristics that enhance survival and reproduction in a specific environment, such as elongated arms in gibbons.

nodos.label: Evolutionary Relationships
nodos.desc: The connections among species based on shared ancestry and genetic similarity.

nodos.label: Variación fenotípica
nodos.desc: Diferencias observables en características físicas o funcionales de individuos, derivadas de variaciones genéticas y condiciones ambientales.

nodos.label: Presión ambiental
nodos.desc: Factores del entorno como clima, disponibilidad de recursos o presión de depredadores que influyen en cuáles rasgos genéticos son seleccionados.

nodos.label: Frecuencia de genotipos
