nodos.desc: El derecho y la capacidad de las personas de acceder a programas educativos, especialmente en contextos donde existen desigualdades por género.

nodos.label: Thematic Connection
nodos.desc: La relación o enlace temático que une varias ideas principales en un texto, permitiendo una comprensión más amplia y coherente del tema central.

nodos.label: Quantitative Information
nodos.desc: Numerical data or statistical measurements that represent measurable quantities, such as player stats or team records.

nodos.label: Statistics
nodos.desc: The process of collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and presenting quantitative data to draw meaningful conclusions.

nodos.label: Graphs and Charts
nodos.desc: Visual representations of numerical data that help illustrate patterns, trends, and relationships within the data.

nodos.label: Player Stats
nodos.desc: Numerical metrics used to evaluate individual athletic performance, such as points, rebounds, assists, steals, and blocks.

nodos.label: Team Records
nodos.desc: Quantitative data that track a team's performance over time, such as win-loss ratios, season outcomes, or standings.

nodos.label: Introducción
nodos.desc: Sección donde el autor presenta el tema y establece su tesis o punto principal, incluyendo información de contexto sobre el asunto.

nodos.label: Afirmación
nodos.desc: Una declaración que el autor considera verdadera, generalmente expresada como una opinión en lugar de un hecho objetivo.

nodos.label: Evidencia
nodos.desc: Información que el autor utiliza para respaldar su afirmación, como estadísticas, estudios, opiniones de expertos o ejemplos del mundo real.

nodos.label: Argumento contrario
nodos.desc: Una afirmación que contradice la tesis del autor, mostrando que ha considerado otras perspectivas y fortaleciendo así su propia argumentación.

nodos.label: Conclusión
nodos.desc: Sección que resume los puntos principales del argumento, reafirma la tesis y puede invitar a la acción del lector o sugerir investigación futura.

nodos.label: Credibility
nodos.desc: La confiabilidad del autor o de las fuentes citadas, evaluada por si son expertos en el tema o provienen de fuentes reputadas.

nodos.label: Bias
nodos.desc: A systematic tendency to favor one perspective over another, which may influence the presentation of information or the selection of evidence.

nodos.label: Connotación
nodos.desc: Affective or emotional meaning of a word or phrase beyond its literal definition, which can vary across cultures and contexts.

nodos.label: Major Character
nodos.desc: Personaje central que aparece frecuentemente en la historia y experimenta cambios significativos debido a los desafíos y conflictos que enfrenta.

nodos.label: Minor Character
nodos.desc: Personaje que desempeña un rol de apoyo y puede aparecer solo brevemente en la historia.

nodos.label: Story Element
nodos.desc: Elemento común presente en todas las historias, como personajes, escenario, trama, etc., que permite a un lector comprender mejor la estructura narrativa.

nodos.label: Narrator
nodos.desc: Persona que cuenta la historia, presentando una secuencia de eventos en un formato literario.

nodos.label: Character Action
nodos.desc: The behaviors, decisions, and activities of characters that contribute to the development of themes in a narrative.

nodos.label: Symbol or Motif
nodos.desc: A recurring element in a story, such as an object, image, or action, that carries symbolic meaning and reinforces thematic ideas.

nodos.label: Author Message
nodos.desc: The underlying message or takeaway that the author intends for readers to understand from the literary work.

nodos.label: Analysis Process
nodos.desc: A structured method for identifying and interpreting themes, including guided questions and independent reflection.

nodos.label: Repeated Words or Phrases
nodos.desc: Patterns of repetition in text that indicate the importance of certain concepts, helping to identify main ideas through emphasis.

nodos.label: Text Organization
nodos.desc: The structural arrangement of a text, such as sections or paragraphs, each focusing on a specific aspect, which helps in identifying and relating multiple main ideas.

nodos.label: Interrelation of Main Ideas
nodos.desc: The connections or relationships between multiple main ideas in a text, which help in understanding how different concepts are linked and contribute to the overall message.

nodos.label: Enunciado principal
nodos.desc: Una afirmación clara y concisa que resume la posición principal del autor, debe ser específica y debatable.

nodos.label: Argumentos contrarios
nodos.desc: Posiciones opuestas que el autor reconoce y responde, lo que demuestra comprensión profunda del tema y fortalece su posición.

nodos.label: Apelación emocional
nodos.desc: Uso de emociones como el miedo, la ira o la esperanza para conectar con el lector, aunque debe equilibrarse con información factual.

nodos.label: Éthos
nodos.desc: La credibilidad o apelación ética del autor, que aumenta la confianza del lector en sus afirmaciones.

nodos.label: grumpiness
nodos.desc: a characteristic of being frequently irritable or complaining, often associated with a person who is ill-tempered.

nodos.label: curmudgeon
nodos.desc: a person who is crusty, ill-tempered, and usually old, often characterized by frequent complaints or irritability.

nodos.label: dogged determination
nodos.desc: a persistent and relentless effort to achieve a goal despite difficulties, indicating refusal to give up.

nodos.label: green thumb
nodos.desc: a metaphorical expression referring to someone with a natural talent or skill in gardening and plant cultivation.

nodos.label: Tone and Style
nodos.desc: El tono describe la actitud general o emoción que el autor transmite hacia el tema. El estilo se refiere a la forma única en que el autor escribe, caracterizada por elección de palabras, estructura de oraciones, lenguaje figurado y diálogo. Juntos, el tono y el estilo contribuyen significativamente a la voz del texto y determinan la experiencia del lector.

nodos.label: Figurative Language
nodos.desc: Language that goes beyond literal interpretation to make comparisons, evoke emotion, and create vivid imagery through devices such as similes, metaphors, personification, and hyperbole.

nodos.label: Author's Purpose
nodos.desc: The underlying intent or message an author seeks to convey through a text, such as to inform, persuade, entertain, or express identity and themes.

nodos.label: Thematic Development
nodos.desc: The process by which central ideas or themes in a text are built and reinforced through narrative elements, character actions, and language choices.

nodos.label: Critical Reading
nodos.desc: The practice of analyzing a text beyond surface-level information to interpret deeper meanings, perspectives, and authorial intentions.

nodos.label: Literary Analysis
nodos.desc: A method of interpreting and evaluating literary works by examining language, structure, and stylistic choices to understand their meaning and impact.

nodos.label: Prose
nodos.desc: A form of written expression using sentences and paragraphs, typically in narrative or descriptive form, used to establish tone through language and style.

nodos.label: Colloquial Language
nodos.desc: The use of informal, everyday language, including contractions and conversational expressions, to create a sense of intimacy and familiarity in writing.

nodos.label: Visual Elements
nodos.desc: Graphical components such as imagery, color, light, shadow, and composition used in graphic novels to convey tone and emotion.

nodos.label: Anthropomorphism
nodos.desc: The attribution of human characteristics to non-human entities, such as animals, used in storytelling to convey deeper symbolic meanings and emotional resonance.

nodos.label: Text Layout
nodos.desc: The arrangement and presentation of written text within panels of a graphic novel, which can influence the reader's emotional response and narrative flow.

nodos.label: Lenguaje
nodos.desc: El lenguaje en un texto incluye la elección de palabras y estructuras gramaticales que influyen en el tono, el significado y la percepción del lector, especialmente cuando se usan palabras con connotaciones emocionales o valorativas.

nodos.label: Valoración
nodos.desc: La valoración se refiere a la evaluación subjetiva que una palabra o frase transmite, como positiva, negativa o neutral, y es clave para entender cómo se construye el tono o el mensaje de un texto.

nodos.label: Paragraph
nodos.desc: A textual unit that focuses on a single main idea or point, often building upon other paragraphs to form a larger argument or presentation of information.

nodos.label: Central Thesis
nodos.desc: The main idea or argument that a text is structured around, which is supported and developed by the various parts of the text.

nodos.label: Ocean Conservation
nodos.desc: The effort to protect and preserve marine ecosystems, often involving innovative solutions and critical evaluation of sources to ensure reliable understanding.

nodos.label: Source Credibility
nodos.desc: The reliability and trustworthiness of a source, assessed by the author's expertise and the publication's reputation for accuracy and fact-checking.

nodos.label: Ejemplo de una bicicleta
nodos.desc: Una bicicleta ilustra una relación parte-whole, donde componentes como las ruedas, el marco, los pedales y los frenos forman un todo funcional.

nodos.label: Hoja de un árbol
nodos.desc: Una hoja es una parte de un árbol, y su significado se entiende solo en el contexto del todo, que es el árbol.

nodos.label: Célula en un organismo
nodos.desc: Una célula es una parte de un organismo, y su función y existencia dependen del sistema completo del organismo.

nodos.label: Párrafo en un ensayo
nodos.desc: Un párrafo es una parte de un ensayo, y su contenido solo tiene sentido cuando se entiende dentro del contexto del ensayo completo.

nodos.label: train
nodos.desc: A vehicle or system of transportation that moves passengers along a fixed route, symbolizing a structured yet unpredictable journey with interconnected elements.

nodos.label: passengers
nodos.desc: Individuals traveling together on a train, representing isolated entities that are brought into a shared environment, illustrating interconnectedness and potential for interaction.

nodos.label: game of chess
nodos.desc: A strategic board game involving movement, rules, and outcomes, symbolizing the structured yet unpredictable dynamics of human interactions and decision-making processes.

nodos.label: pieces
nodos.desc: The components of a game, such as pawns or pieces, representing individuals or elements within a system that move and interact according to defined rules.

nodos.label: rules
nodos.desc: The established guidelines that govern how elements in a system (like a game or society) operate, reflecting constraints and structures that shape behavior and outcomes.

nodos.label: Aero
nodos.desc: means 'air' or 'gas'; related to words like aeroplane, atmosphere, and aerosol

nodos.label: Chrono
nodos.desc: means 'time'; related to words like chronological, synchronize, and prochronistic

nodos.label: Demos
nodos.desc: means 'people' or 'citizens'; related to words like democracy, demographic, and endemic

nodos.label: Geo
nodos.desc: means 'Earth' or 'land'; related to words like geology, geometry, and geocentric

nodos.label: Hydro
nodos.desc: means 'water'; related to words like hydrant, hydroelectric, and hydrosphere

nodos.label: Logos
nodos.desc: means 'word', 'speech', or 'reason'; related to words like logic, biology, and encyclopedia

nodos.label: Morph
nodos.desc: means 'shape' or 'form'; related to words like metamorphosis, polymorphism, and amorphous

nodos.label: Psyche
nodos.desc: means 'soul' or 'mind'; related to words like psychology

nodos.label: Inferencia
nodos.desc: Proceso de deducir ideas no directamente expresadas en un texto, basándose en pistas, contextos y conocimientos previos.

nodos.label: Prueba
nodos.desc: Elemento o evidencia presente en un texto o objeto que permite apoyar una inferencia o conclusión.

nodos.label: Fuente
nodos.desc: Material o documento original que proporciona información para realizar inferencias, como documentos históricos o artefactos.

nodos.label: Conclusión
nodos.desc: Resultado final de un proceso de inferencia, una idea o afirmación derivada de evidencias y análisis.

nodos.label: Observación
nodos.desc: Hecho o detalle notado directamente en un texto o objeto que sirve como base para una inferencia.

nodos.label: Inferencing
nodos.desc: The process of making logical guesses about the meaning of text based on evidence and prior knowledge.

nodos.label: Textual Clues
nodos.desc: Elements within a literary text that provide indirect information, allowing readers to deduce unstated meanings or events.

nodos.label: Background Knowledge
nodos.desc: A reader's existing experiences, cultural understanding, or prior learning that informs their interpretation of a text.

nodos.label: Audience Adaptation
nodos.desc: The adjustment of style, tone, or content in a medium to suit the expectations and characteristics of a specific audience.

nodos.label: Narrative Intention
nodos.desc: The purpose or message an author aims to convey through a literary work, shaped by context and audience.

nodos.label: Storytelling Techniques
nodos.desc: Methods used to engage and maintain audience interest, such as narrative structure, pacing, and character development.

nodos.label: Razonamiento
nodos.desc: El proceso mediante el cual se conecta la evidencia con la afirmación, explicando cómo la evidencia apoya la tesis o conclusión del argumento.

nodos.label: Punto de Vista
nodos.desc: Concepto que describe la perspectiva desde la cual se narran los eventos, indicando quién está hablando o pensando en un momento dado, y cómo cambia entre personajes para influir en la comprensión del relato.

nodos.label: Ironía dramática
nodos.desc: Concepto que ocurre cuando los lectores conocen información que uno o más personajes no poseen, generando tensión y expectativa, ya que el público anticipa consecuencias que los personajes no perciben.

nodos.label: Idioma
nodos.desc: Una expresión cuyo significado no se puede deducir de las palabras individuales (por ejemplo, 'costar un brazo y una pierna').

nodos.label: Alusión
nodos.desc: Una referencia a algo fuera del texto, a menudo histórica o cultural (por ejemplo, la historia de amor de Romeo y Julieta comparada con la de Tristan y Isolde).

nodos.label: Narration
nodos.desc: The method by which a story is told, including the perspective from which the events are presented. In this case, first-person narration, where the protagonist, Mr. Henfertz, recounts his own experiences and thoughts.

nodos.label: Omniscient Narration
nodos.desc: A narrative technique where the narrator has complete knowledge of all characters' thoughts and experiences, often providing a broad, all-encompassing view of events. Example: Middlemarch, Anna Karenina.

nodos.label: First-Person Narrative
nodos.desc: A narrative perspective where the story is told from the point of view of a character, using 'I' or 'we'. This allows readers to access the narrator's thoughts, emotions, and biases directly.

nodos.label: Narrator Reliability
nodos.desc: The trustworthiness of the narrator's account of events. In this text, the first-person perspective raises questions about whether Mr. Henfertz accurately represents what happened, due to potential biases or emotional distortions.

nodos.label: Narrative Bias
nodos.desc: Prejudices or assumptions embedded in the narrator's perspective, such as class, gender, or nationality, which influence how events are described and interpreted.

nodos.label: Emotional Response
nodos.desc: The reader's reaction to the story, shaped by the narrator's inner turmoil, frustration, and use of humor, particularly in a first-person context.

nodos.label: Perspective Shift
nodos.desc: The change in narrative viewpoint, such as moving from first-person to third-person limited, which would alter the reader's access to character thoughts and emotional depth.

nodos.label: Humor in Narration
nodos.desc: The use of wit or sarcasm by the narrator to describe characters or situations, which functions to highlight irony, social commentary, or character traits within the first-person framework.

nodos.label: Assumption
nodos.desc: A statement taken as true without sufficient proof or evidence, which can be scrutinized to validate or refute a hypothesis.

nodos.label: Analytical Prowess
nodos.desc: The ability to critically evaluate information, identify assumptions, and distinguish between fact and opinion.

nodos.label: Controversy
nodos.desc: A state of disagreement or debate over a particular issue, often leading to the presentation of conflicting arguments.

nodos.label: Cherry Picking
nodos.desc: A technique where only supportive facts or data are selected to form a biased or misleading representation of a topic, often omitting contradictory evidence.

nodos.label: Leading Questions
nodos.desc: A rhetorical device that frames a question to suggest a particular answer or bias, influencing reader interpretation and steering them toward a predetermined conclusion.

nodos.label: Strategic Emphasis
nodos.desc: The selective highlighting of certain information—such as dramatic statistics or emotional anecdotes—to draw attention away from broader context or background details.

nodos.label: Lenguaje literal
nodos.desc: Forma de expresar ideas sin uso de figuras de discurso, utilizando el significado directo de las palabras.

nodos.label: Freedom of Speech
nodos.desc: The right of individuals to express their opinions and ideas without censorship or restraint.

nodos.label: Freedom of Worship
nodos.desc: The right of individuals to practice their religious beliefs freely and without persecution.

nodos.label: Freedom from Want
nodos.desc: The economic freedom to have sufficient resources to meet basic needs such as food, shelter, and clothing.

nodos.label: Freedom from Fear
nodos.desc: The security and stability that individuals experience in the absence of threats or violence.

nodos.label: Global Cooperation
nodos.desc: The collaborative efforts of nations to achieve shared goals, such as peace, prosperity, and security.

nodos.label: Qualitative Information
nodos.desc: Descriptive, non-numerical data that conveys qualities, characteristics, or observations, such as mood or appearance.

nodos.label: Scientific Consensus
nodos.desc: The prevailing view among experts that human activities significantly influence climate change, forming the foundation for understanding the issue.

nodos.label: Natural Phenomena
nodos.desc: Natural processes such as solar radiation and climate cycles that are proposed as primary drivers of climate fluctuations, independent of human activity.

nodos.label: Human Intervention
nodos.desc: The role of human activities, such as industrial emissions, in contributing to climate change, which is considered substantial by the scientific community.

nodos.label: Opposing Viewpoint
nodos.desc: The argument that climate change is primarily driven by natural forces, challenging the significance of human contributions.

nodos.label: Critical Evaluation
nodos.desc: The process of analyzing and assessing the strengths and weaknesses of both sides in a debate to form a balanced and informed judgment.

nodos.label: Balanced Discussion
nodos.desc: A structured presentation of opposing arguments to ensure fairness, transparency, and the development of critical thinking in readers.

nodos.label: Independent Conclusion
nodos.desc: The ability of individuals to form their own judgments based on evaluated evidence, rather than relying on authority or preconceived beliefs.

nodos.label: Supporting Evidence
nodos.desc: Facts, statistics, expert opinions, or real-world examples that back up the claim and are relevant, accurate, and reliable.

nodos.label: Argument Structure
nodos.desc: The organized framework of a well-constructed argument, including claim, evidence, reasoning, and counterargument, to ensure clarity and persuasiveness.

nodos.label: Conformidad
nodos.desc: Tendencia de los individuos a cambiar su comportamiento o opiniones para adaptarse a un grupo social.

nodos.label: Experimento de Asch
nodos.desc: Estudio clásico en psicología social en el que participantes conformaban a juicios incorrectos de otros miembros de un grupo, ilustrando la fuerza de la conformidad.

nodos.label: Tema principal
nodos.desc: Ideas centrales o argumentos principales que estructuran y guían el contenido de un texto, alrededor de los cuales se organizan las demás partes.

nodos.label: Estructura textual
nodos.desc: Organización lógica de las partes de un texto, que puede incluir relaciones entre secciones, transiciones y signos que indican el desarrollo del argumento.

nodos.label: Transitional Phrases
nodos.desc: Words or phrases used to connect ideas or sections within a text, helping to show the flow and relationships between parts.

nodos.label: Part-to-Whole Relationship
nodos.desc: The structural connection between individual elements of a text and the overall argument or message it conveys.

nodos.label: Noun
nodos.desc: A word that represents a person, place, thing, or idea, such as 'teacher', 'city', 'book', or 'freedom'.

nodos.label: Parts of Speech
nodos.desc: The categories of words in a language, such as nouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs, which serve specific grammatical functions in sentence construction.

nodos.label: Sentence Structure
nodos.desc: The arrangement of words and phrases to form a grammatically correct sentence, which follows syntactic rules to convey meaning.

nodos.label: Language Function
nodos.desc: The role of language in communication, including the ability to convey ideas, emotions, and information effectively through structured expression.

nodos.label: Concrete Noun
nodos.desc: A noun that refers to a tangible, physical entity that can be perceived by the senses, such as a person, place, or thing.

nodos.label: Abstract Noun
nodos.desc: A noun that refers to an intangible concept, emotion, or idea that cannot be perceived by the senses, such as love, happiness, or justice.

nodos.label: Common Noun
nodos.desc: A general term that refers to a category or type of entity, such as 'cat' or 'city', without specifying a particular instance.

nodos.label: Proper Noun
nodos.desc: A specific name given to a unique entity, such as a person, place, organization, or event, and always begins with a capital letter to distinguish it from common nouns.

nodos.label: Singular and Plural Forms
nodos.desc: Grammatical forms of nouns that differ between singular and plural, often derived from Latin, Greek, or other languages.

nodos.label: Irregular Plural Nouns
nodos.desc: Nouns that do not follow standard pluralization rules, such as adding -s or -es, and instead have unique plural forms based on linguistic origins.

nodos.label: Foreign Linguistic Origin
nodos.desc: The source of a noun's plural form, typically from Latin, Greek, Hebrew, or other languages, influencing English pluralization.

nodos.label: Proper Nouns
nodos.desc: Specific names of people, places, or things that are not generalized and may retain original plural forms from their source language.

nodos.label: Contextual Usage of Plurals
nodos.desc: The way certain nouns are used in both singular and plural forms depending on the context, such as in natural languages like Chinese or Hawaiian.

nodos.label: Pluralization Rules
nodos.desc: Standard grammatical rules for forming plurals in English, such as adding -s or -es, which are overridden by irregular forms from foreign languages.

nodos.label: Singular Verb
nodos.desc: A verb form used when the subject is a single entity, such as 'he' or 'it'.

nodos.label: Plural Verb
nodos.desc: A verb form used when the subject is multiple entities, such as 'they' or 'dogs'.

nodos.label: Compound Subject
nodos.desc: Two or more nouns joined by conjunctions like 'and', 'or', or 'nor', requiring careful verb agreement.

nodos.label: Rule 1: Both parts singular
nodos.desc: When both components of a compound subject are singular, the verb is singular.

nodos.label: Rule 2: One singular, one plural
nodos.desc: When a compound subject has one singular and one plural noun, the verb agrees with the last element mentioned.

nodos.label: Rule 3: Coordinating compounds
nodos.desc: With structures like 'either...or' or 'not only...but also', the verb matches the nearest part of the subject.

nodos.label: Collective Noun
nodos.desc: A noun that refers to a group acting as a single unit, typically taking a singular verb unless emphasizing individual actions.

nodos.label: Indefinite Pronoun
nodos.desc: A pronoun that does not specify a particular entity, such as 'anybody' or 'each', and generally takes singular verbs.

nodos.label: Countable vs Mass Quantities
nodos.desc: Some indefinite pronouns like 'many' or 'some' may take plural verbs when referring to countable items, not mass quantities.

nodos.label: Interrupted Sentence
nodos.desc: A sentence with an interruption that may affect verb agreement, though the text is cut off here.

nodos.label: Verbo enlazante
nodos.desc: Verbo que conecta al sujeto con un complemento que describe una cualidad o estado, como en 'la flor es hermosa'.

nodos.label: Verbo de acción
nodos.desc: Verbo que describe una acción realizada por el sujeto, como en 'el perro ladra'.

nodos.label: Verimiento auxiliar
nodos.desc: Verbo que ayuda a formar diferentes formas verbales, como el tiempo, aspecto o voz pasiva, ej. 'do', 'has', 'have'.

nodos.label: Verbo modal
nodos.desc: Verbo que expresa moods como posibilidad, obligación o capacidad, ej. 'can', 'must', 'should'.

nodos.label: Conjugación
nodos.desc: Proceso de variar una forma verbal según el sujeto, tiempo o persona, como 'do', 'does', 'did'.

nodos.label: Estructura verbal
nodos.desc: Combinación de verbos que forman una expresión gramatical completa, como 'do + base verb' para preguntas o negaciones en presente.

nodos.label: Past Tense
nodos.desc: Form of a verb used to describe an action that occurred in the past, typically formed by adding -ed to regular verbs or through vowel shifts in irregular verbs.

nodos.label: Past Participle
nodos.desc: Verb form used to describe a completed action, often used in passive constructions or perfect tenses; in irregular verbs, it may differ from the past tense and involve internal vowel changes.

nodos.label: Regular Verb
nodos.desc: A verb that follows a standard pattern for forming past tense and past participle by adding -ed to the base form.

nodos.label: Irregular Verb
nodos.desc: A verb that does not follow the standard -ed pattern for past tense and past participle, often involving changes in vowel sounds or spelling.

nodos.label: Vowel Shift
nodos.desc: A phonological process in which the root vowel of a verb changes to indicate grammatical tense, commonly seen in irregular verbs such as 'sing', 'ring', 'swim'.

nodos.label: Ablaut
nodos.desc: A linguistic process involving changes in the root vowel of a word to indicate grammatical function, such as tense, particularly in the formation of past tense and past participle forms of verbs.

nodos.label: Phoneme
nodos.desc: The smallest unit of sound in a language that can distinguish one word from another, such as /ɪ/, /æ/, /ʌ/ in the examples of irregular verbs.

nodos.label: Consonant Cluster
nodos.desc: A sequence of two or more consonants that appear together in a word, such as 'br' in 'bring', which affects pronunciation and vowel behavior in irregular verbs.

nodos.label: Silent Letter
nodos.desc: A letter in a word that does not produce a sound, such as the 'w' in 'swim' or the 'd' in 'drink', which influences vowel pronunciation in irregular verbs.

nodos.label: Tense
nodos.desc: Concepto que describe cuándo ocurre una acción en el tiempo, como presente, pasado o futuro.

nodos.label: Aspect
nodos.desc: Concepto que describe cómo se desarrolla una acción en el tiempo, como simple, progresivo o perfecto.

nodos.label: Simple Aspect
nodos.desc: Aspecto que indica que una acción está completada o no tiene relación con el presente, formado con la forma base del verbo.

nodos.label: Progressive Aspect
nodos.desc: Aspecto que muestra que una acción está en curso o en progreso, formado con el presente participle (verb + ing) y un verbo de ayuda como 'be'.

nodos.label: Perfect Aspect
nodos.desc: Aspecto que indica que una acción está completada y tiene relevancia en el momento presente, formado con 'have' (present perfect) o 'had' (past perfect) seguido del verbo en pasado.

nodos.label: Auxiliary Verb
nodos.desc: Verbo que ayuda a formar otros tiempos o aspectos del verbo principal, como 'have', 'had', o 'be'.

nodos.label: Reflexive Pronoun
nodos.desc: A pronoun that refers back to the subject of the sentence, indicating that the subject performs the action upon itself.

nodos.label: Personal Pronoun
nodos.desc: A pronoun that replaces a noun to avoid repetition, such as I, you, he, she, it, we, they.

nodos.label: Suffix -self
nodos.desc: A grammatical suffix added to personal pronouns to form reflexive pronouns, used for singular subjects (e.g., myself, himself, herself, itself).

nodos.label: Suffix -selves
nodos.desc: A grammatical suffix added to personal pronouns to form reflexive pronouns, used for plural subjects (e.g., ourselves, yourselves, themselves).

nodos.label: Person and Number
nodos.desc: In grammar, person refers to the speaker, listener, or subject of the sentence (first, second, third), and number refers to singular or plural form.

nodos.label: Singular 'They'
nodos.desc: A grammatically correct pronoun used to refer to a single, unspecified person, replacing gendered pronouns like 'he' or 'she' to promote inclusive and gender-neutral communication.

nodos.label: Pronoun Usage
nodos.desc: The application of pronouns in language to refer to individuals, with emphasis on grammatical function, agreement, and syntactic consistency in sentences.

nodos.label: Grammatical Function
nodos.desc: The role of pronouns in sentences, including their ability to serve as subjects or objects and to agree in number with their antecedents.

nodos.label: Inclusive Communication
nodos.desc: The use of language that avoids gender bias and promotes equal representation, reflecting societal awareness of gender diversity and linguistic inclusivity.

nodos.label: Countable Nouns
nodos.desc: Nouns that can be counted, such as cats, apples, or trees, which can have articles like 'a', 'an', or 'the'.

nodos.label: Uncountable Nouns
nodos.desc: Nouns that cannot be counted, such as water, air, or sugar, which typically do not require articles.

nodos.label: Definite Article
nodos.desc: The article 'the' used to specify a particular noun that is known or understood by the listener, e.g., 'the cat'.

nodos.label: Indefinite Article
nodos.desc: The articles 'a' or 'an' used to introduce a non-specific noun, e.g., 'a dog' or 'an apple'.

nodos.label: Zero Article
nodos.desc: The omission of articles for plural countable nouns or mass nouns in a general sense, e.g., 'Cats make good pets' or 'Children need love'.

nodos.label: Articleless Reference
nodos.desc: A colloquial or informal usage where articles are omitted, even when grammatically required, often by native speakers in casual speech.

nodos.label: Adverb
nodos.desc: A word that modifies verbs, adjectives, other adverbs, or entire sentences, providing information about when, where, how, or why an action occurs.

nodos.label: Adverb Modifying Verb
nodos.desc: An adverb that describes the manner in which a verb's action is performed, such as 'beautifully' or 'loudly'.

nodos.label: Adverb Modifying Adjective
nodos.desc: An adverb that intensifies or weakens the meaning of an adjective, such as 'extremely' or 'somewhat'.

nodos.label: Adverb Modifying Adverb
nodos.desc: An adverb that modifies another adverb to create a more precise or nuanced description, such as 'relatively fast' or 'incredibly recklessly'.

nodos.label: Adverb Endings
nodos.desc: Common suffixes like '-ly' (e.g., quickly), '-ward(s)' (e.g., backward), and '-wise' (e.g., lengthwise), though not all adverbs follow these patterns.

nodos.label: Context-Dependent Words
nodos.desc: Words that can function as adverbs or other parts of speech depending on the grammatical context in which they appear.

nodos.label: Preposition
nodos.desc: A word that connects other words in a sentence by indicating relationships between nouns, pronouns, and other parts of speech, such as location (in, on, under), time (before, after, during), or manner (with, about, through).

nodos.label: Prepositional Phrase
nodos.desc: A group of words consisting of a preposition, its object (a noun or pronoun), and any accompanying modifiers, functioning as a single unit within a sentence, typically acting as an adjective or adverb.

nodos.label: Object
nodos.desc: The noun or pronoun that follows a preposition and receives the action or describes the relationship indicated by the preposition.

nodos.label: Modifier
nodos.desc: A word or phrase that adds detail or clarification to another word or phrase, such as adjectives or participles, used to enhance the meaning of a prepositional phrase.

nodos.label: Compound Preposition
nodos.desc: A preposition composed of two or more words that together express a specific relationship, such as time, space, causality, comparison, or exception.

nodos.label: Spatial Relation
nodos.desc: A mathematical or logical concept describing the position or location of objects in space, often represented through coordinate systems or geometric relationships.

nodos.label: Temporal Relation
nodos.desc: A concept that describes the sequence or duration of events in time, often expressed through prepositions like 'before', 'after', or 'during'.

nodos.label: Exception
nodos.desc: A case or instance that deviates from a general rule or pattern, often expressed through prepositional structures indicating 'except' or 'besides'.

nodos.label: Coordinating Conjunctions
nodos.desc: Words that join two independent clauses or simple elements, such as 'so', 'but', 'or', 'and'. They connect clauses of equal grammatical status and are used to show logical relationships like contrast, addition, or cause.

nodos.label: Comma Rule
nodos.desc: A grammatical rule stating that a comma should be used before a coordinating conjunction when joining two independent clauses, to separate them and clarify meaning.

nodos.label: Oxford Comma
nodos.desc: A comma placed before the final item in a list, also known as the serial comma. It is optional but can improve clarity, especially when list items contain internal commas or could be misinterpreted without it.

nodos.label: Subordinating Conjunctions
nodos.desc: Words that introduce dependent clauses and establish a relationship between a dependent clause and an independent clause, such as 'because', 'although', 'when', 'if'. They show logical or temporal connections in sentences.

nodos.label: Independent Clause
nodos.desc: A grammatical unit that can stand alone as a complete sentence, containing a subject and a predicate, and expressing a complete thought.

nodos.label: Dependent Clause
nodos.desc: A grammatical unit that cannot stand alone as a complete sentence and relies on an independent clause to form a complete thought. It is introduced by subordinating conjunctions.

nodos.label: Acciones simultáneas
nodos.desc: Dos o más eventos que ocurren al mismo tiempo, con una relación causal o de dependencia.

nodos.label: Acción inmediata
nodos.desc: Una acción que ocurre de forma inmediata tras un evento desencadenante.

nodos.label: Condición previa
nodos.desc: Una situación que debe ocurrir antes de que otra acción se realice.

nodos.label: Marco temporal relativo
nodos.desc: Una referencia temporal que establece cuándo o cuánto tiempo después de otro evento ocurre algo.

nodos.label: Patrón recurrente
nodos.desc: Una relación entre eventos que se repiten de forma consistente en el tiempo.

nodos.label: Duración a partir de un punto inicial
nodos.desc: Un periodo de tiempo que comienza en un momento específico y continúa hasta otro punto.

nodos.label: Intervalo corto
nodos.desc: La diferencia temporal breve entre dos eventos relacionados.

nodos.label: Marco de tiempo futuro
nodos.desc: Una referencia temporal que indica cuándo comenzará una actividad futura.

nodos.label: Paso subsiguiente
nodos.desc: Una acción que ocurre después de una acción previa en un proceso o secuencia.

nodos.label: Finalización de un periodo
nodos.desc: Un límite claro en el tiempo que marca el final de una actividad prolongada.

nodos.label: Condición hasta un punto
nodos.desc: Una situación que se mantiene verdadera hasta que ocurre un evento específico.

nodos.label: Transformación desencadenada
nodos.desc: Un cambio en un estado o situación que ocurre como resultado de un evento específico.

nodos.label: Relación causa-efecto
nodos.desc: Una relación donde un evento (causa) desencadena otro evento (efecto).

nodos.label: Comma
nodos.desc: A punctuation mark used to separate items in a list or to indicate pauses in sentences.

nodos.label: Semicolon
nodos.desc: A punctuation mark that separates items in a list when one of the items contains a comma, to avoid ambiguity.

nodos.label: Bullet Points
nodos.desc: A formatting element used to visually distinguish items in a list, often in conjunction with numbers or text.

nodos.label: Numbered List
nodos.desc: A list where each item is assigned a number, allowing for easy reference and organization.

nodos.label: Horizontal List
nodos.desc: A list where all items are presented on the same line, separated by commas.

nodos.label: Comma in Quotation Marks
nodos.desc: A comma placed inside quotation marks indicates a pause in direct speech, signaling that the words within the quotes are spoken by a character.

nodos.label: Comma Before Dialogue Tag
nodos.desc: A comma is used before a dialogue tag (e.g., 'she said') to separate the spoken dialogue from the speaker's attribution, ensuring clarity in sentence structure.

nodos.label: Multiple Speakers in Dialogue
nodos.desc: When multiple characters speak consecutively, each speaker's dialogue is separated by a comma followed by a dialogue tag, and each new speaker starts with a capitalized word.

nodos.label: Interrupted Thoughts or Actions
nodos.desc: Interjections or mid-thoughts within dialogue are set off by commas; the interrupted part may begin with lowercase unless it forms a complete sentence.

nodos.label: Direct Address in Dialogue
nodos.desc: When a character directly addresses another person during conversation, the name is enclosed by commas, regardless of its position in the sentence.

nodos.label: Complex Sentences with Dialogue
nodos.desc: In complex sentences containing dialogue, commas are used to maintain clarity and structure, ensuring proper separation of thoughts and actions within speech.

nodos.label: Apostrophe
nodos.desc: A punctuation mark used to indicate possession or to form contractions by replacing omitted letters.

nodos.label: Contraction
nodos.desc: A shortened form of two words combined into one, created by removing some letters and adding an apostrophe.

nodos.label: Possession
nodos.desc: The grammatical relationship indicating ownership, expressed using an apostrophe (e.g., 's in 'John's book').

nodos.label: Logical Structure
nodos.desc: The organization of ideas or elements in a sequence or pattern, such as in the formation of contractions or the use of punctuation rules.

nodos.label: Ambiguity
nodos.desc: The presence of multiple possible interpretations, which can be reduced by proper use of punctuation such as the apostrophe in contractions.

nodos.label: Singular Noun Possessive
nodos.desc: A grammatical form created by adding an 's to the end of a singular noun to indicate ownership (e.g., 'the dog's bone').

nodos.label: Plural Noun Possessive
nodos.desc: A grammatical form formed by adding an apostrophe after the final 's' of a regular plural noun (e.g., 'the dogs' bones').

nodos.label: Irregular Plural Possessive
nodos.desc: A possessive form applied to irregular plurals by adding 's at the end, such as 'children's toys', reflecting the singular form 'child's'.

nodos.label: Pronoun Possessive
nodos.desc: A possessive form of personal pronouns indicating ownership (e.g., 'his book', 'her toy', 'its tail', 'our house', 'your car', 'their cats').

nodos.label: Comma Usage
nodos.desc: The use of a comma to separate items in a list or to clarify ownership in possessive constructions, especially when multiple possessors are involved.

nodos.label: Singular vs Plural
nodos.desc: The grammatical distinction between a single entity and multiple entities, affecting the use of possessive forms and determiners.

nodos.label: Apostrophe Usage
nodos.desc: The use of an apostrophe to indicate possession or contractions, with specific rules depending on context and grammatical structure.

nodos.label: Colon
nodos.desc: A punctuation mark used to link two independent clauses, emphasizing the relationship between them and adding clarity and sophistication to writing.

nodos.label: Possessive Apostrophe
nodos.desc: A punctuation mark used to indicate possession, typically added after a noun with an 's' or a simple apostrophe, depending on the noun's origin and regional usage.

nodos.label: Pronunciation Independence
nodos.desc: The principle that the addition of an 's' after an apostrophe in possessive forms does not depend on the pronunciation of the noun.

nodos.label: Regional Variation
nodos.desc: Differences in grammatical usage between English dialects, such as American English adhering strictly to formal rules and British English allowing more flexibility.

nodos.label: Hyphen
nodos.desc: A punctuation mark shorter than a dash, used to connect words or divide a word at the end of a line, typically without spaces around it. Used in compound modifiers before a noun and in some prefixes to avoid ambiguity.

nodos.label: Em Dash
nodos.desc: A longer punctuation mark traditionally used without spaces, to indicate parenthetical information, abrupt changes in thought, or omissions of words in a sentence. It is visually distinct and often used to set off nonessential information or interruptions in thought.

nodos.label: En Dash
nodos.desc: A punctuation mark slightly shorter than an em dash but wider than a hyphen, used for ranges (e.g., 2000–2020) or to connect compound terms. In modern typography, it is often set with spaces around it for visual clarity.

nodos.label: Compound Modifier
nodos.desc: A combination of words that modify a noun, typically placed before the noun, and connected by a hyphen to form a single idea. Hyphens are used when the modifier precedes the noun, not when it follows.

nodos.label: Prefix Hyphenation
nodos.desc: Some prefixes (e.g., ex-, all-, self-) require a hyphen to prevent ambiguity or misreading when combined with a word, especially when the combination could be misinterpreted as a single word.

nodos.label: Parenthetical Information
nodos.desc: Nonessential information inserted within a sentence, set off by an em dash to indicate that it is supplementary and not central to the main clause.

nodos.label: Abrupt Change in Thought
nodos.desc: A sudden shift in the flow of thought within a sentence, signaled by an em dash to indicate a break or interruption in the narrative or reasoning.

nodos.label: Omission of Words
nodos.desc: A suspension or gap in words within a sentence, indicated by a dash to show that certain words are missing or left out, often for stylistic or structural purposes.

nodos.label: Simple Subject
nodos.desc: The primary noun or pronoun that the sentence is about, representing the core entity being discussed.

nodos.label: Complete Subject
nodos.desc: The entire group of words that function collectively as the subject, including descriptive elements that clarify or expand upon the simple subject.

nodos.label: Simple Predicate
nodos.desc: The main verb that directly relates to the subject, expressing the action or state without additional modifiers.

nodos.label: Complete Predicate
nodos.desc: The full set of words that include the main verb and any auxiliary verbs, adverbial expressions, or additional information related to the action or state.

nodos.label: Oración compuesta
nodos.desc: Una oración compuesta contiene al menos dos cláusulas independientes y se forma al unir dos o más oraciones independientes con conjunciones.

nodos.label: Oración compuesta-compleja
nodos.desc: Una oración compuesta-compleja contiene al menos dos cláusulas independientes y al menos una cláusula dependiente, combinando estructuras de oraciones simples y compuestas.

nodos.label: Modificador colgante
nodos.desc: Un modificador colgante es una cláusula dependiente que parece desconectada de su referente, lo que puede causar ambigüedad o error en la interpretación de la oración.

nodos.label: Puntuación
nodos.desc: La puntuación, como la coma, se utiliza para separar cláusulas y clarificar la estructura de una oración, especialmente al unir cláusulas dependientes e independientes.

nodos.label: Subject
nodos.desc: The noun or pronoun that the sentence is about, serving as the core entity performing or being described in the sentence.

nodos.label: Predicate
nodos.desc: The part of the sentence containing the verb and describing an action or state related to the subject.

nodos.label: Direct Object
nodos.desc: A noun or pronoun that receives the action of the verb, answering the question 'what?' or 'who?' after the verb.

nodos.label: Verb
nodos.desc: A word that expresses an action, occurrence, or state of being, forming the core of the predicate.

nodos.label: Desert
nodos.desc: En matemáticas, no tiene un uso directo, pero puede relacionarse con el concepto de conjunto complementario, que es el conjunto formado por todos los elementos del universo que no pertenecen a un conjunto dado.

nodos.label: Dessert
nodos.desc: No tiene un significado matemático directo, pero puede ser usado como analogía para un elemento que completa un conjunto o una estructura, aunque no es un concepto matemático formal.

nodos.label: Complement Set
nodos.desc: El conjunto complementario de un conjunto A dentro de un universo U es el conjunto de todos los elementos de U que no pertenecen a A. Se denota como A^c o A'. Este concepto es fundamental en teoría de conjuntos y lógica.
